Questions include the meaning of SRY testing within the biological diversity of sex, its implementation in sports, and ethical and social issues such as fairness, dignity, and privacy. This symposium will examine the medical meaning of SRY testing, ethical and social issues, and result disclosure and genetic counseling. Rather than reaching a conclusion for or against testing, we will focus on athletes who may learn unexpected genetic information and discuss how genetics professionals can communicate results and support medical and psychosocial needs.

session: S9 アスリートにおけるSRY検査を考える―公平性・多様性・遺伝医療の接点から―
title: Human Sex Differentiation: Lessons from Disorders of Sex Development (DSD)
ja: ヒトの性分化：性分化疾患（DSD）からの教訓
en: Human Sex Differentiation: Lessons from Disorders of Sex Development (DSD)
abs: Sex differentiation is a biological process that forms the two sex phenotypes, male and female, by operating across a three tiered hierarchy, i.e., chromosomes, gonads, and the body, including the formation of male or female typical internal and external genitalia. Its ultimate functional goal is the acquisition of the functions required for sexual reproduction. In mammals, this differentiation is driven by SRY, a SOX transcription factor located on the Y chromosome. In the presence of SRY, undifferentiated embryonic gonads develop into testes, whereas in its absence, they develop into ovaries. Subsequently, the sexual characteristics of the body - centered on the internal and external reproductive organs - are shaped by hormones, primarily testosterone secreted by the testes. DSDs arise when prenatal developmental processes associated with sex follow an atypical trajectory. This concept is entirely distinct from gender defined sexual minorities. Many of the underlying phenomena in DSD can be described biologically, and understanding the mechanisms of DSD helps illuminate the broader issues surrounding sex and potentially gender. In this lecture, I will discuss the mechanisms of DSD from a clinical perspective, which will deepen our understanding of sex.

session: S9 アスリートにおけるSRY検査を考える―公平性・多様性・遺伝医療の接点から―
title: DSD and SRY Testing for Female-Category Eligibility: JAAF Implementation from a Clinical Geneticist's Perspective
ja: 女子カテゴリー出場資格のためのDSDとSRY検査：臨床遺伝専門医から見た日本陸連の実施
en: DSD and SRY Testing for Female-Category Eligibility: JAAF Implementation from a Clinical Geneticist's Perspective
abs: Ahead of Tokyo 2025 World Athletics Championships, World Athletics (WA) required female entrants to submit results of one-time SRY testing, sparking debate. This was not unprecedented: at Atlanta 1996, eight of 3,387 female athletes tested SRY-positive, yet all were allowed to compete. The IOC ended universal sex testing in 1999. After Caster Semenya's 2009 world title, eligibility for athletes with differences of sex development (DSD) became a major issue. Testosterone-based rules followed in 2011 and were progressively tightened. In 2025, WA returned to genetic screening, citing limitations of testosterone suppression in eliminating androgen-related performance advantages. As the only clinical geneticist on the Japan Association of Athletics Federations (JAAF) Medical Committee, and a certified sports physician involved in DSD issues for over 20 years, I played a central role in implementing blood-based FISH testing for Tokyo 2025. I provided pre-test explanations and obtained informed consent; results were disclosed to athletes with support from certified genetic counselors. Eligibility testing may reveal unexpected genetic findings and prompt evaluation for DSD, affecting health, identity and psychological well-being. SRY positivity alone establishes neither a DSD diagnosis nor performance advantage. This talk reviews post-Atlanta eligibility rules and JAAF's implementation, examining how clinical genetics and sports medicine can protect athletes' dignity, privacy and informed choice within a mandatory eligibility process.

session: S9 アスリートにおけるSRY検査を考える―公平性・多様性・遺伝医療の接点から―
title: A Dialogue Between Sport and Genetic Medicine on SRY Testing: Implementation and Positioning of Genetic Information
ja: SRY検査をめぐるスポーツと遺伝医療の対話：実施と遺伝情報の位置づけ
en: A Dialogue Between Sport and Genetic Medicine on SRY Testing: Implementation and Positioning of Genetic Information
abs: Genetic knowledge and testing technologies developed for research and medicine are now applied to sex-segregated sport for non-medical purposes. The IOC policy announced on March 26, 2026, states that genetic testing targeting SRY (SRY testing) will be used for eligibility confirmation. National sports organizations sending athletes to the Olympic Games must address this new testing system, although its normative and procedural frameworks remain insufficiently defined. Athletes may need to come to terms with genetic information concerning their sexuality, including their bodies and identity, and their lives and close relationships. The choices they face include “self-determined choices” regarding additional testing, medical care, and information sharing, and “choices imposed by the system,” such as appeals, category changes, and whether to continue competing. Sex verification testing in sport was discontinued after 2000, while genetics has advanced understanding of human genetic diversity and sex development, along with standards for responsible genetic testing. Therefore, SRY testing for female athletes, including minors, requires examination not only of accuracy and procedures, but also of responsibility sharing between sport and genetic medicine in system design. It is also necessary to consider how non-medical use of genetic testing in sport may influence the future positioning of genetic information. Furthermore, the appropriateness of uniformly applying SRY testing across all sports, regardless of sport characteristics, must be reconsidered. This presentation discusses these issues through dialogue with genetics and genetic medicine.

session: S9 アスリートにおけるSRY検査を考える―公平性・多様性・遺伝医療の接点から―
title: Supporting Female Athletes Undergoing SRY Gene Testing - A Genetic Counselor's Perspective
ja: SRY遺伝子検査を受ける女性アスリートの支援：遺伝カウンセラーの視点
en: Supporting Female Athletes Undergoing SRY Gene Testing - A Genetic Counselor's Perspective
abs: SRY gene testing has recently been reintroduced to determine eligibility for female athletes in major international competitions. Although not performed for medical purposes, detection of SRY may reveal previously unknown medical and genetic information concerning sex chromosomes and sex development. Further evaluation may identify a difference of sex development (DSD), raising issues beyond eligibility, including health management, reproductive health, family communication, self-concept, body image, and privacy. Previous reports on sex verification in sports have described psychosocial and confidentiality concerns associated with unexpected identification of DSD. Literature on disclosure of a DSD diagnosis also emphasizes gradual, ongoing information provision tailored to the individual’s understanding and needs, together with psychosocial support and interprofessional collaboration. However, there is no direct evidence regarding approaches to, or the effectiveness of, genetic counseling specifically for athletes undergoing SRY testing. Obtaining information required under current eligibility rules and deciding how much one wishes to know about one’s own genetic and medical information are, in principle, distinct decisions. It is therefore important to distinguish screening for competition eligibility from testing for medical diagnosis. Based on existing literature, this presentation will consider how genetics professionals may communicate the implications of unexpected genetic findings to athletes, support decision-making regarding further medical evaluation, and address subsequent psychosocial issues.

session: S10 エピゲノムと再生医療：基礎から応用に向けた取り組みまで
title: Genetic and epigenetic diversity at evolutionarily young transposable elements across human induced pluripotent stem cell lines
ja: ヒトiPS細胞株間における進化的に新しいトランスポゾンの遺伝的・エピジェネティック多様性
en: Genetic and epigenetic diversity at evolutionarily young transposable elements across human induced pluripotent stem cell lines
abs: Epigenome information defines cellular identity, and heterogeneity in epigenome states may underlie phenotypic diversity. However, how such diversity arises during the establishment and maintenance of an epigenome state remains poorly understood. We have previously explored epigenome heterogeneity among different human induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) lines by profiling various histone modifications. Most of the heterogeneity was observed in regions of low transcriptional activity or non-coding regions, such as repressed promoters, intergenic regions, or repeat elements, with little effect on transcriptional profiles. We also found that these epigenetic states are associated with differential kinetics of epigenetic reprogramming during in vitro germ cell fate induction, indicating that such heterogeneity affects future cell fate. Notably, we observed epigenetic heterogeneity at evolutionarily young transposable elements (TEs) across iPSC lines; however, detailed locus-specific discussions have been technically challenging due to their repetitive nature. To explore this further, we performed long-read whole-genome sequencing of eight human iPSC lines and conducted in-depth comparative analyses. DNA methylation profiling revealed that a substantial fraction of evolutionarily young TEs, such as L1HS, carry hypomethylated promoter regions, with variation across lines. In addition, by integrating multiple variant-calling tools, we further identified non-reference TE insertions and found line-specific insertion events, a fraction of which retain the full-length form. Together, these data suggest that TEs may contribute to generating not only genetic but also epigenetic heterogeneity among human iPSC lines.

session: S10 エピゲノムと再生医療：基礎から応用に向けた取り組みまで
title: Understanding developmental compatibility between species toward interspecies organ regeneration
ja: 異種間臓器再生に向けた種間の発生適合性の理解
en: Understanding developmental compatibility between species toward interspecies organ regeneration
abs: We have pursued blastocyst complementation, in which pluripotent stem cells (PSCs) are injected into preimplantation embryos designed to lack a target organ as a potential solution to the shortage of transplantable organs. In mouse–rat chimeras, we demonstrated the generation of various organs from donor PSCs, more recently achieved the birth of human-to-mouse chimeras. However, organ-complementing human-to-animal chimeras have yet to be achieved due to the low chimerism of human cells and commitment to the cardiovascular lineages. We therefore investigate when and how “developmental compatibility” breaks down in interspecies chimeras. One of the barrier arises shortly after implantation: human cells are excluded from the host preimplantation epiblast. This was recapitulated in interspecies PSC coculture, where mouse and rat cells intermixed, whereas human and mouse cells underwent sorting out. In contrast, human and chimpanzee cells intermixed. Consistently, human and mouse cells failed to form a chimeric epiblast in embryo model, whereas human and chimpanzee cells did. These findings suggest that the capacity for systemic chimera formation may correlate with evolutionary distance. We are now investigating the molecular basis of “xeno-barriers” by combining 2D coculture, embryo models, and in vivo chimeras. In addition to sorting out, we observed other abnormalities in interspecies chimeras. These phenotypes provide an opportunity to uncover fundamental mechanisms that invisible in intraspecies chimeras. Understanding and overcoming these xeno-barriers may advance organ regeneration while establishing interspecies chimeras as versatile tools for developmental and cell biology.

session: S10 エピゲノムと再生医療：基礎から応用に向けた取り組みまで
title: Toward the reconstruction of snake “limb” cells through reprogramming
ja: リプログラミングによるヘビの「四肢」細胞の再構築に向けて
en: Toward the reconstruction of snake “limb” cells through reprogramming
abs: Limb bud progenitor cells (LPCs) originate from the lateral plate mesoderm (LPM) and possess unique multipotency and patterning capacity to generate the major tissues of mature limbs. Previously, using the mouse as a primary model, we identified reprogramming factors capable of conferring LPC-like identity on non-limb fibroblasts. Forced co-expression of the transcriptional regulators Prdm16, Zbtb16, Lin28a, and Lin41 (PZLL) induced fibroblasts to acquire gene expression profiles and differentiation potential closely resembling those of LPCs. PZLL expression also reduced let-7 miRNAs, which are abundant in fibroblasts but low in endogenous LPCs, to LPC-like levels, consistent with reactivation of let-7 target genes such as Nmyc and Sall4. Building on this work, we are exploring whether embryonic fibroblasts from snakes, which lack limb buds, retain latent competence to form LPC-like cells despite prolonged adaptive evolution. To address this question, we are pursuing two complementary strategies. First, we introduce PZLL into snake LPM-derived cells to activate the LPC genetic program. Second, we generate induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) from snake fibroblasts and sequentially differentiate them into LPM and LPC-like states. Preliminary results show that PZLL expression in snake LPM-derived cells upregulates LPC-associated genes, including Sall4. In parallel, forced expression of OSKM plus NANOG and LIN28A induces endogenous expression of pluripotency-related genes, including Pou5f1. Ongoing work focuses on validating snake iPSCs and defining the regulatory mechanisms that enable reactivation of the LPC program in the limb-less snake lineage.

session: S10 エピゲノムと再生医療：基礎から応用に向けた取り組みまで
title: Epigenetic control of neuronal identity and brain repair through direct reprogramming
ja: ダイレクトリプログラミングによる神経細胞アイデンティティのエピジェネティック制御と脳修復
en: Epigenetic control of neuronal identity and brain repair through direct reprogramming
abs: Direct reprogramming provides a framework for regenerating neurons and understanding how neuronal identity is established. We showed that the pioneer factor NEUROD1 converts microglia, the resident immune cells of the brain, into neurons through epigenetic remodeling. In a mouse model of ischemic stroke, NEUROD1 reprogramming generated striatal neurons that integrated into neural circuits and contributed to functional recovery. More recently, we found that this approach also promotes recovery in the chronic phase of stroke. Interestingly, while NEUROD1 induces predominantly glutamatergic neurons in vitro, reprogrammed cells in the striatum acquire striatal neuronal characteristics, suggesting that NEUROD1-driven neuronal identity is shaped by the cellular environment. Recent single-cell atlases have identified more than 1,000 transcriptionally distinct neuronal populations in the human brain, highlighting neuronal diversity. We therefore asked how interactions among pioneer and other fate-regulating transcription factors influence neuronal subtype identity. By combining two pioneer factors, NEUROD1 and ASCL1, with additional fate-regulating factors, we generated distinct neuronal identities, including dopaminergic/GABAergic co-transmitting properties. Genome-wide analyses further revealed that transcription factor cooperation reshapes the genomic occupancy of pioneer factors and downstream gene regulatory programs. Together, our findings suggest that pioneer factors do not impose a fixed neuronal fate; rather, their output is shaped by cellular context, providing a conceptual basis for controlling neuronal identity in brain regeneration.

session: S10 エピゲノムと再生医療：基礎から応用に向けた取り組みまで
title: Age-Associated Gene Regulatory Changes in the Choroid Plexus and Their Impact on CSF and Brain Homeostasis
ja: 脈絡叢における加齢関連の遺伝子制御変化と脳脊髄液・脳恒常性への影響
en: Age-Associated Gene Regulatory Changes in the Choroid Plexus and Their Impact on CSF and Brain Homeostasis
abs: The choroid plexus (ChP), which produces cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and forms the blood–cerebrospinal fluid barrier (B-CSFB), is a key interface between the peripheral circulation and the central nervous system. Using mouse models, we found that aging induces broad changes in gene expression in the ChP, including reduced expression of genes involved in miRNA biogenesis and extracellular vesicle secretion. We are investigating how these age-associated alterations in gene regulatory programs affect the CSF microenvironment and influence neural stem cells, neurons, and ultimately cognitive function. These findings raise the possibility that the ChP serves as an important link between age-dependent molecular and epigenomic changes and functional decline in the brain.To translate these findings into a human experimental system, we established a robust protocol for generating ChP organoids from human induced pluripotent stem (iPS) cells. These organoids recapitulate key structural and functional properties of the human ChP and provide a platform for investigating B-CSFB function, CSF homeostasis, and disease-associated molecular alterations.By integrating animal models with human iPS cell-derived ChP organoids, we aim to elucidate how aging-associated molecular and epigenomic changes in the ChP disrupt brain homeostasis. Ultimately, this approach may provide new strategies to maintain brain homeostasis and function during aging.

session: S10 エピゲノムと再生医療：基礎から応用に向けた取り組みまで
title: Astrocyte-enriched cortical organoids for studying human brain development, synaptogenesis and neural circuit formation
ja: アストロサイト富化大脳皮質オルガノイドによるヒト脳発生・シナプス形成・神経回路形成の研究
en: Astrocyte-enriched cortical organoids for studying human brain development, synaptogenesis and neural circuit formation
abs: Human iPSC-derived brain organoids are valuable models of human brain development and disease. However, conventional cortical organoids often lack mature astrocytes, limiting neuron–glia interactions and coordinated network activity. We developed astrocyte-enriched cortical organoids (ACOs) by combining control iPSCs with iPSCs engineered to express astrocyte-inducing factors. By day 65, ACOs contained abundant GFAP- and AQP4-positive astrocytes. Compared with conventional cortical organoids, ACOs exhibited more Synaptophysin- and PSD95-positive puncta and ultrastructurally identifiable postsynaptic densities, indicating enhanced synaptogenesis and maturation. Consistent with these changes, ACOs contained a higher proportion of active neurons and showed increased spontaneous firing, bursting, and coordinated network activity. Six months after transplantation into the mouse brain, ACOs showed robust engraftment and neuronal activity. ACO-derived human astrocytes extended processes toward host blood vessels and ensheathed them, forming blood–brain barrier-like structures. These findings demonstrate that astrocytes promote the structural and functional maturation of brain organoids. ACOs provide an advanced human model for studying neuron–astrocyte interactions, neural circuit dysfunction, transplantation, and future applications in biocomputing.

session: S11 RASopathies- history and future perspective
title: Overview-the molecular genetics of somatic, mosaic, and germline RASopathies
ja: 概説：体細胞性・モザイク・生殖細胞系列RASopathiesの分子遺伝学
en: Overview-the molecular genetics of somatic, mosaic, and germline RASopathies
abs: RASopathies are a group of phenotypically overlapping syndromes caused by mutations in genes encoding molecules of the Ras/MAPK signaling pathway. These disorders include: 1) Noonan syndrome caused by mutations in PTPN11, SOS1, RAF1, KRAS, NRAS, RIT1, MRAS, RRAS2, SOS2, LZTR1, MAPK1, ERF, and SPRED2; 2) Noonan syndrome with multiple lentigines (NSML) caused by mutations in PTPN11, RAF1, and BRAF; 3) Costello syndrome caused by oncogenic mutations in HRAS; 4) cardio-facio-cutaneous (CFC) syndrome caused by mutations in BRAF, MAP2K1/2, and KRAS; 5) Noonan-like syndrome caused by mutations in SHOC2, PPP1CB, or CBL; 6) neurofibromatosis type 1 caused by haploinsufficiency of NF1; 7) Legius syndrome caused by haploinsufficiency of SPRED1. In addition, mosaic or somatic RASopathies, including juvenile myelo-monocytic leukemia and vascular malformations, have been identified, further expanding the disease spectrum. It has been 25 years since the first causative gene (PTPN11) of Noonan syndrome was discovered by Prof. Gelb’s group. We have organized this session to celebrate this significant milestone and to explore the future therapeutic approaches for RASopathies.

session: S11 RASopathies- history and future perspective
title: Noonan syndrome and related disorders: How to get to less but not too little
ja: ヌーナン症候群と関連疾患：「少なく、しかし少なすぎず」にどう到達するか
en: Noonan syndrome and related disorders: How to get to less but not too little
abs: Noonan syndrome (NS) and the related disorders, the RASopathies, are genetic traits with overlapping, pleiomorphic characteristics. Cardiovascular involvement occurs in 85% of individuals with NS and includes pulmonary valve stenosis (PVS) and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). Lymphovascular involvement can present as peripheral lymphedema. Nearly 20 genes cause one or more RASopathies when altered, most engendering gain of function in the RAS/mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signal transduction pathway. Cancer drugs inhibiting that pathway rescued HCM in an NS mouse model. In 2017, two infants with NS and severe HCM were treated with the MEK inhibitor trametinib; both improved dramatically and survived, outcomes unlikely for this disease. Subsequently, trametinib has been used more broadly for cardiovascular and lymphovascular issues for patients with RASopathies. A retrospective study of 31 patients with severe RASopathy-associated HCM treated with trametinib, half infants and half older children and adolescents, showed significantly better outcomes than similar patients treated with standard of care. Based on case reports, trametinib has also been apparently effective for the treatment of atrial tachyarrhythmias and lymphatic issues. Side effects from MEKi treatment are common but generally mild, with dermatological issues being the most prevalent. To date, no clinical trial of a MEKi for a RASopathy indication has been completed. For this invited lecture, the history and current state of development of therapeutics for the RASopathies will be reviewed.

session: S11 RASopathies- history and future perspective
title: RASopathies Model Mice for Elucidating the Pathogenetic Mechanism and Developing Treatments
ja: 病態機序の解明と治療開発のためのRASopathiesモデルマウス
en: RASopathies Model Mice for Elucidating the Pathogenetic Mechanism and Developing Treatments
abs: The RAS/MAPK signaling pathway regulates cell proliferation and differentiation; somatic mutations in related genes contribute to “cancer development,” while mutations in the germline cause “RASopathies,” a group of inherited rare diseases characterized by a distinctive facial appearance, short stature, heart disease, and mental retardation. We have identified several genetic mutations that cause RASopathies, and to date, we have generated four model mouse lines having mutations in the Braf, Hras, Rit1, or Lztr1 genes. In this lecture, we will provide an overview of the history of elucidating the pathophysiological mechanisms of RASopathies and developing treatments using these model mice. In addition, we will discuss a possible treatment for RASopathies with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy that involves the activation of brown adipose tissue, a thermogenic organ, which our laboratory has recently been tackling.

session: S11 RASopathies- history and future perspective
title: RASopathies in vascular anomalies: from somatic variant discovery to pathway-targeted therapy
ja: 血管奇形におけるRASopathies：体細胞バリアントの発見から経路標的治療へ
en: RASopathies in vascular anomalies: from somatic variant discovery to pathway-targeted therapy
abs: Vascular anomalies (VAs) are congenital disorders of blood and lymphatic vessels. Most VAs arise from postzygotic gain-of-function variants in the PI3K-AKT-mTOR or RAS-MAPK pathway detectable only in lesional tissue. Lesions driven by KRAS, NRAS, HRAS, BRAF or MAP2K1, such as arteriovenous malformation (AVM) and kaposiform lymphangiomatosis (KLA), are now regarded as somatic RASopathies, the somatic counterpart of germline RASopathies. Because the variant is confined to a minority of endothelial cells, diagnosis requires high-depth sequencing of tissue or, increasingly, cell-free DNA (cfDNA). We showed that the NRAS p.Q61R variant of KLA is detectable in cfDNA from plasma and lymphatic fluid, enabling minimally invasive diagnosis and monitoring. Genotype now guides therapy: investigator-initiated trials in Japan led to the world's first approval of sirolimus for intractable VAs, and pathway-matched agents are under evaluation, including a PI3Kalpha inhibitor for slow-flow malformations and a MEK inhibitor for AVM. In RAS Q61R-mutant endothelial cells, we found partial endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition with paracrine effects on wild-type neighbors, suggesting how a small mutant population remodels an entire lesion. An AMED-funded program is now establishing Japan's first Vascular Anomaly Expert Panel, with a gene panel, tiered cfDNA testing, a VA-specific variant classification framework and a multicenter registry. This talk traces how RASopathy biology has extended from germline syndromes to somatic mosaic disease and outlines the path to precision medicine for VAs.

session: S11 RASopathies- history and future perspective
title: RASopathies and hematologic malignancies: genetic and immunological analysis of juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia
ja: RASopathiesと血液悪性腫瘍：若年性骨髄単球性白血病の遺伝学的・免疫学的解析
en: RASopathies and hematologic malignancies: genetic and immunological analysis of juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia
abs: Juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia (JMML) is a myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative neoplasm of infancy caused by activation of the RAS/MAPK pathway, which is constitutively activated in the RASopathies. More than 80% of patients carry a mutation in PTPN11, NRAS, KRAS, NF1, or CBL. The clinical course depends on which gene is affected and on how germline and somatic lesions combine. A germline PTPN11 variant (Noonan syndrome) or a germline CBL variant often produces a myeloproliferative disorder that resolves without cytotoxic therapy, whereas somatic PTPN11 mutation gives aggressive disease requiring transplantation. Our group has long contributed to the central genetic diagnosis of JMML in Japan and has analyzed samples from over 300 patients. Applying whole-exome sequencing, RNA sequencing, and methylation arrays to this cohort, we defined secondary genetic events that predict poor outcome, identified ALK and ROS1 fusions in patients without a canonical RAS pathway mutation, and established the DNA methylation classification used for risk stratification. We are currently combining autoantibody profiling on a protein array, mass cytometry, and single-cell DNA sequencing. This approach has identified a subset of patients with JMML who produce autoantibodies and carry RAS pathway mutations in B cells, features shared with RAS-associated autoimmune leukoproliferative disorder. In this lecture I will present these studies and discuss what they mean for the diagnosis and treatment of JMML.

session: S12 希少疾患研究の新展開 ― ゲノム診断から病態解析・創薬へ ―
title: Beyond the exome: genome-transcriptome integration for interpreting non-coding variants in rare disease
ja: エクソームの先へ：希少疾患の非コードバリアント解釈のためのゲノム–トランスクリプトーム統合
en: Beyond the exome: genome-transcriptome integration for interpreting non-coding variants in rare disease
abs: Genome sequencing (GS) has expanded our ability to detect variants beyond protein-coding regions, but interpretation of the large number of non-coding variants remains a major challenge in rare disease diagnosis. Transcriptome analysis provides an important clue by directly revealing the consequences of genomic variants on RNA expression and splicing. However, its utility depends critically on the tissue analyzed, because gene expression is highly cell-type specific. We have therefore established RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) using human urine-derived cells (hUDCs), a non-invasively obtainable cell source that robustly expresses many genes associated with pediatric neurological disorders. By integrating GS with hUDC RNA-seq, we have identified or functionally evaluated deep intronic variants causing aberrant splicing, structural variants associated with altered gene expression, and other variants that were difficult to interpret from genomic data alone. We have also applied this approach to 5′-UTR variants in ATRX and POU3F3, illustrating both the usefulness and limitations of computational prediction of non-coding variants. These studies demonstrate that patient-derived transcriptomic data can provide critical functional evidence linking non-coding genomic variation to disease.

session: S12 希少疾患研究の新展開 ― ゲノム診断から病態解析・創薬へ ―
title: Haplotype-resolved long-read genomic and epigenomic profiling improves variant interpretation in rare disease
ja: ハプロタイプ分解ロングリードによるゲノム・エピゲノムプロファイリングが希少疾患のバリアント解釈を改善する
en: Haplotype-resolved long-read genomic and epigenomic profiling improves variant interpretation in rare disease
abs: Long-read sequencing (LRS) improves the detection and characterization of variant classes relevant to rare genetic diseases, including structural variants and short tandem repeat expansions, while enabling simultaneous assessment of epigenomic features. Despite these technical advantages, the role of long-read whole-genome sequencing (LR-WGS) in clinical diagnostics has yet to be fully established. In clinical practice, combinations of conventional genetic tests remain the standard diagnostic approach for rare diseases. Although an increasing number of studies have demonstrated the ability of LRS to identify previously unrecognized disease-causing variants, its added diagnostic value across rare diseases remains to be fully established. Beyond conventional genomic analysis, emerging LRS-based approaches enable single-molecule profiling of DNA methylation, chromatin accessibility, nucleosome positioning, and genetic variation, providing additional layers of information for interpreting complex genetic alterations. In this session, we will present our experience with LRS, including haplotype-resolved genomic, methylation, and chromatin analyses, and discuss insights gained from its application to our rare disease cohort.

session: S12 希少疾患研究の新展開 ― ゲノム診断から病態解析・創薬へ ―
title: SNUPN-Associated Spinocerebellar Ataxia: From Gene Discovery to Disease Modeling and Mechanistic Insights
ja: SNUPN関連脊髄小脳失調症：遺伝子発見から疾患モデルと機序の解明へ
en: SNUPN-Associated Spinocerebellar Ataxia: From Gene Discovery to Disease Modeling and Mechanistic Insights
abs: Spinocerebellar ataxias (SCAs) are genetically heterogeneous disorders, and their molecular basis remains unknown in a subset of patients. We identified biallelic SNUPN variants in three patients from two unrelated families with childhood-onset cerebellar ataxia and progressive cerebellar atrophy, establishing SNUPN as a causative gene for a novel form of SCA. SNUPN encodes snurportin-1, a key mediator of nuclear import of spliceosomal small nuclear ribonucleoproteins (snRNPs). To investigate the disease mechanism, we generated a Snupn mutant mouse model, which recapitulated key features of the human disease, most notably progressive cerebellar atrophy. Functional analyses revealed impaired snRNP nuclear import in Purkinje cells, accompanied by widespread splicing abnormalities. These molecular defects were associated with impaired Purkinje cell dendritic development and dysregulation of signaling pathways essential for cerebellar development and maintenance. These findings demonstrate a mechanistic link between defective snRNP trafficking, splicing dysregulation, and cerebellar pathology. Building on these findings, we are currently exploring gene supplementation as a potential therapeutic approach, extending our work from gene discovery and mechanistic understanding toward therapeutic development.

session: S12 希少疾患研究の新展開 ― ゲノム診断から病態解析・創薬へ ―
title: From long-read genomic diagnosis to international N-of-1 therapeutic development for rare diseases
ja: 希少疾患におけるロングリードゲノム診断から国際的なN-of-1治療開発へ
en: From long-read genomic diagnosis to international N-of-1 therapeutic development for rare diseases
abs: Long-read sequencing provides access to structural variants, repeat expansions, methylation changes, and transcript isoforms that remain difficult to resolve by conventional short-read approaches. We established a high-throughput long-read genome and transcriptome platform to accelerate molecular diagnosis and mechanistic investigation of rare and undiagnosed diseases. Using PacBio Revio, we performed 2,139 long-read whole-genome sequencing runs during FY2024–2025, with a mean HiFi yield of 110.5–112.4 Gb per flow cell, together with 477 Iso-Seq runs yielding 134.1–135.9 Gb on average. Integrated analyses of sequence variation, repeat structure, methylation, and full-length RNA isoforms have identified disease-associated alterations that were difficult to detect using short-read sequencing, including intermediate LRP12GGC repeat expansions, expanded and methylated NOTCH2NLC repeats, and abnormal MAPT splicing in myotonic dystrophy autopsy brains. We are now extending this platform beyond diagnosis toward mechanism-based therapeutic development. In collaboration with Erasmus University Medical Center in Rotterdam, the Netherlands, we are developing an N-of-1+ framework that connects patient-specific genomic and transcriptomic abnormalities to functional validation and individualized therapeutic strategies, including antisense oligonucleotides. This integrated approach aims to establish a seamless pathway from genome diagnosis to disease mechanism and precision therapy for rare diseases.

session: S12 希少疾患研究の新展開 ― ゲノム診断から病態解析・創薬へ ―
title: From Genetic Diagnosis to Splicing-Directed Therapy: Targeting Pseudoexons in Rare Diseases
ja: 遺伝学的診断からスプライシング標的治療へ：希少疾患における偽エクソンの標的化
en: From Genetic Diagnosis to Splicing-Directed Therapy: Targeting Pseudoexons in Rare Diseases
abs: Aberrant RNA splicing is increasingly recognized as an important and underdiagnosed mechanism in rare genetic diseases. Genetic variants can disrupt canonical splice sites or alter cis-regulatory elements, while deep intronic variants may activate cryptic splice sites and induce pseudoexon inclusion that is often missed by conventional exome-based diagnosis. Accurate interpretation therefore requires integration of genomic analysis with RNA studies, splicing prediction, and functional validation. In this presentation, I will discuss a translational framework that connects genetic diagnosis to splicing-directed therapy, with particular emphasis on pseudoexon activation as a representative and therapeutically tractable mechanism. Disease-causing splice alterations can be corrected by splice-switching oligonucleotides designed to block aberrant splice sites or regulatory elements. Small-molecule splicing modulators provide another strategy by modifying the activity of the splicing machinery. Our studies, including a deep intronic GLA variant causing cardiac Fabry disease, illustrate how identification of a pathogenic splicing event can lead directly to therapeutic development. These approaches position RNA splicing as a key interface between variant interpretation, disease mechanism, and precision therapy. Integrating genomic diagnosis, transcript-level functional analysis, and splicing-directed drug development may expand therapeutic opportunities for patients with rare genetic diseases.

session: S13 小児遺伝医療の羅針盤 ―ゲノム解析と病態理解から医療実装へ―
title: Genetic Etiology of Persistent Truncus Arteriosus: Prevalent TMEM260 Variants in the Japanese Population
ja: 総動脈幹遺残症の遺伝的病因：日本人集団に高頻度なTMEM260バリアント
en: Genetic Etiology of Persistent Truncus Arteriosus: Prevalent TMEM260 Variants in the Japanese Population
abs: Persistent truncus arteriosus (PTA) is a congenital heart defect characterized by a single common arterial trunk, occurring in approximately PTA cases, other major genetic causes remain largely unknown. We performed whole-genome sequencing on 11 Japanese PTA patients without the 22q11.2 deletion. Strikingly, pathogenic variants were identified in 8 patients, including variants in TMEM260 in 6 patients and in GATA6 or NOTCH1 in 2. Biallelic loss-of-function variants in TMEM260 are linked to structural heart defects and renal anomalies syndrome (SHDRA), which commonly presents with PTA. Interestingly, our cohort of Japanese PTA patients with TMEM260 variants showed fewer extracardiac anomalies than previously reported SHDRA cases. Most notably, we identified a prevalent TMEM260 (ENST00000261556.6) variant in the Japanese population, c.1617del (p.Trp539Cysfs*9), in 8 of 22 alleles across the 11 patients, estimated to have originated approximately 23,000 years ago. Based on its allele frequency (0.36%), we estimate that approximately 26% of Japanese PTA patients may carry the homozygous c.1617del variant. Furthermore, by combining this with an approximately 7-kb deletion found in one patient—another prevalent Japanese-specific variant (allele frequency 0.17%)—more than half of Japanese PTA cases could be associated with TMEM260 variants. This study highlights pathogenic variants in the TMEM260 gene as the primary genetic cause of Japanese PTA.

session: S13 小児遺伝医療の羅針盤 ―ゲノム解析と病態理解から医療実装へ―
title: The Importance of Early Detection and Treatment Initiation in Familial Hypercholesterolemia
ja: 家族性高コレステロール血症における早期発見と早期治療開始の重要性
en: The Importance of Early Detection and Treatment Initiation in Familial Hypercholesterolemia
abs: Familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) is one of the most common hereditary disorders, affecting approximately 1 in 300 individuals. Despite its high prevalence, the diagnosis rate in Japan remains only 2.6%, highlighting the urgent need for improved detection strategies. Early identification is particularly important in FH because, according to the cumulative LDL-C burden hypothesis, cardiovascular risk is determined not by LDL-C levels at a single time point but by lifelong cumulative exposure to elevated LDL-C, which begins at birth. In current clinical practice, identifying FH based solely on adult LDL-C levels is challenging due to confounding lifestyle and environmental factors. In contrast, childhood lipid levels more directly reflect genetic background, making pediatric universal screening a practical and effective approach. In Kagawa Prefecture, a model combining universal lipid screening of children aged 9-10 years with reverse cascade screening has achieved a diagnosis rate of 15%, with favorable cost-effectiveness and long-term reductions in healthcare expenditure. However, screening infrastructure alone is insufficient. Raising disease awareness among healthcare professionals, patients, and the public is essential. Close collaboration among schools, medical associations, local governments, and academic organizations is required to ensure that early detection leads to timely treatment initiation, thereby minimizing cumulative LDL-C burden and reducing future cardiovascular events.

session: S13 小児遺伝医療の羅針盤 ―ゲノム解析と病態理解から医療実装へ―
title: A Novel Inborn Error of Immunity Caused by Heterodimeric Interference of BCL11B
ja: BCL11Bのヘテロ二量体干渉による新規先天性免疫異常症
en: A Novel Inborn Error of Immunity Caused by Heterodimeric Interference of BCL11B
abs: Studies in mice demonstrated that Bcl11b is indispensable for T cell development. A de novo missense BCL11BN441K variant was identified from a patient with T cell deficiency and neurological disorders. To understand the molecular pathogenesis caused by BCL11BN441K variant, we generated a mouse strain harboring a corresponding mutation, Bcl11bN440K. While delayed development of T cells in the Bcl11b+/N440K mice recapitulates the human patient phenotype, we observed an emergence of NKp46+ cells in the thymus of Bcl11b+/ N440K and Bcl11b-/N440K, but not in Bcl11b-null neonates. This suggests that Bcl11bN440K exerts dominant negative effects to molecule(s) other than Bcl11b. Given a homodimerization of Bcl11b, we focused on another Bcl11 family member, Bcl11a, and confirmed formation of Bcl11a-Bcl11b heterodimer during early T cell development. Loss of Bcl11a alone resulted in the emergence of NKp46+ cells, which was further enhanced by a combined ablation of Bcl11b. Similarly, Bcl11bN440K mutation caused neurological defect that was induced by the loss of Bcl11a. Our proteomics approaches in T cells revealed that the association of Bcl11b with Tcf1 was impaired by Bcl11bN440K mutation. Together with a weaker repression of Tcf1-luc-reporter activity by Bcl11bN440K mutant than Bcl11b, inhibition of NKp46+ cell differentiation in culture from Bcl11bN440K/N440K fetal liver cells by Tcf1 knock-down suggest that Bcl11bN440K hijacks Bcl11 family proteins function in suppressing development of myeloid-like cells in the thymus through diminishing interaction with Tcf1.

session: S13 小児遺伝医療の羅針盤 ―ゲノム解析と病態理解から医療実装へ―
title: Therapeutic prospects for Fukuyama congenital muscular dystrophy: from splicing pathology to clinical implementation
ja: 福山型先天性筋ジストロフィーの治療展望：スプライシング病態から臨床実装へ
en: Therapeutic prospects for Fukuyama congenital muscular dystrophy: from splicing pathology to clinical implementation
abs: Fukuyama congenital muscular dystrophy (FCMD), the second most common childhood muscular dystrophy in Japan, is an autosomal recessive dystroglycanopathy caused by fukutin (FKTN) variants. Most Japanese patients carry a founder SVA retrotransposon insertion that captures a pseudoexon, causing aberrant splicing and loss of functional fukutin and alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation. We previously showed that antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) masking the pseudoexon restore normal splicing and functional protein. This splice-modulating strategy has advanced to an industry-sponsored phase II trial of NS-035, which received SAKIGAKE designation. A second founder allele, a deep-intronic variant creating another pseudoexon, is likewise amenable to a dedicated ASO. Beyond splice correction, we are developing next-generation modalities, including a non-coding RNA (4.5SH) that enhances exon skipping and small-molecule glycan-enhancement therapy, to broaden the therapeutic window. Delivering these therapies requires more than molecular proof of concept: natural-history data, non-invasive multi-organ biomarkers, regulatory and manufacturing readiness, and regional implementation networks. FCMD also extends across Asia, and characterizing patient numbers and FKTN genotypes in Korea, China and Taiwan is essential for international development. Using FCMD as a model, this talk traces the path from genome analysis and pathophysiology to clinical implementation, and discusses the bottlenecks remaining at the seeds stage and how academia, patient organizations and industry can bridge them.

session: S14 様々な先端解析手法からがんゲノムを探索する（To explore cancer genomes through advanced technologies and large databases）
title: Deciphering VUS Pathogenicity via Phenotypic Enrichment Analysis Using C-CAT Data
ja: C-CATデータを用いた表現型エンリッチメント解析によるVUS病原性の解明
en: Deciphering VUS Pathogenicity via Phenotypic Enrichment Analysis Using C-CAT Data
abs: It has become evident that somatic mutations in cancer-associated genes accumulate in the normal endometrium, but spatiotemporal understanding of the evolution and expansion of mutant clones is limited. To elucidate the timing and mechanism of the clonal expansion of somatic mutations in cancer-associated genes in the normal endometrium, we sequence 1311 endometrial glands from 37 women. By collecting endometrial glands from different parts of the endometrium, we show that multiple glands with the same somatic mutations occupy substantial areas of the endometrium. We demonstrate that “rhizome structures”, in which the basal glands run horizontally along the muscular layer and multiple vertical glands rise from the basal gland, originate from the same ancestral clone. Moreover, mutant clones detected in the vertical glands diversify by acquiring additional mutations. These results suggest that clonal expansions through the rhizome structures are involved in the mechanism by which mutant clones extend their territories. Furthermore, we show clonal expansions and copy neutral loss-of-heterozygosity events occur early in life, suggesting such events can be tolerated many years in the normal endometrium. Our results of the evolutionary dynamics of mutant clones in the human endometrium will lead to a better understanding of the mechanisms of endometrial regeneration during the menstrual cycle and the development of therapies for the prevention and treatment of endometrium-related diseases.

session: S14 様々な先端解析手法からがんゲノムを探索する（To explore cancer genomes through advanced technologies and large databases）
title: ABO Blood Group as an Inherited Host Trait: Survival and Spatial Tumour Immunity in Pancreatic Cancer
ja: 遺伝的宿主形質としてのABO血液型：膵がんにおける生存と空間的腫瘍免疫
en: ABO Blood Group as an Inherited Host Trait: Survival and Spatial Tumour Immunity in Pancreatic Cancer
abs: ABO blood group is an inherited host trait whose clinical relevance may depend on treatment context. We analysed survival in 395 patients with resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (205 deaths) and integrated spatial transcriptomics, multiplex imaging and bulk RNA sequencing. Two spatial panels profiled different sections from the same 16 patients. After surgery-first treatment, median survival was longer for O than non-O patients (41.2 vs 25.3 months; P=0.026). The unadjusted ABO-by-treatment interaction ratio was 0.45 (95% CI 0.24-0.84; P=0.011); proportional-hazards diagnostics indicated time dependence. Tertiary lymphoid structure (TLS)-associated tissue was enriched for lymphoid and endothelial cells, with organized lymphoid and follicular-stromal programs. A tumour-cell HK2/PKM/ SLC2A1 expression score in TLS-associated cores showed opposite treatment-context associations across ABO groups, with adjusted interaction support in both panels. TLS-interior T-lineage proliferation-associated expression showed concordant directions, with adjusted support in 5K. In separate ABO- and treatment-adjusted models in 84 bulk-profiled patients (24 deaths), higher TLS12 and three-gene scores were associated with lower and higher mortality hazards, respectively (HR per SD 0.639 and 2.142). These findings connect ABO-associated survival heterogeneity with spatial tumour-immune states, motivating independent validation.

session: S14 様々な先端解析手法からがんゲノムを探索する（To explore cancer genomes through advanced technologies and large databases）
title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of clonal selection and diversification of somatic mutations in normal human endometrial epithelium
ja: 正常ヒト子宮内膜上皮における体細胞変異のクローン選択と多様化の時空間動態
en: Spatiotemporal dynamics of clonal selection and diversification of somatic mutations in normal human endometrial epithelium
abs: Cancer development and progression are driven by aberrant gene regulatory programs, yet the roles of non-coding regulatory elements remain incompletely understood. Enhancers are key regulators of cell-type-specific gene expression, and enhancer RNAs (eRNAs) provide a powerful means to identify active enhancers and investigate their roles in cancer. We have developed advanced 5' end RNA sequencing technologies, including cap analysis of gene expression (CAGE), single-cell transcription start site profiling, and improved full-length RNA sequencing, to systematically characterize human gene regulation and structure across diverse normal and cancer samples. By integrating large-scale transcriptomic datasets, we aim to identify cancer-specific enhancers and their associated transcriptional programs. In particular, our analysis of hepatocellular carcinoma explores alterations in enhancer activity and eRNA expression that may contribute to malignancy. Integrating enhancer landscapes with gene expression, genetic variation, and computational approaches provides a framework for understanding cancer-specific regulatory mechanisms and identifying potential therapeutic targets. Together, these approaches offer new insights into the non-coding regulatory landscape of cancer and opportunities for developing novel diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

session: S14 様々な先端解析手法からがんゲノムを探索する（To explore cancer genomes through advanced technologies and large databases）
title: Decoding Cancer-Specific Enhancers and Gene Regulation through Large-Scale Transcription Start Site Analysis
ja: 大規模転写開始点解析によるがん特異的エンハンサーと遺伝子制御の解読
en: Decoding Cancer-Specific Enhancers and Gene Regulation through Large-Scale Transcription Start Site Analysis
abs: Genetic testing of peripheral blood is widely used to diagnose hereditary tumor syndromes, but variants of uncertain significance (VUS) are frequently encountered and remain difficult to manage. Missense variants account for a high proportion of VUS; in MSH2, for instance, missense variants comprise 1,764 (74.0%) of 2,384 VUS, and more than half (1,041) were submitted by a single institution, reflecting the limited information available for interpretation. To address this, based on the hypothesis that tumors with phenotypes characteristic of a given hereditary tumor syndrome are enriched for pathogenic variants in the causative gene, we analyzed the degree to which specific missense variants in MMR genes are enriched in MSI-H tumors using C-CAT data from over 120,000 cases. Pathogenic and Benign variants showed markedly different enrichment rates, and some VUS appeared closer to Benign. We similarly analyzed POLE/POLD1 variants versus TMB, and CDH1 variants versus diffuse gastric cancer and invasive lobular carcinoma. We present a method for inferring variant pathogenicity from a simple index—the degree of enrichment of a gene's variants in tumors with a specific phenotype—using tumor sequencing data, which are more readily available and more numerous than germline data. This approach requires no special equipment and can be performed by anyone registered for C-CAT data use. As some data processing is needed, we are developing a simple tool for this purpose. We encourage others to examine VUS encountered in daily practice, as doing so may change one's impression of them.

session: S14 様々な先端解析手法からがんゲノムを探索する（To explore cancer genomes through advanced technologies and large databases）
title: Embryonic origins of epigenetic mosaicism in the human colorectal epithelium
ja: ヒト大腸上皮におけるエピジェネティックモザイクの胚発生期起源
en: Embryonic origins of epigenetic mosaicism in the human colorectal epithelium
abs: Somatic cells can acquire epigenetic changes throughout life, generating epigenetic mosaicism among cells of the same type. However, the extent, timing and persistence of this somatic epimosaicism remain poorly understood. Here, by integrating whole-methylome and whole-genome sequencing of 406 single-cell-derived colorectal epithelial clones from 16 donors, we show that, by ~60 years of age, a somatic colorectal lineage accumulates ~1.2 million CpG methylation differences from the consensus epiallelic state. Remarkably, we find that the majority of these differences (>60%) are established during early embryogenesis and are subsequently stably propagated across somatic lineages throughout life, rather than representing age-associated CpG epimutations. These early CpG methylation differences frequently clustered and recurred at specific genomic regions, consistent with embryonic lineage-specific commitment to one of several possible epiallelic states rather than stochastic epimutation. We identified 14,402 such embryonic epiallelic commitment (EEC) regions, which were enriched at CpG islands and gene promoters, particularly those of homeobox genes and zinc-finger/KRAB-domain-containing genes, consistent with a role in early developmental regulation. Notably, EECs were often associated with differences in gene expression across the adult colorectal epithelium, suggesting that their functional consequences may persist into adulthood. EECs also accounted for ~70% of LINE-1 promoter demethylation frequently observed in adult colorectal epithelium and enabled more accurate reconstruction of early developmental phylogenies than somatic mutations alone. This principle extended to the DNA methylation landscape underlying X-chromosome inactivation and escape in female cells. Together, our study reveals early embryogenesis as a major source of lifelong somatic epigenetic mosaicism and establishes clonal multi-omics as a high-resolution framework for tracing its origins, persistence and functional consequences.

session: S15 日本列島人の形成・多様化・適応を探るゲノム研究
title: From Jomon to Present-Day Japan: Genomic Insights into Population Formation and Regional Diversity
ja: 縄文から現代日本へ：集団形成と地域多様性へのゲノムからの洞察
en: From Jomon to Present-Day Japan: Genomic Insights into Population Formation and Regional Diversity
abs: Present-day Japanese populations have been shaped by population differentiation, migration, and admixture throughout the history of the Japanese archipelago. Here, I present genomic studies tracing this history from prehistoric Jomon hunter-gatherers to the regional diversity of present-day Japanese. Analysis of high-coverage Jomon genomes spanning approximately 9,000–2,800 years ago revealed broad genetic continuity within the Jomon lineage, accompanied by fine-scale heterogeneity in genetic affinities to present-day Japanese. High-quality diploid genotypes also enabled polygenic score analyses, revealing differences between Jomon and present-day Japanese in genetic predispositions for several complex traits. Genome analysis of a Yayoi individual from the Doigahama site further provided insight into subsequent admixture. The individual showed a close genetic affinity to populations from the Korean Peninsula, and admixture modeling supported a scenario in which populations with Korean-related ancestry migrated to the archipelago and admixed with local Jomon populations. Finally, genome-wide analysis of more than 11,000 individuals from all 47 prefectures revealed fine-scale regional population structure, largely reflecting regional differences in Jomon-related ancestry and geographic location. Together, these findings illustrate how Jomon diversity and subsequent admixture contributed to the formation and regional diversification of present-day Japanese populations.

session: S15 日本列島人の形成・多様化・適応を探るゲノム研究
title: Jomon genomes illuminate the formation, diversity, and adaptation of populations in the Japanese Archipelago
ja: 縄文人ゲノムが照らす日本列島集団の形成・多様性・適応
en: Jomon genomes illuminate the formation, diversity, and adaptation of populations in the Japanese Archipelago
abs: The Jomon people, hunter-gatherer-fishers who inhabited the Japanese Archipelago for more than 10,000 years, represent a key ancestral population for understanding the formation of present-day Japanese. Ancient genome studies have shown that the Jomon formed a deeply diverged East Eurasian lineage and contributed approximately 10-20% of the ancestry of mainland Japanese through admixture with later migrants from continental East Asia beginning around 3,000 years ago. Our recent analyses of 42 Jomon genomes further reveal substantial regional structure within the archipelago, including a geographic gradient in genetic affinity to northern Paleolithic Eurasians. Genome-wide scans for natural selection also identify signals at loci related to thermogenesis, lipid metabolism, and cold sensation, including FTO, APOA5, UCP1, and TRPM8, suggesting adaptation to environments encountered during the Late Pleistocene. Some of these Jomon-derived variants persist in present-day Japanese and may contribute to phenotypic diversity. We are extending these population-genomic findings through analyses of Jomon ancestry in large contemporary cohorts and experimental studies using donor-derived cells and induced pluripotent stem cells. Together, these approaches connect ancient population history with regional diversity and functional adaptation, providing a framework for understanding how Jomon ancestry continues to shape the genetic and phenotypic landscape of populations in the Japanese Archipelago.

session: S15 日本列島人の形成・多様化・適応を探るゲノム研究
title: Genetic Diversity, Population Structure, and Natural Selection in the Japanese Population
ja: 日本人集団における遺伝的多様性・集団構造・自然選択
en: Genetic Diversity, Population Structure, and Natural Selection in the Japanese Population
abs: The genetic diversity and evolutionary history of the Japanese population remain incompletely understood. We investigated population structure, natural selection, and disease-associated genetic variations using large-scale genome-wide genotyping (DNA microarray) and whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data. First, we conducted genome-wide selection scans of 20,366 individuals from two major Japanese subpopulations, Hondo and Ryukyu. We identified distinct signatures of natural selection, including population-specific signals at the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) region, a novel candidate locus at IKZF2, and differences in selection patterns at ALDH2. These findings suggest heterogeneous evolutionary pressures across Japanese subpopulations. Second, we established the Japanese Encyclopedia of Whole-Genome/Exome Sequencing Library (JEWEL), comprising high-depth WGS data from 3,256 individuals across Japan. Rare variant analyses revealed fine-scale population structure and supported three ancestral components in present-day Japanese individuals. We also identified previously unreported loss-of-function variants, 44 archaic introgressed segments associated with complex traits, including a Denisovan-derived segment at NKX6-1 associated with type 2 diabetes, and additional candidate loci under recent natural selection. Together, these studies provide insights into the evolutionary history and genetic architecture of the Japanese population, highlighting the importance of population diversity for understanding human evolution and disease susceptibility.

session: S15 日本列島人の形成・多様化・適応を探るゲノム研究
title: Genomic perspective on the peopling of the Ryukyu Archipelago
ja: 琉球列島への人類の移住に関するゲノム的視点
en: Genomic perspective on the peopling of the Ryukyu Archipelago
abs: In the Ryukyu Islands, where limestone caves provide an ideal environment for bone preservation, numerous human skeletal remains have been discovered, extending far beyond the Shell-Mound period into the Paleolithic period. Recent systematic excavations at various cave and rock-shelter sites across the archipelago have yielded a succession of ancient human skeletal materials possessing exceptionally high scholarly value. These breakthroughs have also yielded crucial artifacts bridging the chronological and cultural gap traditionally believed to exist between the Paleolithic and subsequent Shell-Mound periods. While conventional archaeological frameworks assumed the Shell-Mound period commenced approximately 7,000 years ago, recent excavations in the Amami and Okinawa regions have unearthed early pottery assemblages securely dating back over 10,000 years, fundamentally reshaping regional prehistory. In parallel with these advancements, cutting-edge biomolecular and scientific approaches have progressed rapidly, accumulating novel insights into these ancient populations. Focusing primarily on the latest results from ancient genome analysis, this presentation comprehensively synthesizes the current knowledge regarding the complex migratory history and population dynamics of humans into the Ryukyu Islands. Furthermore, it outlines future perspectives and directions for multidisciplinary anthropological research in the region, highlighting how genomic datasets continue to redefine the ancestral origins and prehistoric trajectories of the archipelago's inhabitants.

session: S15 日本列島人の形成・多様化・適応を探るゲノム研究
title: Human Evolution in the Era of Complete Genome Sequencing
ja: 完全ゲノム配列決定時代のヒト進化
en: Human Evolution in the Era of Complete Genome Sequencing
abs: Advances in long-read sequencing and de novo assembly have enabled high-resolution analysis of complex genomic regions and structural variation that were poorly represented in conventional reference genomes. Telomere-to-telomere assemblies and human pangenome resources now provide a framework for capturing gene content variation across populations. Using complete genome assemblies, we identified LILRA7, a previously unrecognized gene within the leukocyte immunoglobulin-like receptor (LILR) cluster. This region is highly complex because of extensive segmental duplications and sequence similarity, making it difficult to resolve using short-read sequencing. Complete genome analysis revealed that LILRA7 represents a gene-level structural polymorphism that is absent from the conventional reference genome. We further investigated the distribution of LILRA7 using publicly available whole-genome sequencing datasets from diverse global populations. Its frequency showed marked population differences, with relatively high prevalence in South Asian populations and little or no representation in African populations. These findings suggest that presence/absence variation of immune-related genes may provide additional information on human population history and regional differentiation beyond SNP-based analyses. In this presentation, I will introduce the discovery and genomic structure of LILRA7, its global population distribution, and its diversity in East Asian populations, including the Japanese population. I will also discuss how structural variation in complex immune-related loci may contribute to our understanding of human diversification and adaptation to local infectious environments.

session: S16 多因子疾患の遺伝的基盤解明に向けたゲノム解析の新展開
title: Experimentally-Informed Cell-State Modelling: Linking Single-Cell Genomics to GWAS Interpretation
ja: 実験に基づく細胞状態モデリング：シングルセルゲノミクスとGWAS解釈をつなぐ
en: Experimentally-Informed Cell-State Modelling: Linking Single-Cell Genomics to GWAS Interpretation
abs: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified numerous loci associated with complex diseases, but linking these associations to effector genes, relevant cell types, and cellular mechanisms remains challenging. Expression quantitative trait locus (eQTL) analyses help address this gap, yet conventional bulk RNA-seq can obscure cell-type- and cell-state-specific genetic effects. Single-cell RNA-seq offers finer resolution, but defining biologically interpretable cell-state axes and modelling their interactions with genotype remain key challenges. Drawing on our recent work on T-cell division history, this talk illustrates how integrating experimentally measured cell states with machine learning can reveal context-dependent genetic regulation within a cell type. We generated a division-resolved single-cell atlas of 112,454 CD4+ T cells and developed a deep learning model to infer division state from single-cell transcriptomes (r = 0.881 on independent data). Applying this model to 655,349 T cells from 119 individuals enabled cohort-level analysis of proliferation phenotypes. Single-cell dynamic eQTL analyses incorporating inferred division state revealed regulatory effects missed by analyses that do not account for division-state heterogeneity. These findings highlight the importance of considering not only cell identity but also cell state when interpreting genetic effects. We discuss the opportunities and challenges of integrating human genetics with experimentally informed cell-state modelling to connect disease-associated variation to cellular mechanisms.

session: S16 多因子疾患の遺伝的基盤解明に向けたゲノム解析の新展開
title: Alcohol-Metabolism Genotypes and Multifactorial Cancer Risk in Japan
ja: アルコール代謝遺伝子型と日本における多因子がんリスク
en: Alcohol-Metabolism Genotypes and Multifactorial Cancer Risk in Japan
abs: Alcohol-related carcinogenesis in Japan represents an informative example of multifactorial cancer risk because inherited variation in alcohol-metabolizing genes affects both drinking behavior and biological susceptibility. Functional variants in ALDH2 and ADH1B alter ethanol and acetaldehyde metabolism. Therefore, the same reported alcohol intake may lead to different internal exposure and cancer risk. In this symposium, I will discuss molecular epidemiologic evidence linking alcohol-metabolism genotypes, alcohol consumption, and cancer risk, with emphasis on digestive tract cancers. The presentation will focus on how these genotypes influence drinking behavior, modify exposure-disease associations, and help explain heterogeneity in alcohol-related cancer susceptibility across cancer sites. Evidence will be drawn from case-control and cohort studies, including analyses of genotype-specific associations between alcohol intake and cancer incidence or mortality. Finally, I will briefly consider how aldehyde-metabolism genotypes may be integrated with inherited susceptibility in DNA repair pathways to examine cancer-site-specific heterogeneity. Together, these examples illustrate how population-specific genetic variation can deepen our understanding of multifactorial cancer risk and generate evidence relevant to cancer prevention.

session: S16 多因子疾患の遺伝的基盤解明に向けたゲノム解析の新展開
title: Rare k-mers reveal centromere haplogroups underlying human diversity and cancer translocation
ja: 希少k-merが明らかにするセントロメアのハプログループ：ヒト多様性とがん転座の基盤
en: Rare k-mers reveal centromere haplogroups underlying human diversity and cancer translocation
abs: Centromeres are highly variable, rapidly evolving genomic regions frequently involved in cancer. Their repetitive α-satellite higher-order repeats (HORs) make them difficult to analyze by conventional sequencing, while large-scale long-read sequencing remains challenging. Using rare k-mer markers, we show that α-satellite HOR haplotypes cluster into genetically related haplogroups. We developed ascairn (https://github.com/friend1ws/ascairn) to infer these haplogroups from short-read whole-genome sequencing data. Analysis of >3,300 human samples revealed extensive centromere diversity and geographic variation. Applying the method to centromere sequences from variation. We also investigated der(1;19), the class-defining translocation associated with 1p/19q co-deletion in oligodendroglioma. Analysis of sequencing in two cases. These results indicate that der(1;19) forms a dicentric chromosome with two functional centromeres. Rearrangements preferentially occurred on haplotypes with longer centromeric arrays, and specific centromere haplogroups were associated with increased or decreased likelihood of der(1;19). These findings establish rare k-mer analysis as a powerful approach for studying centromere diversity and centromere-associated chromosomal abnormalities in cancer.

session: S16 多因子疾患の遺伝的基盤解明に向けたゲノム解析の新展開
title: Beyond Mendelian Inheritance: Unraveling the Complex Genetic Architecture of Cardiomyopathies
ja: メンデル遺伝の先へ：心筋症の複雑な遺伝的構造の解明
en: Beyond Mendelian Inheritance: Unraveling the Complex Genetic Architecture of Cardiomyopathies
abs: Cardiomyopathies have long served as paradigms of Mendelian cardiovascular disease, yet rare pathogenic variants alone cannot fully explain their genetic and phenotypic diversity. Incomplete penetrance, variable expressivity, and genetically unresolved cases raise a fundamental question: to what extent do cardiomyopathies represent a continuum between monogenic and multifactorial disease? Recent advances in whole-genome sequencing and large-scale population genomics have expanded our view of this architecture. Rare coding and noncoding variants, structural variation, and common polygenic backgrounds may contribute differently to disease susceptibility, onset, and progression. Dilated and hypertrophic cardiomyopathies provide valuable models for examining these contributions and the potential modifying effects of genetic and environmental factors. In this presentation, I will discuss how integrating rare-variant analysis, genome-wide association studies, polygenic risk scores, and deeply characterized clinical cohorts can refine our understanding of cardiomyopathy genetics. I will also consider how biobank-linked genomic and longitudinal phenotypic data can support studies of penetrance and clinical heterogeneity. Ultimately, defining this complex architecture may help move cardiovascular genomic medicine beyond molecular diagnosis toward more precise prediction of disease onset and severity, risk stratification, and future therapeutic intervention

session: S16 多因子疾患の遺伝的基盤解明に向けたゲノム解析の新展開
title: Machine learning-guided interpretation of rare variants affecting RNA splicing
ja: 機械学習に基づくRNAスプライシングに影響する希少バリアントの解釈
en: Machine learning-guided interpretation of rare variants affecting RNA splicing
abs: Interpreting the functional consequences of rare genetic variants remains a major challenge in human genetics. Altered RNA splicing is an important but often overlooked mechanism, particularly when variant effects are not apparent from conventional protein-coding annotations. Recent advances in deep learning and transcriptomics offer new opportunities to characterize these effects in relevant cellular contexts. In this talk, I will introduce an approach that combines tissue-informed deep learning models of RNA splicing with complementary genomic features to prioritize splice-altering rare variants. Integrating these functional predictions into junction-based rare variant association analyses of whole-genome sequencing data can improve both gene discovery and the biological interpretation of association signals. As an application, I will present findings from a large-scale study of Alzheimer's disease, including insights from microglia-informed splicing prediction and independent brain transcriptomic data. Comparisons of tissue-informed models further illustrate how cellular context can influence the genetic signals and biological pathways highlighted by these analyses. Together, this work demonstrates the potential of integrating deep learning, transcriptomics, and human genetics to better understand how rare variation contributes to complex diseases.

session: S17 ヒト遺伝学の解像度を高める新技術
title: Comprehensive understanding of lung cancer abnormalities using genomic and multi-omics measurement technologies
ja: ゲノム・マルチオミクス計測技術による肺がん異常の包括的理解
en: Comprehensive understanding of lung cancer abnormalities using genomic and multi-omics measurement technologies
abs: Missense variants in glycan-related genes underlie many congenital disorders of glycosylation, yet a large fraction remain classified as variants of uncertain significance (VUS). These genes often show low evolutionary conservation, so conventional sequence- and conservation-based predictors are frequently uninformative. In this presentation, we discuss how structure-based and glycosylation-aware approaches can improve variant interpretation for these genes. With protein structure prediction by AlphaFold, the structural impact of a missense substitution can now be assessed from features such as solvent accessibility, thermodynamic stability (ΔΔG), and local model confidence (pLDDT). We describe VarMeter and VarMeter2, structure-based tools that combine these features and have helped reach molecular diagnoses in undiagnosed patients, and compare them with conservation-based and deep-learning predictors. We then consider challenges for clinical interpretation, including the limited accuracy of stability prediction, variants that increase rather than decrease stability, and the cost of proteome-scale computation. We also point out that current tools evaluate variants on deglycosylated models and therefore miss the stabilizing contribution of glycans: a variant that adds or removes a glycosylation site can be pathogenic through this mechanism even when the protein fold is preserved. Incorporating glycosylation into structure-based prediction should allow these variants to be interpreted more accurately.

session: S17 ヒト遺伝学の解像度を高める新技術
title: Transcriptome analysis using long-read sequencing technology
ja: ロングリードシーケンス技術を用いたトランスクリプトーム解析
en: Transcriptome analysis using long-read sequencing technology
abs: Genetic variations linked to changes in gene expression are known as expression quantitative loci (eQTLs). The identification of eQTLs helps to understand the mechanisms governing gene expression. However, prior studies have primarily utilized short-read sequencing techniques, and the analysis of eQTLs on isoforms has been relatively limited. In this study, we employ long-read sequencing technology (Oxford Nanopore) on B cells from 67 healthy Japanese individuals to explore genetic variations associated with isoform expression levels, referred to as isoform eQTLs (ieQTLs). Our analysis reveals 17,119 ieQTLs, with 70.6% remaining undetected by a gene-level analysis. Additionally, we identify ieQTLs that have significantly different effects on isoform expression levels within a gene. A functional feature analysis demonstrates a significant enrichment of ieQTLs at splice sites and specific histone marks, such as H3K36me3, H3K4me1, H3K4me3, and H3K79me2. Through an experimental validation using genome editing, we observe that a distant genomic region can modulate isoform-specific expression. Moreover, an ieQTL analysis and minigene splicing assays unveils functionally crucial variants in splicing that splicing prediction software did not assign a high prediction score. A comparison with GWAS data reveals a higher number of colocalizations between ieQTLs and GWAS findings compared to gene eQTLs. These findings highlight the substantial contribution of ieQTLs identified through long-read analysis in our understanding of the functional implications of genetic variations and the regulatory mechanisms governing isoforms.

session: S17 ヒト遺伝学の解像度を高める新技術
title: Deciphering human functional genome using Massively Parallel Reporter Assays
ja: 大規模並列レポーターアッセイ（MPRA）によるヒト機能ゲノムの解読
en: Deciphering human functional genome using Massively Parallel Reporter Assays
abs: During cancer progression, cancer cells accumulate genomic, epigenomic and transcriptomic aberrations. To understand the molecular mechanisms of cancer progression, it is essential to comprehensively capture these aberrations by utilizing novel genomic and multi-omics measurement technologies. In this study, we focused on large-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC) which is an aggressive type of lung cancer and of which these molecular bases are still elusive. First, by performing long-read whole-genome sequencing, we identified very complicated genomic rearrangements, such as chromothripsis and extrachromosomal DNA. To confirm precise structures of these aberrations and evaluate their biological significance for LCNEC malignancy, we are now conducting ultra-long read sequencing of cell line genomes. In addition to harboring complicated genomic alterations, individual cancer cells exist in various differentiation states, ranging from well-differentiated cells to those undergoing de-differentiation or trans-differentiation. Our research group also conducted single-cell and spatial omics analysis using Xenium and Trekker Multiome to investigate how cancer cells changed their states. Further, we try to apply the recent spatial omics technologies, such as Atera and Pyxa to lung cancer research. By comprehensively profiling the complicated multi-omics features in cancers using the novel technologies, we would precisely understand molecular features that might be associated with cancer aggressiveness and therapeutic difficulties.

session: S17 ヒト遺伝学の解像度を高める新技術
title: Interpreting Disease Variants in Glycan-Related Genes from Protein Structure and Glycosylation
ja: タンパク質構造と糖鎖修飾から読み解く糖鎖関連遺伝子の疾患バリアント
en: Interpreting Disease Variants in Glycan-Related Genes from Protein Structure and Glycosylation
abs: Most malignant tumors of the eye and ocular adnexa are classified as rare cancers. Their genomic characteristics remain incompletely understood, and evidence-based treatment options remain limited for many of these tumors. We have investigated the genomic landscape of eyelid and conjunctival malignancies, primarily through exome sequencing, and identified major cancer-associated genes in these tumors. To utilize the identified somatic mutations clinically, we are developing a tear-based liquid biopsy approach. This approach aims to detect tumor-derived somatic mutations in tear DNA using next-generation sequencing, with potential applications in diagnosis and assessment of treatment response. Since only a small volume of tears is available from the ocular surface, the amount of DNA available for analysis is extremely limited. By incorporating whole-genome amplification and other technical modifications, we have demonstrated proof of concept for this approach. In this presentation, I will discuss our genomic findings in ocular malignancies and the ongoing development of tear-based liquid biopsy.

session: S17 ヒト遺伝学の解像度を高める新技術
title: Development of a Sequencing Method for Tear-Derived DNA: Application to Liquid Biopsy of Ocular Malignancies
ja: 涙液由来DNAのシーケンス法の開発：眼部悪性腫瘍のリキッドバイオプシーへの応用
en: Development of a Sequencing Method for Tear-Derived DNA: Application to Liquid Biopsy of Ocular Malignancies
abs: 98% of our genome is non-coding, and its function remains largely unknown. The non-coding genome contains a variety of enhancers that play crucial roles in gene regulation. Mutations and variations in enhancers are thought to be a major source of human diseases, individual differences, and evolution. lentivirus-based massively parallel reporter assay (lentiMPRA), a cutting-edge technology that enables high-throughput functional characterization of enhancers at single-nucleotide resolution by quantifying transcribed barcodes. We have leveraged the lentiMPRA technology to dissect enhancer function in the human genome and understand the molecular basis of gene regulation underlying complex biological phenomena, such as cell differentiation, disease and evolution. In my presentation, I will introduce the lentiMPRA methodology and various applications, and discuss the future direction of functional genomics.

session: 教育セッション1（臨床遺伝専門医ブラッシュアップ）
title: Genetic Medicine in Reproductive and Perinatal Care: Current Practice and Emerging Challenges
ja: 生殖・周産期医療における遺伝医療：現状と新たな課題
en: Genetic Medicine in Reproductive and Perinatal Care: Current Practice and Emerging Challenges
abs: Genetic testing in reproductive and perinatal medicine has changed substantially with advances in genomic technologies and their implementation in clinical practice. Prenatal genetic testing includes both screening tests, such as maternal serum screening, ultrasound-based screening and non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT), and diagnostic tests using chorionic villi or amniotic fluid. Since the introduction of NIPT in Japan in 2013, the landscape of prenatal genetic testing has changed considerably, accompanied by the development of a national framework for its provision. Genetic counselling remains essential to support informed and autonomous decision-making, including the option not to undergo testing. Preimplantation genetic testing (PGT) is another important component of reproductive genetic medicine and includes PGT for monogenic disorders (PGT-M), structural rearrangements (PGT-SR), and aneuploidy (PGT-A).
