In PGT-M, assessment of disease severity has long been a central issue. Such assessment requires consideration not only of the natural history, age at onset, phenotype, penetrance and availability of treatment, but also of individual and familial circumstances. Recent therapeutic advances and the expansion of potential indications, including adult-onset disorders, have made these assessments increasingly complex. In this educational session, I will review the historical development and current practice of prenatal genetic testing and PGT in Japan, and discuss emerging clinical, ethical and social challenges associated with advances in reproductive and perinatal genetic medicine.

session: 教育セッション2（臨床遺伝専門医ブラッシュアップ）
title: Hereditary Cancer: Clinical Insights from Endometrial and Ovarian Cancer
ja: 遺伝性腫瘍：子宮体がん・卵巣がんからの臨床的知見
en: Hereditary Cancer: Clinical Insights from Endometrial and Ovarian Cancer
abs: Hereditary cancer care integrates genetic findings with clinical features to guide management of patients and their relatives. This lecture reviews hereditary cancer syndromes, focusing on endometrial cancer in Lynch and Cowden syndromes and ovarian cancer in hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome (HBOC), illustrated by clinical cases. For endometrial cancer, molecular classification provides a framework for recognizing hereditary disease. In Lynch syndrome, mismatch repair gene defects, associated cancer risks, and clinical clues such as early onset and lower uterine segment tumors are discussed. Personal and family histories complement tumor testing, as endometrial cancer may precede other associated cancers. In Cowden syndrome, PTEN pathogenic variants and features including macrocephaly, mucocutaneous lesions, and breast and thyroid disease offer diagnostic clues. Surveillance, risk-reducing surgery, and decision support concerning treatment-related loss of fertility are also addressed. For HBOC, the lecture covers BRCA1/2-associated cancer risks and risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy, focusing on serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma (STIC) detected by detailed pathological examination. Its relationship to high-grade serous carcinoma and challenges in subsequent management are discussed. Pathological and molecular findings illustrate STIC heterogeneity and the need for collaborative research. These examples highlight the integration of genetic and clinical findings into diagnosis and long-term care.

session: 教育セッション3（臨床遺伝専門医ブラッシュアップ）
title: Core Pillars of Comprehensive Practice in Pediatric Genetics
ja: 小児遺伝医療における包括的診療の柱
en: Core Pillars of Comprehensive Practice in Pediatric Genetics
abs: Pediatric genetic disorders encompass a diverse spectrum of conditions, among which multiple congenital anomaly (MCA) syndromes occupy a central role due to their immediate need for comprehensive, lifelong medical management from birth. Over the course of a child's development, pediatric genetic practice is grounded in four core pillars. First, thorough clinical genetic evaluation centers on detailed family history taking, evaluation of associated complications, and face-to-face physical examination—including inspection and palpation using dysmorphology techniques—which forms the basis for comprehensive phenotypic assessment while helping to build trust with families. Second, genetic testing requires the appropriate selection between targeted and genomic approaches, followed by rigorous variant evaluation and pathogenicity classification alongside reverse phenotyping, ultimately leading to a comprehensive diagnosis. Third, etiology-based medical management coordinates personalized, multidisciplinary care tailored to pediatric life stages, informed by insights into natural history. Fourth, genetic counseling provides psychosocial support for parents regarding familial genetic implications, while supporting growing patients in understanding their condition across life stages. Integrating these four pillars optimizes medical outcomes and quality of life for children and their families.

session: 教育セッション4（臨床遺伝専門医ブラッシュアップ）
title: Ethical Challenges and Clinical Practice in Presymptomatic Genetic Testing for Adult-Onset Hereditary Disorders
ja: 成人発症遺伝性疾患の発症前遺伝学的検査における倫理的課題と臨床実践
en: Ethical Challenges and Clinical Practice in Presymptomatic Genetic Testing for Adult-Onset Hereditary Disorders
abs: Presymptomatic genetic testing for adult-onset hereditary disorders raises distinctive ethical challenges, as individuals at risk must decide whether to learn about their future disease risk. The emergence of disease-modifying therapies is transforming the clinical significance of presymptomatic genetic testing. Using hereditary neuromuscular diseases as the main examples, this lecture examines this shift through the four principles of biomedical ethics: autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence, and justice. Presymptomatic testing has traditionally been approached cautiously because many adult-onset hereditary neuromuscular diseases lacked effective treatment and testing could cause psychological or social harm. Recently, treatment options have expanded, including antisense therapy for SOD1-ALS, treatment for GNE myopathy, and disease-modifying therapies for ATTRv amyloidosis, increasing the potential value of early diagnosis. A related shift is emerging in Alzheimer's disease with anti-amyloid therapies, although its genetic context differs from that of monogenic disorders. This lecture addresses the resulting ethical challenges, including ambivalence about testing and learning results, conflicts between an individual's right not to disclose genetic information and relatives' interest in their own risk, and potential social disadvantage. Drawing on the Japanese Society of Neurology's 2025 guidelines and neuropalliative-care approaches, it also discusses how decision support for presymptomatic testing can respect individual values and the practical challenges faced by specialists.

session: 教育セッション5（臨床遺伝専門医ブラッシュアップ）
title: Navigating Genetic Testing for Patients with Undiagnosed Diseases: Test Selection and Result Interpretation
ja: 未診断疾患患者の遺伝学的検査の進め方：検査選択と結果解釈
en: Navigating Genetic Testing for Patients with Undiagnosed Diseases: Test Selection and Result Interpretation
abs: This lecture presents a practical approach to genetic testing for patients with undiagnosed diseases, particularly those with congenital anomalies or other features suggestive of a rare genetic disorder. It addresses how clinical findings, family history, and the suspected disease mechanism guide the choice among array comparative genomic hybridization (array CGH), gene panels, and exome sequencing. The capabilities and limitations of each method are reviewed to clarify when it is appropriate and what it may miss. Result interpretation is then discussed in relation to the patient’s phenotype and inheritance pattern. Particular attention is given to the distinction between variant classification and a clinical diagnosis, the evaluation of variants of uncertain significance, and the implications of a negative result. These considerations inform decisions about additional testing or reassessment of the clinical presentation. Finally, the lecture examines how far to pursue clinical testing before referral to a research team. It considers when further testing may be useful, when research-based investigation may be appropriate, and what clinical information and previous test results should accompany a referral. The aim is to help clinicians make informed decisions at each stage of the diagnostic process and facilitate the transition from clinical evaluation to research.

session: 教育セッション6（臨床遺伝専門医ブラッシュアップ）
title: Advances in genomic medicine
ja: ゲノム医療の進歩
en: Advances in genomic medicine
abs: The costs of whole-genome and whole-exome sequencing (WGS/WES) have fallen dramatically, and so has the cost of analysis. Cloud-based platforms with pay-per-use pricing now take clinicians from raw reads to annotated and prioritized variants without in-house computing, and large language models (LLMs) allow analysis code to be written from natural-language prompts. These tools greatly broaden access to genomic analysis, although they also raise new questions about data governance and the validation of automated outputs. However, while the cost of finding variants has dropped sharply, the cost of resolving them has not. As testing expands, variants of uncertain significance (VUS) and secondary findings will inevitably accumulate, and resolving them still requires careful phenotyping, segregation analysis, additional testing and time. In this seminar, I will outline practical approaches to VUS from both genomic and epigenomic perspectives: points-based ACMG/AMP classification, calibrated in silico predictors, RNA analysis and periodic reanalysis; DNA methylation episignatures as functional evidence; and long-read sequencing, which captures structural variants, phasing and methylation in a single assay but shifts cost toward computational infrastructure. Drawing on our own cases, I will argue that the role of the clinical geneticist is not diminishing but shifting: from performing analyses to asking the right questions, choosing the next test, and communicating uncertainty through genetic counseling.

session: 教育セッション7（臨床遺伝専門医ブラッシュアップ）
title: Multifactorial Diseases, Genetic Susceptibility, and Polygenic Risk Scores: Basic Concepts and Clinical Interpretation
ja: 多因子疾患・遺伝的感受性・ポリジェニックリスクスコア：基本概念と臨床的解釈
en: Multifactorial Diseases, Genetic Susceptibility, and Polygenic Risk Scores: Basic Concepts and Clinical Interpretation
abs: Multifactorial diseases arise from the combined contributions of genetic and environmental factors. This educational session reviews fundamental concepts relevant to genetic susceptibility, including familial aggregation, heritability, allele frequency, and effect size, and introduces genome-wide association studies (GWAS), emphasizing the distinction between statistical association and causation. The RNF213 p.Arg4810Lys variant provides an illustrative example. Originally identified as a major susceptibility variant for moyamoya disease, a rare cerebrovascular disorder, it is a low-frequency founder variant enriched in East Asian populations and strongly associated with disease risk. Associations with a broader spectrum of systemic vascular phenotypes have also been reported. This example highlights the distinctions among allele frequency, effect size, and penetrance, as well as the concept of pleiotropy. We then introduce polygenic risk scores (PRS), which quantify an individual's polygenic susceptibility by summing allele dosages weighted by estimated effect sizes. We explain the basic principles of PRS construction and validation and discuss key considerations for interpretation, including relative versus absolute risk, discrimination and calibration, and differences in predictive performance across populations. The session concludes by discussing how genetic findings can be integrated with family history and clinical information, and how their implications can be communicated to patients and families without implying that genetic risk determines clinical outcomes. The aim is to provide a practical foundation for understanding the potential and limitations of genetic risk assessment in multifactorial diseases.

session: 教育セッション8（臨床遺伝専門医ブラッシュアップ）
title: The 2026 Revision of Medical Service Fees under public health insurance system
ja: 2026年度 診療報酬改定
en: The 2026 Revision of Medical Service Fees under public health insurance system
abs: The key points of the 2026 revision to Medical Service Fees regarding genetics and genomic medicine can be summarized as follows: 1) The Hereditary Disease Care Guidance and Management Fee (B001-11) is newly introduced as a medical management fee, while the Genetic Counseling Surcharge and Hereditary Tumor Counseling Surcharge were eliminated. 2) Insurance coverage for genetic testing (D006-4) has been extended to include newly designated intractable diseases. 3) The Cancer Genome Profiling Evaluation Service Fee (B011-5) is covered once per patient, after a cancer genome profiling test (D006-19) targeting solid tumors, completion of an expert panel review. Additional conditions permit billing this fee without an expert panel review. 4) Regarding BRCA1/2 genetic testing (D006-18) related to hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome, the testing of variants in first-degree relatives is also covered. These four points mark significant progress in genetic medicine. However, they also introduce new challenges. One challenge is the removal of genetic counseling from insurance-covered medical services. Additionally, since BRCA1/2 genetic testing for relatives remains under an LDT (Laboratory-Developed Test) rather than an IVD (In Vitro Diagnostic), testing for known variants may be billed at the same rate as initial testing. In this seminar, we will outline the key points and challenges of the 2026 revision to medical reimbursement rates for genetic medicine and review the Society’s Insurance Committee's activities.

title: Discordant ovarian phenotypes in sisters carrying an identical novel FOXL2 nonsense variant (p.Tyr143Ter)
ja: 同一の新規FOXL2ナンセンスバリアント（p.Tyr143Ter）を持つ姉妹における卵巣表現型の不一致
en: Discordant ovarian phenotypes in sisters carrying an identical novel FOXL2 nonsense variant (p.Tyr143Ter)
abs: Purpose: We report a novel heterozygous FOXL2 nonsense variant (c.429C>G; p.Tyr143Ter) identified in two sisters with blepharophimosis-ptosis-epicanthus inversus syndrome (BPES) type I who showed markedly discordant ovarian phenotypes and assisted reproductive technology (ART) outcomes. This case illustrates the breadth of intrafamilial variable expressivity in BPES type I and its implications for fertility counseling. Methods: Targeted Sanger sequencing of FOXL2 was performed at a national genomics research center. Family history was obtained and a three-generation pedigree constructed. Variant pathogenicity was assessed using ACMG/AMP criteria. Results: Both sisters carried the identical variant p.Tyr143Ter, absent from ClinVar and gnomAD. The older sister (age 37) had low AMH (227.1 pg/mL) consistent with diminished ovarian reserve and achieved a live birth following ART. The younger sister (age 31) showed a paradoxically preserved AMH (627.6 pg/mL) yet experienced follicular unresponsiveness resembling resistant ovary syndrome, with no conception to date. Family history revealed blepharophimosis in the proband's father and paternal grandmother, confirming autosomal dominant transmission across three generations. Conclusions: A single novel FOXL2 truncating variant can produce a wide spectrum of ovarian phenotypes within the same family. Early individualized fertility evaluation is recommended for all female carriers in affected families.

title: Somatic C>A/G>T substitutions acquired early in human placental development: implications for oxidative stress
ja: ヒト胎盤発生初期に獲得される体細胞性C>A/G>T置換：酸化ストレスへの示唆
en: Somatic C>A/G>T substitutions acquired early in human placental development: implications for oxidative stress
abs: Objectives: The placenta after the second trimester is known to have a higher proportion of somatic C>A/G>T substitutions compared with other organs. These substitutions are mostly ascribed to SBS (single base substitution) 18, an oxidative stress-associated mutational signature. Reportedly, placental development requires proper levels of reactive oxygen species. This study aims to clarify whether C>A/G>T substitutions accumulate in the placenta from very early developmental stages. Methods: We analyzed seven term placentas from uncomplicated pregnancies. Villous tissues were excised from 10 to 12 cotyledons of each placenta. DNA samples were subjected to whole-genome sequencing and placenta-specific somatic single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) were extracted. First, we calculated the proportion of C>A/G>T substitutions among all somatic SNVs. Next, we counted the number of C>A/G>T substitutions shared by two cotyledons or by more than two cotyledons in one placenta and subsequently performed signature analysis. Results: C>A/G>T substitutions accounted for 35.1% of all somatic SNVs in the placenta (2,064 of 5,877). The 314 SNVs shared by two cotyledons and 144 SNVs shared by more than two cotyledons included 129 (41.1%) and 57 (39.6%) C>A/G>T substitutions, respectively. Many of these C>A/G>T substitutions were attributed to SBS18. Discussion: Somatic SNVs shared by multiple cotyledons, likely arising very early in development, were enriched for SBS18-linked C>A/G>T substitutions. Our findings suggest oxidative stress-associated mutagenesis in the early human placenta.

title: Universal routine molecular genotyping for suspected hydatidiform moles: A multicenter retrospective cohort study
ja: 胞状奇胎疑い症例への分子遺伝学的genotyping一律実施：多施設後方視的コホート研究
en: Universal routine molecular genotyping for suspected hydatidiform moles: A multicenter retrospective cohort study
abs: Objective: Histomorphological diagnosis of early-stage hydatidiform mole (HM) is unreliable. We evaluated whether universal short tandem repeat (STR)-based molecular genotyping, when applied concurrently with histopathological assessment, improves diagnostic accuracy and clinical management. Methods: Forty-four consecutive first-trimester suspected HM cases were divided into a combination group (duo-analysis STR genotyping plus histopathological assessment; n=29) and a conventional group (histopathological assessment only; n=15). Results: The diagnostic yield of STR genotyping was 96.6%. The diagnostic concordance rate between genotyping and histopathological diagnosis was 55.2%. The re-evacuation rate was significantly lower in the combination group (44.8 % vs. 86.7 %; p=0.007). The definite diagnostic yield was 100% in the combination group versus 73.3% in the conventional group (p=0.01). All 15 CHMs were androgenetic homozygous diandric diploid; all 3 PHMs were heterozygous diandric triploid. The single undiagnosed case was attributable to inadvertent decidual sampling. Conclusions: Universal STR genotyping concurrently with histopathological assessment substantially reduced the re-evacuation rate and achieved 100% definite diagnostic yield. A multisite model with genotyping at a centralized reference laboratory proved operationally feasible at approximately 10,000 JPY (~65 USD) per case. These findings support repositioning STR genotyping as a routine frontline diagnostic tool for suspected HM.

title: The effects of assisted reproductive technology on epimutation-mediated imprinting disorders
ja: 生殖補助医療がエピ変異によるインプリンティング疾患に与える影響
en: The effects of assisted reproductive technology on epimutation-mediated imprinting disorders
abs: Background: Assisted reproductive technology (ART) has been associated with epimutation-mediated imprinting disorders (epi-IDs). However, whether methylation abnormalities arise from ART procedures or underlying infertility remains unclear. Targeted long-read sequencing (T-LRS) enables quantitative and allele specific evaluation of CpG methylation within target regions. We hypothesized that methylation abnormalities affecting both parental alleles are more likely to arise during ART procedures than from defects in gametes, and performed allele-specific methylation analysis using T-LRS. Objective: To compare the proportion of CpGs with methylation abnormalities between ART- and non-ART-conceived individuals and determine whether ART-conceived individuals exhibit genome-wide methylation abnormalities affecting both parental alleles. Results: We enrolled 6 Silver-Russell syndrome (SRS) patients (ART-conceived [n = 3], non-ART-conceived [n = 3]) and 6 Beckwith- Wiedemann syndrome (BWS) patients (ART-conceived [n = 3], non- ART-conceived [n = 3]) with epimutations. T-LRS was performed for 78 known differentially methylated regions (DMRs). ART-conceived individuals showed a greater proportion of aberrantly methylated CpGs involving both parental alleles, compared with non-ART-conceived individuals. Discussion and Conclusions: Our results demonstrate for the first time that ART-conceived individuals exhibit genome-wide methylation abnormalities affecting both parental alleles, suggesting that these abnormalities may arise from ART procedures rather than parental infertility.

title: Improving mitochondrial function in in vitro fertilized ova did not affect embryo telomere length
ja: 体外受精卵のミトコンドリア機能改善は胚のテロメア長に影響しなかった
en: Improving mitochondrial function in in vitro fertilized ova did not affect embryo telomere length
abs: Telomeres serve to protect the ends of chromosomes. The length of the telomeric DNA that constitutes telomeres shortens with each cell division and eventually becomes too short to perform its protective function. Preimplantation embryonic development is an exception in which telomere DNA length increases. In particular, rapid elongation of telomere DNA length is believed to occur during the early stages of embryo development. In this study, we used bovine fertilized ova to investigate the effects of drugs that improve mitochondrial function on telomere length in preimplantation embryos. We analyzed the temporal changes in telomere length in bovine oocytes, two-cell-stage embryos, morulae, and blastocysts using qPCR. Next, we cultured bovine embryos in medium supplemented with C14H22N4O2 2HCl (BGP-15) (10 μM), a drug developed for the treatment of insulin resistance. We measured the oxygen consumption rate (OCR) of the resulting morulae and analyzed the telomere length and mitochondrial (mt) DNA copy number of the morulae and blastocysts using qPCR. Telomere DNA length was calculated as the relative copy number relative to β-actin using qPCR. Telomere length in bovine embryos initially shortened at the two-cell stage and then lengthened as the embryos developed into morulae and blastocysts. BGP-15 increased mtDNA copy number and OCR in morulae (p < 0.01). However, BGP-15 had no effect on the telomere length of the fertilized ova. BGP-15 improved mitochondrial function and mitochondrial DNA copy number in bovine morulae, but no effect on telomere length was observed.

title: Age-Associated Alterations in Symbiotic Microbiota in the Human Reproductive Tract: Implications for Embryo Implantation
ja: ヒト生殖器官の共生細菌叢の加齢性変化：胚着床への示唆
en: Age-Associated Alterations in Symbiotic Microbiota in the Human Reproductive Tract: Implications for Embryo Implantation
abs: <Objective> Female reproductive aging is associated with a decline in fertility, largely through deterioration in oocyte quality. However, the effects of aging on the reproductive tract microbiota and the peri-implantation microenvironment are unclear. This study aimed to investigate age-associated alterations in the reproductive tract microbiota and to evaluate their correlation with in vitro fertilization (IVF) outcomes. <Methods> A total of 38 participants was enrolled, comprising 22 in the successful pregnancy (S-) group (35.0 ± 3.8 years) and 28 in the unsuccessful (U-) group (36.5 ± 2.9 years). Vaginal and intrauterine samples were collected in IVF and frozen embryo transfer cycles. Extracted microbial genomic DNA was sequenced by next-generation sequencing and analyzed by QIIME2 at genus and species levels. <Results> Vaginal microbiota changed across the menstrual cycle and showed greater diversity and higher Lactobacillus species abundance than intrauterine samples. Overall Lactobacillus abundance was not significantly associated with IVF outcomes. In women aged ≥35 years (n = 38), microbiota profiles clustered closely together, whereas in women aged 30~34 years (n = 12), two distinct clusters emerged. Longitudinal analysis of participants sampled before and after pregnancy (n = 4) revealed marked shifts in vaginal microbial diversity. <Conclusion> Female reproductive aging is associated with changes in reproductive tract microbial composition and diversity. These alterations may influence the peri-implantation microenvironment and contribute to IVF outcomes.

title: Characterization of URST1 as a new prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target for lung cancer
ja: 肺がんの新規予後バイオマーカー・治療標的としてのURST1の特性解析
en: Characterization of URST1 as a new prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target for lung cancer
abs: By comprehensive analysis of human gene expression, we identified URST1 (up-regulated in solid tumor 1) as a new prognostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target for lung cancer. URST1 mRNA and its gene product were highly expressed in most lung cancer cell lines and clinical tissues but barely detectable in normal lung epithelial cells and tissues as detected by real-time qPCR, western blotting, and immunocytochemistry. Immunohistochemical analysis using tissue microarray showed that URST1 expression was observed in 231 (64.5%) of 358 non-small cell lung cancers (NSCLC). Strong URST1 expression was significantly associated with poor prognosis for NSCLC patients (P = 0.0003). Knockdown of URST1 expression using URST1-specific siRNAs significantly inhibited the growth of lung cancer cells probably by induction of G2/M arrest and subsequent apoptosis through the activation of several proteins associated with apoptosis. Treating lung cancer cells with small-molecule inhibitors against URST1 suppressed cell growth, partly by inducing G2/M arrest. Microarray analysis and gene knock-down assays using lung cancer cells by siRNAs for URST1 suggested various URST1-related cancer-related signaling pathways. These data suggest that URST1 could be a potential biomarker and therapeutic target for lung cancer.

title: Structure-Based Identification and Functional Validation of Cancer Driver Gene Candidates
ja: 構造ベースのがんドライバー遺伝子候補の同定と機能検証
en: Structure-Based Identification and Functional Validation of Cancer Driver Gene Candidates
abs: Large-scale cancer genome sequencing has advanced driver gene discovery, yet low-frequency functional drivers remain difficult to identify. Because protein function depends on three-dimensional structure, mutations distant in the primary sequence may converge spatially and affect common functional regions. We therefore applied a structure-based framework to detect spatial clustering of somatic mutations as a signal of driver gene candidates. We mapped somatic mutations from 15,305 tumors across 27 cancer types provided by the US National Cancer Institute onto AlphaFold2-predicted protein structures and evaluated inter-mutation distances of 18,966 genes. This identified 441 genes with significant spatial clustering in pan-cancer analysis and 296 genes in cancer-type-specific analyses, including known drivers such as TP53, KRAS, PTEN, and BRAF. We then characterized these clusters using Pfam domains. Tumor suppressor genes (TSGs) showed the lowest fraction of mutations within annotated domains, whereas oncogenes showed the highest, suggesting distinct mutation patterns between loss-of-function and gain-of-function drivers. We further validated 16 candidates in lung cancer cell lines. Knockdown of several genes suppressed proliferation. Among them, GeneX overexpression promoted cell growth, and its mutation enhanced proliferation compared with wild-type. Patients with somatic GeneX mutations also showed poorer survival. Together, these results suggest that structure-based mutational clustering is useful for prioritizing functionally relevant cancer driver gene candidates.

title: Alternative splicing rewires therapeutic response to RAS/MAPK pathway inhibitors in lung cancer
ja: 選択的スプライシングが肺がんのRAS/MAPK経路阻害薬への治療応答を書き換える
en: Alternative splicing rewires therapeutic response to RAS/MAPK pathway inhibitors in lung cancer
abs: Acquired resistance to targeted therapy is a major cause of cancer relapse. Although alternative splicing has the potential to reconfigure oncogenic signaling, its involvement in resistance to RAS/MAPK pathway inhibitors remains unclear. We analyzed RNA-seq data from 473 CCLE cell lines with matched DepMap drug response data. JuncBASE analysis showed that splicing variations in RAS/MAPK-related genes were linked to drug response, independent of total gene expression. PCA and k-means clustering separated cells into two splicing-defined groups. Cluster 2 was more sensitive to osimertinib (EGFRi) and RMC-6236 (pan-RASi), whereas cluster 1 was less sensitive. KRAS, YAP1, and SCRIB exons showed distinct usage patterns between clusters. Differential expression analysis identified an RNA-binding and splicing regulator as a candidate driver of the phenotype. Long-read RNA-seq data from 8 CCLE cell lines further suggested that expression change in this splicing regulator was correlated with target isoform usage and drug sensitivity. We generated knockout models using EGFR-mutant (PC-9, HCC4006) and KRAS-mutant (H358) lung cancer cells. Loss of the splicing regulator altered key splicing events and promoted resistance to osimertinib or RMC-6236. Knockout cells showed enhanced survival during long-term drug exposure, with little effect in short-term assays, suggesting a drug-tolerant state. These findings indicate RNA splicing regulation enhances tolerance to RAS/MAPK inhibitors. RNA binding protein expression and splicing signatures may be therapeutic response biomarkers.

title: Multi-omic analysis of Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 1 with spatial transcriptomics
ja: 空間トランスクリプトミクスを用いた多発性内分泌腫瘍症1型のマルチオミクス解析
en: Multi-omic analysis of Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 1 with spatial transcriptomics
abs: Background: Since January 2014, we have conducted multi-omics analyses of cancer patients undergoing surgery at a single institution, enrolling and analyzing > 10,000 cases. In this cohort, we observed three cases of multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1) and performed multi-omics analysis using whole-genome sequencing (WGS), RNA sequencing, gene expression profiling (GEP), in situ spatial analysis, and immunohistochemistry. Methods and Materials: All experimental protocols were approved by the Institutional Review Board of Shizuoka Cancer Center (Authorization Number: 25-33). WGS and RNA sequencing were performed using the NovaSeq 6000 System, and GEP was conducted using a microarray platform. Xenium was used for spatial transcriptomic analysis. Immunohistochemical staining was performed by a pathologist. Results: All three patients were clinically diagnosed with MEN1 before genomic analysis. Pathogenic germline MEN1 mutations were identified using WGS, and loss of heterozygosity was confirmed in the tumors of the patients. Immunohistochemical staining for menin further supports the pathogenic significance of these alterations. In the most recently registered case, spatial transcriptomic analysis revealed differential MEN1 expression between tumor and normal tissues, which was not detected by conventional GEP. The tumor microenvironment is currently under investigation. Discussion: Further analyses and additional cases are needed; however, these findings may provide novel insights into the molecular pathogenesis of MEN1-associated neuroendocrine tumors.

title: Identification of URST4 as a promising candidate biomarker and therapeutictarget for breast cancer.
ja: 乳がんの有望なバイオマーカー・治療標的候補としてのURST4の同定
en: Identification of URST4 as a promising candidate biomarker and therapeutictarget for breast cancer.
abs: To improve diagnostic efficacy and therapeutic strategy in breast cancer, we selected URST4 (Up regulated in solid tumor 4) and investigated its biological role and potential as a candidate diagnostic and therapeutic target. Real-time qPCR, western blotting, and immunocytochemistry revealed that URST4 was overexpressed in breast cancer cell lines and clinical breast cancer tissues compared with normal breast epithelial cells and normal breast tissues. Immunohistochemistry using tissue microarrays revealed that URST4 was expressed in 72.3% (188 out of 260) of breast cancer tissues but was barely detectable in normal breast tissues. Higher expression of URST4 was significantly correlated with a poor prognosis in patients with breast cancer (P = 0.0105). Knock-down of URST4 expression using siRNAs significantly inhibited breast cancer cell growth through G2/M cell cycle arrest, mitotic program disruption as well as senescence formation, and also suppressed invasive ability of breast cancer cells. In contrast, overexpression of URST4 by plasmid transfection increased growth and invasion of cells. These findings suggest URST4 could be a potential biomarker and therapeutic target for breast cancer.

title: Deep learning reinterpretation of germline VUS in hereditary cancer syndromes
ja: 遺伝性腫瘍症候群における生殖細胞系列VUSの深層学習による再解釈
en: Deep learning reinterpretation of germline VUS in hereditary cancer syndromes
abs: The implementation of routine next-generation sequencing (NGS) in clinical genetics has led to a high prevalence (∼40%) of variants of uncertain significance (VUS). We evaluated a Fujitsu-developed deep learning model (FDLM) for reanalysis of germline VUS in genes related to DNA repair. These have been linked to hereditary cancer syndromes (HCS) such as Lynch Syndrome and Hereditary Breast- Ovarian Cancer. The model, trained on ClinVar (2023), was applied to historical HCS cases (2017–2025) from Complexo Hospitalario Universitario de Ourense (Spain) carrying germline VUS, totalling 61 variants. Updated expert re-classification per ClinGen-ACMG/AMP specifications (03/2026) identified 35 VUS, 25 benign/likely benign (B/LB), and 1 pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP). Among 25 expert B/LB variants, for 23 (92%) variants FDLM showed concordant predictions; 1 (4%) was reclassified P/LP and 1 (4%) inconclusive. The single expert-classified P/LP variant was concordantly identified by FDLM. Out of the 35 expert VUS, FDLM reclassified 14 (40%) as P/LP, 18 (51.4%) as B/LB, and 3 (8.6%) as inconclusive. Ongoing work integrates tumour mutational signature analysis to evaluate whether tumours carrying reclassified germline variants exhibit the expected genomic profiles, thereby validating FDLM classification. Concordance between FDLM predictions and tumour mutational patterns may provide orthogonal biological evidence supporting variant pathogenicity and algorithm predictive capability.

title: Identification of Disease-Associated Genes in Status Epilepticus Associated with Fever and Acute Encephalopathy
ja: 発熱・急性脳症に伴うてんかん重積の疾患関連遺伝子の同定
en: Identification of Disease-Associated Genes in Status Epilepticus Associated with Fever and Acute Encephalopathy
abs: Background: Reports of status epilepticus associated with fever (SEF) and acute encephalopathy (AE) are frequent in East Asia, particularly in Japan. Although a genetic predisposition has been suggested, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Methods: We analyzed mainly pediatric patients with SEF/AE referred for genetic testing at Kobe University from 61 collaborating institutions across Japan. Genetic analyses included either a targeted encephalopathy 331-gene panel or whole-exome sequencing (WES). Results: A total of 118 patients were enrolled, including 38 with SEF and 80 with AE. WES was performed in 75 cases. According to ACMG guidelines, pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants were identified in 18 patients, including 10 with SEF and 8 with AE; variants in SCN1A accounted for approximately half of these cases. Notably, in patients without identified pathogenic variants, rare variants were observed in genes previously implicated in epilepsy, mitochondrial disorders, or related conditions. Additionally, some de novo variants of uncertain significance were identified in immune-related genes. These variants are relatively more frequent in Japanese, suggesting a potential contribution to the higher incidence of SEF/AE in this region. Conclusion: This is the first large-scale comprehensive study investigating monogenic disease-associated variants in SEF/AE. The overall diagnostic yield among the analyzed cases was about 20%. A substantial number of candidate variants were identified, highlighting the need for further functional studies to clarify their pathogenic roles.

title: Functional and protein structural analyses of 4 GNAS-Gsα variants associated with gain-of-function phenotypes
ja: 機能獲得型表現型に関連する4つのGNAS-Gsαバリアントの機能・タンパク構造解析
en: Functional and protein structural analyses of 4 GNAS-Gsα variants associated with gain-of-function phenotypes
abs: Background and Objectives: GNAS-Gsα mediates signal transduction of multiple G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs). We investigated functional and structural properties of four germline GNAS-Gsα variants associated with ligand-independent gain-of-function (GOF) phenotypes, including nephrogenic syndrome of inappropriate antidiuresis (NSIAD), osteolytic bone lesions (OPLBD), and peripheral precocious puberty (PPP). Identified Variants and Clinical Features: (1) p.T55A on paternal allele identified in NSIAD and OPLBD and that on parent-of-unknown allele found in NSIAD, OPLBD, and borderline PPP; (2) p.I56F on maternal allele found in NSIAD, OPLBD, and borderline PPP; (3) p.N167K on maternal allele found in NSIAD; and (4) p.L198F on paternal and maternal-alleles identified in NSIAD and OPLBD. The three variants other than p.T55A were also associated with borderline pseudohypoparathyroidism when present on the maternal allele. Functional and Structural Analyses: Luciferase assays revealed ligand-independent GOF or its tendency for AVPR2 and PTH1R signaling, together with ligand-dependent loss-of-function (LOF) for PTH1R signaling. Structural analyses showed that the four variants destabilized both inactive and active conformations. Discussion: The results indicate that the four variants have constitutive GOF effects on specific GPCR pathways while preserving tissue-specific imprinting. GPCR selectivity may depend on interactions between GPCRs and the Gsα α5-helix, and ligand-dependent LOF may be masked by constitutive signaling.

title: Progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis type 7 with refractory rickets after improvement of coagulopathy
ja: 凝固異常改善後に難治性くる病を呈した進行性家族性肝内胆汁うっ滞症7型
en: Progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis type 7 with refractory rickets after improvement of coagulopathy
abs: Background: Progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis (PFIC) is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by genetic defects affecting bile secretion and transport. PFIC type 7 is caused by mutations inUSP53 and is known to be associated with cholestasis and occasionally hearing loss. Case: A 7-month-old girl presented with generalized purpura and was found to have vitamin K deficiency-associated coagulopathy and cholestatic liver dysfunction. She received treatment with fat-soluble vitamins and hepatoprotective drugs, and her symptoms improved. A targeted PFIC gene analysis was negative. During outpatient follow-up, hepatobiliary enzymes normalized. At 1 year and 5 months of age, intact-PTH levels increased, and vitamin D administration was started. However, hypocalcemia and rickets progressively worsened despite dose escalation. No pathogenetic variants were identified in VDR or CYP27B1 by further examination at 2years of age. However, comprehensive genetic analysis through IRUD identified a homozygous mutation in USP53, leading to a diagnosis of PFIC type 7. By 4 years of age, liver function including bile acid levels normalized and rickets findings gradually improved. No hearing impairment has been identified to date. Conclusion: The clinical symptoms of PFIC are diverse. Symptoms can be intermittent and can change over time. Currently available targeted PFIC gene analysis does not cover all types of PFIC. This case highlights the clinical importance of comprehensive genomic analysis in patients with unexplained cholestasis and fat-soluble vitamin deficiency.

title: Identification of loss of heterozygosity identified by paired tumor-germline WGS in a patient with ROHHAD syndrome
ja: ROHHAD症候群患者における腫瘍-生殖細胞系列ペアWGSで同定されたヘテロ接合性消失
en: Identification of loss of heterozygosity identified by paired tumor-germline WGS in a patient with ROHHAD syndrome
abs: Background ROHHAD syndrome is a rare pediatric disorder characterized by rapid-onset obesity, hypothalamic dysfunction, and autonomic dysregulation The association with neural crest tumors and the recent identification of ZSCAN1 autoantibodies suggest a possible tumor-associated autoimmune mechanism; however, the genomic background of associated tumors remains poorly understood. Objective To explore somatic genomic alterations in a neural crest tumor associated with ROHHAD syndrome using paired tumor-germline whole-genome sequencing. Methods Paired WGS was performed using tumor tissue and peripheral blood DNA obtained from a patient with ROHHAD syndrome and neural crest tumor. Somatic alterations including copy number abnormalities and loss of heterozygosity (LOH) were evaluated. Results Multiple chromosomal regions demonstrating LOH were identified in tumor tissue compared with germline DNA. Several affected regions included loci potentially relevant to tumor biology, genomic imprinting, and immune regulation. No clearly pathogenic germline coding variants explaining the phenotype were identified. These findings suggest possible tumor-associated genomic instability in ROHHAD syndrome. Additional epigenomic and transcriptomic analyses are currently ongoing to further investigate the biological significance of these alterations. Conclusion Comprehensive paired tumor-germline WGS identified multiple somatic LOH regions in a ROHHAD-associated neural crest tumor, suggesting possible genomic and epigenomic mechanisms underlying disease pathophysiology.

title: Comprehensive Genetic Analysis of Severe Early-Onset Obesity at a Single Institution in Japan
ja: 本邦単一施設における重症早期発症肥満の包括的遺伝学的解析
en: Comprehensive Genetic Analysis of Severe Early-Onset Obesity at a Single Institution in Japan
abs: Background: In recent years, molecular genetic analysis for pediatric severe obesity has rapidly advanced in Western countries, but Japanese data remain limited. Methods: We analyzed 35 patients with pediatric severe obesity [BMI at least 120% of the 95th percentile, obesity index at least 50% for ages 6-17 years, or at least 30% for children under 6 years]. Targeted next-generation sequencing (NGS) panel analysis for obesity-related genes and copy number variation (CNV) analysis using MLPA were performed. Results: One patient carried a previously reported pathogenic heterozygous MC4R variant, c.164G-to-A (p.G55D). In addition, microdeletions were identified in 3 patients (proximal 16p11.2 deletion, 15q13.2 deletion), and a 15q13.2 microduplication was detected in 1 patient. Overall, genetic abnormalities were identified in 5 patients (14.3%). Deletions involving 16p11.2 and 15q13 are CNVs that have attracted international attention in recent years because of their association with neurodevelopmental and obesity-related phenotypes, and our findings suggest that these CNVs may also contribute to Japanese pediatric obesity. Conclusion: Pediatric severe obesity has a highly heterogeneous genetic background involving both monogenic abnormalities and CNVs. Comprehensive genetic evaluation including CNV analysis in addition to NGS may help clarify disease mechanism and support future precision medicine approaches.

title: Early Genomic Diagnosis of Distal Deletion 14q Syndrome Triggered by Research-Based Trio Exome Sequencing
ja: 研究ベースのトリオエクソーム解析を契機とした14q遠位欠失症候群の早期ゲノム診断
en: Early Genomic Diagnosis of Distal Deletion 14q Syndrome Triggered by Research-Based Trio Exome Sequencing
abs: Distal Deletion 14q Syndrome is a rare chromosomal disorder characterized by developmental delay, growth restriction, and craniofacial dysmorphism. Most cases are diagnosed after developmental delay becomes apparent, and neonatal diagnosis remains uncommon because early phenotypic findings are often subtle. We report a male infant born at 37+6 weeks of gestation with fetal growth restriction, hypotonia, feeding difficulties, mild dysmorphic features, and cardiopulmonary instability requiring NICU admission. Echocardiography demonstrated mild pulmonary artery branch narrowing and distal aortic arch tapering without significant hemodynamic obstruction. Bilateral hearing loss was confirmed by auditory brainstem response testing. These subtle multisystem neonatal findings raised suspicion of an underlying genetic condition, and research-based trio exome sequencing was performed and suggested a terminal deletion of chromosome 14q. Chromosomal microarray subsequently confirmed a 6.5Mb deletion at 14q32.2-q32.33 (GRCh37: Chr14:100,801,148-107,287,505). The deletion was absent in both parents, consistent with a de novo event. Early genetic diagnosis provided important information regarding prognosis and recurrence risk, enabling timely genetic counseling and multidisciplinary planning, including growth and neurodevelopmental follow-up, audiological intervention, and cardiovascular assessment.

title: A Case with repeated Meckel Gruber Syndrome, Preimplantation Genetic Test Performed, Resulting in a normal Pregnancy
ja: Meckel-Gruber症候群反復例に着床前遺伝学的検査を行い正常妊娠に至った1例
en: A Case with repeated Meckel Gruber Syndrome, Preimplantation Genetic Test Performed, Resulting in a normal Pregnancy
abs: Introduction We report a case in which a fetus was diagnosed with Meckel Gruber syndrome (MKS) on consecutive pregnancies. Following exome sequencing,preimplantation genetic testing for monogenic disorders (PGT M) was performed,resulting in a non affected fetus pregnancy. Case Report At 12 weeks of gestation, a mass was noted in the head of fetus. The patient was referred to Hospital A for prenatal diagnosis (PD). The karyotype was normal. An encephalocele and renal enlargement were detected by ultrasonography leading to a diagnosis of MKS. Following genetic counseling, the patient opted for termination of pregnancy. Subsequently, a pregnancy was achieved and head mass was detected at 11 weeks of gestation. The patient decided to terminate the pregnancy. We explained that on the results of genetic testing (GT) of the miscarried fetus, PD or PGT M might be possible. Initially, GT was not requested. However, since a subsequent pregnancy was also diagnosed with MKS, the patient requested GT. Exome sequencing was performed, and heterozygous variants in TMEM231 gene exon 1 and 3 were detected in both the affected specimen and parental blood. PGT M were performed after approval by the Japan Society of Obstetrics and Gynecology. A pregnancy was established following the second transfer of a non-affected embryo. The patient is currently 25 weeks pregnant, and the pregnancy is progressing with no apparent fetal morphological abnormalities. Discussion The results of GT allowed us to support the clients decision to proceed with another pregnancy through PGT M.

title: Pregnancy-Related Risk Perception and Preconception Care in Women with Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease
ja: 常染色体顕性多発性嚢胞腎の女性における妊娠関連リスク認識とプレコンセプションケア
en: Pregnancy-Related Risk Perception and Preconception Care in Women with Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease
abs: Background: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) is a hereditary renal disorder associated with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and renal deterioration. Although ADPKD carries a 50% transmission risk to offspring, reports on preconception support are limited. Objective: To investigate pregnancy-related risk perception and preconception care practices among women with ADPKD. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed pregnancies complicated by ADPKD and pregnancies in women with a family history of ADPKD managed at our institution between 2016 and 2026. Renal deterioration, awareness of genetic inheritance, and implementation of genetic counseling and preconception care were evaluated. Results: Nine pregnancies complicated by ADPKD and two pregnancies with a family history of ADPKD were included. Most women recognized ADPKD as hereditary; however, some had limited understanding of the genetic nature of the disease, pregnancy-related renal deterioration, and perinatal risks. No patients had received preconception care. In two women with a family history of ADPKD, concerns regarding transmission to offspring emerged after pregnancy, leading to nephrology referral. Among nine ADPKD pregnancies, three developed hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and two showed renal deterioration after pregnancy. Discussion: Women with ADPKD may have insufficient understanding of pregnancy-related risks and long-term renal prognosis despite recognizing the disease as hereditary. These findings highlight the importance of preconception care and genetic counseling before pregnancy.

title: Cases in which chromosomal abnormalities undetected by PGT-A were identified during pregnancy
ja: PGT-Aで検出されなかった染色体異常が妊娠中に判明した症例
en: Cases in which chromosomal abnormalities undetected by PGT-A were identified during pregnancy
abs: When embryos classified as euploid with preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A) are transferred, many people assume that fetal chromosomal abnormalities are unlikely, although a residual risk remains. We encountered three pregnancies in which chromosomal abnormalities not predicted by PGT-A were identified after conception. In the first case, detailed fetal ultrasonography showed no abnormalities; however, SNP microarray analysis of amniotic cells revealed a pathogenic 1.4 Mb duplication in the 17q12 region, below the resolution detectable by PGT-A. In the second case, an XX embryo was selected at a non-authorized facility. During pregnancy, male external genitalia were observed, and NIPT ordered from a non-accredited clinic showed a positive result for XXY, suggesting mosaic XXY constitution. In the third case, amniocentesis revealed 20% mosaic trisomy 12. Retrospective review of the original PGT-A data demonstrated evidence of trisomy 12 below the reporting threshold for mosaicism, resulting in classification as euploid. Although PGT-A is highly accurate, it cannot detect small chromosomal deletions or duplications, as well as uniparental disomy. Furthermore, in embryos with chromosomal mosaicism, the chromosomal status of biopsied cells for PGT-A may not correspond to that of the fetus. At our clinic, SNP microarray analysis with amniocentesis is offered as an option after transfer of a euploid embryo, although uptake is approximately one-third. For patients, appropriate and balanced information provision regarding the limitations of PGT- A is important.

title: Clinical Outcomes of Fetuses with Increased Nuchal Translucency and Negative NIPT or Normal Karyotype
ja: NT肥厚かつNIPT陰性または核型正常の胎児の臨床転帰
en: Clinical Outcomes of Fetuses with Increased Nuchal Translucency and Negative NIPT or Normal Karyotype
abs: [Objective] Increased fetal nuchal translucency (NT) in early pregnancy is associated with chromosomal and cardiac abnormalities, serving as a key prenatal marker. This study aimed to investigate the outcomes of cases with increased NT and negative non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT) or normal amniocentesis karyotypes to improve future clinical management. [Methods] This retrospective study included cases with increased NT (defined as NT >= 3.5 mm) identified at our hospital or affiliated clinics between November 2016 and December 2025, with negative NIPT or normal karyotype. [Results] Out of 67 cases meeting the criteria, structural anomalies were detected in 25 (37.3%). Out of these, 10 cases presented with isolated congenital heart defects, and another 10 cases presented with multiple structural anomalies including heart defects. Other identified structural abnormalities included diaphragmatic hernia (n=1), left radial defect/aplasia (n=1), biliary atresia (n=1), a complex case presenting with thoracic hypoplasia, horseshoe kidney, bilateral lower leg shortening, and right fibular absence (n=1), and sacrococcygeal teratoma (n=1). [Conclusions] Even in cases with negative NIPT or a normal karyotype, structural anomalies occurred in approximately one-third of cases with NT >= 3.5 mm, with cardiac defects representing 80% of these anomalies. Detailed mid-trimester ultrasound evaluation targeting a wide range of anomalies is essential, and appropriate counseling should be provided to patients regarding these risks.

title: Maternal plasma level of miR-518b at 36 weeks gestation may predict the labor induction outcome in late-term pregnancy
ja: 妊娠36週の母体血漿miR-518b値は過期妊娠の分娩誘発転帰を予測しうる
en: Maternal plasma level of miR-518b at 36 weeks gestation may predict the labor induction outcome in late-term pregnancy
abs: Objective: To identify a predictive marker for the outcome of labor induction in late-term pregnancy. Methods: Maternal plasma miRNAs within the chromosome 19 miRNA cluster (miR-515-3p, miR-517a, miR-517c, miR-518b) and chromosome 14 miRNA cluster (miR-323-3p) were evaluated as candidate markers. Plasma samples at 30 and 36 weeks of gestation were collected from women who subsequently delivered at term following spontaneous labor (n = 21) and those who underwent labor induction in late-term pregnancy (n = 20). Maternal plasma cell-free microRNA levels were quantified using RT-qPCR. The late-term pregnancy group were further classified into successful (n = 13) and failed (n = 5) groups of labor induction. Results: Plasma cell-free miR-517a and cell-free miR-518b levels at 36 weeks of gestation were significantly higher in the failed labor induction group than in the successful labor induction group (miR-517a: median, 368.6 [9.9-1223.0] vs 30.0 [2.7-441.0], P = 0.030; miR-518b, 37.9 [5.5-58.2] vs 5.6 [1.5-20.3], P = 0.014). A receiver operating characteristic analysis comparing term delivery and successful labor induction (n = 34) with failed labor induction (n = 5) showed that plasma cell-free miR-518b levels at 36 weeks of gestation discriminated induction failure (area under the curve: 0.871, 95% confidence interval: 0.70-1.00). The optimal cutoff value was 23.3, with a sensitivity of 80% and a specificity of 94%. Conclusion: Maternal plasma miR-518b at 36 weeks were associated with failed labor induction and showed a better discriminatory performance than the Bishop score.

title: Three consecutive pregnancies in a woman with hypochondroplasia: prenatal management and offspring outcomes
ja: 軟骨低形成症女性の3回連続妊娠：出生前管理と児の転帰
en: Three consecutive pregnancies in a woman with hypochondroplasia: prenatal management and offspring outcomes
abs: A woman with clinically diagnosed hypochondroplasia based on characteristic radiographic findings and marked short stature (120 cm) experienced three consecutive pregnancies between 2019 and 2025. Genetic testing in the mother revealed no identifiable pathogenic variant. During the first pregnancy, threatened preterm labor developed at 24 weeks of gestation, and emergency cesarean delivery was required at 32 weeks and 1 day because of uncontrollable uterine contractions. The first daughter subsequently showed clinical findings consistent with hypochondroplasia. During the second pregnancy, elective cesarean delivery was performed at 33 weeks and 0 days considering the previous obstetric course. The second daughter also exhibited clinical features compatible with hypochondroplasia. During the third pregnancy, recurrent preterm labor developed and emergency cesarean delivery was required at 32 weeks and 5 days. In contrast, the male infant showed normal growth and development without evidence of skeletal dysplasia during follow-up. Thus, among three offspring, two inherited the maternal phenotype while one was unaffected. This family demonstrated segregation consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance and highlights the importance of prenatal surveillance, delivery planning, and genetic counseling for women with skeletal dysplasia.

title: Healthcare utilization after return of genomic results among BRCA1/2 pathogenic variant carriers in general population
ja: 一般集団のBRCA1/2病的バリアント保持者へのゲノム結果返却後の医療利用
en: Healthcare utilization after return of genomic results among BRCA1/2 pathogenic variant carriers in general population
abs: Background: The Tohoku Medical Megabank Organization (ToMMo) has pioneered the return of genomic results (ROGR) to BRCA1/2 pathogenic variant (PV) carriers in the general population, and their subsequent medical care is essential for evaluating the significance of ROGR. Objective: To assess healthcare utilization after ROGR and identify related challenges. Methods: This retrospective study analyzed participants in the ROGR study within the ToMMo cohort. Individuals who received BRCA1/2 PV results between Dec 2020 and Oct 2025 and visited Tohoku University Hospital (TUH) at least once were included. Results: Of 113 individuals (23 men and 90 women), 89 (17 men and 72 women) visited TUH. Prior cancers included breast (n=19), ovarian (n=3), prostate (n=1), and pancreatic (n=1). Four had undergone risk-reducing mastectomy (RRM) before ROGR; after ROGR, one developed breast cancer and two underwent RRM. Eight underwent bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy before ROGR for risk reduction or gynecologic disease, while 14 underwent risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy (RRSO) after ROGR; one had ovarian cancer. Among women, continued surveillance at TUH or other institutions was observed in 52/68 in breast surgery and 55/71 in gynecology, indicating discontinuation in approximately 20%. Conclusion: The ROGR study showed relatively high follow-up adherence. Seamless collaboration between research institutions and hospitals may facilitate access to care for BRCA1/2 PV carriers, while long-term cancer prevention requires prevention strategies that are feasible and sustainable for each individual.

title: Factors Associated with Reducing Image Sensitivity for BRCA-Related Breast Cancer
ja: BRCA関連乳がんにおける画像感度低下に関連する因子
en: Factors Associated with Reducing Image Sensitivity for BRCA-Related Breast Cancer
abs: Background: MRI is recommended for surveillance of BRCA-positive breast cancer, whereas mammography (MG) and ultrasound (US) are considered less accurate. We evaluated the sensitivity of each modality and related factors in BRCA-positive cases treated at our institution and explored a feasible surveillance strategy. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 36 women (47 breasts) with BRCA-positive breast cancer. Clinical and pathological data and imaging findings (MG, US, MRI) were reviewed. Sensitivity was defined as category >3, and category sensitivity as >4. Results: ER positivity was 53.8%, median tumor size was 19 mm, lymph node metastasis was present in 29.8%, and 48.9% were stage >2. Lesions were mainly located in the central to posterior regions (56.7%). Sensitivity (category sensitivity) was 76.1% (50%) for MG, 89.4% (76.6%) for US, and 95.5% (93.2%) for MRI. MG showed low sensitivity regardless of tumor size, especially in dense breasts and posterior lesions. US frequently missed tumors <10 mm and centrally or deeply located tumors, and calcifications. Combined MG and US achieved 100% sensitivity, indicating complementary value, although category sensitivity remained around 70% for tumors <20 mm. Adding MG and US to MRI provided minimal improvement. Conclusion: BRCA-positive breast cancers are often located posteriorly, requiring careful assessment of dense breast tissue on MG and US. A practical surveillance strategy may include annual MRI, with combined MG and US at 6 months, comparison with prior images, and additional MRI when new findings are detected.

title: Germline secondary findings in cancer whole-genome sequencing: experience and disclosure in 198 patients
ja: がん全ゲノム解析における生殖細胞系列二次的所見：198例の経験と開示
en: Germline secondary findings in cancer whole-genome sequencing: experience and disclosure in 198 patients
abs: Background: Cancer whole-genome sequencing (WGS) is being implemented in Japan under the national Whole Genome Analysis Project, but real-world data on interpretation and disclosure of germline secondary findings (SFs) remain limited. Methods: Tumor-normal WGS from 198 patients with intractable or rare cancers (May- Oct 2025) was processed with DeepVariant and ANNOVAR, filtered by ToMMo allele frequency <1%. A multidisciplinary panel reviewed SFs against ACMG SF v3.2 and the Kosugi list, cross-checked with a commercial pipeline, and reassessed via ClinVar, IGV, and phenotype review. Results: Disclosed hereditary cancer variants included BRCA1/2, RAD51D, BARD1, ATM, SDHA, and SDHB. Other ACMG SF disclosures included PKP2 frameshifts in two asymptomatic ARVC cases, a PAX6 splice variant with congruent ocular phenotype, a FLNC splice variant in cardiomyopathy reviewed with cardiology, and a COL3A1 nonsense in a patient with intraoperative bleeding. Non-disclosed variants included TTN truncations in cardiac-only isoforms, EPCAM nonsense outside Lynch regions, and low-penetrance FLG/KCNQ4. A recurrent TSC2 splice variant was deemed false-positive by IGV. Commercial cross-checking identified five P/LP-annotated variants not flagged by the in-house annotation due to ClinVar-version lag. Conclusion: A systematic expert-panel workflow integrating curated gene lists, manual inspection, and multi-pipeline cross-validation enabled meaningful SF disclosure while avoiding false positives. Database maintenance and specialist consultation for incompletely penetrant genes are essential.

title: Germline Findings Following Increased Use of Tumor-Normal Paired Comprehensive Genomic Profiling
ja: 腫瘍-正常ペアの包括的がんゲノムプロファイリング拡大に伴う生殖細胞系列所見
en: Germline Findings Following Increased Use of Tumor-Normal Paired Comprehensive Genomic Profiling
abs: Background: Tumor-normal paired (T-N) comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) directly assesses germline pathogenic variants (GPVs), whereas tumor-only (T-only) CGP requires confirmatory testing when presumed germline pathogenic variants (PGPVs) are detected. GenMineTOP, a DNA/RNA-based T-N CGP, became available at our institution in April 2024. Whether increased use of T- N CGP is associated with higher GPV detection in clinical practice remains unclear. Methods: We analyzed consecutive tissue-based CGP reimbursed under Japan's national health insurance system from our prospective clinical database. We evaluated the proportion of T-only and T-N CGP, GPVs confirmed by germline testing after T-only CGP, and GPVs identified by T-N CGP in Period 1 (June 2019-March 2024) and in Period 2 (April 2024-March 2026). Overall GPV detection rates were compared using Fisher's exact test. Results: Among 1,133 tissue-based CGP, T-N CGP accounted for 49/705 (7.0%) and 258/428 (60.3%) in Periods 1 and 2, respectively. In Period 1, PGPVs were detected in 46/656 T-only CGP (7.0%), and GPVs were confirmed in 11 cases (1.7%). One GPV was identified among 49 T-N CGP (2.0%). In Period 2, PGPVs were detected in 27/170 T-only CGP (15.9%), and GPVs were confirmed in four cases (2.4%). Fifteen GPVs were identified among 258 T-N CGP (5.8%). Overall GPV detection was 12/705 (1.7%) in Period 1 and 19/428 (4.4%) in Period 2 (p=0.0081). Conclusions: Increased use of T-N CGP was associated with higher overall GPV detection and may provide more opportunities to detect germline findings in clinical practice.

title: Performance of Insurance-Coverage Criteria for Detecting BRCA Pathogenic Variants in Breast Cancer
ja: 乳がんにおけるBRCA病的バリアント検出のための保険適用基準の性能
en: Performance of Insurance-Coverage Criteria for Detecting BRCA Pathogenic Variants in Breast Cancer
abs: Background: BRACAnalysis is used to diagnose HBOC and guide genetic counseling and risk-reducing care. We evaluated which insurance-coverage criteria best detect BRCA pathogenic variants. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 811 breast cancer patients who underwent BRACAnalysis under Japanese insurance coverage between July 2022 and November 2025, excluding tests performed for PARP inhibitor eligibility. Criteria assessed were age 45 years or younger, triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) at age 60 years or younger, multiple primary breast cancers, family history, ovarian/ fallopian tube/peritoneal cancer, male breast cancer, and known familial BRCA variants. Sensitivity, positive predictive value (PPV), and Youden index were calculated. Results: BRCA pathogenic variants were detected in 57 patients (7.0%). Family history showed the highest sensitivity (71%). TNBC at age 60 years or younger showed the highest PPV (20%) and Youden index (0.19). Age 45 years or younger and multiple primary breast cancers showed intermediate performance (PPV 8% and 10%; Youden index 0.12 and 0.13, respectively). Ovarian/fallopian tube/peritoneal cancer and male breast cancer had high PPVs (29% and 25%, respectively), although few patients met these criteria. Conclusions: Family history showed the highest sensitivity, whereas TNBC at age 60 years or younger showed the highest PPV and Youden index. Criterion utility should be assessed using both diagnostic performance and the number of eligible patients.

title: Impact of a Cancer Genetics Program at a Pediatric Tertiary Care Center
ja: 小児三次医療センターにおけるがん遺伝学プログラムの効果
en: Impact of a Cancer Genetics Program at a Pediatric Tertiary Care Center
abs: Approximately 15% of pediatric patients with cancer are genetically predisposed to cancer. However, clinical management and surveillance strategies are still based on limited evidence. To provide real-world data to guide clinical management and future directions, we conducted a retrospective review of cases seen in our Cancer Genetics Program from 2001 to 2024. Over 2,000 children were referred, of whom 620 patients had a genetically confirmed diagnosis of cancer predisposition (67 different diagnoses). The most common indications for germline testing were a personal history of cancer (42%), cascade testing (40%), and non-tumor manifestations associated with known cancer predisposition syndromes (12%). In 6% of cases, diagnoses were made through genetic testing performed for non-cancer indications. Across major cancer predisposition syndromes, surveillance facilitated early tumor detection. In Li-Fraumeni syndrome, the most common diagnosis in this cohort, no patients died of 10 surveillance-detected tumors, while 3 deaths occurred among 8 symptomatically diagnosed tumors during the surveillance interval, suggesting the need for more sensitive methods. Surveillance-detected tumors were associated with less intensive therapy compared to symptomatically detected tumors, highlighting an important impact on morbidity in this young population. Additionally, analysis of our long-term follow-up data led to modifications of surveillance protocols. These findings highlight the significant impact of a cancer genetics program on improving clinical management of at-risk patients.

title: De novo SVA type D insertion in a deep intronic region of NIPBL causing Cornelia de Lange syndrome
ja: NIPBL深部イントロンのde novo SVA type D挿入によるCornelia de Lange症候群
en: De novo SVA type D insertion in a deep intronic region of NIPBL causing Cornelia de Lange syndrome
abs: Introduction: Cornelia de Lange syndrome (CdLS) is a developmental disorder primarily caused by mutations in NIPBL. Despite advancements in sequencing technology, a significant proportion of clinically diagnosed CdLS cases remain genetically undiagnosed after standard whole-exome sequencing (WES), likely due to variants in non-coding regions. We aimed to identify the underlying genetic cause in a patient presenting with classic CdLS features who remained undiagnosed after standard WES analysis. Methods and Results: To reveal unexpected pathogenic variants in our WES-negative patient with typical CdLS, we performed long-read whole-genome sequencing (LRS) using Oxford Nanopore Technologies. Manual inspection of the genomic data revealed a ~2.9 kb insertion within a deep intronic region of NIPBL (intron 44). The insertion was characterized as a de novo SINE-VNTR-Alu (SVA) type D element. This deep intronic variant was not detectable by standard WES due to its location and the nature of the repetitive sequence. Conclusion: Our findings demonstrate that de novo SVA type D insertions in deep intronic regions of NIPBL can cause CdLS. Notably, this represents one of the very few reported instances of a Mendelian disorder caused by an active SVA_D retrotransposition. This study not only highlights the clinical utility of LRS in resolving WES-negative rare genetic disorders, but also provides crucial evidence that evolutionarily older SVA_D elements retain pathogenic mobilization capacity in the human genome.

title: Targeted long-read sequencing reveals allele-specific methylation profiles at the GNAS locus in pseudohypoparathyroidism
ja: ターゲットロングリードシーケンスが明らかにする偽性副甲状腺機能低下症のGNAS座位アレル特異的メチル化
en: Targeted long-read sequencing reveals allele-specific methylation profiles at the GNAS locus in pseudohypoparathyroidism
abs: Background: Pseudohypoparathyroidism (PHP) features PTH resistance due to reduced Gs α expression. Maternal GNAS pathogenic variants cause PHP1A, while methylation defects in GNAS differentially methylated regions (DMRs) lead to PHP1B. Although STX16 enhances NESP transcription, and NESP55 transcription is required to establish maternal imprints for AS2-DMR and A/B-DMR, the regulatory mechanisms of methylation imprint for GNAS-DMR remain unclear. Methods and Results: Using targeted long-read sequencing (T-LRS), we evaluated allele-specific methylation and structural variants in six patients. Patient 1 (PHP1A), with a deletion from 3' A/B-DMR to GNAS exon 1, showed normal methylation in the intact A/B-DMR, narrowing its critical maternal imprinted region. Among five PHP1B patients, Patient 2 with an STX16 deletion exhibited AS2-DMR hypomethylation, helping define precise AS2- DMR boundaries. Patient 3, carrying a maternal duplication that increased the STX16 - AS2-DMR distance, also showed AS2-DMR hypomethylation, proving that increased distance from STX16 drives hypomethylation. Patient 4, with a maternal retrotransposon insertion, exhibited marked A/B-DMR hypomethylation alongside mild AS1- and XL-DMR hypomethylation on the maternal allele, which was undetected by conventional methods. Patients 5 and 6, presenting with atypical GNAS-DMR methylation patterns, had mosaic abnormalities across all DMRs, indicating early embryonic epigenetic errors. Conclusion: T-LRS is a powerful tool for clarifying the complex genomic and epigenetic regulation underlying GNAS-DMR methylation.

title: Complete Paternal Isodisomy of Chromosome 10 Harboring a Novel ERLIN1 Variant Causing Spastic Paraplegia Type 62
ja: 新規ERLIN1バリアントを含む10番染色体完全父性イソダイソミーによる痙性対麻痺62型
en: Complete Paternal Isodisomy of Chromosome 10 Harboring a Novel ERLIN1 Variant Causing Spastic Paraplegia Type 62
abs: Introduction Spastic paraplegia type 62 (SPG62; MIM:615681) is a complex form of hereditary spastic paraplegia caused by biallelic deleterious variants in the ERLIN1 gene. We report a case of SPG62 resulting from complete paternal uniparental isodisomy (UPiD) of chromosome 10 with a novel variant in the ERLIN1 gene. Case Report The patient was born at 39 weeks of gestation, weighing 3,412 g, by spontaneous vaginal delivery without neonatal asphyxia. At 4 years and 5 months of age, the patient developed toe-walking and was referred to our hospital for further evaluation. At the initial examination, restricted ankle dorsiflexion was observed. The patellar and Achilles tendon reflexes were hyperactive, the Babinski sign was positive, and spasticity was evident. Routine blood tests and brain and spinal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed no abnormalities. Given the suspicion of a hereditary neurodegenerative disorder, whole-exome sequencing was performed as part of Rare and Undiagnosed Diseases (IRUD). Genetic analysis identified a homozygous deletion encompassing exon 4 of the ERLIN1 gene, derived from complete paternal uniparental isodisomy. This deletion was determined to be the pathogenic variant responsible for SPG62. Discussion Although etiology due to uniparental isodisomy - as seen in this case -is extremely rare, parental segregation analysis remains essential during genetic counseling for homozygous variants involving an autosomal recessive inheritance pattern.

title: A neonatal case of CHARGE syndrome with a synonymous CHD7 variant shown to be pathogenic by RNA analysis
ja: RNA解析で病的と示された同義CHD7バリアントを持つCHARGE症候群の新生児例
en: A neonatal case of CHARGE syndrome with a synonymous CHD7 variant shown to be pathogenic by RNA analysis
abs: Background: CHARGE syndrome is an autosomal dominant disorder mainly caused by heterozygous pathogenic variants in CHD7 and shows variable phenotypes. We report a neonate in whom a synonymous CHD7 variant was considered causative through aberrant splicing. Case: A male infant had an atrioventricular septal defect (AVSD) at 34 weeks of gestation and was delivered vaginally at 41+0 weeks, weighing 3242 g. Apgar scores were 4 and 5 at 1 and 5 minutes, and he required intubation after birth. He had a coloboma, right facial nerve palsy, micrognathia, retrognathia, cleft right earlobe, and mild scrotal anomaly. Cardiac findings included unbalanced AVSD, right atrioventricular valve atresia, moderate left atrioventricular valve regurgitation, and Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome. These findings led to a clinical diagnosis of CHARGE syndrome. His parents and sister had no anomalies or developmental delay. Genetic testing identifiedCHD7 NM_017780.4:c.5841A>G p.(Glu1947=), absent in both parents. SpliceAI predicted donor gain. RT-PCR using leukocyte RNA detected an abnormal band only in the proband. Sequencing showed an aberrant transcript with a 53-bp deletion, predicted to cause a frameshift. Discussion: The phenotype was compatible with a CHD7-related disorder. Although synonymous variants do not alter the encoded amino acid, they may be pathogenic when they cause aberrant splicing and loss of function. Conclusion: Synonymous CHD7 variants should not be dismissed solely because no amino acid substitution is predicted. Prediction tools, parental testing, and RNA analysis are important.

title: Clinical Comparison of Disorders Caused by Abnormalities of Histone H3 Lysine Methyltransferases
ja: ヒストンH3リジンメチル基転移酵素異常による疾患群の臨床比較
en: Clinical Comparison of Disorders Caused by Abnormalities of Histone H3 Lysine Methyltransferases
abs: Kabuki syndrome is a relatively common congenital anomaly syndrome characterized by distinctive facial features, neurodevelopmental disorders, short stature, and other clinical manifestations. Pathogenic variants in KMT2D (formerly MLL2) are recognized as the major cause of this condition. The KMT2D protein functions as a histone methyltransferase that catalyzes the methylation of lysine 4 on the tail of histone H3 (H3K4), thereby promoting gene expression through alterations in chromatin structure. In recent years, several disorders caused by pathogenic variants in other enzymes that similarly catalyze H3K4 methylation have been identified. We encountered and genetically diagnosed patients with Kleefstra syndrome 2, caused by variants in KMT2C, and ODLURO syndrome, caused by variants in KMT2E. In addition, we evaluated a patient with Kleefstra syndrome 1, which results from pathogenic variants in EHMT1, a gene encoding an enzyme that catalyzes methylation of another lysine residue on the histone H3 tail, H3K9. We discuss the shared neurodevelopmental phenotypes observed among these patients, as well as the characteristic facial features associated with each disorder. Furthermore, the diagnostic pathways that ultimately led to the identification of these conditions were particularly informative, and we present these clinical courses as part of our analysis.

title: A case of SUFU haploinsufficiency presenting with mild Joubert syndrome spectrum and intellectual developmental disorder
ja: 軽症Joubert症候群スペクトラムと知的発達症を呈したSUFUハプロ不全の1例
en: A case of SUFU haploinsufficiency presenting with mild Joubert syndrome spectrum and intellectual developmental disorder
abs: Joubert syndrome (JS) is a genetically heterogeneous ciliopathy characterized by hypotonia, developmental delay, abnormal ocular movements, and the molar tooth sign (MTS). Recently, heterozygous truncating variants in SUFU have been recognized as a cause of a mild neurodevelopmental phenotype within the JS spectrum with reduced penetrance. Our patient was a 3-year-old boy referred because of delayed motor and language development. He was born at 38 weeks of gestation after an uneventful pregnancy and delivery. He achieved independent walking at 23 months and had no meaningful words at 3 years of age. Neurological examination revealed congenital ocular motor apraxia, hypotonia, and macrocephaly without characteristic dysmorphic features. Brain MRI demonstrated an incomplete MTS. No retinal, renal, or hepatic involvement was identified. Comprehensive genetic testing revealed a heterozygous frameshift variant in SUFU (p.Gln217Profs*21). Unlike most forms of JS, which are inherited in an autosomal recessive manner,previously reported SUFU-related disorders have shown autosomal dominant inheritance with reduced penetrance. Consistent with these reports, our patient carried a heterozygous SUFU variant inherited from an unaffected parent. He showed no neonatal respiratory abnormality or multiorgan involvement. As previously reported, our case suggests that SUFU haploinsufficiency represents a relatively mild neurological subtype within the JS spectrum. Accurate phenotypic understanding is essential for genetic counseling and developmental support.

title: Clinical Outcomes of BRCA1/2 Testing and Olaparib Treatment in Patients with mCRPC at Gunma Univesrsity Hospital
ja: 群馬大学病院におけるmCRPC患者のBRCA1/2検査とオラパリブ治療の臨床転帰
en: Clinical Outcomes of BRCA1/2 Testing and Olaparib Treatment in Patients with mCRPC at Gunma Univesrsity Hospital
abs: Background: BRCA1/2 gene alterations are identified in approximately 10% of patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). We analyzed the results of BRACAnalysis testing and the clinical outcomes of olaparib (Ola) treatment at our institution. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed patients with mCRPC who underwent BRACAnalysis testing at our institution between April 2021 and December 2025, including those subsequently treated with olaparib. The prevalence of BRCA1/2 alterations detected by BRACAnalysis, additional alterations identified by comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP), and the efficacy of olaparib treatment were evaluated. Results: A total of 92 patients were included, with a median age of 74 years. Metastatic sites included lymph node metastases in 79.3%, bone metastases in 82.6%, lung metastases in 5.4%, and liver metastases in 5.4% patients. BRACAnalysis identified BRCA1/2 alterations in 7 patients (7.6%), including BRCA2 alterations in 6 patients and a BRCA1 alteration in 1 patient. Among the 85 patients who were negative by BRACAnalysis, FoundationOne CDx (F1CDx) testing subsequently detected BRCA2 alterations in 2 additional patients, resulting in an overall BRCA1/2 positivity rate of 9.8% (9/92). Olaparib was administered to 8 of the 9 patients with BRCA1/2 alterations, and the median progression-free survival was 12 months (range, 0.5-50 months). Conclusions: Our retrospective analysis demonstrated that the prevalence of BRCA1/2 alterations in patients with mCRPC at our institution was generally consistent with previous reports.

title: Molecular and Clinical Analyses of Patients with Anterior-Segment Dysgenesis/Aniridia and Microphthalmia/Anophthalmia
