ja: 前眼部形成異常/無虹彩症および小眼球症/無眼球症患者の分子・臨床解析
en: Molecular and Clinical Analyses of Patients with Anterior-Segment Dysgenesis/Aniridia and Microphthalmia/Anophthalmia
abs: Objective: To clarify the molecular and clinical characteristics of anterior-segment dysgenesis (ASD)/aniridia and microphthalmia/ anophthalmia caused by monogenic variants. Methods: A total of 111 patients and their family members were recruited through a multicenter collaborative study in Japan. Next-generation sequencing using custom-designed panels for 11 genes associated with ASD/aniridia and 12 genes associated with microphthalmia/anophthalmia. We analyzed the clinical information of patients with pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants. Results: We achieved genetic diagnosis rates of 50.0% for ASD/aniridia and 37.5% for microphthalmia/anophthalmia. De novo variants in the PAX6, PITX2, or GJA8 genes, and parentally derived variants in the FOXC1 and CYP1B1 genes were the major causes of ASD/aniridia. Microphthalmia/anophthalmia-associated variants in the ABCB6, BMP4, and OTX2 genes were predominantly inherited from parents with no or different ocular phenotypes. We observed phenotypic diversity and variable ocular and systemic complications in variant-positive patients. Conclusions: Our targeted panel approach effectively clarified the mutation spectrum and phenotypic characteristics of ASD/aniridia and microphthalmia/ anophthalmia due to monogenic variants. Our genetic study confirmed that various phenotypes classified as ASD, such as Peters anomaly and Axenfeld anomaly, constitute a group of disorders on the same spectrum, may overlap with aniridia, and exhibit genetic heterogeneity.

title: Four Adult Cases of Hyper IgE Syndrome diagnosed in Dermatology Outpatient Clinic
ja: 皮膚科外来で診断された成人高IgE症候群の4例
en: Four Adult Cases of Hyper IgE Syndrome diagnosed in Dermatology Outpatient Clinic
abs: Case 1: A 38-y.o. male had atopic dermatitis (AD) since childhood. He had esophageal stenosis, scoliosis, recurrent pneumonitis and asthma followed by esophageal cancer and gastrointestinal stromal tumor. Serum IgE 12304 U/mL, TARC 1925 pg/mL, peripheral eosinophils 2500/μL. Genetic test identified a novel heterozygous ERBIN variant (NM_018695.4: c.3781C>T, p.Arg1261Trp). Case 2: A 44 y.o. male had AD since childhood, with cystic lung disease, recurrent pneumonia, multiple skin abscesses, and delayed exfoliation of primary teeth. Cervical lymph node biopsy demonstrated fungal infectious granulomas. Serum IgE 55,435 U/mL, TARC 1545 pg/mL, eosinophils 300/μL. A previously reported heterozygous STAT3 variant (NM_139276.3: c.1414A>G, p.Asn472Asp) was identified. Case 3: A 19 y.o. extremely obese male developed AD in childhood, with recurrent otitis media, paronychia, cutaneous candidiasis, and sinusitis. He exhibited a broad nasal base and prominent forehead. Serum IgE 4670 U/mL, TARC 789 pg/mL, eosinophils 900/μL. A novel heterozygous ZNF341 variant (NM_001282933.2: c.2165G>A, p.Arg722His) was identified. Case 4: 44-y.o. male had AD since childhood. He repeated subcutaneous abscess on his buttocks, otitis media and multiple fungal granulomas in his scrotum. He had diffuse large B cell lymphoma at the age of 35. Serum IgE 38319 U/mL, TARC 997 pg/mL, Eosinophils 868 μ/mL. Splice site variant in STAT3 gene; NM_139276.3: c.1139+2dup (T/TA) was identified. Conclusion: Detailed history taking is a key to identify hyper IgE syndrome overlooked until adulthood.

title: Long-read phasing demonstrates allelic dose effects of COL4A4 variants: Implications for living donor kidney transplant
ja: ロングリードフェージングが示すCOL4A4バリアントのアレル量効果：生体腎移植ドナーへの示唆
en: Long-read phasing demonstrates allelic dose effects of COL4A4 variants: Implications for living donor kidney transplant
abs: Alport syndrome (AS) is characterized by locus heterogeneity(i.e. COL4A3, COL4A4, and COL4A5) and significant variable expressivity . A 36-year-old man with childhood-onset hematuria progressed to end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) and developed hearing loss in his 30s. Multiple maternal relatives had microscopic hematuria and his deceased father had ESKD. Whole exome sequencing identified two rare COL4A4 variants: c.2165-5A<G, predicted by SpliceAI to cause aberrant splicing and frameshift, and c.1323_1340del, an in-frame deletion previously reported in autosomal dominant AS. Because parental samples were unavailable, long-read sequencing (LRS) was performed and demonstrated the two variants were in trans. The compound heterozygous state likely produced an allelic dose effect, resulting in severe disease with early-onset ESKD and extrarenal manifestations, whereas heterozygous family members showed only mild renal findings. These findings suggest that COL4A4-related disease severity may be better understood as a phenotypic spectrum influenced by allelic dose effects rather than a simple autosomal dominant/recessive classification. In genetic counseling, precise long-read phasing was particularly important in the context of potential living donor kidney transplantation. Some reports support kidney donation from relatives carrying a single COL4A4 variant, even with hematuria, whereas others warn of increased risk of kidney failure. Thus, LRS-based phase determination is clinically valuable for accurate genetic counseling and medical management, even without parental samples.

title: Ocular-Neural Genetics in Aging: ToMMo Eye-Brain General Neuroimaging Initiative in Japan
ja: 加齢における眼・神経遺伝学：ToMMo眼・脳一般神経画像イニシアチブ
en: Ocular-Neural Genetics in Aging: ToMMo Eye-Brain General Neuroimaging Initiative in Japan
abs: Background: The retina reflects central nervous system pathology. However, shared polygenic networks among retinal morphology, brain structures, and tau/APOE-related neurodegeneration remain unmapped in East Asians. Purpose: This study elucidated genetic overlaps to establish ethnicity-specific imaging-genetics foundations. Methods: In the Tohoku Medical Megabank Organization (ToMMo) cohort, we conducted GWAS for retinal metrics from Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) images (N=40,714) and integrated results with Brain-MRI GWAS (N=12,218). LDSC, Bayesian colocalization, and Mendelian Randomization identified genetic correlations and causal variants. An age-related polygenic risk score (PRS) was tested against Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) subscales. A linear mixed-effects model evaluated longitudinal Delta Retinal Neural Fiber Layer/Ganglion Cell Layer Slope, adjusting for glaucoma/myopia variants. This study followed relevant ethical guidelines, with informed consent obtained from all participants. Results: GWAS identified significant loci for retinal traits and brain volumes, peaking at the right parahippocampal area. We pinpointed causal colocalizing loci shared between eye and brain. Joint PRS showed these risks significantly drive MMSE "Orientation to Time" subscores. Adjusting for glaucoma PRS unmasked novel tau-pathway pleiotropic loci governing structural atrophy speed. Conclusion: This triangulation uncovers the shared retina-brain genetic architecture, establishing an ethnicity-specific foundation for precision screening of preclinical neurodegeneration.

title: Clinical Outcomes of Insurance-Covered Genetic Testing and Expert Panel Evaluation for Suspected RPE65-Retinopathy
ja: RPE65網膜症疑いに対する保険収載遺伝学的検査とエキスパートパネル評価の臨床転帰
en: Clinical Outcomes of Insurance-Covered Genetic Testing and Expert Panel Evaluation for Suspected RPE65-Retinopathy
abs: Background: Inherited retinal dystrophies (IRDs) are a major cause of blindness. In Japan, voretigene neparvovec (Luxturna R) and its companion diagnostic, the PrismGuide TM IRD Panel System, were approved in 2023 for RPE65-retinopathy. We evaluated outcomes of expert panel review following insurance-covered genetic testing. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 275 cases discussed at the Ophthalmic Genetics Expert Panel between December 2023 and May 2026. Eligibility for insurance-covered testing required suspected autosomal recessive disease, childhood-onset severe night blindness with visual impairment, and markedly reduced full-field electroretinogram responses. Variant interpretation followed ACMG specifications adapted by the Japanese Retina and Vitreous Society. Results: Seventeen of 275 cases (6.2%) underwent insurance-covered genetic testing. Median age was 29 years (range 2 to 53). Six patients (35.3%) were eligible for Luxturna, four (23.5%) had RPE65-retinopathy without treatment eligibility, five (29.4%) received alternative genetic diagnoses, and two (11.8%) had other outcomes. Conclusions: Expert panel review identified Luxturna candidates in over one-third of tested patients. Despite potential referral bias, the high frequency of RPE65-retinopathy suggests that current eligibility criteria effectively enrich for affected patients, supporting the clinical utility of genetic testing and expert panel review.

title: Genome-wide association study of age at onset of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis reveals a novel European-specific locus.
ja: 筋萎縮性側索硬化症の発症年齢GWASが新規ヨーロッパ系特異的座位を同定
en: Genome-wide association study of age at onset of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis reveals a novel European-specific locus.
abs: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive motor neuron degeneration. Age at onset (AAO) influences disease progression and survival; however, whether genetic determinants of AAO are shared across populations and analytical frameworks remains unclear. We performed a genome-wide association study of AAO using data from 9,252 European ancestry ALS patients from dbGaP (phs000101). We used REGENIE for linear regression model and gwasurvivr with a Cox proportional hazards model to evaluate associations between SNPs and AAO. The Cox model identified no genome-wide significant loci, whereas linear regression identified a novel significant locus, with SNP X as the lead variant (p = 2.05 × 10-8, β = -1.443). These findings suggest that linear regression and survival models may detect different genetic effects on disease onset. SNP X was observed only in European ancestry populations and is in strong linkage disequilibrium with SNP Y, previously associated with eosinophil-related traits, suggesting possible involvement of immune-related pathways in ALS onset timing. In contrast, the ADAM29-GPM6A locus previously reported in Japanese ALS patients (Nakamura et al. Commun Biol 8:1720 2025) was not replicated in European ancestry patients. These findings suggest ancestry-related differences in AAO-associated loci and model-dependent association patterns, providing new insights into ALS heterogeneity.

title: Genome Mapping and HiFi Sequencing Identified a Novel Complex Structural Variant in Hereditary Neuralgic Amyotrophy
ja: ゲノムマッピングとHiFiシーケンスで同定した遺伝性神経痛性筋萎縮症の新規複雑構造多型
en: Genome Mapping and HiFi Sequencing Identified a Novel Complex Structural Variant in Hereditary Neuralgic Amyotrophy
abs: [Background] Sequencing analysis provides detailed information at the nucleotide level. However, detecting complex structural abnormalities is often challenging. In contrast, genome mapping analysis (GMA) enables visualization of structural variants. We report on complex chromosomal structural abnormalities that were identified and solved by combining these two methods. [Patients and Methods] We performed short-read whole-genome sequencing (srWGS) analysis in a family with suspected axonal neuropathy, including hereditary neuralgic amyotrophy (HNA) and other related conditions. No pathogenic variants had been identified in previous genetic testing. Since srWGS analysis suggested an abnormality spanning 17q25.1 to q25.3 in affected individuals, we performed GMA and HiFi long-read sequencing analysis (HiFi sequencing) using high molecular weight DNA extracted from blood to further elucidate the details. [Results] GMA yielded a contig of over 1 Mb spanning 17q25.1 to q25.3. Within this region, we identified an inverted duplication exceeding 500 kb, including the SEPTIN9 gene, and a duplicated insertion exceeding 151 kb. Detailed analysis of this region using HiFi sequencing revealed additional insertions of multiple small DNA fragments (less than 50 bp). To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of such a complex structural abnormality in the SEPTIN9 region in patients with HNA. [Conclusion] Combining GMA with Hi-Fi sequencing is highly effective in identifying and elucidating complex chromosomal structural variants.

title: TPK1 Deficiency Successfully Managed by Empirical Vitamin B1 Supplementation Before Genetic Diagnosis
ja: 遺伝学的診断前の経験的ビタミンB1補充で管理し得たTPK1欠損症
en: TPK1 Deficiency Successfully Managed by Empirical Vitamin B1 Supplementation Before Genetic Diagnosis
abs: A 50-year-old woman presented with hypotonia from 3 months of age. At 7 months, she developed decreased activity, recurrent vomiting, and impaired consciousness, and was hospitalized with suspected acute encephalopathy. Head control was achieved at 12 months. At 3 years, she developed acute cerebellar ataxia following a febrile illness. A metabolic disorder was suspected, and vitamin B1 administration partially improved her symptoms. Epileptic seizures occurred between 3 and 9 years of age, and antiseizure medication was continued until age 13. At 13 years, reduction of vitamin supplementation resulted in generalized weakness and bulbar symptoms, which improved after intravenous vitamin B1 administration. A vitamin B1-responsive disorder was suspected, and supplementation was continued thereafter. Her condition remained stable. At age 47, she was referred for follow-up. Neurological examination revealed gaze-evoked nystagmus, dysarthria, limb and truncal ataxia, spasticity, rigidity, hyperreflexia, and bilateral positive Babinski and Chaddock signs. She required assistance for walking. Brain MRI demonstrated encephalomalacia in the bilateral caudate heads and cerebellar vermian atrophy. Whole-genome sequencing identified pathogenic variants consistent with TPK1 deficiency. TPK1 encodes thiamine pyrophosphokinase, which converts vitamin B1 into thiamine pyrophosphate. Early vitamin B1 supplementation is crucial in this disorder. In this case, empirical vitamin B1 supplementation before genetic diagnosis was considered effective in preventing further neurological deterioration.

title: A Patient of Familial amyloidosis of the Finnish type with GSN Variant presenting with aortic valve regurgitation.
ja: 大動脈弁逆流を呈したGSNバリアントによるフィンランド型家族性アミロイドーシスの1例
en: A Patient of Familial amyloidosis of the Finnish type with GSN Variant presenting with aortic valve regurgitation.
abs: Background: Gelsolin amyloidosis is an autosomal dominant hereditary amyloidosis caused by deposition of mutant gelsolin fragments as amyloid in multiple organs. We report a case of gelsolin amyloidosis presenting with aortic regurgitation (AR). Case Presentation: A 72-year-old woman presented with ptosis and drooping of the mouth corners beginning in her 40s and had undergone three previous surgeries for ptosis. Several family members, including her mother, second son, one sibling, maternal grandmother, and maternal cousin, had similar symptoms, all developing ptosis in their 40s. Neurological examination revealed muscle weakness and atrophy involving the facial, tounge, and cervical muscles. No sensory disturbance was observed. Laboratory tests showed elevated BNP levels of 836 pg/mL and renal dysfunction with a serum creatinine level of 1.72 mg/dL and. Echocardiography demonstrated moderate-to-severe AR. No definitive findings suggestive of cardiac amyloid deposition were identified. Results: Whole-exome sequencing identified a heterozygous pathogenic variant in the GSN gene, c.487G>A (p.Asp163Asn), which has been previously reported. Discussion: Clinically significant cardiomyopathy in gelsolin amyloidosis is considered rare; however, several small case series have reported cardiac involvement and conduction abnormalities. Only one case with AR was found to the best of our knowledge. Conclusion: We experienced a case of gelsolin amyloidosis presenting with AR. This case highlights the importance of cardiac screening in patients with this disease.

title: Dopaminergic dysfunction in proximal 18q12.1-q12.3 deletion presenting with adult-onset tremor
ja: 成人発症振戦を呈した18q12.1-q12.3近位欠失のドパミン機能障害
en: Dopaminergic dysfunction in proximal 18q12.1-q12.3 deletion presenting with adult-onset tremor
abs: Proximal 18q deletion syndrome is a rare contiguous gene deletion disorder primarily associated with neurodevelopmental abnormalities. Although tremor and other movement disorders have occasionally been described, involvement of the dopaminergic system has not been clearly demonstrated. We report a 53-year-old woman with intellectual disability since childhood who developed adult-onset tremor. Neurological examination revealed postural and intention tremor involving the neck and both upper limbs, accompanied by orofacial dyskinesia. Brain MRI showed mild atrophy of the dorsal pons and midbrain. Dopamine transporter scintigraphy demonstrated reduced bilateral striatal uptake, suggesting nigrostriatal dysfunction. Cardiac MIBG scintigraphy was normal, and the overall findings were not suggestive of an underlying α-synucleinopathy. Targeted next-generation sequencing did not detect pathogenic variants associated with hereditary parkinsonism. Chromosomal microarray analysis identified a 5.5-Mb interstitial deletion at 18q12.1-q12.3. The deleted region encompasses multiple genes involved in neuronal development and synaptic regulation, including CELF4, ZNF24, MAPRE2, and ELP2. Haploinsufficiency of these genes may contribute not only to neurodevelopmental abnormalities but also to vulnerability of the dopaminergic system. This case provides evidence that proximal 18q deletion can be associated with dopaminergic dysfunction and adult-onset movement disorder, expanding the phenotypic spectrum of this condition.

title: Childhood-onset white matter disease and brain malformations caused by heterozygous end-truncating LAMB1 variants
ja: LAMB1ヘテロ接合性末端切断バリアントによる小児期発症白質疾患と脳形成異常
en: Childhood-onset white matter disease and brain malformations caused by heterozygous end-truncating LAMB1 variants
abs: LAMB1 encodes laminin subunit β1, a basement membrane protein critical in neurodevelopment. Biallelic LAMB1 variants, especially loss-of-function alleles, are classically associated with severe pediatric-onset neurodevelopmental disorders, including cobblestone lissencephaly, hydrocephalus, and cortical malformations. More recently, heterozygous end-truncating variants, predicted to escape nonsense-mediated mRNA decay, have been linked to a distinct adult-onset disorder characterized by neurological symptoms and diffuse white matter lesions on brain MRI. Because heterozygous end-truncating LAMB1 variants have been reported in only a few cases, the associated clinical and radiological spectrum remains unclear. Here, we report affected individuals from two unrelated families carrying novel heterozygous end-truncating variants in LAMB1 (NM_002291.3:c.5263_5269del and c.5224+5G>C), identified by whole exome or genome sequencing. The first variant was identified in six affected relatives and segregated with neurological symptoms and diffuse white matter lesions, already evident at 6 years of age in the youngest individual. The second variant occurred de novo in a 5-year-old girl with multiple brain malformations including cobblestone lissencephaly, resembling the phenotype of biallelic LAMB1 variants. These findings expand the clinical spectrum associated with heterozygous end-truncating LAMB1 variants, suggesting that their clinical phenotypes range from childhood-onset white matter disease and severe neurodevelopmental abnormalities to adult-onset leukoencephalopathy.

title: Integration of palliative care into the management of pediatric genetic diseases
ja: 小児遺伝性疾患の管理への緩和ケアの統合
en: Integration of palliative care into the management of pediatric genetic diseases
abs: Introduction: Recent genomic sequencing enables early diagnosis of pediatric genetic diseases, and gives a chance of considering palliative care (PC). This report indicated our experiences of integration of PC into the management of pediatric genetic diseases. Methods: Data drive from our hospital between 2018 and 2025. Patients with pediatric genetic diseases who received PC by PC health professionals were included. Results: Of the 69 patients who received PC, 34 (49%) were pediatric genetic diseases including 4 patients with Duchenne muscular dystrophy, 4 patients with Mitochondrial disease, 3 patients with Down syndrome and 2 patients with Fukuyama congenital muscular dystrophy. In addition, there were 21 cases of other rare genetic diseases, such as Pelizaeus-Merzbacher disease. The total number of advance care planning (ACP) sessions was 114. ACP was conducted repeatedly depending on the trajectory of patients, ranging from 1 to 11 sessions per patient (median, 2). The initial ACP age ranged from 4 to 35 years (median age 14 years). Two patients died at 12 years of age (Down syndrome) and at 15 years of age (SENEBAC syndrome), respectively. Bereavement care was conducted to both families. Conclusions: Integration of PC into genomics is important. However, a policy gap related to integrating PC into genomics exists. Genetic health professionals need the knowledge about PC and collaborate with PC health professionals, providing more appropriate management of pediatric genetic diseases.

title: Era-based changes in cardiac intervention and survival in infants with trisomy 18
ja: 18トリソミー児の心臓介入と生存の時代的変化
en: Era-based changes in cardiac intervention and survival in infants with trisomy 18
abs: <Background> Management of congenital heart disease in infants with trisomy 18 remains controversial. Our center increasingly considered cardiac surgery beginning around 2020. We evaluated the association between this change and clinical outcomes. <Methods> This retrospective cohort study compared cardiac intervention rates and survival in infants with trisomy 18 born at our center between Era 1 (2015-2019) and Era 2 (2020-2024) using Fisher's exact test and Kaplan-Meier analysis with log-rank test, respectively. Cardiac interventions included catheter-based and surgical procedures. <Results> A total of 31 infants were identified, including 17 in Era 1 and 14 in Era 2. Five infants whose families did not choose intensive care were excluded (4 in Era 1 and 1 in Era 2), leaving 26 infants for analysis. Baseline characteristics were similar between eras. Cardiac intervention was more frequently performed in Era 2 than Era 1, although the difference was not significant (46.2% vs 7.7%, p = 0.07). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed significantly longer survival in Era 2 (p < 0.05). Infants who underwent cardiac intervention showed significantly longer survival than non-surgical patients (p < 0.05). <Conclusions> Cardiac intervention gradually increased following changes in institutional practice and was associated with improved survival. Although limited by small sample size, selection bias, and temporal improvements in neonatal care, these findings suggest a potential role for cardiac intervention in selected infants with trisomy 18.

title: Diagnostic pathways of Rett syndrome-like cases: A five-year review at a single pediatric center
ja: Rett症候群様症例の診断経路：単一小児センターの5年間の検討
en: Diagnostic pathways of Rett syndrome-like cases: A five-year review at a single pediatric center
abs: Background; Rett syndrome-like neurodevelopmental disorders (RTT-like NDDs) form a phenotypic cluster defined by combinations of stereotypic movements, autistic traits, developmental delay, sleep disturbance, autonomic dysfunction, feeding difficulties, and epilepsy. This cluster is clinically recognizable but independent of classic Rett criteria and genetically heterogeneous. Without a guiding framework, prediction and treatment remain uncertain, and families manage care without clear direction. This study aimed to describe real-world diagnostic trajectories of RTT-like cases. Methods; We retrospectively reviewed eight patients seen between 2021 and 2026 with RTT-like features who received molecular diagnoses through insurance-based testing, IRUD, national research programs, or self-funded external analyses. Results; Only one patient underwent MECP2 testing at a referring institution; Rett syndrome was excluded at our center, and the final diagnosis was Lessel-Kreienkamp syndrome. Six patients were diagnosed through varied routes, with genetic causes spanning RNA-related, chromatin, metabolic, chromosomal, imprinting, and synaptic disorders, showing mechanisms beyond MECP2. Conclusions; RTT-like NDDs constitute a coherent clinical cluster, yet diagnostic routes and management remain inconsistent, increasing uncertainty for clinicians and families. Flexible genetic evaluation using broad panels or comprehensive genomic testing, together with a structured care framework tailored to this cluster, is needed.

title: Five children of Macrocephaly Associated with PTEN Hamartoma Tumor Syndrome
ja: PTEN過誤腫症候群に伴う大頭症の小児5例
en: Five children of Macrocephaly Associated with PTEN Hamartoma Tumor Syndrome
abs: Introduction: PTEN hamartoma tumor syndrome (PHTS) is an autosomal dominant disorder caused by pathogenic PTEN variants. It is characterized by hamartomas and an increased risk of malignancy, requiring surveillance. Although PHTS is often diagnosed in adulthood, it may also present in childhood with macrocephaly and intellectual disability (ID). We analyzed five children with PHTS. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed patients with pathogenic PTEN variants identified between August 2020 and March 2026. Genetic testing was performed using next-generation sequencing and Sanger sequencing. This study was approved by the ethics committees of Kobe University and Hyogo Prefectural Kobe Children Hospital. Results: There were two males and three females. Age at diagnosis ranged from 1 to 5 years. Macrocephaly ranged from +2.5 to +4.9 SD, whereas tall stature was absent. Developmental quotient ranged from 41 to 82 (mean 64.8). Brain MRI showed T2 hyperintensities in the peritrigonal white matter in three patients. One patient had gastrointestinal hamartomas with hypoalbuminemia and punctate palmoplantar keratosis. Missense variants were identified in two patients, nonsense variants in two, and one patient harbored both missense and splice-site variants. Discussion: In children with macrocephaly and ID, Sotos syndrome is often suspected; however, PHTS should also be considered. PHTS carries a tumor risk from childhood and requires follow-up; therefore, genetic testing should be actively considered when this disease is suspected based on clinical findings.

title: Acute recurrent pancreatitis in a 3-year-old girl with SPINK1 and compound heterozygous UBR1 variants
ja: SPINK1とUBR1複合ヘテロ接合バリアントを持つ3歳女児の急性反復性膵炎
en: Acute recurrent pancreatitis in a 3-year-old girl with SPINK1 and compound heterozygous UBR1 variants
abs: Multiple genetic factors can contribute to acute recurrent pancreatitis (ARP) in children. We report a 3-year-old girl with ARP requiring four hospitalizations, who carried a SPINK1 variant and compound heterozygous UBR1 variants. Targeted next-generation sequencing identified a heterozygous SPINK1 splice-site variant (c.194+2T>C), predicted to cause loss of function of pancreatic secretory trypsin inhibitor. This variant was also present in her unaffected father, suggesting that SPINK1 alone was insufficient to explain the phenotype. Whole-exome sequencing identified two rare UBR1 missense variants, c.2924T>C (p.Ile975Thr) and c.4856A>T (p.Asp1619Val) in trans. Both variants were predicted to be deleterious by multiple in silico tools. p.Ile975Thr is located in the WHD domain and p.Asp1619Val in the CHD domain; structural analysis suggested possible effects on interactions or folding. No variants were found in other major pancreatitis-associated genes. UBR1 encodes an E3 ubiquitin ligase. Biallelic loss-of-function variants cause Johanson- Blizzard syndrome, although milder impairment may produce variable phenotypes. The patient had no syndromic features except pancreatic involvement. Given that Ubr1-knockout mice show exocrine pancreatic dysfunction and susceptibility to injury, partial UBR1 dysfunction may have contributed to her pancreatitis susceptibility. Although the risk of compound heterozygous UBR1 variants or coexistence with SPINK1 variants remains unclear, UBR1 may be involved in a subset of idiopathic pancreatitis, including pediatric cases.

title: Spectrum of Congenital Malformations and Syndromic Pathology in Neonates: A Retrospective Analysis of 167 Clinical Cases
ja: 新生児の先天奇形と症候群性病態のスペクトラム：167例の後方視的解析
en: Spectrum of Congenital Malformations and Syndromic Pathology in Neonates: A Retrospective Analysis of 167 Clinical Cases
abs: Background: Congenital malformations (CM) and genetic pathology significantly drive neonatal morbidity and mortality. We evaluated clinical and genetic features in neonates to optimise diagnostic algorithms. Materials and Methods: A retrospective analysis of 167 neonates was conducted, assessing prenatal screening, ultrasound, clinical phenotypes, cytogenetic, and molecular genetic findings. Results: Dysmorphism/stigmata of dysembryogenesis were identified in 52 infants (31.1%), multiple CM in 18 (10.8%), and confirmed chromosomal anomalies in 14 (8.4%; 10 Down syndrome, 1 Turner, 1 Triple X, 1 Edwards, 1 microdeletion/microduplication). Cardiovascular CMs were most frequent (30.5%), followed by genitourinary (16.2%), gastrointestinal (13.2%), and pulmonary (9.6%) defects. Monogenic diagnoses included Beckwith–Wiedemann syndrome (n=2). A comparative analysis revealed that all 14 verified chromosomal cases occurred in 2025 (n=121), whereas zero were registered among live births in 2026 (n=46). This shift reflects enhanced prenatal screening, ultrasound quality, and NIPT coverage, enabling timely antenatal detection. Concurrently, non-chromosomal CM referrals increased in 2026. Conclusion: The high prevalence of dysmorphism (31.1%) contrasted with low chromosomal resolution (8.4%) highlights the limitations of standard karyotyping. Effective prenatal screening successfully reduced postnatal chromosomal births in 2026. Transitioning to chromosomal microarray analysis and next-generation sequencing as a standard is essential to improve diagnostic yield and genetic counselling.

title: Autosomal recessive spastic ataxia of Charlevoix-Saguenay (ARSACS):Clinical and genetic analyses in the 22 patients
ja: 常染色体潜性Charlevoix-Saguenay型痙性失調症（ARSACS）：22例の臨床・遺伝学的解析
en: Autosomal recessive spastic ataxia of Charlevoix-Saguenay (ARSACS):Clinical and genetic analyses in the 22 patients
abs: Objectives: Autosomal recessive spastic ataxia of Charlevoix- Saguenay (ARSACS) is a hereditary neurodegenerative disorder caused by SACS gene. The aim of this study was to elucidate the clinical and genetic characteristics of 22 Japanese patients in our cohort. Methods: We examined the clinical presentation and MRI findings. We performed Sanger sequencing of the SACS gene after obtaining consent for genetic testing. Results: A total of 24 variants in the SACS gene were identified in 22 Japanese patients from 16 families. Most of these variants were located in different regions of the gene, and the majority were nonsense or insertion/deletion variants; only 5 were missense variants. The mean age at onset was 6.95 years. Clinical symptoms included cerebellar ataxia and peripheral neuropathy in nearly all cases; however, 8 cases lacked hyperreflexia, 6 cases lacked lower limb spasticity, and 4 cases lacked pathological reflexes. No retinal hypermyelination was observed in 10 patients, and 9 patients had intellectual impairment. In almost all cases where MRI findings could be confirmed, atrophy of the superior vermis and cervical spinal cord, as well as T2 low signal intensity in the pons, were observed. However, T2 high signal intensity around the thalamus and thinning of the corpus callosum were observed in only about two-thirds of cases. Conclusion: In our cohort which genetic analysis was performed and variants in the SACS gene were identified, the clinical manifestations, MRI findings and the genetic variant locations were highly diverse.

title: Characterization of Somatic Instability and Repeat Interruptions in Japanese Patients with Myotonic Dystrophy Type 1
ja: 日本人筋強直性ジストロフィー1型患者の体細胞不安定性とリピート中断の特性解析
en: Characterization of Somatic Instability and Repeat Interruptions in Japanese Patients with Myotonic Dystrophy Type 1
abs: Background: Myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1) is caused by abnormal CTG repeat expansion in the 3' untranslated region of the DMPK gene. Somatic instability has been associated with disease progression, whereas repeat interruptions are known to be linked to delayed onset and milder symptoms. Objective: To characterize somatic instability and repeat interruptions in Japanese patients with DM1 using multiple methods. Methods: Lymphocyte DNA was analyzed. Repeat interruptions were screened by triplet repeat-primed PCR (TP-PCR), followed by Sanger sequencing and long-read sequencing (LRS) using PureTargetTM Repeat Expansion Panel (Pacific Biosciences). Somatic instability was evaluated by small-pool PCR (SP-PCR) and LRS. Results: Genomic DNA was obtained from 116 Japanese patients with DM1. TP-PCR followed by Sanger sequencing identified CCG interruptions in six samples from four families. Sanger sequencing and LRS demonstrated variation in the number and position among clones and reads. Interruption sites were relatively conserved within families. SP-PCR and LRS showed similar modal repeat lengths and distribution ranges in most samples, although discrepancies were observed in congenital cases. Expansion bias was more pronounced in samples with modal repeat lengths <600, whereas it tended to plateau in those with repeat lengths >600. Conclusion: LRS showed results largely consistent with SP-PCR and TP-PCR while enabling detailed analysis of somatic instability and repeat interruptions, supporting its utility in DM1 genetic research.

title: A Comparative Review of International Guidelines for Asymptomatic Hereditary ATTR Amyloidosis
ja: 無症候性遺伝性ATTRアミロイドーシスに関する国際ガイドラインの比較検討
en: A Comparative Review of International Guidelines for Asymptomatic Hereditary ATTR Amyloidosis
abs: [Objective] Recent advancements in disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) have optimized hereditary ATTRv amyloidosis management. Although predictive genetic testing identifies at-risk individuals, standardized clinical protocols for pre-emptive monitoring remain poorly established. This study systematically compared international consensus guidelines regarding clinical surveillance for asymptomatic ATTRv carriers. [Methods] International consensus frameworks and guidelines published since 2013 regarding asymptomatic ATTRv carrier management were evaluated. [Results] Frameworks universally converge on four core principles: (1) comprehensive baseline evaluation upon variant identification; (2) individualized surveillance tailored to mutation type and family history; (3) continuous subclinical assessments; and (4) mandatory care coordination through multidisciplinary teams with genetic counseling. Conversely, significant discrepancies remain regarding tissue biopsy recommendations and non-invasive modalities like bone scintigraphy. [Conclusion] While ATTRv amyloidosis is a paradigm model for pre-emptive medicine, harmonizing diagnostic discrepancies remains essential to maximize therapeutic efficacy. To facilitate sustainable surveillance, establishing minimally invasive monitoring methodologies, such as longitudinal serum biomarker assays, remains critical

title: Enrichment of LRP12 CGG repeat expansions in adult-onset non-5q spinal muscular atrophy
ja: 成人発症非5q型脊髄性筋萎縮症におけるLRP12 CGGリピート伸長の濃縮
en: Enrichment of LRP12 CGG repeat expansions in adult-onset non-5q spinal muscular atrophy
abs: Background: Adult-onset non-5q spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is genetically heterogeneous, and many cases remain molecularly undiagnosed. We tested whether LRP12 CGG repeat expansions are enriched in patients with clinically diagnosed adult-onset non-5q SMA. Methods: Eight consecutive Japanese families with clinically diagnosed adult-onset non-5q SMA meeting prespecified criteria were analyzed after excluding SMN1-related SMA, SBMA, and pathogenic variants in known SMA-, ALS-, and neuropathy-associated genes. LRP12 expansions were defined by a sawtooth repeat-primed PCR pattern and sized by Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing. Expansion frequencies were compared with 1,000 controls using two-sided Fisher's exact test. Results: LRP12 CGG repeat expansions were found in 6/8 probands (75.0%; 5/5 familial, 1/3 sporadic). Seven affected individuals carried heterozygous expansions of 58-92 repeat units, shorter than typical LRP12-OPDM expansions. They showed adult-onset, slowly progressive, proximal-predominant pure lower motor neuron weakness, preserved bulbar and sensory function, and no upper motor neuron signs throughout follow-up. The expansion frequency was markedly higher than in controls (2/1,000; P=5.4 x 10-13), whereas expansions were rare in an ALS series (2/496, 0.40%). Conclusions: LRP12 CGG repeat expansions may represent an underrecognized genetic cause of unresolved adult-onset lower motor neuron syndromes with SMA-like features and broaden the clinical spectrum of LRP12-related disease. LRP12 repeat-expansion testing should be considered in such patients.

title: Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Digenic TBP/STUB1 Spinocerebellar Ataxia
ja: TBP/STUB1二遺伝子性脊髄小脳失調症のミトコンドリア機能障害
en: Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Digenic TBP/STUB1 Spinocerebellar Ataxia
abs: Digenic TBP/STUB1 spinocerebellar ataxia (SCATBP/STUB1) is a recently proposed disorder characterized by the coexistence of an intermediate TBP repeat expansion and a STUB1 variant. However, its pathology remains poorly understood. We report a 44-year-old woman with progressive myoclonus, cerebellar ataxia, and cognitive impairment. Brain magnetic resonance imaging showed cerebellar atrophy with hyperintense dentate nuclei (Crab sign). Muscle biopsy revealed ragged-red fibers with cytochrome c oxidase deficiency and scattered succinate dehydrogenase-positive fibers, consistent with mitochondrial myopathy. Despite these findings, no pathogenic variants were detected in mitochondrial DNA or in nuclear genes associated with mitochondrial disease. Whole-exome sequencing identified a heterozygous missense variant in STUB1 [NM_005861.4: c.146A>G p.(Tyr49Cys)], while ONT target long-read sequencing confirmed an intermediate TBP repeat expansion (36/42 repeats), establishing the diagnosis of SCATBP/STUB1. This is the first description of skeletal muscle pathology in SCATBP/STUB1, which expands the pathological spectrum of this recently recognized digenic disorder and suggests that mitochondrial dysfunction may contribute to its pathogenesis. The findings also suggest that intermediate TBP expansions may modify the clinical impact of STUB1 variants and contribute to disease expression. The SCATBP/STUB1 should be considered in patients with suspected mitochondrial disease, particularly those with MERRF-like features and negative mitochondrial genetic testing.

title: Mitochondrial DNA Variant Screening in 646 Japanese Patients with Hereditary Spastic Paraplegia
ja: 日本人遺伝性痙性対麻痺646例のミトコンドリアDNAバリアントスクリーニング
en: Mitochondrial DNA Variant Screening in 646 Japanese Patients with Hereditary Spastic Paraplegia
abs: Background: Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) variants have been reported in hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP), but their role in HSP cohorts remains unclear. Methods: Using MitoHPC, we called mtDNA variants from exome data of 646 patients with HSP collected through the Japan Spastic Paraplegia Research Consortium (JASPAC). Variants with allele fraction >0.1 were annotated using ClinVar, APOGEE2, population databases, and literature. Candidates were prioritized by rarity, disease reports and predicted impact. Results: In MT-ATP6, five rare missense variants with APOGEE2 probability >0.1 were found, including the homoplasmic m.9176T>C, p.(Leu217Pro), reported in maternally inherited spastic paraplegia, and four additional variants classified as variants of uncertain significance (VUS). Among these four VUS, one was found in a family that did not show maternal inheritance, and another in a patient with a likely pathogenic variant in a nuclear gene. Heteroplasmic MT-ATP6 m.9205_9206del, p.(Ter227MetextTer?), a likely pathogenic variant reported in neonatal-onset mitochondrial disease, was also identified, although its relevance to HSP remains unclear. In MT-TV, homoplasmic m.1661A>G, previously reported in spastic paraplegia, was found in three unrelated patients. Pathogenic mtDNA variants related to hearing loss and Leber hereditary optic neuropathy were also found. Conclusions: This exome-based mtDNA screening identified candidate mtDNA variants in patients with HSP. Further family studies and functional validation are needed to clarify their clinical significance.

title: Genetic diagnosis of sibling cases guided by outlier expression analysis using urine-derived cell transcriptomics
ja: 尿由来細胞トランスクリプトームの外れ値発現解析に基づく同胞例の遺伝学的診断
en: Genetic diagnosis of sibling cases guided by outlier expression analysis using urine-derived cell transcriptomics
abs: Background: Transcriptome analysis can improve the diagnostic yield for neurodevelopmental disorders. However, identifying pathogenic non-coding variants remains challenging when exome sequencing detects only a single heterozygous pathogenic variant in a recessive disease. Case Report: We applied RNA-seq using urine-derived cells (UDCs) to a family with two affected brothers with muscular dystrophy-dystroglycanopathy and dilated cardiomyopathy. Exome sequencing identified a maternally inherited heterozygous B3GALNT2 splice-site variant (NM_152490.5:c.261-2A>G) but no second pathogenic allele. UDCs RNA-seq with OUTRIDER detected markedly decreased expression of B3GALNT2 in the proband and a milder decrease in the father, suggesting a paternally inherited non-coding variant. Genome sequencing revealed a 357-bp heterozygous deletion encompassing the B3GALNT2 promoter and transcription start site, which segregated with the phenotype. RNA-seq supported aberrant splicing from the splice-site allele and reduction of transcripts from the deletion allele. Conclusion: These findings provide proof of concept that UDCs RNA-seq-guided outlier-expression analysis can identify non-coding second hits and support genetic diagnosis. They also suggest that cardiac surveillance may be warranted in B3GALNT2-related disorder as affected individuals age.

title: Genome clustering using GDD-ENS enables reinterpretation of diagnoses and inference of cancer of unknown primary
ja: GDD-ENSを用いたゲノムクラスタリングによる診断の再解釈と原発不明がんの推定
en: Genome clustering using GDD-ENS enables reinterpretation of diagnoses and inference of cancer of unknown primary
abs: Cancers of unknown primary (CUP) and diagnostically challenging cases remain a major obstacle in precision oncology. Genome- Derived-Diagnosis Ensemble (GDD-ENS) is a deep learning model trained on MSK-IMPACT genomic profiles to predict cancer type. We examined whether GDD-ENS can be implemented in a Japanese comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) setting to support diagnostic reinterpretation and cancer type inference. We analyzed 2,133 non- CUP cases from 13 institutions. While GDD-ENS showed high discrimination (macro-averaged AUC 0.87 in tissue CGP), concordance with pathological diagnosis was modest. UMAP-based dimensionality reduction of predictive scores revealed clusters enriched for specific cancer types with varying heterogeneity. Focusing on discordant cases between genomic prediction and pathological diagnosis, we identified 160 candidates for diagnostic reconsideration using cluster- and neighborhood-based criteria. Among these, 126 showed higher genomic similarity to alternative cancer types than to their original diagnoses. Expert review confirmed clinically meaningful discordance in selected cases, particularly metastatic lesions and ambiguous samples. We further applied this framework to 68 CUP cases. Neighborhood-based inference enabled cancer type estimation in a subset with low entropy in neighboring cancer composition. These results demonstrate that GDD-ENS-derived genomic clustering identifies diagnostically ambiguous cases and supports cancer type inference in CUP, complementing pathology by incorporating genomic similarity into clinical decisions.

title: CLAVI: an LLM-agent framework for contextual interpretation of variants of uncertain significance
ja: CLAVI：VUSの文脈的解釈のためのLLMエージェントフレームワーク
en: CLAVI: an LLM-agent framework for contextual interpretation of variants of uncertain significance
abs: Genome sequencing in patients with suspected genetic disorders increasingly identifies variants of uncertain significance (VUS), including putative splicing variants. Although prediction tools support initial prioritization, direct clinical or functional evidence for the query variant is often unavailable. Evidence from analogous variants affecting the same gene, region/domain, and molecular consequence can provide contextual support, but systematic collection and integration of such evidence remain labor-intensive. We developed CLAVI, an LLM agent-based framework for hypothesis generation on the functional impact and disease relevance of VUS. CLAVI searches literature and variant resources to identify high-grade similar variant evidence, defined as evidence from analogous variants supported by functional studies and/or patient reports. It summarizes the findings in the context of gene and domain information, and interprets the potential functional impact of the query VUS. Benchmarking across repeated runs showed that CLAVI achieved reliable recall and precision despite run-to-run fluctuation inherent to LLM agents, while generating interpretable evidence summaries. We are also applying CLAVI to approximately 1,000 putative splicing VUS extracted from SRA-derived genomic data. CLAVI prioritizes VUS lacking direct variant-specific evidence by leveraging analogous variant evidence, without assigning ACMG/AMP classifications. This approach may help efficiently identify candidate variants for expert review or functional validation in genetic disorders.

title: Development and Evaluation of ZebraSeek, an Integrated Generative AI Based Diagnostic Support Tool for Rare Diseases
ja: 希少疾患向け生成AI統合診断支援ツールZebraSeekの開発と評価
en: Development and Evaluation of ZebraSeek, an Integrated Generative AI Based Diagnostic Support Tool for Rare Diseases
abs: Diagnosis of rare diseases remains a major clinical challenge because of the limited number of reported cases. Existing systems, such as PubCaseFinder and GestaltMatcher, are useful as diagnostic aids; however, they are limited by the types of data they can accept and are often biased toward a narrow range of diseases. In recent years, generative AI such as ChatGPT has attracted attention for clinical use, but simple prompt-based use alone lacks sufficient medical accuracy and carries the risk of hallucinations. To address these limitations, we developed ZebraSeek, a diagnostic support tool that integrates information from generative AI, existing diagnostic support programs, medical databases, and search engines. ZebraSeek uses generative AI as its core and applies a custom workflow to sequentially process and integrate information from multiple sources. This enables the system not only to present accurate diagnostic candidates but also to provide detailed textual explanations for why each disease is suggested. We evaluated the system using data derived from actual case reports. While the diagnostic accuracy of conventional methods and standalone generative AI with simple prompting was approximately 30-50%, ZebraSeek achieved an accuracy of over 60%. By efficiently organizing and integrating previously scattered medical information, ZebraSeek may reduce the physical and psychological burden on clinicians and help address the long-standing challenge of the diagnostic odyssey in rare disease care.

title: Long-read RNA sequencing reveals gene- and transcript-level expression changes in Alzheimer's disease
ja: ロングリードRNAシーケンスが明らかにするアルツハイマー病の遺伝子・転写産物レベル発現変化
en: Long-read RNA sequencing reveals gene- and transcript-level expression changes in Alzheimer's disease
abs: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a common type of dementia, and its prevalence is increasing worldwide including in Japan. Early intervention is essential for delaying disease progression, highlighting the urgent need for novel biomarkers for early diagnosis. In this study, we aimed to identify blood-based biomarkers through gene- and transcript-level expression patterns associated with AD using long-read RNA sequencing. Long-read RNA sequencing using Oxford Nanopore Technologies was performed using blood samples from 116 AD patients (mean age=75.2±4.5) and 72 cognitively normal individuals (mean age=72.0±4.8) aged >64 years, obtained from the National Center for Geriatrics and Gerontology Biobank. Differential expression analyses were conducted at both the gene (DEG) and transcript (DET) levels. DEG analysis identified 525 significantly differentially expressed genes (FDR < 0.05, FC > 1.2) and four enriched KEGG pathways. DET analysis, excluding genes identified in the DEG analysis, identified 449 significantly altered transcripts and two enriched KEGG pathways. Notably, the Neutrophil extracellular trap formation pathway was detected in both DEG and DET analyses. Among the genes in this pathway, six neutrophil-enriched gene exhibited significant alterations at the transcript level, without corresponding gene-level changes. These findings demonstrate that transcript-level analysis can detect expression changes that are undetectable by conventional gene-level approaches. Such transcript-specific alterations may contribute to the development of early diagnostic biomarkers.

title: A trio-based long-read sequencing workflow identifies a pathogenic Alu element insertion in an undiagnosed patient
ja: トリオベースのロングリード解析ワークフローが未診断患者の病的Alu挿入を同定
en: A trio-based long-read sequencing workflow identifies a pathogenic Alu element insertion in an undiagnosed patient
abs: Long-read sequencing (LRS) is a powerful tool for detecting structural variants (SVs), which are major causes of genetic diseases. However, the application of trio-based analysis to LRS data remains challenging due to the complexity of merging and comparing SVs across individuals. Here, we established a workflow to prioritize pathogenic SVs using trio-based LRS whole-genome sequencing. The workflow integrates high-accuracy basecalling, trio-based phasing, and multiple SV callers (CuteSV and Sniffles2). We employed the PanPop Realign and Thin (PART) process to merge SVs and utilized the JSV1 Japanese population-specific SV frequency dataset to filter common variants. We evaluated this workflow using 12 family trios from the Initiatives for Rare and Undiagnosed Diseases (IRUD) project. The workflow successfully prioritized candidate SVs by narrowing down tens of thousands of loci to less than approximately 20 with X-linked homozygous and de novo models for manual inspection. Notably, we identified a pathogenic AluY element insertion in the GPC3 gene in a patient with Simpson-Golabi-Behmel syndrome. This variant had been missed by previous short-read whole-exome sequencing but was clearly prioritized by our LRS workflow. Our workflow effectively prioritizes pathogenic SVs from LRS data, demonstrating the clinical utility of LRS for diagnosing rare diseases involving complex SVs without prior knowledge of candidate genes or loci.

title: Aortic Dissection During the Perinatal Period in Women with Marfan-Related Disorders: A Retrospective Cohort Study
ja: Marfan関連疾患女性の周産期大動脈解離：後方視的コホート研究
en: Aortic Dissection During the Perinatal Period in Women with Marfan-Related Disorders: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abs: Background: Marfan-related disorders are one of the congenital diseases which is known to elevate the risk of aortic dissection during the perinatal period. This study aimed to investigate the incidence of aortic dissection during the perinatal period in women with Marfan-related disorders by using a nationwide administrative claims database. Methods: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using data extracted from the Japanese Diagnosis Procedure Combination database. Women diagnosed with Marfan-related disorders who delivered between 2010 and 2023 were included in the study. Results: We identified a total of 226 deliveries by 175 women with Marfan-related disorders. Cesarean section accounted for 69.0% of deliveries. Among all deliveries, 15.0% of patients received beta-blockers from admission until postpartum day 2. The prevalence of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy was high among patients who experienced aortic dissection. During pregnancy, 1.8% of cases (4/226) experienced aortic dissection and required aortic surgery. In the postpartum period, 2.7% of cases (6/226) experienced aortic dissection during postpartum hospitalization. Within 1 year after delivery, 2.7% of cases (6/226) were re-hospitalized for aortic dissection. Conclusions: Women with Marfan-related disorders were at a high risk of aortic dissection even in the postpartum period. The prevalence of cesarean delivery was higher than that in the overall population in Japan. Beta-blockers may be underused to prevent aortic dissection in women with Marfan-related disorders.

title: Perinatal outcomes of rare autosomal trisomies and sex chromosome aneuploidies detected by NIPT in Japan
ja: 本邦NIPTで検出された稀な常染色体トリソミーと性染色体異数性の周産期転帰
en: Perinatal outcomes of rare autosomal trisomies and sex chromosome aneuploidies detected by NIPT in Japan
abs: Genome-wide non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT) can detect chromosomal abnormalities beyond common trisomies, including rare autosomal trisomies (RATs) and sex chromosome aneuploidies (SCAs). However, the clinical significance of these findings remains unclear because they are not routinely disclosed in Japan. We retrospectively evaluated the association between RATs/SCAs and perinatal outcomes in 30,373 pregnancies with known delivery outcomes among 46,082 women who underwent NIPT between 2015 and 2021. RATs and SCAs were identified through cfDNA-based NIPT data reanalysis, and cases were classified into RAT, SCA, and normal groups. Maternal characteristics and perinatal outcomes, including miscarriage or stillbirth, fetal growth restriction, and fetal abnormalities, were compared among groups. RATs were detected in 187 cases (0.62%) and SCAs in 117 (0.39%). Compared with the normal group, both RAT and SCA groups showed significantly higher rates of miscarriage or stillbirth (RAT: 3.7% vs 0.7%; SCA: 7.7% vs 0.7%) and fetal abnormalities (RAT: 13.9% vs 4.7%; SCA: 7.8% vs 4.7%) (all P values were less than 0.001). Overall adverse outcomes occurred in 13.9% of RAT cases and 18.8% of SCA cases, exceeding those in the normal group, although more than 80% of pregnancies showed favorable outcomes. Because NIPT reflects placental cfDNA, these findings may support careful prenatal and perinatal assessment in selected cases and may provide clinically relevant information for perinatal risk assessment in current Japanese practice.

title: Oocyte Donation ART in Mosaic Turner Syndrome: Treatment Outcomes and Perinatal Prognosis in Four Cases
ja: モザイクTurner症候群への卵子提供ART：4例の治療成績と周産期予後
en: Oocyte Donation ART in Mosaic Turner Syndrome: Treatment Outcomes and Perinatal Prognosis in Four Cases
abs: Background: Turner syndrome (TS) features haploinsufficiency of SHOX (short stature) and ovarian-function genes (BMP15, DIAPH2), causing premature ovarian insufficiency. Mosaic TS may confer better live-birth rates via oocyte donation than non-mosaic 45,X. A 2024 meta-analysis reported HDP in 8-14% of TS pregnancies, though karyotype-specific risk differences remain unclear. Pregnancy eligibility depends on aortic pathology severity. Methods: Four TS patients (five pregnancies, six deliveries) achieving live births via oocyte donation at St. Mother Hospital were reviewed. Karyotypes were confirmed by G-band analysis. All underwent frozen-thawed blastocyst transfer with hormone replacement. Informed consent was obtained. Results: Karyotypes: 45,X (case 1), mos 45,X/46,X,i(X) (q10)/47,X,i(X)(q10)x2 (case 2), mos 46,X,del(X)(p11.4)/ 46,X,idic(X)(p11.4) (case 3), mos 46,X,i(X)(q10)/45,X (case 4). Pregnancy was achieved within 1-2 transfers. Case 1 (45,X) developed HDP at 16 weeks, progressing to superimposed preeclampsia at 35 weeks; emergency cesarean at 37 weeks (2,030 g, Apgar 7/9). Mosaic cases were uncomplicated. Case 3 delivered vaginally twice at 40 weeks (148 cm). No neonatal anomalies were detected. Conclusions: When cardiovascular evaluation is reassuring, oocyte donation enables live birth even in TS with aortic-risk gene haploinsufficiency (e.g., TIMP1). Early diagnosis and timely Kaufmann therapy are critical for uterine development and favorable perinatal outcomes.

title: A CVS case with an NGS-detected deletion missed by karyotyping and classified as VUS by SNP array
ja: 核型分析で見逃されSNPアレイでVUSとされた欠失をNGSで検出したCVS症例
en: A CVS case with an NGS-detected deletion missed by karyotyping and classified as VUS by SNP array
abs: Case: A 43-year-old woman, gravida 3, visited our clinic at 37 for primary infertility. After unsuccessful intrauterine insemination, she began IVF at age 38. She underwent nine oocyte retrievals and seven embryo transfers, with two miscarriages. In January 2025, ICSI and transfer of two frozen embryos resulted in a singleton pregnancy. Because of advanced maternal age and recurrent miscarriage, transabdominal chorionic villus sampling was performed under local anesthesia at 12 weeks 0 days. Results: NGS detected a 21q22.3 deletion. SNP microarray confirmed 21q22.3(45,044,960-46,673,449)x1. The same deletion was found in the mother. According to ACMG/ ClinGen criteria, it was classified as a variant of uncertain significance (VUS) and clinically interpreted as a normal variant. The 1.6-Mb deleted region contained four genes/regions related to haploinsufficiency and phenotypic abnormalities: DIP2A, LSS, 21q22.3 population region, and FTCD. None had a haploinsufficiency score of 3, indicating pathogenicity by deletion alone. DIP2A showed little evidence for haploinsufficiency, and the other three were judged normal variants. FTCD haploinsufficiency does not cause disease, but if the remaining allele carries a pathogenic variant, glutamate formiminotransferase deficiency (OMIM 229100) may rarely occur. Conclusion: Although prenatal diagnosis for advanced maternal age usually relies on chromosomal testing, NGS detected a deletion that conventional analysis could miss. Detailed evaluation enabled accurate clinical interpretation and assessment of possible future genetic risks.

title: Mildly Increased Nuchal Translucency and Progressive Fetal Findings Associated With 5p Abnormality
ja: 軽度NT肥厚と進行性胎児所見を伴う5p異常
en: Mildly Increased Nuchal Translucency and Progressive Fetal Findings Associated With 5p Abnormality
abs: Introduction The significance of mildly increased nuchal translucency (NT) below 3.5 mm remains controversial in prenatal genetic counseling. We report a prenatal case initially presenting with mildly increased NT, followed by cystic hygroma and diagnosis of 5p abnormality. Case Presentation A 27-year-old nulliparous woman underwent first-trimester combined screening at 12 weeks. Crown-rump length was 65.6 mm and NT measured 2.8 mm, above the 95th percentile. Nasal bone was present. Tricuspid regurgitation, abnormal ductus venosus flow, and structural abnormalities were not observed. The estimated risk for trisomy 21 was 1/676, higher than the background risk; however, no additional genetic testing was requested after counseling. Ultrasonography at 16 weeks revealed septated cystic hygroma. No hydrops or structural abnormalities were observed. Amniocentesis was performed. G-banding and FISH demonstrated 46,XX,add(5)(p15.1). Chromosomal microarray was not requested. The abnormality was considered to involve chromosome 5p deletion with duplication of unknown origin. After information sharing, the couple opted for pregnancy termination. Because the couple hoped for future pregnancy, parental karyotyping was subsequently performed and showed normal results, suggesting a likely de novo abnormality. Discussion This case suggests that chromosomal abnormalities beyond common trisomies may occur even in fetuses with mildly increased NT. Individualized genetic counseling, information on additional testing, and follow-up ultrasound evaluation should therefore be considered in such cases.

title: Maternal copy number variations detected by noninvasive prenatal testing in Japanese women
ja: 日本人女性のNIPTで検出された母体コピー数多型
en: Maternal copy number variations detected by noninvasive prenatal testing in Japanese women
abs: Noninvasive prenatal testing (NIPT) is a screening test for fetal chromosomal trisomies using cell-free DNA in maternal plasma. Because NIPT uses next-generation sequencing, it can also provide maternal genetic information. Although most copy number variations (CNVs) are benign, some have been associated with pathological phenotypes, and population-specific CNV profiles have attracted increasing attention. However, most large-scale CNV studies have been conducted in Western populations, and data from Japanese cohorts remain scarce. In this study, we conducted the first multicenter, large-scale cohort analysis of maternal CNVs detected by NIPT in Japanese women. A total of 46,082 participants were analyzed to establish a reliable detection threshold and to evaluate the clinical significance of maternal CNVs. Detected CNVs were validated using array CGH, and ROC curve analysis identified 0.8 Mb as the minimum threshold achieving 100% specificity. Using this criterion, maternal CNVs were identified in 2,907 cases (6.3%), most frequently as an 8p23.2 duplication. Comparison with public genomic databases, including ToMMo and gnomAD, showed that all CNVs detected in this study had been previously reported, with particularly high concordance with ToMMo. Several rare CNVs were also identified. These findings indicate that NIPT can reliably detect maternal CNVs of 0.8 Mb or larger. The presence of these CNVs in ongoing pregnancies also suggests that they are unlikely to exert a major adverse effect on fertility or very early pregnancy loss.

title: Clinical management of secondary findings in hematologic malignancy panel testing: a single-institution analysis
ja: 血液腫瘍パネル検査における二次的所見の臨床管理：単一施設解析
en: Clinical management of secondary findings in hematologic malignancy panel testing: a single-institution analysis
abs: Background: Comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) for hematologic malignancies can identify potential germline pathogenic variants (PGPVs) as secondary findings. However, interpretation is often complicated by tumor-derived variants, clonal hematopoiesis, and mosaicism. At our institution, CGP is performed with the Division of Clinical Genetics, and certified genetic counselors provide GC. Real-world data on PGPV interpretation and management remain limited. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 23 patients who underwent CGP between June 2025 and April 2026. Patients with PGPVs were evaluated for GC, confirmatory testing, and subsequent management. Results: PGPVs were identified in 4 of 23 patients (17%), involving CHEK2, DDX41, CDKN2A, and BRCA1. All four received GC. Confirmatory testing was performed in three cases: CHEK2 and DDX41 were confirmed as germline variants, whereas CDKN2A remained indeterminate due to suspected mosaicism. Testing was not performed in the BRCA1 case because of patient preference. No relatives underwent cascade testing. Management varied according to confirmatory test results, variant interpretation, and patient preferences. Conclusions: In this single-institution analysis, PGPVs were detected in 17% of patients undergoing CGP for hematologic malignancies. Variant interpretation was occasionally complicated by suspected mosaicism, and cascade testing was not implemented despite a structured GC program. Further studies are needed to establish clearer criteria for confirmatory testing and to identify factors influencing cascade testing.

title: Pan-cancer germline findings beyond BRCA1/2 in 8,109 paired tumor-normal CGP cases
ja: 8,109例の腫瘍-正常ペアCGPにおけるBRCA1/2以外のpan-cancer生殖細胞系列所見
en: Pan-cancer germline findings beyond BRCA1/2 in 8,109 paired tumor-normal CGP cases
abs: Background: Paired tumor-normal CGP testing with GenMineTOP enables direct identification of germline pathogenic variants (GPVs). We characterized GPVs across solid tumors, focusing on non- BRCA1/2 GPVs and challenges in low variant allele frequency (VAF) findings. Methods: We analyzed 8,109 solid tumor patients in C-CAT who underwent GenMineTOP testing (August 2023 to March 2026). Pathogenic/likely pathogenic GPVs were summarized by cancer type/ gene. HBOC-related cancers were breast, ovarian, prostate, and pancreatic cancers. Results: GPVs were detected in 410/8,109 patients (5.1%; 424 variants). Frequent genes were BRCA2 (n=83), BRCA1 (n=53), TP53 (n=46), ATM (n=31), NF1 (n=30), RAD51D (n=29), and PALB2 (n=22). Non-BRCA1/2 GPVs comprised 67.9% of all GPVs (288/424) and 33.6% of GPVs detected in HBOC-related cancers (38/113). The proportion of BRCA1/2 among GPVs in HBOC-related cancers differed significantly: 78.9% (breast), 66.7% (ovarian), 100% (prostate), 51.4% (pancreatic) (Fisher's exact test, p=0.0199). In pancreatic cancer, PALB2 (n=6), TP53 (n=4), and ATM (n=3) were prominent. TP53 was the most common GPV in brain tumors (14/61) and soft tissue sarcomas (13/59). Across all cancers, low-VAF findings were observed in TP53 (n=9), NF1 (n=2), and CHEK2 (n=1), with VAF 0.169-0.299. Conclusions: Among GPVs detected by GenMineTOP, 67.9% were non-BRCA1/2, supporting clinical systems for managing GPVs beyond BRCA1/2. BRCA1/2 proportions varied significantly across HBOC-related cancers. Low-VAF findings require careful interpretation for mosaicism or clonal hematopoietic changes

title: Clinical Genetics Collaboration for Suspected Germline Findings Triggered by Hematologic Malignancy Expert Panel Review
ja: 血液腫瘍エキスパートパネルを契機とした生殖細胞系列所見疑いへの臨床遺伝連携
en: Clinical Genetics Collaboration for Suspected Germline Findings Triggered by Hematologic Malignancy Expert Panel Review
abs: Background: Genomic profiling for hematologic malignancies can identify variants suspicious for germline predisposition in addition to clinically relevant somatic alterations. These findings may affect family counseling, confirmatory testing, and related donor selection for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. However, the clinical workflow linking Expert Panel (EP) review to clinical genetics assessment and genetic counselling remains poorly characterized. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed consecutive patients discussed at the institutional hematologic malignancy EP after HemeSightR testing at Kyushu University Hospital and affiliated centers between June 2025 and March 2026. Patients requiring clinical genetics collaboration because of suspected germline findings were identified. Results: Among 121 patients, median age was 61 years (range, 9-85), and 61% were male. Nine patients (7.4%) required clinical genetics involvement for disclosure and post-test management. Suspected genes included TP53 (n=3), BRCA1/2 (n=3), DDX41 (n=2), and ATM (n=1). Relevant family history was identified in six patients. Two patients required additional multidisciplinary discussion regarding suitability of related hematopoietic stem cell donors. Conclusions: EP review served as an important pathway linking patients with suspected germline findings to clinical genetics care. Integration of clinical genetics into hematologic malignancy genomic practice may improve management of suspected germline findings, particularly in transplantation settings where donor selection can be affected.

title: Feasibility of the Chrovis Platform for CGP Decision Support: A Concordance Study with Expert Panel Interpretations
ja: CGP意思決定支援におけるChrovisプラットフォームの実現可能性：エキスパートパネル解釈との一致性
en: Feasibility of the Chrovis Platform for CGP Decision Support: A Concordance Study with Expert Panel Interpretations
abs: Background: Comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) has been reimbursed in Japan since 2019, but its clinical use is limited by interpretive complexity and the burden on expert panels (EPs). Scalable decision-support systems are required. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed CGP data from Kyoto University Hospital between 2019 and 2022 (FoundationOne CDx and OncoGuide TMNCC OncoPanel). Our originally-developed structured EP rules were integrated into the Chrovis platform (Xcoo, Inc., Tokyo), which automatically matched alterations to therapeutic recommendations using curated databases and YAML (a human-readable format)-based rules. EP interpretations served as the reference, and concordance was assessed by two specialists, with discrepancies resolved using validated evidence. Actionable variants were defined as Evidence Levels A to D under JSMO/JSCO/JCA criteria. Results: Of 356 patients, 305 were eligible after excluding trial referrals and VUS. Concordance was achieved in 271 cases (88.9%), including 67 with actionable findings (82 genes), of which 33 (10.8%; 38 genes) were Evidence Level A; 204 had no actionable annotations. Overall, 237/305 (77.7%) were amenable to streamlined EP review. Discordances occurred in 34 cases (11.1%): 26 (8.5%) from pending EP rule updates, and 8 (2.6%) were attributable to annotation-related inconsistencies. Conclusion: Auto-annotation using YAML-based rules showed high concordance with EP interpretations, indicating that it can streamline CGP interpretation for individual physicians and supporting its feasibility as a decision-support tool.

title: DNA Degradation in Prostate Cancer Tissue: Analysis Across Multiple CGP Platforms
ja: 前立腺がん組織のDNA分解：複数CGPプラットフォーム横断解析
en: DNA Degradation in Prostate Cancer Tissue: Analysis Across Multiple CGP Platforms
abs: Background: Comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) is increasingly important in prostate cancer, particularly for identifying BRCA1/2 mutations to guide PARP inhibitor therapy. However, CGP test failure due to poor DNA quality of FFPE specimens remains a critical issue. This study aimed to characterize DNA quality impairment in prostate cancer across multiple CGP platforms. Methods: Cases submitted to NCC Oncopanel (NCC) or GenMineTOP (TOP) between August 2023 and April 2025 were analyzed. Failure rates were assessed by DNA quantity and delta-delta Cq-based DNA quality metrics. Results: A total of 2,716 NCC and 4,700 TOP cases were included. DNA quantity-related failure rates in prostate cancer were low (NCC: 2.0%; TOP: 3.5%). In contrast, delta-delta Cq-based failure rates were markedly elevated and the highest among all cancer types on both platforms (NCC: 15.3%; TOP: 17.2%). Conclusions: CGP failure in prostate cancer is predominantly driven by DNA degradation rather than insufficient tumor quantity, consistent across both platforms. This likely reflects tissue-intrinsic characteristics of prostate cancer. Optimizing pre-analytical procedures and considering liquid biopsy are essential strategies. Further analysis incorporating FoundationOne CDx data will be reported in future work.

title: Clinical interpretation of low variant allele fraction variants in blood-based hereditarycancer testing
ja: 血液ベース遺伝性腫瘍検査における低アレル頻度バリアントの臨床的解釈
en: Clinical interpretation of low variant allele fraction variants in blood-based hereditarycancer testing
abs: Background: Low-variant allele fraction (VAF) clinically significant variants in blood-based hereditary cancer testing may suggest constitutional mosaicism, but may reflectclonal hematopoiesis, blood-restricted events, tumor contamination, or artifacts. Accurate classification is key for surveillance, counseling, and testing of relatives. Methods: We reviewed a case series of patients with suspected hereditary cancermosaicism involving TP53, CHEK2, NF1, and ATM. Variant allele fraction, age,phenotype, treatment exposure, hematologic findings, clonal hematopoiesis relevance,and available tissue results were assessed. Results: Constitutional mosaicism was supported by non-hematopoietic tissue positivityand gene-consistent phenotypes. TP53 mosaicism was favored in young patients withLi-Fraumeni syndrome-spectrum tumors and non-blood positivity. One CHEK2 caseshowed low-level detection in multiple non-blood tissues, consistent with constitutionalmosaicism and possible blood-clone expansion. In contrast, blood-only variants in olderor treated patients, especially with cytopenia or no confirmatory tissue results, favoredclonal hematopoiesis/blood-restricted events. Conclusions: Low-VAF blood variants require interpretation beyond allele fraction. Integrating tissue distribution, phenotype, treatment exposure, hematologic findings,and clonal hematopoiesis relevance, together with multi-tissue validation, helpsdistinguish constitutional mosaicism from acquired blood-restricted events and guideshereditary cancer management.

title: Proteomic patterns associated with serum urate level and dysfunctional ABCG2 urate transporter variants
ja: 血清尿酸値およびABCG2尿酸トランスポーター機能低下バリアントに関連するプロテオームパターン
en: Proteomic patterns associated with serum urate level and dysfunctional ABCG2 urate transporter variants
abs: Recent proteomic studies have focused on gout flares or symptomatic hyperuricemia, with limited investigation of circulating proteomic profiles in relation to serum urate (SU) level as a continuous trait. This study examined associations between SU level and serum proteomic profiles. We enrolled 176 Japanese individuals aged >=50 years from participants of the Kita-Nagoya Genomic Epidemiology (KING) Study and measured serum protein using Olink Explore 3072. Associations were analyzed using linear regression adjusted for age, sex, renal function and insulin resistance, with a false discovery rate of 5%. Tissue-specific and gene set enrichment analyses were performed. Among 2886 proteins, 63 were significantly associated with SU; uromodulin (UMOD) showed the strongest association (padj=2.21×10-5). These proteins were enriched in the liver, kidney and duodenum. We further examined the dysfunctional ABCG2 single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) p.Q141K. In minor allele carriers (n=91), 11 SU-associated proteins were identified, whereas none were detected in wild-type homozygotes (n=85). Gene set enrichment analysis indicated xenobiotic metabolism in wild-types and additional inflammation- and disease-related pathways in carriers. We confirmed UMOD SNP rs77924615 showed a strong association with serum UMOD levels (p<5×10-8), but no significant association with SU level was observed. This study identifies a proteomic signature of SU level and suggests that SU-associated proteomic profiles differ by ABCG2 genotypes, highlighting genetic contributions to SU-related pathophysiology.

title: Functional analyses of SHARPIN variants associated with the risk of late-onset Alzheimer's disease using genome editing
ja: ゲノム編集を用いた遅発性アルツハイマー病リスク関連SHARPINバリアントの機能解析
en: Functional analyses of SHARPIN variants associated with the risk of late-onset Alzheimer's disease using genome editing
abs: Despite the large-scale genomic cohort studies that identified many novel genetic variants associated with the risk of late-onset Alzheimer's disease (LOAD), the direct biological relevance of these variants remains unresolved. We have explored LOAD-risk genetic factors in Japanese patients and identified a rare functional SHARPIN variant, rs572750141 (p.Gly186Arg), that is associated with LOAD. Recent large-scale Caucasian GWAS meta-analyses have identified additional common SHARPIN variants associated with LOAD, suggesting SHARPIN's significant role in LOAD pathogenesis. To elucidate the role of SHARPIN variants in disease pathogenesis, we performed functional analyses using knock-in cells and mice generated through genome editing using CRISPR/Cas9. We performed the knock-in of the targeted SNV into cultured cells and obtained SHARPIN G186R homozygous cells by single-cell cloning. Using these knock-in cell lines, we found a suppressed NF-κB pathway and increased amyloid-β secretion into the culture medium. Then, we introduced the Sharpin G183R, which is equivalent to the human SHARPIN G186R, into mice and conducted behavioral analyses that revealed increased persistent behavior and anxiety toward stimuli. Furthermore, we prepared primary microglia from the knock-in mice and performed RNA-Seq analysis. We are now conducting comprehensive analyses of gene expression, pathways, and networks. The differential expression analysis has identified genes with altered expression in knock-in microglia. Further investigation may elucidate the mechanism underlying the onset of LOAD.

title: Polygenic risk analyses reveal shared genetic architecture between narcolepsy type 1 and type 2 beyond HLA-DQB1*06:02
en: Polygenic risk analyses reveal shared genetic architecture between narcolepsy type 1 and type 2 beyond HLA-DQB1*06:02
abs: Narcolepsy type 2 (NT2) is a sleep disorder characterized by excessive daytime sleepiness without cataplexy, a symptom of narcolepsy type 1 (NT1). Almost all NT1 patients carry HLA-DQB1*06:02. Although the positivity of DQB1*06:02 is higher in NT2 (30-50%) than in the general population, it remains considerably lower than in NT1. Previous studies suggest that NT2 comprises heterogeneous subgroups based on DQB1*06:02 status. However, whether NT2 shares a polygenic background with NT1, independent of HLA status, remains unclear. We performed polygenic risk score analyses (PRS) using data from a genome-wide association study of NT1 (5,339 cases and 20,518 controls). Target datasets included 275 NT2 patients, 228 idiopathic hypersomnia (IH) patients, and 1,509 controls. SNPs within the HLA region were excluded to evaluate non-HLA polygenic effects. NT1-derived PRS showed a significant association with NT2 (P = 2.0×10-11). This association remained significant in both DQB1*06:02-positive (P = 2.5×10-7) and -negative NT2 (P = 7.5×10-7) subgroups, indicating that NT2 shares a polygenic background with NT1 independent of HLA status. In contrast, only modest associations were observed between NT1-derived PRS and IH (P = 6.9×10-3). The number of sleep onset REM periods (SOREMPs) in IH patients was associated with higher NT1-derived PRS (P = 3.7×10-4). These findings support genetic continuity between NT1 and NT2 beyond the well-established HLA effect and suggest that non- HLA polygenic factors contribute to susceptibility to NT2, including in DQB1*06:02-negative individuals.

title: Longitudinal Analysis of HBV Mutations in Serum Samples Using Survival Analysis
en: Longitudinal Analysis of HBV Mutations in Serum Samples Using Survival Analysis
