abs: We previously reported that the HBV basal core promoter mutations A1762T/G1764A markedly increase the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in patients homozygous for HLA-DPB1*05:01 (OR=8.8), whereas HBV mutation alone has been associated with a lower risk (OR=4.1). These findings highlight the importance of monitoring HBV mutation emergence. We aimed to estimate HBV mutation rates using longitudinal serum samples and survival analysis. Serum samples were collected from chronic HBV patients in Japan. HBV mutation status was determined by sequencing serial serum samples. Assuming irreversible mutations and an exponential distribution of waiting time to mutation, mutation rates were estimated using maximum likelihood methods with censored observations. As of January 2025, 881 cases had been collected, and 406 had undergone mutation analysis. HBV mutations were detected in 140 cases, while 73 remained wild type throughout follow-up. Preliminary analysis of 17 patients with wild-type HBV at baseline estimated the mutation rate of A1762T/G1764A to be 8.2×10^-4 per week (approximately 4.2% per year). The exponential model was consistent with Kaplan-Meier estimates, and simulations suggested that >100 cases would provide stable estimates. No reversion from mutant to wild type or emergence of new mutations during nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy was observed. These findings demonstrate that survival analysis of longitudinal serum samples enables estimation of HBV mutation rates and may contribute to prediction of HBV-related hepatocarcinogenesis.

title: Association analysis between tryptase genotypes and food allergy in Japanese population
en: Association analysis between tryptase genotypes and food allergy in Japanese population
abs: Hereditary α-tryptasemia is an autosomal dominant trait defined by an increase in the copy number of the TPSAB1 gene coding for α or β tryptase. Several studies have demonstrated that an increase in the copy number of α tryptase-coding sequences within the TPSAB1 gene significantly elevates basal serum tryptase levels and raises the prevalence of severe anaphylaxis. Despite these findings in white populations, the relationship between TPSAB1 region CNVs and the anaphylaxis and food allergies in other racial groups, including Asians, remains under-investigated. In this study, we analyzed the TPSAB1 locus in Japanese pediatric samples and examined its association with food allergy and anaphylaxis. The considerable sequence homology between TPSAB1 and TPSB2, which exceeds 97%, makes it difficult to use conventional single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) array-based genotyping techniques. Thus, we used a stepwise genotyping strategy combining long-range PCR, deletion-specific PCR, direct sequencing, quantitative PCR, and droplet digital PCR in a subset of samples to characterize structural variation within the region. The results showed that in Japanese population, increased α-tryptase allele count was rare, whereas the TPSAB1 deletion allele was frequently observed. Furthermore, α-tryptase, β-tryptase, and deletion allele distributions were not associated with food allergy or anaphylaxis. Our findings highlight the importance of population-specific assessment of structurally complex immune-related loci.

title: Multi-ancestry genome-wide association studies elucidate spatio-cellular features of multiple sclerosis genetics
en: Multi-ancestry genome-wide association studies elucidate spatio-cellular features of multiple sclerosis genetics
abs: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic inflammatory disease of the central nervous system characterized by demyelination disseminated in space and time. Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) in European populations have identified over 200 MS susceptibility loci, but no GWAS has been conducted in East Asian populations. Moreover, recent advancements in single-cell and spatial transcriptomics technologies hold considerable promise for interpreting GWAS findings in MS, which is characterized by spatial heterogeneity, but have not been fully leveraged for this purpose. Here, we performed the first Japanese MS GWAS using 688 cases and 205,199 controls and identified an East Asian-specific risk variant in 11q24. Furthermore, through cross-population GWAS meta-analyses using a total of 29,374 cases and 1,843,563 controls from four ancestral populations, we identified 22 novel loci. To detect cell types associated with MS susceptibility, we integrated our MS GWAS and sc/snRNA-seq datasets. In PBMC scRNA-seq data, MS genetic risk was enriched in CD4+ T cells. In snRNA-seq data from MS subcortical lesions, T cells, myeloid cells, endothelial cells, and B cells showed significant enrichment. Furthermore, we integrated our MS GWAS with spatial transcriptomics of MS subcortical lesions. MS genetic risk was enriched in the "vascular infiltrating" and "lesion rim" regions, specifically in active lesions. Our study underscores the value of investigating spatio-cellular features of disease genetics across diverse populations and omics modalities.

title: S-Nitrosylation at Cys406 Drives Aberrant Androgen Receptor Condensate Formation and Transcriptional Dysfunction in SBMA
en: S-Nitrosylation at Cys406 Drives Aberrant Androgen Receptor Condensate Formation and Transcriptional Dysfunction in SBMA
abs: Spinal and bulbar muscular atrophy (SBMA) is an adult-onset, X-linked neuromuscular disorder caused by CAG repeat expansion in the androgen receptor (AR). While S-nitrosylation (SNO), a redox-dependent post-translational modification of cysteine thiols, is implicated in aging, cancer, and neurodegeneration, its role in SBMA remains unknown. Here, we identify SNO as a key regulator of AR function by modulating liquid liquid phase separation (LLPS). We focused on Cys406 in the activation function-1, a low-complexity intrinsically disordered region critical for LLPS, and generated a cysteine-to-serine substitution (C406S) in both wild-type AR and polyglutamine-expanded AR (polyQ-AR), abolishing SNO at this site. Confocal imaging revealed that C406S markedly enlarged nuclear AR condensates. Fluorescence recovery after photobleaching demonstrated reduced molecular dynamics in C406S mutants, indicating a shift toward more static condensates, with greater effects in polyQ-AR. Functionally, C406S impaired androgen-dependent transcriptional activity, resulting in decreased expression of the AR target genes TMPRSS2 and ERG and reduced MED1 recruitment to AR condensates. Our findings demonstrate that SNO at Cys406 regulates the material properties of AR condensates and transcriptional output, revealing a redox-dependent mechanism linking LLPS dysregulation to SBMA pathogenesis, and suggest that nitrosative stress may contribute to the transcriptional dysfunction observed in this disease.

title: AGG Repeat Expansion and Aggregation of BIN1 in Multiple System Atrophy
en: AGG Repeat Expansion and Aggregation of BIN1 in Multiple System Atrophy
abs: [Introduction] Multiple system atrophy (MSA) is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by autonomic failure, cerebellar ataxia, and parkinsonism. Although several MSA-associated genetic factors have been reported, the molecular pathogenesis of MSA remains incompletely understood. [Methods] Whole-genome sequencing was performed for a patient with familial MSA. The AGG repeat expansion in BIN1 was screened for 224 patients with clinically diagnosed MSA, 67 patients with pathologically confirmed MSA, and control groups including 574 blood samples and 65 brain samples from neurologically healthy individuals. [Results] Long-read sequencing identified an AGG repeat expansion in the first intron of BIN1 in the proband. Patients with MSA carried a higher frequency of repeat expansions exceeding 80 repeats in the pathological MSA group compared to the brain control group (frequency: 13.4% vs. 0%; odds ratio: infinity; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.1 to infinity; P = 0.003) and in the clinical multiple system atrophy group compared to the blood control group (frequency: 4.5% vs 2.4%; odds ratio: 1.87; 95% CI, 0.8 to 4.5; P = 0.16). Neuropathological analysis revealed BIN1-positive glial cytoplasmic inclusions more frequently in the brains of patients with repeat expansions. In immunoblot analysis, insoluble BIN1 was increased in the brains of multiple system atrophy, irrespective of repeat status. [Discussions] Our findings indicate that the AGG repeat expansion in BIN1 and BIN1 protein aggregation play an important role in the pathogenesis of multiple system atrophy.

title: Whole-genome sequencing reveals genetic risk factors associated with Amyloid-β accumulation rate
en: Whole-genome sequencing reveals genetic risk factors associated with Amyloid-β accumulation rate
abs: Amyloid-β protein (Aβ), the primary component of neuritic plaques in late-onset Alzheimer's disease (LOAD), is considered a key molecular trigger underlying its pathogenesis and progression. However, the Aβ accumulation rate varies substantially among individuals with LOAD, suggesting that individual genetic background may contribute to this variability. In this study, we aimed to identify genetic variants associated with the Aβ accumulation rate using whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data. A total of 139 cognitively normal individuals aged ≥60 (mean age 73.6±5.8 years, 52 females, mean follow-up year 3.1±2.8 years, baseline Centiloid value 15.3±23.1) were included. The Aβ accumulation rate was defined as the annual change in Centiloid values derived from longitudinal Aβ-PET scans. WGS analysis identified common variants and rare variants. Genome-wide association studies for common variants were performed using the Aβ accumulation rate as the dependent variable. Three genome-wide significant and eleven suggestive association signals were identified and further evaluated in an independent validation cohort of 20 participants. As a result, two variants, rs200006811 near AGAP6 and rs142619754 near HAO1, reached genome-wide significance. For rare variants, gene-based association analyses identified eight candidate genes comprising 17 rare variants. Among these, rs61754856 on ADAMTSL3 reached genome-wide significance in replication analysis. These findings may contribute to the development of early-stage prediction models for LOAD and support personalized prevention strategies.

title: A Study of Epilepsy Cases with GABAA Receptor Mutations: Mutations and Clinical Characteristics
en: A Study of Epilepsy Cases with GABAA Receptor Mutations: Mutations and Clinical Characteristics
abs: Purpose: GABAA receptor (GABR) mutations are known to cause a variety of epilepsy syndromes. GABR consists of five subunits (SUs) α, β, and γ, that assemble to form a central anion channel. Each SU is a four-transmembrane protein with a common structure in which the second transmembrane domain (M2) faces the center. We will examine the relationship between molecular information on GABR subunit gene mutations in epilepsy cases and epilepsy diagnosis. Methods: We selected 12 cases diagnosed with SU gene mutations in GABR from patients treated at our center and estimated the functional impact (LOF, GOF) using databases such as Clin Var. Results: The 12 cases consisted of 2 cases with GABRA1 mutations, 1 case with a GABRB2 mutation, 4 cases from 3 families with GABRB3 mutations, and 5 cases from 3 families with GABRG2 mutations. Five of the eight amino acid substitution mutations were located in the M2 region. The three extracellular domain mutations were presumed to be LOF. Three of the five M2 mutations were presumed to be LOF, one was a mixed LOF+GOF type, and one was presumed to be GOF. Two of the three LOF extracellular domain mutations followed a course of generalized epilepsy. Three of the five M2 mutations were LOF and followed a mild course with GEFS+. The one case presumed to be a GOF mutation in the M2 region followed the course of the most severe type of EIMFS. Discussion: It is possible that only mutations in the M2 region are GOF, and these may contribute to the onset of EIMFS, a severe form of early-infancy epilepsy, related with increased GABR excitability.

title: Population-specific genetic architecture underlies prevalence of NOTCH2NLC CGG repeat expansion in East Asians
en: Population-specific genetic architecture underlies prevalence of NOTCH2NLC CGG repeat expansion in East Asians
abs: Non-coding CGG repeat expansions in NOTCH2NLC cause neuronal intranuclear inclusion disease and have also been associated with a broad spectrum of neurological phenotypes including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. NOTCH2NLC-associated disorders show a distinct East Asian predominance, yet previous studies have not identified a single shared founder haplotype among expanded alleles. We sought to clarify the population-genetic background underlying this regional enrichment. To resolve haplotypes flanking the repeat locus, we analyzed long-read whole-genome sequencing data from eight NOTCH2NLC repeat expansion carriers. In parallel, publicly available whole-genome sequence data of 1,011 individuals from diverse populations were analyzed to examine the distribution of repeat-size classes and linked variants among populations. We found no evidence of a single extended founder haplotype flanking expanded NOTCH2NLC alleles, consistent with previous studies. Instead, large-normal alleles, defined as 35-43 repeat units, were observed exclusively in East Asian individuals. We further identified five single-nucleotide variants on chromosome 1 (149365556G>A, 149383714C>T, 149414210C>T, 149426030G>C, and 149428432A>G) linked to the expanded alleles in affected individuals and to large-normal alleles in the East Asian population. The frequency of these variants increased with repeat size in East Asians, but not in Europeans. Our findings suggest that susceptibility to NOTCH2NLC CGG repeat expansion arises from a population-specific genetic background rather than from a single founder allele.

title: Genetic stratification of Parkinson's disease by NOTCH2NLC and LRP12 repeat expansions.
en: Genetic stratification of Parkinson's disease by NOTCH2NLC and LRP12 repeat expansions.
abs: Parkinson disease (PD) is a complex genetic disorder with multiple variants, yet conventional genome-wide approaches can explain its heritability insufficiently. In neurodegenerative diseases, the importance of tandem repeat expansions and structural variants has been demonstrated in several disorders, exemplified by the GGGGCC repeat expansion in C9orf72 in ALS. In PD, tandem repeat expansions such as the ATXN2 CAG repeat and structural variants in SNCA have been recognized; however, the contribution of tandem repeat expansions and structural variants to PD pathogenesis has not been systematically investigated. Recent advances in long-read sequencing have expanded the spectrum of analyzable genetic variation, including tandem repeat expansions and structural variants. Noncoding CGG repeat expansions in oculopharyngodistal myopathy (OPDM)-related genes LRP12, GIPC1, and NOTCH2NLC have been implicated in some disorders, but the role of these expansions in PD has been poorly explored. In this study, we screened 1,011 Japanese patients with PD using repeat-primed PCR and GC-rich PCR targeting these three genes and identified 23 individuals suspected of harboring intermediate or larger repeat expansions. Long-read sequencing provided a powerful approach for resolving the detailed structures of these repeat expansions and evaluating their pathogenic relevance to PD. These findings highlight the contribution of LRP12 and NOTCH2NLC repeat expansions to the genetic architecture of PD and suggest the utility of long-read sequencing for molecular stratification and precision medicine.

title: MMR Loss Patterns and Lynch Syndrome Detection in Young Japanese Endometrial Cancer: A Prospective Study
en: MMR Loss Patterns and Lynch Syndrome Detection in Young Japanese Endometrial Cancer: A Prospective Study
abs: Background: Universal tumor testing for mismatch repair (MMR) deficiency is recommended for Lynch syndrome (LS) detection. However, prospective data in young Asian patients remain limited, and the implications of specific MMR loss patterns are not fully defined. Methods: This prospective observational study included patients aged under 50 years with endometrial cancer (EC) at a single Japanese institution (2021-2024). Immunohistochemistry for MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, and PMS2 was performed. Clinicopathologic features, MMR loss patterns, and germline testing results were analyzed. Results: Among 111 patients, 26 (23.4%) exhibited dMMR. Loss patterns included MLH1/PMS2 (n=12), MSH2/MSH6 (n=8), and isolated MSH6 loss (n=6). Germline testing was performed in 12 patients, identifying LS in 9 (75%). Detection rates appeared to vary across patterns: MSH2/MSH6 loss (4/4), isolated MSH6 loss (2/3), and MLH1/PMS2 loss (3/5). dMMR tumors were more likely to present with advanced stage and higher-grade histology. MLH1/PMS2 loss accounted for nearly half of dMMR cases. Conclusions: In young Japanese patients with EC, dMMR frequency was comparable to that in unselected populations. Germline testing yield appeared to differ across MMR loss patterns, with high detection rates in MSH2/MSH6 loss and non-negligible rates in MLH1/PMS2 loss. LS was identified across patterns, including MLH1/PMS2 loss. In young patients, such cases should not be assumed to represent sporadic methylation, supporting the importance of MMR IHC-guided genetic evaluation.

title: Sustainable HBOC surveillance: survey of current challenges and implementation of a surveillance program
en: Sustainable HBOC surveillance: survey of current challenges and implementation of a surveillance program
abs: Purpose: Sustainable surveillance for hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome (HBOC) remains an important issue in genetic medicine. This study aimed to clarify challenges in HBOC surveillance in Japan. Methods: 1) A web-based questionnaire survey was conducted among participants of a public seminar held at Keio University Hospital in 2024, including HBOC carriers, healthcare professionals, and the general public. The survey assessed surveillance practices, financial burden, and barriers to sustainable surveillance. 2) Based on the survey findings, our institution introduced a surveillance program for unaffected HBOC carriers. Results: 1) Responses were obtained from 121 of 274 participants. Among 66 HBOC carriers, 57 were affected. Surveillance uptake among affected carriers was 89.5%, although nearly half attended multiple institutions. Across respondent groups, annual out-of-pocket costs below 50,000 yen were considered acceptable. Healthcare professionals identified interfacility collaboration and shortages of genetic medicine specialists as major barriers. 2) Twenty-five unaffected HBOC carriers participated in the surveillance program, accounting for 48 visits. All participants continued surveillance, and two subsequently underwent risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy. Conclusion: Sustainable HBOC surveillance in Japan may require improved care coordination, reduced financial burden, and expansion of the genetic medicine workforce. Structured surveillance programs may support long-term adherence and may also become important in the management of secondary findings.

title: Multi-locus Inherited Neoplasia Allele Syndrome (MINAS): Clinical Characteristics of Nine Individuals
en: Multi-locus Inherited Neoplasia Allele Syndrome (MINAS): Clinical Characteristics of Nine Individuals
abs: Background: With the increasing use of multigene panel testing (MGPT) and comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP), multi-locus inherited neoplasia allele syndrome (MINAS), characterized by germline pathogenic variants (GPVs) in multiple cancer predisposition genes, is increasingly identified. However, its clinical characteristics remain incompletely characterized. We report nine individuals with MINAS identified at our institution. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed the medical records of nine individuals with MINAS identified through germline genetic testing at our institution. Results: The identified gene combinations included ATM/SDHA, BRCA1/ATR, BRCA1/BRCA2, BRCA1/BRIP1, BRCA2/ATM, BRCA2/BARD1, BRCA2/BRIP1, MSH2/BRIP1 and MSH6/RAD51D. Among the nine individuals, seven had breast cancer (unilateral, n=4; synchronous bilateral, n=2; metachronous bilateral, n=1), one had endometrial cancer, and one had multiple cutaneous cancers. The median age at initial cancer diagnosis was 49 (range, 28-68). Six were identified by MGPT, two by CGP, and one by BRACAnalysis. Discussion: Eight of the nine individuals may not have been identified as MINAS without MGPT or CGP, highlighting the risk of missing a second GPV through through syndrome-specific genetic testing. Most combinations involved high- and moderate-risk genes, consistent with previous reports. Clinical management of MINAS requires individualized risk assessment based on the penetrance and cancer risks of each involved gene. Although limited by a small sample size, further accumulation of clinical data is warranted.

title: Clinical Characteristics of Patients with Endometrial Cancer Associated with Lynch Syndrome at Our Hospital
en: Clinical Characteristics of Patients with Endometrial Cancer Associated with Lynch Syndrome at Our Hospital
abs: Background/Objective: Endometrial cancer (EC) occurs in 21-57% of women with Lynch syndrome (LS), with less than 1% reportedly developing EC before age 40. However, in Japan, LS cases of EC onset before age 40 have been occasionally observed. This study aimed to clarify the clinical characteristics of LS-related EC and provide foundational data on EC development in Japanese patients with LS. Methods: Among patients diagnosed with LS by genetic testing (GT) at our institution between January 2000 and May 2026, we analyzed EC frequency, age at onset, multiple primary cancers, and gene-specific characteristics. Results: Of 220 patients suspected of LS following EC diagnosis who underwent GT, 138 (62.7%) were confirmed as LS. Among the 237 women with LS, EC frequency by gene was as follows: MLH1: 41/73 (56.2%), MSH2: 80/120 (66.7%), MSH6: 20/35 (57.1%), and PMS2: 1/9 (11.1%) (MSH2 vs. PMS2: p=0.0016). Median age at EC onset was MLH1: 47.0, MSH2: 45.0, and MSH6: 48.5 years (p=0.0313). Among patients with LS who developed cancer, the 1st primary cancer type was EC in MLH1: 43.8%, MSH2: 54.2%, MSH6: 63.0%, and PMS2: 16.6% (p=0.1063). EC onset before age 40 occurred in MLH1: 8.2%, MSH2: 20.0%, MSH6: 8.6%, and PMS2: 11.1% of LS women (p=0.0986). Discussion: In our cohort, especially MSH6 carriers developed EC before age 40, exceeding previously reported rates. Limitations include its single-center design and potential selection bias, as early onset prompted GT. Nonetheless, this finding may serve as informative foundational data for optimizing surveillance timing in Japanese female LS.

title: Comprehensive genomic profiling reveals a higher prevalence of Li-Fraumeni syndrome than previously estimated
en: Comprehensive genomic profiling reveals a higher prevalence of Li-Fraumeni syndrome than previously estimated
abs: Background: Li-Fraumeni syndrome (LFS), caused by germline TP53 alterations, often remains undiagnosed due to the lack of public insurance coverage for dedicated genetic testing in Japan. We investigated LFS prevalence using comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP). Methods and Results: Among 912 patients who underwent CGP at our hospital, three were diagnosed with LFS. Case 1: A teenage female with recurrent glioblastoma. CGP identified a germline TP53 pathogenic variant with a variant allele frequency (VAF) of 29%. Despite a low VAF suggesting mosaicism, multi-site testing confirmed a non-mosaic constitutional variant, likely skewed by sequencing artifacts of CGP. Case 2: A female in her 60s with unresectable pancreatic cancer and a history of triple primary malignancies including early-onset sarcoma. A TP53 loss-of-function variant with a VAF of 49% was omitted from the standard CGP report but confirmed via subsequent germline testing. Case 3: A teenage female presented with glioblastoma. Both her mother and a sibling had been diagnosed with LFS at another hospital. CGP was utilized for both therapeutic target screening and definitive genetic confirmation. Conclusion: The LFS prevalence in our cohort was 0.3%. It is markedly higher than the historical estimate of 0.005-0.02%. When interpreting CGP results, clinicians must remain vigilant for low VAFs or variants excluded from standard reporting criteria to avoid overlooking LFS.

title: Integrated genomic analysis reveals HBOC in patients with inconclusive BRCA test results
en: Integrated genomic analysis reveals HBOC in patients with inconclusive BRCA test results
abs: Background: Standard germline BRCA testing occasionally yields inconclusive results, preventing diagnosis of hereditary breast and ovarian cancer (HBOC). Cryptic germline alterations such as structural variants, mosaic events, and intronic retrotransposon insertions may escape detection by conventional assays. We evaluated the diagnostic utility of integrated genomic analyses in patients with inconclusive BRCA test results. Methods: Three patients with HBOC-associated malignancies and inconclusive germline BRCA1/2 test results underwent whole-genome sequencing (WGS), Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing, direct RNA sequencing, and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH). Results: Case 1 was a patient with prostate cancer diagnosed at age 67. WGS identified a germline mosaic translocation involving chromosomes 13 and 3, accompanied by a deletion encompassing BRCA2. FISH confirmed mosaic BRCA2 deletion in peripheral blood. Cases 2 and 3 were patients with breast cancer diagnosed at ages 31 and 26 years, respectively. Long-read sequencing identified a 2.7-kb SVA_E retrotransposon insertion within intronic regions of BRCA1 and BRCA2. Direct RNA sequencing demonstrated loss of BRCA1/BRCA2 function at the transcript level. All three patients were ultimately diagnosed with HBOC. Conclusions: Clinically significant pathogenic variants may underlie inconclusive BRCA test results. Integrated genomic approaches combining WGS, long-read sequencing, and RNA sequencing can improve the diagnostic yield of hereditary cancer testing and support appropriate clinical management.

title: A case report of hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis with transthyretin p.Thr80Ala in Japanese family
en: A case report of hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis with transthyretin p.Thr80Ala in Japanese family
abs: Hereditary transthyretion amyloidosis (ATTRv) is characterized by various symptoms including cardiomyopathy, polyneuropathy and other organs disorders. We experienced a case of ATTRv with transthyretin genotype of c.238A>G (p.Thr80Ala). A 65-year-old man was referred to our hospital because of edema of lower extremities and dyspnea on exertion. His mother died of congestive heart failure due to ATTRv with same genotype at the age of 72. His older sister has been followed as cardiomyopathy for 20 years and genetic test lately revealed ATTRv with p.Thr80Ala. Echocardiography showed ejection fraction of 19%. He was diagnosed as severe congestive heart failure of at least NYHA III and admitted. Endomyocardial biopsy using Congo red staining showed the deposition of amyloid fibrils. 99mTc-pyrophosphate scintigraphy showed uptake in heart. He also has noticed hand and foot paresthesia. He was found to be a carrier of the p.Thr80Ala pathological variant. He was diagnosed with ATTRv. He has underwent the treatment of Vutrisiran, an RNA interference therapeutic that reduces TTR production. When six months elapsed after Vutrisiran administration start, echocardiography showed ejection fraction of 38%. In the Irish population, ATTRv with p.Thr80Ala has been recognized as the most common. Meanwhile, in the Japanese population, there is only one case report, that was his mother's report, as far as we investigated. The genotype manifests both cardiac and neurological phenotypes.

title: Varporter-based AI system for pathogenicity assessment of germline variants by comprehensive genomic profiling in cancer
en: Varporter-based AI system for pathogenicity assessment of germline variants by comprehensive genomic profiling in cancer
abs: Comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) testing is increasingly essential for cancer care, making the appropriate evaluation of germline variants as secondary findings ever more important. We previously reported "Varporter," a CGP support software (https:// web.sapmed.ac.jp/canmol/varporter.html) that consolidates multi-panel results into Excel, extracts germline variant candidates (PGPVs and GPVs) based on the Secondary Findings disclosure list, and incorporates ACMG classifications from GeneBe, ClinVar pathogenicity, gnomAD/ToMMo allele frequencies, and functional prediction scores via auto-generated database links. Building on this, we developed an AI chatbot integrated with Varporter for assessing germline pathogenicity. Static information is retrieved from a pre-built RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) model. In contrast, frequently updated resources, including ClinVar, gnomAD, guidelines, therapeutic evidence, and clinical trial information, are queried via web search APIs, limiting the AI's role to information synthesis and suppressing hallucinations. This enables AI-assisted ACMG classification referencing gene-specific ClinGen guidelines, with dedicated support for TP53 (ClinGen TP53 guidelines v2.1) and BRCA1/BRCA2 (ClinGen ENIGMA criteria). The chatbot also performs automatic liftover between GRCh37 and GRCh38 and HGVS normalization from free-text input, addressing key technical challenges in multi-panel CGP. This system is expected to improve the quality and efficiency of germline variant assessment in CGP.

title: A novel de novo RBBP5 variant impairs KMT2D-SET binding and clusters within the Kabuki syndrome episignature
en: A novel de novo RBBP5 variant impairs KMT2D-SET binding and clusters within the Kabuki syndrome episignature
abs: Kabuki syndrome (KS) is characterized by multiple congenital anomalies and distinctive dysmorphic features caused by loss-of-function variants in KMT2D or KDM6A. We identified a novel de novo RBBP5 variant in a patient with KS-like phenotypes and mild intellectual disability by trio exome sequencing. No pathogenic variants were identified in KMT2D or KDM6A by whole-gene sequencing. Genome-wide DNA methylation analysis of peripheral blood demonstrated an episignature highly similar to that of KS. RBBP5 is a component of the MLL/COMPASS histone methyltransferase complex together with KMT2D and ASH2L, and it directly binds to the SET domain of KMT2D. To evaluate the functional impact of the identified variant on MLL/COMPASS complex formation, co-immunoprecipitation assays were performed using the KMT2D SET domain and ASH2L. The assays demonstrated that the variant selectively impaired binding to the KMT2D SET domain, whereas interaction with ASH2L was preserved. These findings indicate that the novel RBBP5 variant disrupts SET domain binding within the KMT2D/ASH2L/RBBP5 complex. Previously reported RBBP5 variants, including p.T232I and p.E296D, are thought to impair nucleosome binding while preserving the complex's intrinsic catalytic activity. In contrast, the novel RBBP5 variant affects a residue critical for interaction with the KMT2D SET domain. This defect is expected to impair KMT2D-dependent histone methyltransferase function, providing a possible mechanistic explanation for the KS-like phenotype observed in this case.

title: Initiation of a prospective study on clinical management of Fabry disease identified through newborn screening
en: Initiation of a prospective study on clinical management of Fabry disease identified through newborn screening
abs: Recently, spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID) and lysosomal storage disease were added to newborn screening test (NBS). Until Jan. 31, 2026, totally 33,870 newborn babies were tested in Miyazaki Prefecture. Among them, 10 cases (7 male and 3 female) were positive in screening and verified with genetic testing. Incidence of the Fabry disease was higher than expected (One to 3081case). And, interestingly, 7 cases had same variant (GLA M296I) suggesting founder effect. This variant classified as late onset type, in other words, clinical symptom suspects to appear 20 to 30 years later. Therefore, not only strict follow up of newborn but also investigation of the family member is very important. In this situation, we started clinical trial. In this trial not only pediatricians but cardiologists, nephrologists, neurologists, obstetrician, doctor of emergency center, geneticist and genetic counselor joined the meeting. We shared information of each family in periodical meeting. We found 2cases of grandfather have a renal and heart failure with unknown etiology. Genetic testing verified M296I variant, then, started enzyme replacement therapy. In conclusion, newborn screening test of Fabry disease is effective for identification and treatment of the family member. However, strict follow up of the identified baby and translation from pediatrician to cardiologist, nephrologist and neurologist seems to be essential procedure. In addition, genetic counseling to the mother also important to understanding importance of follow up.

title: Genomic Re-evaluation of an Xp11.3 Deletion in a Man Reveals a Contiguous Gene Deletion Syndrome Involving KDM6A and RP2
en: Genomic Re-evaluation of an Xp11.3 Deletion in a Man Reveals a Contiguous Gene Deletion Syndrome Involving KDM6A and RP2
abs: Background Chromosomal microdeletions involving Xp11.3 are associated heterogeneous clinical phenotypes depending on the genes included. Haploinsufficiency of KDM6A causes Kabuki syndrome type 2 (KS2), whereas contiguous gene deletions may result in more complex phenotypes. We report a man whose genetic etiology was redefined through re-evaluation of genomic copy number variations (CNVs). Case Presentation The patient was a 22-year-old man with severe intellectual disability, intractable epilepsy, and retinitis pigmentosa. Although an Xp11.3 deletion had been identified by a BAC-based microarray analysis during childhood, detailed molecular characterizations were unavailable. A CGH+SNP-based microarray analysis revealed a 2.4 Mb hemizygous deletion encompassing KDM6A, RP2, and SLC9A7. Based on these findings, the patient was diagnosed with KS2. The retinal phenotype was consistent with RP2-associated retinal degeneration. Previous studies have suggested that male patients with pathogenic KDM6A variants exhibit more severe manifestations than females. Although SLC9A7 has been implicated in X-linked neurodevelopmental disorders, the contribution of SLC9A7 haploinsufficiency remains uncertain. Conclusion This case expands the clinical spectrum of Xp11.3 contiguous gene deletion involving KDM6A and RP2. Genomic re-evaluation established a molecular diagnosis and improved access to medical support programs. These findings highlight the importance of genomic re-evaluation and careful interpretation of contiguous gene effects in chromosomal microdeletion syndromes.

title: Common features and differences among three cases of myotonic dystrophy first suspected during pregnancy
en: Common features and differences among three cases of myotonic dystrophy first suspected during pregnancy
abs: Background Myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1) is an autosomal dominant disorder caused by CTG repeat expansion in the DMPKgene and characterized by anticipation. DM1 may first be suspected during pregnancy based on abnormal blood test findings or fetal ultrasound findings, although pregnant women may have no subjective symptoms or apparent family history. Cases We experienced three cases in which DM1 was first suspected during pregnancy. Common features were pregnancy through in vitro fertilization, elevated maternal serum creatine kinase levels leading to suspicion of DM1, and polyhydramnios. In contrast, reactions to the suspected diagnosis varied among the cases, including difficulty accepting the diagnosis by both partners, limited understanding by the patient and difficulty accepting the diagnosis by the husband, and good acceptance by both partners. Accordingly, the timing and target of genetic testing also varied, including postnatal testing of both mother and neonate, postnatal maternal testing alone, and maternal testing during pregnancy. Discussion Advances in reproductive medicine would increase pregnancies among previously undiagnosed patients with hereditary disorders, and such cases would increase in the future. Although perinatal care requires maternal treatment, fetal evaluation, and management decisions under time constraints, responses to diagnosis acceptance and decision-making differed among the cases.

title: A candidate biomarker for ML: reduced urinary heparan sulfate after unrelated cord blood transplantation
en: A candidate biomarker for ML: reduced urinary heparan sulfate after unrelated cord blood transplantation
abs: Mucolipidosis (ML) is an ultra-rare lysosomal storage disorder caused by pathogenic variants in GNPTAB or GNPTG, encoding subunits of GlcNAc-1-phosphotransferase. There is no established treatment response monitoring biomarker in ML, and we present heparan sulfate (HS) as a candidate biomarker based on a case with ML III α/β, whose clinical condition stabilized and urinary HS levels markedly decreased following unrelated cord blood transplantation (UCBT). The patient presented at age 3 with mitral regurgitation, growth delay, and dysostosis multiplex. Compound heterozygous GNPTAB variants were identified, and she was diagnosed with ML. She underwent UCBT at age 5. Neutrophil engraftment occurred on day 16, with stable donor chimerism (>95%). At 2 years post-UCBT, cardiac and respiratory function remained stable, and joint range of motion improved slightly. Cognitive development was maintained (WISC-V FSIQ: 101; pre-transplant KSPD DQ: 90). Urinary HS as a proportion of total glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) decreased from 46% to 13%, paralleling clinical improvement. Ammer et al. suggested that therapy for ML, through mechanisms such as cross-correction, decreases urinary GAGs. Blood, urine, and CSF HS are established biomarkers in mucopolysaccharidosis. Although several studies have reported elevated blood and urinary HS levels in ML, a reduction in urinary HS following therapies such as UCBT has not been previously described. Our findings suggest that HS may represent a candidate biomarker in ML.

title: Non-coding spliceosomal defects in mitochondrial disease: evidence from RNU4-2 andRNU4ATAC
en: Non-coding spliceosomal defects in mitochondrial disease: evidence from RNU4-2 andRNU4ATAC
abs: Background: Mitochondrial diseases are characterized by impaired energy production and often remain genetically unresolved despite advances in next-generation sequencing. Focusing on non-coding regions, we identified two patients with the same de novo RNU4-2 variant, implicating spliceosome dysfunction in mitochondrial disease. Aim: To investigate the relationship between spliceosomal dysfunction and mitochondrial disease, focusing on the impact of RNU4ATAC variants on mitochondrial-related splicing abnormalities and mitochondrial function. Method: Patient-derived fibroblasts harboring the RNU4-2 variant were analyzed by RNA sequencing to detect aberrant splicing events. Whole genome sequencing re-analysis also identified a patient with compound heterozygous pathogenic/ likely pathogenic variants in RNU4ATAC. Results: RNA sequencing revealed clear aberrant splicing of NDUFV1, a nuclear-encoded component of mitochondrial respiratory chain complex I, in RNU4-2 variant fibroblasts, despite no pathogenic variants in NDUFV1 itself. In addition, we identified a patient with compound heterozygous pathogenic RNU4ATAC variants previously reported in ClinVar. The patient presented with short stature, diabetes mellitus, and intellectual disability. Conclusion: Abnormalities involving RNU4-2 and RNU4ATAC may represent an underrecognized mechanism, which is likely aberrant splicing, contributing to mitochondrial disease. Our findings highlight the importance of reanalyzing non-coding spliceosomal genes in genetically unresolved mitochondrial disease cases.

title: Clinical Spectrum and Liver Transplant Outcomes of DGUOK-Related MTDPS in Japan: Comparison With an International Cohort
en: Clinical Spectrum and Liver Transplant Outcomes of DGUOK-Related MTDPS in Japan: Comparison With an International Cohort
abs: Background: DGUOK-related mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome (MTDPS) is a rare, fatal disorder causing early-onset liver disease. Although an international cohort of 202 patients clarified its natural history, Japanese data remain limited. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed genetically confirmed DGUOK-related cases in the Japanese mitochondrial disease database. Clinical features, hepatic and extrahepatic involvement, liver transplantation, and prognosis were compared with the international cohort. Results: Thirteen Japanese patients were identified. Most presented in the neonatal or infantile period, and 8 of 13 developed severe liver disease, including acute liver failure. This spectrum was consistent with the international cohort, in which neonatal and infantile onset accounted for 55.7% and 32.3% of cases, and hepatocerebral disease was the most common phenotype. Liver disease was the main determinant of morbidity and mortality in both cohorts. Two Japanese patients with neurological manifestations underwent liver transplantation, but both had unfavorable outcomes, suggesting that neurological involvement may worsen post-transplant prognosis. Conclusions: Japanese patients with DGUOK-related disease show a clinical spectrum similar to that reported internationally, dominated by early-onset liver disease. DGUOK deficiency should be considered in neonates and infants with cholestasis, progressive liver dysfunction, or acute liver failure. Early molecular diagnosis and assessment of extrahepatic involvement are essential for prognosis and transplant decisions.

title: Genetic counseling and reproductive options for mitochondrial diseases: a retrospective review of 24 families.
en: Genetic counseling and reproductive options for mitochondrial diseases: a retrospective review of 24 families.
abs: Background: Mitochondrial diseases are clinically and genetically heterogeneous. Genetic counseling regarding recurrence risk and reproductive options including prenatal diagnosis (PND) and preimplantation genetic testing for monogenic disorders (PGT-M) requires substantial expertise. We evaluated the clinical and genetic background, and counseling outcomes of families seeking reproductive medicine. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 24 families with mitochondrial disease who underwent PND or PGT-M at our hospital. Results: Among 18 families with nuclear DNA defects, which were generally severe and inherited in an autosomal recessive or X-linked manner, PND (n=14) and PGT-M (n=6) were feasible options depending on clinical severity and familial preference. For 6 families with mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) defects, PND (n=4) was viable when maternal blood and urine were negative for the variant, suggesting a de novo mutation; no variant was identified in fetuses tested by chorionic villus sampling or amniocentesis. In contrast, when mothers carried the same mtDNA variant (n=2), PND was difficult to interpret due to obligatory transmission and limited phenotype predictability, whereas PGT-M remained a potential option for selected variants. Conclusions: Reproductive options for mitochondrial disease differ according to whether the causative defect is located in nuclear DNA or mtDNA and, in mtDNA disease, whether the variant is de novo or maternally inherited. Precise molecular diagnosis and individualized genetic counseling are essential for informed reproductive decision-making.

title: Antisense oligonucleotide-mediated skipping of an 84-bp pseudoexon restores PCC activity in propionic acidemia
en: Antisense oligonucleotide-mediated skipping of an 84-bp pseudoexon restores PCC activity in propionic acidemia
abs: Background: Propionic acidemia (PA) is a severe inherited metabolic disorder caused by pathogenic variants in PCCA or PCCB, resulting in propionyl-CoA carboxylase (PCC) deficiency. Current treatment is mainly supportive, and novel treatment strategies are needed. In an individual with neonatal-onset PA, we identified a homozygous deep-intronic variant of PCCA causing inclusion of an 84-bp pseudoexon. We evaluated antisense oligonucleotide (ASO)-mediated skipping of the 84-bp pseudoexon as a potential treatment strategy for PA. Methods: ASOs targeting the 84-bp pseudoexon were transfected into fibroblasts from the affected individual. We evaluated splicing, transcripts, PCCA protein, and PCC activity. Fibroblasts harboring other mutations were also analyzed. Results: In fibroblasts from the individual, the 84-bp pseudoexon was included in the majority of PCCA transcripts. PCCA protein was undetectable, and PCC activity was markedly reduced to 0.5% of wild-type (WT). ASO treatment restored normal splicing to 98.9% of transcripts (p<0.001), increased PCCA protein expression, and improved PCC activity to approximately 300% of WT (p<0.001). In fibroblasts carrying other mutations retaining >1% of WT PCC activity, ASO treatment also increased PCC enzyme activity. Conclusion: ASO-mediated correction of the 84-bp pseudoexon represents a viable molecular therapeutic approach for PA caused by the deep-intronic PCCA variant and may have broader applicability. Further in vivo studies are required to validate the efficacy and generalizability of ASO-mediated pseudoexon skipping.

title: A Founder Tandem Duplication at the APOC4-APOC2 Locus in Severe Hypertriglyceridemia with Markedly Reduced apoC-II
en: A Founder Tandem Duplication at the APOC4-APOC2 Locus in Severe Hypertriglyceridemia with Markedly Reduced apoC-II
abs: Introduction: Apolipoprotein C-II (apoC-II) is a cofactor of lipoprotein lipase, and apoC-II deficiency, mostly caused by APOC2 coding-region mutations, leads to severe hypertriglyceridemia (HTG). In several atypical cases, mutations in the promoter region or a splice site of APOC2 cause markedly reduced but detectable plasma apoC-II with massive HTG (hereafter referred to as hypoapoC-II). We previously reported a case of hypoapoC-II with severe HTG (Case 1) in which no rare APOC2 coding variant was identified; however, the clinical entity remains controversial as evidence of causality is weak. Methods: Case 1 and an additional case (Case 2) of hypoapoC-II were analyzed by whole genome/exome sequencing, Southern blot hybridization (APOC2 or APOC4 cDNA probes), breakpoint analysis (PCR, subcloning, and direct sequencing), custom-made array CGH around the APOE/APOC4/APOC2 gene cluster, and microarray-based haplotype analysis. Results: Whole genome sequencing of Case 1 revealed a two-fold increase in coverage spanning APOC4 and the noncoding exon of APOC2. Array CGH, Southern blot, and breakpoint analyses confirmed a homozygous tandem duplication. Case 2 harbored the same tandem duplication as Case 1. Although apparently unrelated, Cases 1 and 2 shared a founder haplotype. Conclusions: We found two independent cases of hypoapoC-II harboring the same founder tandem duplication containing APOC4 and a noncoding exon of APOC2, representing a distinct clinical subtype of hyperchylomicronemia with markedly reduced apoC-II.

title: A case of germline pathogenic variant in EGFR identified through comprehensive genomic profiling in lung cancer
en: A case of germline pathogenic variant in EGFR identified through comprehensive genomic profiling in lung cancer
abs: In CGP, EGFR variants in lung cancer are usually interpreted as therapeutic biomarkers, but some may indicate germline pathogenic variants (GPV). We report a 50-year-old man with disseminated lung adenocarcinoma. His father and sister had lung cancer at 65 and 54 years, respectively. Initial OncomineDx testing detected the activating EGFR driver p.G719S, and afatinib provided disease control for 3 years. At progression, repeat OncomineDx testing did not detect resistance-associated EGFR p.T790M. After another 3 years of chemotherapy, liver metastasis developed; FoundationOne CDx on this biopsy newly revealed EGFR c.2327G>A (p.R776H; VAF 0.488), outside OncomineDx coverage, together with p.G719S. Based on VAF and family history, p.R776H was suspected to be germline and confirmed by germline testing. In our 247-case institutional lung cancer series, 60 EGFR variants were detected in 42 cases. Among reported EGFR GPV, p.V843I and p.P848L were not detected, and p.T790M was detected in 7 cases but was not considered suggestive of germline origin based on VAF, co-occurring EGFR variants, and clinical context. EGFR p.R776H was first observed in this case and co-occurred with p.G719S. This case highlights the need to distinguish potential EGFR GPV from co-occurring therapeutic drivers and to link selected patients to germline testing and counseling.

title: Bioinformatics analysis of lung cancer using TCGA data set for the insight of impaired tumor immune microenvironment
en: Bioinformatics analysis of lung cancer using TCGA data set for the insight of impaired tumor immune microenvironment
abs: Lung cancer is an immunogenic cancer for which immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) work. However, current biomarkers cannot perfectly predict ICI response. Analysis of the tumor microenvironment (TME) is important to predict and improve the outcome. We performed bioinformatic analysis of TCGA data to identify key molecules distinguishing hot from cold TMEs. Chemokines and their receptors whose mRNA levels were strongly associated with CD8A were identified in lung adenocarcinoma (Ad). In particular, CXCL9/10/11 and their receptor CXCR3, which are essential for ICI response, as well as XCL1/2, which recruit cDC1, were highly correlated with CD8A in Ad. EGFR-mutated (EGFRmt) Ad represents a cold TME characterized by exclusion of CD8+ T cells. We demonstrated that CXCL9/10/11 are epigenetically suppressed through induction of HDACs under oncogenic EGFR signaling. We also focused on tissue-resident memory T cells (Trm) that are specialized T cells adapted for long-term residence within tissues. A high frequency of Trm cells, which are considered terminally differentiated precursor exhausted T cells (Tpex), a presumed target of anti-PD-1 Ab, correlates with favorable prognosis in lung cancer. TCGA data revealed that ITGAE (CD103), a marker of Trm cells, and Trm-associated effector molecules including GZMH, GZMA, and GZMB were significantly decreased in EGFRmt Ad. We confirmed a significant reduction of CD103+ cells in EGFRmt Ad tissues. These findings suggest that analysis of public databases can provide important insights into mechanisms underlying impaired antitumor immunity.

title: Hereditary multiple lung adenocarcinomas in identical twins with germline PCLO variant
en: Hereditary multiple lung adenocarcinomas in identical twins with germline PCLO variant
abs: Multiple primary lung adenocarcinomas are often associated with somatic driver alterations in such as EGFR, HER2 or MET. However, the contribution of germline variants to lung cancer susceptibility remains poorly understood. Here, we report monozygotic twin sisters harboring multiple lung adenocarcinomas in a family with an apparent aggregation of lung cancer. In the proband, three tumors harbored independent EGFR L858R mutations, whereas her co-twin developed distinct tumors carrying MET exon 14 skipping or no detectable driver mutation. Whole-exome sequencing identified a shared heterozygous germline variant in PCLO encoding the presynaptic cytomatrix protein Piccolo. PCLO mutations near the variant detected in this pedigree have been reported in EGFR- or KRAS-mutant lung cancer cell lines PC-9, HCC2279 and DFCI024, suggesting its role in oncogenesis. Our findings indicate that a germline PCLO variant may predispose to multiple lung adenocarcinomas by enhancing susceptibility especially to EGFR/MET-driven tumorigenesis in genetically identical individuals.

title: Evaluating the impact of epidemiologic factors on cancer risk and diagnosis age across eight hereditary cancer genes
en: Evaluating the impact of epidemiologic factors on cancer risk and diagnosis age across eight hereditary cancer genes
abs: The risk variability of hereditary cancer remains poorly characterized, limiting personalized clinical management. Given the importance of verifying the impact of epidemiologic factors in carriers of hereditary cancer genes, we assessed their effects on cancer risk and age at diagnosis. We used our previously reported data on 8 hereditary cancer genes (BRCA1, BRCA2, CHEK2, MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PTEN, and TP53) across 12 significantly associated cancer types from BioBank Japan. Epidemiologic factors included smoking, alcohol consumption, family history, age at menarche/menopause, and cancer-specific polygenic risk scores. Parallel analyses in noncarriers were conducted as references. Statistical significance was set at q<0.05 after Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction. In 59,503 cases and 38,212 controls, we found that family history of gastric cancer was significantly associated with the same cancer risk in BRCA2 carriers (OR 4.9, q=2.9x10-3), with a descriptively higher OR than in non-carriers (OR 2.2, q=2.9x10-206). Notably, for breast (BRCA1, BRCA2) and ovarian cancer (BRCA2), age at menarche =<12 years was significantly associated with a younger mean age at diagnosis, with differences ranging from 8.1 to 12.5 years, despite having no significant impact on these cancer risks. In summary, our findings suggested that some epidemiologic factors impact disease risk with a different magnitude in carriers compared to non-carriers. Furthermore, they implied the importance of independently evaluating cancer risk and onset age, supporting surveillance and risk-reduction strategies.

title: Subsite-specific analysis of biliary tract cancer using genome-wide and gene-based analysis in Japanese subjects
en: Subsite-specific analysis of biliary tract cancer using genome-wide and gene-based analysis in Japanese subjects
abs: Biliary tract cancer (BTC) is a highly lethal malignancy with poor prognosis due to challenges in early detection. Both environmental and genetic factors are considered to contribute to its development. To identify genetic variants associated with BTC and its anatomical subsites, we conducted a genome-wide association study (GWAS) and gene-based analysis in a Japanese population. The GWAS included 529 BTC cases and 4,454 apparently healthy controls. Cases were further classified into four subsites: gallbladder cancer, intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, and ampullary cancer. GWAS were performed for overall BTC as well as for each subsite separately. Subsequently, gene-based analyses were conducted using MAGMA based on the GWAS summary statistics. Although no single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) reached genome-wide significance, subsite-specific analyses identified X, Y, and Z as statistically significant genes in gallbladder cancer. These genes were located in close proximity to one another. Previous studies in European populations have reported associations between these genes and gallstone disease, a known risk factor for gallbladder cancer. Our findings suggest that this genomic region may contribute to susceptibility to both gallstone disease and gallbladder cancer in the Japanese population. Further validation studies in independent cohorts are warranted.

title: Multiple HPVs are Common in Cervical Cancer Cytological Specimens with HPV16 with a High Incidence Rate
en: Multiple HPVs are Common in Cervical Cancer Cytological Specimens with HPV16 with a High Incidence Rate
abs: Human papillomavirus (HPV) causes cervical cancers. HPV is epidemiologically classified, but unclassified-risk HPVs exist. This study comprehensively elucidates HPV infection status in cervical cancer using next-generation sequencer analysis. With the approval of the ethics committee and the patient consent, DNA was extracted from cervical cytology specimens from 48 patients with cervical cancer. Following target capture of HPV genomic DNA, next-generation sequencing was performed. Multiple HPVs were detected in all samples and all samples had at least one high-risk HPV. Notably, the infection rate of HPV16 was higher than in previous reports. Hybridization capture detected HPV16 genomic DNA in all samples, while E7-specific PCR detected HPV16 in only 35 of 48 samples(73%). It is possible that conventional HPV testing may have underestimated the HPV16 infection rate. Assuming HPV16 infection is a prerequisite for carcinogenesis, persistent multiple infections with at least one high-risk HPV may play a significant role in cancer progression.

title: Expression and chromatin accessibility QTL of 29 FACS-sorted immune cells reveal mechanisms of immune-mediated disease
en: Expression and chromatin accessibility QTL of 29 FACS-sorted immune cells reveal mechanisms of immune-mediated disease
abs: Background: Molecular QTL enable functional interpretation of GWAS risk loci for immune-mediated diseases (IMDs). Chromatin accessibility QTL (caQTL) complements expression QTL (eQTL) by providing additional regulatory insights. Methods: Peripheral blood immune cells from 72 healthy individuals were FACS-sorted into 29 cell types. Bulk RNA-seq and ATAC-seq were performed to map eQTL and caQTL. Additionally, 5' scRNA-seq was conducted on >350,000 cells across all cell types from five donors. Results: We identified 7,250 eQTL and 11,243 caQTL in 29 immune cell types, including substantial signals in rare populations such as pDC (1,907 eQTL and 3,317 caQTL). caQTL were more enriched in enhancer regions than eQTL, indicating regulatory mechanisms beyond gene expression. Colocalization with GWAS of 12 IMD traits in East Asian populations identified loci colocalizing with eQTL and caQTL (e.g., the SHOC2 locus in pDC for SLE), highlighting cell-type-specific regulatory effects. GWAS risk projection onto scRNA-seq data revealed trait-relevant cellular enrichment (e.g., SLE in pDC). Using 5' scRNA-seq, we identified 2,896-13,022 bidirectionally transcribed candidate enhancers (btcEnhs) per cell type, enriched for both eQTL and caQTL within related lineages. Stratified LDSC analysis using ATAC peaks and btcEnhs further revealed cell-type-specific heritability enrichment (e.g., Th17/Tfh in RA and B cells/pDC in SLE). Conclusion: Integrative analysis of eQTL and caQTL across FACS-sorted immune cell types reveals cell-type-specific regulatory mechanisms underlying IMD pathogenesis.

title: Shared and ASD-preferential whole-genome risk layers in autism and schizophrenia
en: Shared and ASD-preferential whole-genome risk layers in autism and schizophrenia
abs: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and schizophrenia (SZ) are clinically distinct, but genomic studies show partially shared liability. We asked which WGS-detectable risk layers are shared or disorder-preferential. We analyzed PCR-free short-read WGS from 11,335 Japanese participants (ASD/SZ cases, controls and relatives), using harmonized variant calling, ancestry QC and pedigree-aware designs. We evaluated rare protein-truncating variants (PTVs), exonic and recurrent genomic-disorder CNVs, PRS (PRS-CSx), rare genic-proximal TRE outliers detected by ExpansionHunter Denovo/STRling with 5-fold cross-fitting, and rare deletions/duplications overlapping developmental topologically associating domain (TAD) boundaries. TAD boundaries are genomic borders organizing local regulatory contacts, including enhancer-gene contacts; here we focused on boundaries differing across developing brain cell types. Rare coding and CNV analyses recovered known risk layers. Rare TRE outlier carriage was increased in both ASD and SZ (OR=1.37-1.61 across callers), with no clear ASD- SZ heterogeneity. In contrast, rare deletions overlapping developmental cell-type-differential TAD boundaries were enriched in ASD (OR=1.43, P=2.9e-5), but not in SZ or duplications. This ASD deletion signal was supported by independent ASD cohorts (IVW OR=1.25, P=2.2e-3) and retained in joint-layer models. These findings support a layered WGS architecture: ASD and SZ share TRE burden, whereas rare deletions overlapping developmental 3D-genome regulatory borders show an ASD-preferential pattern.

title: Comprehensive analysis of Japanese-specific multiple-nucleotide variants and their potential regulatory effects
en: Comprehensive analysis of Japanese-specific multiple-nucleotide variants and their potential regulatory effects
abs: Large-scale genome studies have advanced rapidly with high-throughput sequencing. While single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) have been extensively characterized across diverse populations, multiple-nucleotide variants (MNVs), defined as clusters of adjacent nucleotide substitutions occurring simultaneously, remain comparatively underexplored, especially in Japanese populations. In this study, we analyzed MNVs using the 60KJPN whole-genome sequencing dataset from the Tohoku Medical Megabank Organization. By comparing MNV allele frequencies with gnomAD, we identified many MNVs observed only in the Japanese dataset (969,700 MNVs; 85.5% of jMorp MNVs). Annotation analysis showed that more than 80% of Japanese MNVs were located in non-coding regions, mainly intergenic and intronic regions, suggesting that their effects may not be captured by coding-focused interpretation. To investigate the potential functional impact of these non-coding MNVs, we applied AlphaGenome, a genome language model, to predict changes in gene expression and epigenomic features. We also compared the predicted effects of MNVs with those of the corresponding SNVs, enabling evaluation of effects that may emerge only when adjacent substitutions are considered jointly. A subset of Japanese-specific MNVs showed predicted regulatory effects that were not fully captured by analysis of the corresponding SNVs alone. These findings highlight the importance of MNV-aware analyses for characterizing population-specific genomic variation and improving the interpretation of disease risk in Japanese populations.

title: Cross-ancestry transferability of mitochondrial DNA copy number-associated variants in a Japanese population
en: Cross-ancestry transferability of mitochondrial DNA copy number-associated variants in a Japanese population
abs: Background: Mitochondrial DNA copy number (mtCN) reflects mitochondrial content and cellular bioenergetic capacity and is influenced by nuclear genetic variation and systemic physiology. However, most genetic determinants of mtCN have been identified in populations of European ancestry, and their transferability to non- European populations remains incompletely understood. Methods: We quantified blood mtCN by quantitative PCR in 857 participants from the Shika population-based cohort in Japan. We applied effect-size equivalence testing to evaluate the transferability of 66 previously reported mtCN-associated variants. We also performed a genome-wide association study (GWAS) to identify novel loci and a phenome-wide association study (PheWAS) to characterize phenotypic correlates of mtCN. Results: Sixty-two of 66 previously reported mtCN-associated variants showed statistically equivalent effects in our cohort, supporting cross-ancestry transferability of mtCN-associated genetic effects. GWAS identified three loci exceeding the suggestive significance threshold, although none reached genome-wide significance. PheWAS revealed a significant positive association between mtCN and serum aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels after false discovery rate correction (q = 0.02). Conclusion: These findings support the transferability of previously reported mtCN-associated variants to a Japanese population and suggest that the genetic architecture of mtCN is largely conserved across ancestries. The association between blood mtCN and AST warrants further investigation.

title: Trans-ethnic meta-analysis reveals the contribution of HLA-A*31:01 to susceptibility to carbamazepine- induced SJS/TEN
en: Trans-ethnic meta-analysis reveals the contribution of HLA-A*31:01 to susceptibility to carbamazepine- induced SJS/TEN
abs: [Introduction] We demonstrated a strong association between HLA- B*15:11 and carbamazepine (CBZ)-induced Stevens-Johnson syndrome/toxic epidermal necrolysis (SJS/TEN) in the Japanese population. In contrast, HLA-A*31:01 is an established risk allele for CBZ-induced drug-induced hypersensitivity syndrome/drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DIHS/DRESS), but its contribution to SJS/TEN susceptibility remained unclear. We investigated whether the association between HLA-A*31:01 and SJS/TEN could be replicated by a trans-ethnic meta-analysis of Japanese and Korean cohorts and evaluated the predictive performance of combined HLA biomarkers. [Methods] Meta-analyses were conducted using Japanese and Korean cohorts with CBZ-induced SJS/TEN and DIHS/DRESS. ROC analyses were performed. [Results] The association between HLA-B*15:11 and SJS/TEN was replicated in Japanese and Korean populations. HLA-A*31:01 showed a strong association with DIHS/DRESS and a moderate but statistically significant association with SJS/TEN in the meta-analysis (OR = 3.18, p = 1.1 × 10 -4 ). In the Japanese SJS/TEN cohort, the area under the ROC curve (AUC) increased from 0.698 to 0.749 after adding HLA- A*31:01 to HLA-B*15:11 alone. Similarly, in the Korean SJS/TEN cohort, the AUC improved from 0.681 to 0.793 after adding HLA- A*31:01. [Discussion] These findings suggest that HLA-A*31:01 contributes not only to DIHS/DRESS but also to SJS/TEN susceptibility. Combining HLA-A*31:01 with HLA-B*15:11 substantially improves the prediction of CBZ-induced SJS/TEN in East Asian populations.

title: Detection and analysis of complex genome structural variation in postmortem brains of donors with psychiatric disorders
en: Detection and analysis of complex genome structural variation in postmortem brains of donors with psychiatric disorders
abs: Complex structural variations (cxSVs) are often overlooked in genome analyses due to detection challenges. We developed ARC-SV, a probabilistic and machine learning-based method that enables accurate detection and reconstruction of cxSVs from standard datasets. Applying across 4,262 genomes representing all continental populations, we identified cxSVs as a significant source of natural human genetic variation. Rare cxSVs have a propensity to occur in neural genes and loci that underwent rapid human-specific evolution, including those regulating corticogenesis. By performing single-nuclei multiomics in postmortem brains, we discovered cxSVs associated with differential gene expression and chromatin accessibility across various brain regions and cell types. Additionally, cxSVs detected in brains of psychiatric cases are enriched for linkage with psychiatric GWAS risk alleles detected in the same brains. Furthermore, our analysis revealed significantly decreased brain region- and cell type-specific expression of cxSV-genes specifically for psychiatric cases, implicating cxSVs in the molecular etiology of major neuropsychiatric disorders.

title: Optical genome mapping resolves complex chromosomal rearrangements in three patients with developmental delay
en: Optical genome mapping resolves complex chromosomal rearrangements in three patients with developmental delay
abs: Conventional cytogenetic analyses may not fully resolve complex chromosomal rearrangements (CCRs). We applied optical genome mapping (OGM) to three patients with developmental delay and suspected CCRs. Case 1 was a 4-year-old boy with macrocephaly, developmental delay, and autistic features. G-banding, FISH, and chromosomal microarray (CMA) identified five structural variants (SVs) involving chromosomes 2, 8, and 14 and a 4.2-Mb deletion at 2q13-q14.1, whereas OGM detected at least 12 SVs, including a breakpoint disrupting CHD8 at 14q11.2. Case 2 was a 6-year-old boy with seizures, developmental delay, and cleft lip and palate. CMA and spectral karyotyping suggested a CCR involving chromosomes 2, 10, 12, and 14, and OGM identified at least 11 translocation breakpoints, clarifying the rearrangement architecture. Case 3 was a 6-year-old boy with developmental delay and infantile epileptic spasms syndrome. G-banding showed 46,XY,t(2;11)(p21;p15.1),t(8;21)(p11.2;q11.2), but OGM identified chromosome 3, rather than chromosome 11, as a rearranged chromosome, revealing a CCR involving chromosomes 2, 3, 8, and 21, four translocation breakpoints, and a 1.13-Mb deletion at 21q21.1. Across all three cases, OGM revealed substantially greater structural complexity than conventional methods. OGM corrected a chromosome misidentification in Case 3 and identified gene-level disruption of CHD8 in Case 1, providing a plausible molecular basis for the phenotype. These findings support OGM for comprehensive characterization of CCRs in patients with developmental delay.

title: Supporting Healthcare Transition in Congenital Genetic Disorders: Insights from a Survey on Mowat- Wilson Syndrome
en: Supporting Healthcare Transition in Congenital Genetic Disorders: Insights from a Survey on Mowat- Wilson Syndrome
abs: Introduction) Healthcare transition (HCT) from pediatric to adult care is critical for patients with congenital genetic disorders requiring lifelong multidisciplinary management. To develop an HCT system tailored to patient needs, we surveyed families of patients with Mowat- Wilson syndrome (MWS). Methods) In collaboration with the MWS Family Association, we conducted a web-based questionnaire survey on transition support and adult medical care between December 2025 and January 2026 (ethics approval R7-03). Results) Fifty families responded (response rate 68.3%); 54% had patients under 15 years and 46% were aged 15 or older. All recognized the need for adult medical care, and 86% had a primary physician (pediatrics 50%, neurology 25%, genetics 10%, pediatric surgery 10%, home-visit care 5%). The most desired specialty for future care was general internal medicine (61.1%), followed by neurology and genetics (16.7% each). Among the 10 families under pediatric care, only one wished to continue with a pediatrician; others preferred adult specialists. Only 26.1% had received transition support, and just one-third of those felt it was adequate. Only 15% reported being informed about adult-onset complications or future medical needs. Conclusion) This survey reveals a substantial gap between patient needs and the reality of HCT support for rare genetic disorders. There is an urgent need to organize disease-specific medical data and establish effective systems for transition support and information provision.

title: Segmental uniparental isodisomy due to deletion rescue in a girl with mosaic partial monosomy 9p
en: Segmental uniparental isodisomy due to deletion rescue in a girl with mosaic partial monosomy 9p
abs: Post-zygotic correction of chromosomal monosomy, monosomy rescue, can result in whole-chromosome uniparental isodisomy. Recently, post-zygotic correction of partial chromosomal deletion, deletion rescue, has been proposed as a mechanism underlying segmental uniparental isodisomy. Here, we report a girl with mosaic partial monosomy of chromosome 9p arising from deletion rescue. The proband was a 10-year-old girl. She was born to non-consanguineous parents at 40 weeks of gestation. Developmental milestones were delayed: head control achieved at 3 months, sitting at 7 months, creeping at 2 years, and pulling herself up at 7 years of age. At 10 years of age, she was able to speak only a few words. She developed epilepsy at 10 years of age with generalized spike-and-wave discharges observed on electroencephalography during sleep. She showed linear pigmentation along the lines of Blaschko, suggesting a mosaic disorder. G-banding confirmed mosaic partial monosomy 9p (mos 46,XX,del(9) (p22)[7]/46,XX[23]). Chromosomal microarray analysis (CMA) of peripheral blood identified a region of homozygosity on 9p24.3-p22.3 without detectable copy number loss. In contrast, CMA of buccal mucosa revealed a deletion on 9p24.3-p22.3 with a normalized log2 ratio of -0.8: mosaic ratio of the deletion was estimated 86%. These results indicated that the 9p24.3-p22.3 deletion was orthotopically corrected during post-zygotic cell division. In conclusion, the coexistence of partial monosomy mosaicism and a region of homozygosity in the corresponding region is a clue of deletion rescue.

title: Clinical Utility of Genetic Testing for Patients with Suspected Neurofibromatosis Type 1
en: Clinical Utility of Genetic Testing for Patients with Suspected Neurofibromatosis Type 1
abs: Background: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1), caused by pathogenic NF1 variants, is characterized by cafe-au-lait macules (CALMs) and neurofibromas. However, diagnosis is challenging when CALMs are the sole feature, particularly in differentiating NF1 from Legius syndrome (LS). We evaluated the clinical utility of genetic testing (GT) for suspected NF1. Methods: We reviewed patients with suspected NF1 who underwent GT (targeted sequencing and chromosomal microarray) at Tottori University Hospital between January 2017 and January 2026. Results: Of the 23 patients included, the median age at the initial visit was 5 years (0-67). Manifestations included multiple CALMs in 22 (95.7%), freckling in 7 (30.4%), and neurofibromas in 4 (17.4%). Definitive diagnosis was established in 12 patients (52.2%), comprising 10 with NF1 (43.5%) and 2 with LS (8.7%). Among 9 patients meeting NF1 clinical criteria, 6 were genetically diagnosed (66.7%, 5 NF1, 1 LS). Notably, among 15 patients with CALMs alone, 8 achieved definitive diagnosis (53.3%, 7 NF1, 1 LS). Identified NF1 variants included 4 nonsynonymous, 3 frameshift, 1 splice-site, and 2 NF1 whole-gene deletions. Conclusion: GT confirmed diagnoses in 53.3% of patients presenting solely with CALMs, supporting its utility when clinical signs are insufficient. Furthermore, pathogenic variants such as frameshifts and NF1 whole-gene deletions were identified in NF1, allowing for accurate assessment of complication risks based on genotype-phenotype correlations. GT is valuable for early diagnosis and tailored follow-up.

title: Genetic Analysis of Skeletal Dysplasia Using Whole-Exome Sequencing: A Single-Center Study
en: Genetic Analysis of Skeletal Dysplasia Using Whole-Exome Sequencing: A Single-Center Study
abs: [Introduction] Skeletal dysplasias are a heterogeneous group of rare genetic disorders affecting ~ 1 in 5,000 individuals, encompassing 771 conditions caused by pathogenic variants in 552 genes. Next-generation sequencing has accelerated detection of causative variants. [Aim] To evaluate the diagnostic utility of whole-exome sequencing (WES) in patients with skeletal dysplasia at a single center. [Method] Between December 2016 and November 2025, WES was performed in 192 patients referred nationwide to the University of Osaka. Our pipeline integrated SNV/CNV detection, annotation, and disease-specific gene filtering. [Result] The overall diagnostic yield was 58.9% (113/192), ranging from 52% (26/50; Osteogenesis imperfecta) to 90% (9/10; Type II collagenopathy). Heterozygous variants predominated (n=94), including missense (n=41), frameshift (n=20), nonsense (n=14), splice-site (n=12), CNVs (n=4), in-frame (n=2), and delins (n=1). In 22 patients, diagnoses were revised after genetic analysis; for instance, a case initially diagnosed with brachydactyly was reclassified as aggrecanopathy due to an ACAN variant. [Discussion] WES showed high diagnostic yield with expert clinical evaluation. Limitations included reduced sensitivity for deep intronic variants and imprecise CNV breakpoint resolution, requiring whole-genome sequencing (WGS). [Conclusion] WES is an effective first-tier tool for skeletal dysplasia diagnosis. However, complementary approaches, including WGS, transcriptome/methylome analyses, and collaboration, are needed to improve yield.

title: Prenatal Diagnosis of Noonan Syndrome/RASopathy
en: Prenatal Diagnosis of Noonan Syndrome/RASopathy
abs: Noonan syndrome and related disorders (RASopathies) are known to be the most common conditions associated with cases where fetal nuchal translucency (NT) thickening was observed in early pregnancy but chromosomal testing yielded normal results. We provide information on these conditions during genetic counseling and offer Noonan/RASopathies panel testing to those who request it. We investigated the ultrasound findings and the diagnostic process for cases of RASopathies diagnosed at our hospital. Among the 9 cases in which prenatal RASopathies panel testing was performed due to nuchal translucency (NT) thickening between January 2022 and January 2026, variants were identified in 4 cases. The breakdown was as follows: 2 cases with pathogenic BRAF variants, 1 case with a pathogenic SOS1 variant, and 1 case with a variant of unknown significance (VUS) in LZTR1. In addition, there was one case in which multiple anomalies were detected by ultrasound, and a pathogenic variant in SOS1 was identified through chorionic exome sequencing following termination of pregnancy. There was also one case in which the pregnant woman herself exhibited suspicious physical characteristics; testing revealed a pathogenic variant in her RIT1, and it was considered likely that this variant had been transmitted to the fetus. If nuchal translucency thickening is observed during the first trimester, the possibility of RASopathies must always be kept in mind when planning genetic counseling and testing.

title: Differences in phenotypes of carriers with loss-of-function type SCN5A variants in the families
en: Differences in phenotypes of carriers with loss-of-function type SCN5A variants in the families
abs: Backgrounds: SCN5A encodes a cardiac sodium channel, and its loss-of-function (LOF) variants cause various cardiac phenotypes, such as Brugada syndrome (BrS), sick sinus syndrome (SSS) and so on. The penetrance of these phenotypes is variable depending on age and sex, however, the detailed phenotypes in families with the same SCN5A variant have not been well elucidated yet. Purpose: We aimed to clarify age and sex-dependent differences in phenotypes caused by the same SCN5A variants in families. Methods and Results: The study cohort consisted of 41 probands (male n=24) with LOF SCN5A variants and their parents with the same variants as the probands. The median age for genetic testing of probands is 15 (7-24) years old. The phenotypes of probands were classified into BrS (n=24, male n=18), SSS (n=21, male n=9) and others (n=1). Five probands showed overlapping phenotypes of BrS and SSS. In 24 BrS probands, SCN5A variants were inherited from 11 fathers and 13 mothers. Ten (90%) fathers and 4 (31%) mothers showed BrS phenotype, and 1 mother without BrS phenotype was SSS. Among 11 male probands who inherited SCN5A variants from their mothers, only 3 (27%) mothers showed BrS phenotype.
