In 21 SSS probands, SCN5A variants were inherited from 9 fathers, none of whom had SSS, but 2 of whom showed BrS phenotype. In contrast, 5 (42%) out of 12 mothers suffered SSS, and 4 of them were implanted with pacemakers. Conclusions: Phenotypes of LOF SCN5A variants are variable even within a family. We must be careful when providing genetic counseling to patients with LOF SCN5A variants.

title: Real-World Characteristics of Genetic Counseling in the Cardiovascular Field: A 10-Year Single- Center Experience
en: Real-World Characteristics of Genetic Counseling in the Cardiovascular Field: A 10-Year Single- Center Experience
abs: The clinical importance of genetic medicine in the cardiovascular field has increased in recent years; however, the real-world characteristics of genetic counseling in this field remain insufficiently understood. We retrospectively reviewed 122 cases related to cardiovascular and connective tissue disorders among 2,018 genetic counseling cases performed at our institution between April 2016 and March 2025. The 122 cases included Fabry Disease in 44 (36%), connective tissue disorders in 33 (27%), inherited arrhythmia disorders in 27 (22%), mitochondrial diseases in 10 (8%), cardiomyopathies in 6 (5%), and other disorders in 2 (2%). Suspected and disease-related cases were also included in each category. Only 38 cases (31%) were referred from the cardiology department, whereas 40 (33%) were referred from other departments and 43 (36%) were self-referred at-risk individuals without formal physician referral. Family-based cascade screening was observed particularly in patients with Fabry Disease, connective tissue disorders, and arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy-related conditions. Genetic medicine in the cardiovascular field encompasses multisystem disorders, including metabolic diseases, connective tissue disorders, highlighting the need for multidisciplinary collaboration across departments. In addition, many at-risk individuals do not initially present to a specialized department. Establishing a clinical framework in which cardiology departments actively accept and evaluate at-risk individuals may therefore be desirable in future clinical practice.

title: Homozygous SGCB splice-site variant causes isolated dilated cardiomyopathy through sarcoglycan complex destabilization
en: Homozygous SGCB splice-site variant causes isolated dilated cardiomyopathy through sarcoglycan complex destabilization
abs: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a genetically heterogeneous disorder characterized by ventricular dilatation and impaired systolic function, leading to heart failure and sudden cardiac death. Despite advances in genomic technologies, the genetic causes of DCM remain unidentified in more than half of patients. Here, we performed an integrative analysis of genomic and transcriptomic data from patient-derived cardiac tissue to identify causative variants in genetically undiagnosed DCM. This approach enabled us to identify a homozygous splice-site variant, c.243+6T to A, in the sarcoglycan gene SGCB, which results in exon 2 skipping. This variant was significantly enriched in patients with DCM compared with the general population, with consistent genotype-phenotype correlations observed across multiple families. Protein-level analysis of cardiac tissue from homozygous individuals revealed loss of beta-sarcoglycan, the protein product of SGCB, and destabilization of the sarcoglycan complex. Although SGCB has been previously associated with limb-girdle muscular dystrophy, these homozygous individuals showed no biochemical or clinical signs of skeletal muscle involvement, indicating an absence of myopathy. Compared with patients with DCM without this variant, homozygous individuals also had a higher risk of early-onset adverse cardiac events. Together, these findings identify c.243+6T to A in SGCB as a cause of isolated DCM associated with unfavorable clinical outcomes.

title: Expanded Non-p.R4810K RNF213 Variant Spectrum in East Asian Pediatric PAH
en: Expanded Non-p.R4810K RNF213 Variant Spectrum in East Asian Pediatric PAH
abs: Background: Pediatric idiopathic and heritable pulmonary arterial hypertension (IPAH/HPAH) is increasingly recognized as biologically distinct from adult-onset disease. Although the RNF213 p.R4810K founder variant has been implicated in East Asian vasculopathy, the broader spectrum and clinical significance of non-p.R4810K RNF213 variants in pediatric PAH remain unclear. Methods: We retrospectively investigated 203 Japanese and Chinese patients diagnosed with IPAH/ HPAH before 20 years of age. The result of genetic testing, clinical characteristics and outcomes were evaluated according to RNF213 variant status, including comparisons between p.R4810K and non-p.R4810K carriers. Results: Pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants of disease-causing genes were identified in 79 patients (38.9%). In addition, isolated RNF213 rare variants in 34 patients (16.7%). Non-p.R4810K carriers demonstrated higher pulmonary arterial pressure than did p.R4810K carriers. Survival differences between RNF213 subgroups were not statistically significant. Several non-p.R4810K variants demonstrated high predicted deleteriousness, supporting their potential clinical relevance. Conclusions: East Asian pediatric IPAH/ HPAH demonstrates an expanded RNF213 variant spectrum extending beyond the canonical p.R4810K founder variant. The identification of clinically significant non-p.R4810K variants broadens the genetic and phenotypic spectrum of RNF213-associated pulmonary vasculopathy and suggests genetic heterogeneity in pediatric PAH susceptibility across East Asian populations.

title: Polygenetic, cellular, and spatial contrasts distinctly between dilated and hypertrophic cardiomyopathies
en: Polygenetic, cellular, and spatial contrasts distinctly between dilated and hypertrophic cardiomyopathies
abs: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) are both primary cardiac muscle diseases but with morphologically and functionally contrasting phenotypes. The genetic architectures distinguishing between them remain unresolved. We conducted the largest-scale genome-wide association studies (GWAS) in non-European populations to date, analyzing 2,385 DCM and 2,089 HCM Japanese individuals in parallel (N = 150K). We identified three novel risk loci (CACNA1D, SORCS1, GAREM1) in Japanese HCM GWAS. Cross-population GWAS meta-analyses with 23,000 DCM and 11,113 HCM cases (N = 1,900K) identified 64 and 56 significant loci each, including 12 novel loci, and demonstrated shared and distinct risk variants across populations. Two cardiomyopathies showed genome-wide opposing architectures by comparing polygenic risk scores (PRS). Comprehensive cross-trait association analyses of DCM/ HCM-PRS in BioBank Japan and UK Biobank revealed that both PRSs predicted other cardiovascular and metabolic phenotypes in the same positive direction, while echocardiographic and cardiac MRI parameters showed consistently inverse associations between DCM- PRS and HCM-PRS. When integrating GWAS with human heart single-cell/single-nucleus RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics, both cardiomyopathies are spatiotemporally associated with stressed cardiomyocytes, but with gene expression profiles in opposite directions. This study highlights the polygenetic, cellular, and spatial contrasts between DCM and HCM and provides further insights into their unresolved pathogenesis.

title: Ethical Challenges in Genetic Testing for Cardiovascular Diseases: A Comprehensive Framework
en: Ethical Challenges in Genetic Testing for Cardiovascular Diseases: A Comprehensive Framework
abs: Background: Rapid implementation of cardiovascular genomic medicine has highlighted critical ethical, legal, and social issues (ELSI). While monogenic disorders provide clear actionability, polygenic risk scores involve probabilistic risks, complicating results return. Objective: To characterize ELSI and practical challenges in establishing frameworks for returning genomic results in cardiovascular diseases. Methods: From January to March 2026, we conducted multi-stakeholder deliberations within our AMED project. Concurrently, we investigated domestic return practices at Shizuoka Cancer Center. In March 2026, we performed international inquiries with key stakeholders implementing national genomics in the UK (NHS, Genomics England, Our Future Health) and Singapore (PRECISE) to analyze global infrastructure and engagement strategies. Results: Three core ELSI themes emerged: (1) Divergent protocols for monogenic vs. polygenic risks; explaining shifting risk models requires robust literacy support. (2) Longitudinal accountability; managing the reinterpretation of variants of uncertain significance (VUS) and post-mortem disclosure requires pre-obtained consent. (3) Workforce gaps; lack of pathways for non-specialists handling secondary findings hinders heart-team and genetic-professional synergy. Conclusion: Cardiovascular genomic delivery requires a life-course knowledge loop rather than one-time disclosure. Developing cross-disciplinary guidance and pilot infrastructure to evaluate behavioral outcomes is urgent.

title: Refractory Epilepsy Associated With a Final-Exon Nonsense Variant in MSL2
en: Refractory Epilepsy Associated With a Final-Exon Nonsense Variant in MSL2
abs: Variants in the MSL2 gene were newly established as a disease entity in 2024 and registered in OMIM as Karayol-Borroto-Haghshenas neurodevelopmental syndrome (KBHS). KBHS is a rare disorder characterized by developmental delay, intellectual disability, hypotonia, epilepsy, and ophthalmologic abnormalities caused by loss-of-function MSL2 variants. An 8-year-old boy, born at 38 weeks of gestation, presented with developmental delay, refractory epilepsy consistent with Lennox-Gastaut spectrum, and ophthalmologic abnormalities including hyperopia and astigmatism. Genetic testing identified a heterozygous nonsense variant in MSL2 (NM_018133(MSL2): c.1429C>T, p.Arg477Ter). This variant is located in the terminal exon and is predicted to escape nonsense-mediated decay (NMD), resulting in a truncated protein. The variant has not been registered in ClinVar or population genome databases, including ExAC and the 1000 Genomes Project. According to ACMG guidelines, the variant was classified as pathogenic (Class Ia) based on PVS1 and PS2 evidence, together with previously reported iPSC-based functional analyses of MSL2 and localization within a DNA-binding domain. Among 25 previously reported cases, variants predicted to undergo NMD were predominantly associated with severe phenotypes and early-onset epilepsy. Although the present variant is predicted to escape NMD, the patient exhibited refractory epilepsy, suggesting this case may provide important insights into the disease mechanism of KBHS.

title: Pathogenic mobile element insertions as overlooked causes of unresolved rare disease: ancestry- enriched founder alleles
en: Pathogenic mobile element insertions as overlooked causes of unresolved rare disease: ancestry- enriched founder alleles
abs: Background: Mobile element insertions (MEIs), including LINE-1 (L1) and Alu insertions, are established causes of human genetic disease but are often overlooked in routine genome analysis. We investigated the clinical utility of dedicated MEI detection in unresolved rare disease cases. Methods: We analyzed 4,570 Illumina short-read whole-genome sequencing datasets from patients and relatives using MEGAnE. Coding-disrupting MEIs were evaluated according to phenotype and inheritance pattern. Results: We identified four patients in whom MEIs represented the disease-causing mechanism. Patient 1, with Angelman syndrome, harbored a de novo L1 insertion in exon 5 of UBE3A on the maternally derived allele. Patients 2 and 3, both with retinitis pigmentosa, carried the same heterozygous AluY insertion in exon 4 of RP1 together with different frameshift variants. Patient 4, with Joubert syndrome, carried an L1 insertion in exon 7 of CC2D2A together with a splice-site variant in exon 29. The recurrent RP1 and CC2D2A MEIs were identified in 14 and 10 individuals, respectively, among 4,570 analyzed subjects, suggesting ancestry-enriched pathogenic alleles. Discussion: Dedicated MEI analysis identified pathogenic variants missed by standard SNV/indel-focused pipelines and provided diagnoses for previously unresolved cases. Recurrent coding-disrupting MEIs in RP1 and CC2D2A may represent founder alleles in the Japanese population. These findings support incorporating MEI detection into routine genome analysis to improve rare disease diagnosis.

title: Current Status of High-Risk Screening for Fabry Disease Using Urinary Mulberry Bodies and Cells at Our Institution
en: Current Status of High-Risk Screening for Fabry Disease Using Urinary Mulberry Bodies and Cells at Our Institution
abs: Background: Fabry disease is a systemic hereditary disorder that frequently leads to complications such as renal failure, cardiomyopathy, and stroke. Urinary mulberry cells and bodies, which appear in the early stages of Fabry disease, serve as highly sensitive and specific non-invasive diagnostic markers, with near 100% sensitivity and specificity. At our institution, we collaborate with multiple departments to conduct high-risk screening, termed "Mulberry Screening", using urinary sediment analysis. Methods: This was a single-center, retrospective observational study conducted between May 2024 and April 2025. Patients were eligible for screening if they presented with any of the following conditions: unexplained renal dysfunction, proteinuria, cerebrovascular disease (age < 60 years), left ventricular hypertrophy (13 > mm), or cardiac dysfunction. Urinary sediment was examined for the presence of mulberry cells or bodies. Results and Discussion: Mulberry screening was performed in 76 patients: 28 from the Department of Cardiology, 28 from Nephrology, 13 from Neurosurgery, and 7 from Cardiovascular Surgery. One true-positive case was identified, and treatment was initiated. Two false-positive cases were also noted. In these false-positive cases, phospholipid accumulation in glomerular epithelial cells, potentially due to medications such as amiodarone, was considered a contributing factor. Given that patients with left ventricular hypertrophy may be on anti-arrhythmic agents such as amiodarone, careful interpretation of mulberry screening results is warranted.

title: Assessment of Structural and Copy Number Variants in Constitutional Samples Using Electronic
en: Assessment of Structural and Copy Number Variants in Constitutional Samples Using Electronic
abs: Background The detection and interpretation of structural variants (SVs), including copy number variants (CNVs), is the key function of modern cytogenetic laboratories and are important for diagnosis, clinical management, and genetic counseling. Current cytogenetic laboratory methods such as chromosomal microarray analysis (CMA), fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), and chromosome banding chromosome analysis (CBA) can each provide structural genomic information, but each technique has specific limitations in their ability to resolve certain types or sizes of SVs. Electronic genome mapping (EGM) enables genome-wide analysis of SVs using long DNA molecules in a single workflow. We present a proof of concept for the use of EGM for the detection of SVs in a cohort of constitutional and prenatal samples with findings previously characterized by conventional cytogenetic testing. Methodology EGM, a solid-state nanochannel-based platform, is a high-resolution technology capable of detecting a broad range of structural genomic variations. To evaluate the utility of EGM for cytogenetic testing of constitutional disorders, peripheral blood specimens referred for follow up of known chromosomal abnormality were analyzed in this study. DNA was extracted using NEB Monarch® HMW DNA Extraction Kit and processed using a dual-enzyme workflow and the OhmX™ Platform. SVs were identified using Human Chromosome Explorer® (HCE) de novo assembly, while copy number alterations was assessed using a CNV analysis pipeline. The study cohort included samples with genomic findings previously characterized using orthogonal methods such as CMA, qPCR and CBA. Results EGM enabled assessment of structural and copy number alterations across the analyzed cohort, with findings concordant with previously characterized genomic abnormalities. HCE de novo assembly enabled the detection of SVs less than one megabase, while the CNV analysis pipeline was configured to detect larger copy number alterations (>1 Mb), with both approaches demonstrating findings consistent with prior orthogonal characterization. EGM was able to detect abnormalities as small as ~80kb and up to whole chromosome aneuploidies in our cohort. Conclusions EGM represents a promising, emerging technology for integrated genome-wide assessment of SVs in constitutional and prenatal samples. The combination of de novo assembly and CNV analysis enables identification of genomic abnormalities across multiple size ranges, highlighting the potential utility of EGM as a tool to simplify and improve the clarification of SVs in standard cytogenetic workflows.

title: CRISPR/Cas9 Customization of Electronic Genome Mapping Repeat Expansion Assays
en: CRISPR/Cas9 Customization of Electronic Genome Mapping Repeat Expansion Assays
abs: Many genetic disorders are caused by simple sequence repeat expansions, including Fragile X syndrome and Friedreich’s ataxia. Accurate sizing of these expansions is critical for determining pathogenicity. Conventional PCR and sequencing methods are unreliable for long repeat regions. Electronic genome mapping (EGM) uses solid-state nanodetectors to survey long DNA molecules and detect structural variants, including those caused by repeat expansions. We assessed EGM’s ability to detect FMR1, FXN, DMPK, and c9orf72 repeat expansions. Single injections and replicates were analyzed for concordance with published repeat lengths using the custom RepX™ Repeat Expansion Analysis pipeline. Results were concordant with expectations across all FMR1 cell lines, but some FXN cell lines did not match published findings. Because FXN has been shown to be an unstable repeat within the same cell line, we analyzed the FXN cell lines by PCR and EGM. Some cell lines were found to have multiple repeat alleles via PCR, and these patterns were mirrored by the single-molecule EGM results. This confirms the accuracy and robustness of EGM for detecting and sizing repeat expansions that are challenging to analyze by standard techniques. In addition, we have customized the FMR1 and FXN assays by including specific nicks and blocks to optimize the interval size for calling premutation alleles. The impact of CRISPR customization will be shown for these repeat expansion assays. EGM offers integrated workflows for high-resolution analysis of repeat regions in either whole-genome or gene-specific mode.

title: CRISPR/Cas9 Optimization Using Electronic Genome Mapping
en: CRISPR/Cas9 Optimization Using Electronic Genome Mapping
abs: Cas9’s ability to bind both targeted and non-targeted sites, and its functional interactions with other proteins and domains, have been studied using many technologies. We show how electronic genome mapping (EGM), which can detect DNA nicks in single molecules covering the whole genome, can be used to determine how gRNA mismatches affect target versus off-target binding and how Cas9 interacts with other proteins when bound to DNA. Cas9 binding to perfectly matched gRNA sites was examined and compared with binding to sites with mismatches at each position in the gRNA. The PAM site and nearby bases in the seed region were found to be critical for binding activity, while single mismatches in positions toward the 5’ end of the recognition region allowed significant off-target binding. The impact of mismatches varied by gRNA. In addition, we used EGM to determine, at base-pair resolution, how physically close the bound CRISPR/dCas9 complex can be relative to nearby nickase recognition sites and still allow activity. Using gRNAs that each bind many different sites in the human genome, we determined the minimum distance between the bound CRISPR/dCas9 complex and nearby nickase recognition sites required for nickase activity. Nickase recognition sites 4-7 bp from the gRNA showed reduced activity, while those 8 bp or more from the gRNA were minimally impacted. Coupled with EGM’s ability to simultaneously evaluate hundreds of singly and doubly mismatched off-target sites, these findings provide insight into Cas9 activity that may be extended to other CRISPR systems.

title: Regional Trends in Genetics Terminology in PubMed Abstracts: A 1996-2025 Bibliometric Analysis
en: Regional Trends in Genetics Terminology in PubMed Abstracts: A 1996-2025 Bibliometric Analysis
abs: Background: Stigma-free, standardized terminology in genetics has been increasingly encouraged. The ACMG/AMP sequence variant interpretation guideline recommended replacing terms such as "mutation" and "polymorphism" with "variant." However, regional uptake of these recommendations remains unclear. We examined long-term trends in genetics-related terminology in PubMed abstracts. Methods: PubMed baseline and update XML files were parsed to extract bibliographic and affiliation data. English-language records published from 1996 to 2025 containing "gene" in the title or abstract were defined as the gene corpus. Countries were grouped into Asia, Europe, and North America, with separate G7 analyses. Twenty-nine genetics-related terms were assessed across six 5-year periods by Poisson regression with token count as an offset. Results: The gene corpus included 7,592,401 abstracts and 1.62 billion tokens. Over time, "mutation" decreased (IRR per 5 years 0.87, 95% CI 0.85-0.88), whereas "variant" increased (1.08, 1.07-1.10) and "pathogenic variant" markedly increased (3.10, 2.25-4.27). In 2021-2025, among the 3 regions, "mutation" and "polymorphism" were most frequent in Asia, "variant" in Europe, and "pathogenic variant" in Europe. Among G7 countries, "mutation" and "polymorphism" were most frequent in Japan, "variant" in Italy, and "pathogenic variant" in France. Conclusion: Genetics terminology shifted from mutation-centered wording toward variant- and pathogenicity-oriented language, but the pace of change differed across regions and countries.

title: Common and Distinct Genetic Characteristics in Maternal Lineages of ASD: A Next-Generation Sequencing Study
en: Common and Distinct Genetic Characteristics in Maternal Lineages of ASD: A Next-Generation Sequencing Study
abs: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a highly heritable neurodevelopmental disorder. To gain insights into its complex genetic architecture, family-based genomic analyses can provide insights into shared and inherited variants associated with ASD. In this study, we performed whole-genome sequencing (WGS) using saliva samples from a mother and her two daughters, all of whom were clinically diagnosed with ASD. Their clinical features were assessed in detail by the ADOS-2, K-ABCII, SRS-2, and AQ. Genomic DNA was extracted from saliva samples and subjected to WGS. The data obtained were processed using standard pipelines, including alignment to the GRCh38 reference genome and variant calling with the GATK. Variants were annotated using snpEff and filtered by SnpSift based on their population frequencies and predicted functional impacts. ASD-associated candidates were further searched for in the following order: (1) variants shared among the three individuals or transmitted from the mother to both daughters; (2) rare variants; (3) loss-of-function and predicted damaging missense variants; and (4) annotations based on ASD-associated genes from the SFARI Gene database. Shared copy number variants (CNVs) were identified using Control-FREEC. In this presentation, we will report ASD-associated genetic variants shared by all three family members and those specific to the siblings, and explore associations between genetic variants and phenotypic profiles.

title: Rare variant analysis identifies candidate genes potentially involved in nephrotic syndrome
en: Rare variant analysis identifies candidate genes potentially involved in nephrotic syndrome
abs: <Background> Nephrotic syndrome (NS) is a heterogeneous disorder characterized by proteinuria due to glomerular filtration barrier dysfunction. Podocyte injury is central to its pathogenesis, with genetic and immune-mediated mechanisms implicated. While monogenic causes and genome-wide association studies have identified susceptibility loci, many cases remain unexplained. The contribution of rare variants is not well defined. <Methods> Whole genome sequencing data from 10,659 Japanese individuals (1,290 cases and 9,369 controls) were analyzed. Rare variants were restricted to predicted loss-of-function variants and aggregated at the gene level. The dataset was randomly divided into a training set (70%) and a test set (30%). In the training set, gene enrichment was assessed using Fishers exact test followed by Bayesian gene-based analysis. Genes with high posterior probability and multiple variants were selected. In the test set, burden analysis was performed. <Results> A total of 150 genes were identified in the discovery phase, from which a subset was prioritized. In the test set, rare variant carriers were more frequent in cases than controls (17.0% vs 15.6%, odds ratio 1.11, p=0.26), although not statistically significant. At the gene level, several candidates showed relatively large effect sizes, including PARP2 and ERO1B. Expression data indicated that these genes are expressed in podocytes and immune-related cell types. <Conclusion> This study identifies biologically plausible candidate genes for NS and suggests that rare variants may contribute in a polygenic manner.

title: Effects of ABCG2 SNPs on hyperuricemia progression: the potential for implementation of genome- personalized nursing
en: Effects of ABCG2 SNPs on hyperuricemia progression: the potential for implementation of genome- personalized nursing
abs: Gout develops after prolonged hyperuricemia with elevated serum uric acid (SUA) levels. Sex, overweight/obesity, heavy drinking, aging and menopause (if female) are its risks, in addition to two common dysfunctional SNPs in ABCG2/BCRP. Here we evaluate the individual and population genetic effects in 9,244 Japanese to implement genome-personalized nurse-led hyperuricemia/gout care. First, ABCG2 SNPs had a higher population-attributable fraction (PAF; approximately 30%) for hyperuricemia than those for other typical environmental risk factors except for menopause. In premenopausal individuals, the PAF for ABCG2 SNPs was 45.8%, much higher than that after menopause (29.6%). Second, all these factors also showed significant individual risk of increased SUA level, and ABCG2 SNPs had sufficient effect size to allow them to be converted into other environmental factors. For example, a 25% ABCG2 dysfunction was equivalent to the effects of a 1.67 kg/m2 increase in BMI in females from the viewpoint of SUA increase. Third, to implement genome-personalized nursing with these results above, we mapped onto the process a theoretical framework that is based on a psychological model from behavioral change theory. Because the present results for convertibility will improve the predictability of genetic effects, cognitive interventions could encourage behavioral change through efficacy expectations (self-efficacy) and outcome expectations. We conclude that this framework would function effectively and has potential as a basis for implementing genome-personalized nurse-led care.

title: CaseSharing: a privacy-preserving case matchmaking platform for rare disease diagnosis and research
en: CaseSharing: a privacy-preserving case matchmaking platform for rare disease diagnosis and research
abs: Case matchmaking supports diagnosis of ultra-rare genetic diseases and rare disease research by identifying related cases across institutions. However, sharing clinical and genomic data raises privacy and practical concerns. We developed a matchmaking function in CaseSharing, a web-based platform within PubCaseFinder, to discover related cases while keeping sensitive information under user control. CaseSharing stores case records locally in the browser and represents clinical information as standardized data. The function searches cases using diagnosis names, candidate genes, and phenotypic profiles. Inheritance and zygosity are contextual information to prioritize matches, while avoiding disclosure of variant-level or identifying information. Users can register, manage, and search cases through one interface. Once a query is submitted, matchmaking is performed immediately against registered cases. When a match is identified, contact information is shared with both parties, enabling collaboration or joint research. The system supports domestic discovery and future interoperability with Matchmaker Exchange. Combining standardized data and controlled exposure, CaseSharing links local management with collaborative diagnosis and research. To our knowledge, CaseSharing is the first platform to integrate local rare disease case management with privacy-conscious case matchmaking. It may accelerate diagnosis, promote discovery of novel disease entities, and provide a foundation for future interoperability with Matchmaker Exchange.

title: Prevalence of Germline Pathogenic Variants in Uterine Cervical Cancer: A Large-Scale Analysis Using the C-CAT Database
en: Prevalence of Germline Pathogenic Variants in Uterine Cervical Cancer: A Large-Scale Analysis Using the C-CAT Database
abs: Objective: To investigate the prevalence of germline pathogenic variants (GPVs) in cervical cancer and their possible contribution to carcinogenesis. Methods: Using the C-CAT (Center for Cancer Genomics and Advanced Therapeutics) database, we collected variant data from cervical cancer patients. Variant annotations and pathogenicity classifications were re-evaluated according to the ACMG/AMP guidelines. GPVs were extracted from tumor-normal paired analyses. For tumor-only testing, presumed GPVs (PGPVs) of 26 genes with high germline conversion rates were extracted according to the "Guideline for handling GPV/PGPV in comprehensive genomic profiling (2025)"; for liquid biopsy testing, PGPVs of 73 genes were identified using our original germline/somatic sorting algorithm. GPV/ PGPV frequencies were calculated and compared with other cohorts. Results: A total of 2,585 cervical cancer cases were analyzed. Median age was 51 years (range: 15-90). Pathological diagnoses included 1,259 squamous cell carcinomas, 808 adenocarcinomas, 164 neuroendocrine carcinomas, and 354 others/unclassified. Among 299 tumor-normal paired cases, eight GPVs (2.7%) were identified. From 2,076 tumor-only and 210 liquid biopsy panels, 158 (7.6%) and seven PGPVs (3.3%) were detected, respectively. For BRCA1/2, five GPVs (1.7%) and 62 PGPVs (2.7%) were found, slightly exceeding the C- CAT off-tumor cohort prevalence (1.2%). Conclusions: A relatively high GPV/PGPV prevalence in cervical cancer was observed in C- CAT, suggesting a possible association between germline alterations and carcinogenesis.

title: A genome -wide association study for dementia with grain.
en: A genome -wide association study for dementia with grain.
abs: Argyrophilic grain (AG) is an age-associated neurodegenerative accumulation of 4-repeat (R) tau in dendritic spines. Dementia with grain (DG) is defined as AGs with a sole pathological basis for cognitive decline. As with other multifactorial diseases, DG could result from interactions of environmental and genetic factors. Other neurogenerative disorders characterized by abnormal aggregates of 4R tau, corticobasal degeneration (CBD) and progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP), have the major genetic risk factor, the H1 haplotype of MAPT locus. However, the genetic basis of DG is largely unknown. To clarify the genetic architecture of DG pathogenesis, we conducted a genome-wide association studies (GWAS) with 214 DG cases versus 12,405 controls (DG-GWAS) and 214 DG cases versus 4,015 Alzheimer's disease (AD)(DG-AD GWAS). We have identified three candidate loci associated with the risk of DG, the SVIL locus on chr10, the NBAS locus on chr2, and the PLPPR1 locus on chr9 at both GWAS. Transcriptome-wide association analysis using summary statistics for DG-GWAS identified DAPK2 as a novel candidate causal gene for DG pathogenesis in the brain frontal cortex. The genetic association analysis for the APOE locus revealed that the APOE allele did not affect DG pathogenesis. We also identified new variants in MAPT encoding tau protein that could potentially affect DG pathology. This is the first report on the genetic basis for DG. Our findings provide biological and clinical insights into the pathogenesis of DG.

title: Pharmacogenomic architecture of antihypertensive switching implicates neurotensin-NTSR1 signaling in ACE inhibitor cough
en: Pharmacogenomic architecture of antihypertensive switching implicates neurotensin-NTSR1 signaling in ACE inhibitor cough
abs: Background and Aims: Up to half of patients switch or discontinue antihypertensive drugs within the first year, but underlying mechanisms remain elusive. We identified genetic predictors of antihypertensive drug use trajectories in the first year. Methods: Using longitudinal drug data from >400,000 genotyped antihypertensive drug users in FinnGen, the UK Biobank, and the Estonian Biobank, we classified short-term antihypertensive drug use trajectories as Continue, Switch, or Discontinue. We then performed genome-wide association studies and downstream analyses across five drug classes. Results: We identified 14 genome-wide significant loci for switching from angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors (ACEI) and dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (dCCB) to other antihypertensive drugs. For ACEI switching, evidence converged on the neurotensin-NTSR1 pathway, including a 320-fold Finnish-enriched protective missense variant in the neurotensin receptor gene NTSR1 (rs148569146 [G301R], odds ratio [OR] 0.49, P=3.3×10-43) and a variant near RASSF9 (rs181941187, OR=0.74, P=1.2×10-49) tagging the neurotensin gene NTS. In drug-gene interaction analyses, NTSR1 G301R conferred reduced ACEI-induced cough risk (OR=0.39, P=8.1×10-4). The dCCB switching locus at CYP3A43 was in near-complete linkage (r2=0.99) with the functional CYP3A4*22 allele (rs35599367, OR=1.23, P=6.1×10-10). Conclusions: We extend the bradykinin hypothesis of ACEI-induced cough by implicating neurotensin-NTSR1 signaling and pinpointing CYP3A4*22 as a novel functional predictor of dCCB switching.

title: Cardiometabolic multi-trait polygenic risk score is associated with vascular dementia risk
en: Cardiometabolic multi-trait polygenic risk score is associated with vascular dementia risk
abs: Vascular dementia (VaD) is the second most common subtype of dementia and a complex neurocognitive disorder influenced by both environmental exposures and genetic susceptibility. Although previous studies have linked genetic predisposition to individual vascular risk factors with VaD, an integrated polygenic architecture underlying VaD was unexplored. We therefore investigated the associations of a cardiometabolic multi-trait polygenic risk score (mPRS) with VaD. This study targeted 9,503 Japanese adults (Mean age: 73 years old, Women: 57.5%) who participated in the Japan Prospective Studies Collaboration for Aging and Dementia (JPSC-AD) Study. We applied the PRS-CS method to calculate 12 single-trait PRSs using summary statistics from genome-wide association studies in the Biobank Japan Project. We integrated these PRSs to construct mPRS, with trait-specific weights from leave-one-site-out ridge regression. After the 5-year follow-up period, 985 participants developed all-cause dementia, including 146 VaD cases. Single-trait PRS analyses showed that PRSs for systolic blood pressure and chronic heart failure were positively associated with VaD (false discovery rate (FDR) < 0.05). Cardiometabolic mPRS showed an independent association with VaD (odds ratio per SD: 1.46, p=1.47×10-5), while it showed modest discriminatory capacity for VaD with an area under the curve of 0.569. These findings highlight that cardiometabolic polygenic burden contributes to VaD, suggesting potential utility for early risk stratification and primary prevention.

title: East Asian-specific genetic architecture of circulating plasma metabolite concentrations
en: East Asian-specific genetic architecture of circulating plasma metabolite concentrations
abs: Metabolome-genome-wide association studies (MGWAS) have improved our understanding of the genetic factors of metabolites, providing valuable insights into how lifestyle influences disease development. We performed an MGWAS of 48 plasma metabolites measured using NMR in 31,232 Japanese participants from the Tohoku Medical Megabank Community-Based Cohort Study. We identified 317 independent variant-metabolite associations, including 161 new associations. These results build on previous MGWAS by expanding both ancestry and metabolite coverage. As the East Asian-enriched variant rs671 showed the broadest pleiotropic associations, we examined rs671 in detail, including models of rs671, daily alcohol consumption, and their interactions. Rs671 showed significant direct associations with only four metabolites, suggesting that most rs671-metabolite links depend on alcohol consumption. In contrast, daily alcohol consumption was associated with a wide range of metabolites and biochemical traits that are often modified by the rs671 SNP. These findings imply that rs671 influences metabolism not only through differences in drinking behavior but also by changing how alcohol affects metabolism. The association patterns were well-matched to the glutathione-related metabolic responses, leading us to propose a mechanism involving disruption of glutathione balance in rs671_A carriers. Our study underscores the East Asian-specific genetic architecture of metabolites and highlights rs671 as a key regulator of alcohol-related metabolic variations.

title: Clinical Genetics, Bayesian Interpretation, and BRCA1/2 Spectrum in Fukushima
en: Clinical Genetics, Bayesian Interpretation, and BRCA1/2 Spectrum in Fukushima
abs: Background: In radiation-affected regions, assessing whether ambient dose, exposure age, and BRCA1/2 spectra increase the posterior probability of a radiation-origin hypothesis is clinically and scientifically important. Methods: We analyzed 177 breast cancer patients who underwent BRCA1/2 testing after counseling from July 2020 to December 2025. BRCA positivity was limited to pathogenic variants. HER2 2+/FISH-negative tumors were HER2-negative, PgR negativity was 0%, and two or more primary breast cancers included bilateral, ipsilateral multiple, or metachronous cancers. We used Bayes' formula, P(R|D)=P(D|R)P(R)/[P(D|R)P(R)+P(D|non-R)P(non-R)], with robust Poisson regression. Results: Pathogenic BRCA1/2 variants were found in 34 patients (19.2%): BRCA1 in 15 and BRCA2 in 19. PgR negativity and TNBC at 60 years or younger were associated with BRCA positivity in univariable analyses. In multivariable analysis, two or more primary breast cancers remained independently associated with BRCA positivity (IRR 2.30, 95% CI 1.23-4.29; p=0.009), whereas PgR negativity was attenuated and young-onset TNBC retained an association. These features showed no association with dose, distance, or exposure age. Variants were mainly loss-of-function, without structural enrichment, domain clustering, abnormal hotspot, or C-to- T/G-to-A pattern. Conclusion: Bayesian interpretation suggests that the data support general germline BRCA1/2 clinical-genetic features more than low-dose radiation-specific effects, providing a Fukushima baseline for counseling and precision medicine.

title: Ethnic distribution of EYS pathogenic variants detected in Japanese patients across global genomic databases
en: Ethnic distribution of EYS pathogenic variants detected in Japanese patients across global genomic databases
abs: Purpose: Eyes shut homolog (EYS) is the most common genetic cause of autosomal recessive retinitis pigmentosa (RP) in Japan. This study aimed to investigate the ethnic distribution of EYS pathogenic variants detected in Japanese patients by calculating their cumulative allele frequencies (CAF) across multiple ethnic groups in an international genomic database. Methods: We evaluated EYS pathogenic variants detected in 1,204 previously reported Japanese patients with RP (Koyanagi Y et al., J Med Genet. 2019). CAF was calculated for seven ethnic groups in the Genome Aggregation Database (gnomAD): East Asian (EAS), South Asian (SAS), Admixed American (AMR), Non- Finnish European (NFE), African/African American (AFR), Finnish (FIN), Ashkenazi Jewish (ASJ). Results: EAS showed the highest CAF at 1.318%, markedly exceeding the total population CAF of 0.129%. All other ethnic groups showed substantially lower frequencies: SAS (0.080%), AMR (0.053%), NFE (0.044%), AFR (0.025%), FIN (0.016%) and ASJ (0.000%). Conclusions: EYS pathogenic variants detected in Japanese patients show marked East-Asian specificity, with substantially lower frequencies in South Asian and American populations, and exceedingly low rates in other global groups. These findings provide a foundation for population-tailored medicine and genetic counseling for RP.

title: Systematic Re-evaluation of Genetic Variants in Pediatric Inherited Arrhythmia Syndrome
en: Systematic Re-evaluation of Genetic Variants in Pediatric Inherited Arrhythmia Syndrome
abs: Background: Interpretation of genetic variants associated with pediatric inherited arrhythmia syndromes may change over time as genetic knowledge evolves. However, variant reclassification in pediatric arrhythmia cohorts remains insufficiently characterized. Methods: Pediatric patients with inherited arrhythmia syndromes followed at Aichi Childrens Health and Medical Center between 2005 and 2025 were retrospectively included. Genetic variants identified through clinical genetic testing in 77 pediatric probands and their family members (200 genetic tests) were systematically re-evaluated at the variant level using updated American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics criteria. Re-evaluation incorporated population databases, ClinVar, published literature, in silico prediction tools, and functional evidence. Results: A total of 62 variants across 10 arrhythmia-related genes were re-evaluated. The most frequently affected genes were KCNQ1 (n=19), KCNH2 (n=13), and RYR2 (n=10). Following re-evaluation, 49 variants (80%) remained classified as pathogenic or likely pathogenic, whereas 12 variants (20%) were reclassified as variants of uncertain significance or likely benign. No benign or likely benign variants were upgraded to pathogenic or likely pathogenic. Conclusions: Systematic re-evaluation of genetic variants in pediatric inherited arrhythmia syndromes corrected potential overclassification while preserving the stability of benign variants. Periodic reinterpretation may improve long-term genetic diagnosis and clinical management in pediatric patients.

title: Shwachman-Diamond syndrome as a mitochondrial disease mimic identified by integrated genomic and transcriptomic analysis
en: Shwachman-Diamond syndrome as a mitochondrial disease mimic identified by integrated genomic and transcriptomic analysis
abs: Mitochondrial diseases are clinically and genetically heterogeneous disorders that often present with multisystem involvement, including growth failure, neurological symptoms, liver dysfunction, and impaired mitochondrial function. We have performed genetic investigations in patients suspected of having mitochondrial disease using whole-exome sequencing (WES), whole-genome sequencing (WGS), and RNA sequencing (RNA-seq). Through this comprehensive diagnostic approach, we unexpectedly identified pathogenic variants in SBDS, the causative gene of Shwachman- Diamond syndrome, in six patients initially suspected for mitochondrial disease. All six patients carried combinations of a known stop-gain variant and splice variant in SBDS that were identified by WES or WGS. In selected cases, RNA-seq confirmed aberrant splicing, providing functional evidence for pathogenicity. Clinically, many patients showed features overlapping with mitochondrial disease, including liver involvement and reduced oxygen consumption in patient-derived fibroblasts. These findings suggest that Shwachman- Diamond syndrome can mimic mitochondrial disease and may be associated with secondary mitochondrial dysfunction. Integrated genomic and transcriptomic analyses are valuable for identifying noncanonical mitochondrial disease mimics and improving diagnostic accuracy.

title: Genetic Landscape and Clinical Features in 282 Japanese Patients with Thoracic Aortic Aneurysm and Dissection
en: Genetic Landscape and Clinical Features in 282 Japanese Patients with Thoracic Aortic Aneurysm and Dissection
abs: Background: Thoracic aortic aneurysm and dissection (TAAD) exhibits genetic and phenotypic heterogeneity, and data on Asian patients are limited. We aimed to clarify the genetic landscape and clinical features of TAAD in a large Japanese cohort. Methods: We performed whole-exome sequencing in 282 Japanese patients with TAAD. Variants in 40 established TAAD-associated genes were classified according to ACMG guidelines as pathogenic (P), likely pathogenic (LP), or variants of uncertain significance (VUS). Clinical data, including age at onset, family history, and syndromic features, were collected and compared between variant-positive and variant-negative patients. Results: P/LP variants were identified in 2-3% of patients, mainly in FBN1 and rarely in other TAAD genes. Several variants recurred in unrelated families, suggesting possible founder mutations. Many unreported variants were observed across multiple genes, most classified as VUS and broadly distributed without a single dominant gene. The median age at onset in the overall cohort was 59 years, whereas patients with P/LP variants presented at a median age of 36 years, indicating earlier onset in monogenic cases. Conclusions: This study provides a population-specific overview of the genetic landscape of TAAD in Japanese patients. It highlights founder-like recurrent variants, many unreported changes, and earlier onset in P/LP carriers, and may inform future functional studies, longitudinal phenotyping, and consideration of updates to diagnostic criteria and testing strategies.

title: Assessment of Genetic Risk and Clinical Outcomes in Heritable Thoracic Aortic Disease: A Japanese Cohort of 41 Patients
en: Assessment of Genetic Risk and Clinical Outcomes in Heritable Thoracic Aortic Disease: A Japanese Cohort of 41 Patients
abs: Background: Diagnostic criteria and intervention thresholds for heritable thoracic aortic disease (HTAD) have been established primarily based on Western cohorts, and their applicability to Japanese patients remains unclear. We evaluated the utility of genetic analysis for risk stratification and clinical outcome assessment in Japanese HTAD. Methods: A total of forty-one unrelated probands and five relatives, classified as syndromic (n=14), non-syndromic (n=17), or systemic-only phenotype (n=10), were analyzed by HTAD panel sequencing. Results: Pathogenic or likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants were identified in 27% of probands (11/41). FBN1 was the predominant disease gene (10/11 P/LP cases) and accounted for 50% of the syndromic subgroup (7/14). Compared with Western patients, Japanese FBN1 carriers exhibited milder systemic manifestations, including lower Ghent scores and fewer skeletal and ocular features, despite a comparable risk of aortic events. Three novel variants were identified, and four variants were reclassified from VUS to P/LP, improving genetic counseling and family screening. Notably, 55% of patients with P/LP variants experienced aortic dissection at near-normal aortic diameters. Conclusion: Japanese HTAD patients exhibit milder systemic phenotypes while remaining susceptible to aortic dissection at diameters below conventional surgical thresholds. These findings underscore the importance of incorporating genetic information into risk assessment and the need for population-specific diagnostic and management strategies to advance precision medicine in HTAD

title: Identifying EOLA1 Loss of Function as a Novel Cause of X-Linked Mitochondrial Translation Disease
en: Identifying EOLA1 Loss of Function as a Novel Cause of X-Linked Mitochondrial Translation Disease
abs: Background : The patient was a boy born at 37 weeks by uneventful normal spontaneous delivery with unremarkable antenatal progress. He was admitted at day 23 for prolonged neonatal jaundice and irritability. The head circumference, weight, and length were below the third percentiles. Biochemical, hematological, and sepsis workups were unremarkable. However, the patient exhibited persistently elevated plasma lactate (3.4–9.4 mmol/L) and a high cerebrospinal fluid lactate of 3.5 mmol/L. Magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) demonstrated prominent lactate peaks within the bilateral basal ganglia and the frontal and parieto-occipital white matter, highly suggestive of an underlying mitochondrial disease. Methods : In our previous investigations into undiagnosed rare diseases, whole-exome sequencing (WES) was used to identify novel disease genes in patients with diagnostic odysseys. The novel gene in the present case was identified through trio-based WES and bulk RNA sequencing of peripheral blood. Results : WES identified hemizygous EOLA1: c.368_369del p.(Val123Aspfs*13) in the patient inherited from the asymptomatic mother. RNA sequencing showed mRNA with the frameshift variant, suggesting that the mRNA transcript with the frameshift variant escapes nonsense-mediated decay. EOLA1 was previously shown to localize within the mitochondria and EOLA1-knockout cells exhibit reduced mRNA and protein levels of mitochondrially translated subunits within the electron transport chain. Conclusions : In summary, we have identified EOLA1 as a novel cause of X-linked mitochondrial translation defects in an infant presenting with developmental delay and persistent lactic acidosis. The EOLA1 gene should be incorporated into targeted gene panels for the evaluation of undiagnosed inherited metabolic and neurodevelopmental diseases.

title: Perceptions of Family Planning Among Patients and Families with Retinoblastoma: A qualitative study
en: Perceptions of Family Planning Among Patients and Families with Retinoblastoma: A qualitative study
abs: Background: Retinoblastoma (RB) is a rare pediatric tumor occurring in one in 15,000 individuals, with 40-50% of cases caused by pathogenic germline RB1 variants. Preimplantation genetic testing for monogenic disorders (PGT-M) for RB was approved in Japan for the first time in 2023. This study explored perceptions of family planning among patients with RB and their families in the current medical and social context. Methods: We reviewed patients with RB who visited our genetic counseling clinic between January 2022 and April 2026. Medical records were examined to identify reasons for consultation, and patient and family member statements were extracted and qualitatively analyzed. Results: Seventy-five individuals visited during the study period: 40 pediatric probands with their parents, 31 adult probands, and 4 other cases. Some adult probands (67.7%) attended the consultation accompanied by family members or partners. Eight thematic categories emerged, including: desire to understand genetic testing for future children, desire to obtain information necessary for decision-making, feelings of difficulty in undergoing PGT-M. Conclusion: This study identified adult RB survivors who sought information about their hereditary conditions and reproductive options in relation to life events, as well as parents of patients with RB. Given that some patients experience anxiety about the inheritance of RB and wish to take proactive steps, providing tailored medical options may support their family planning and decision-making.

title: Family Communication of Genetic Risk: Lifeworld Integration Through a Dynamic Process
en: Family Communication of Genetic Risk: Lifeworld Integration Through a Dynamic Process
abs: Background: Intrafamilial communication of genetic risk is important for relatives' health management, yet remains insufficient. Psychological processes underlying family communication and subsequent interactions remain unclear. Objective: This study aimed to clarify genetic risk perceptions, family communication processes, and post-communication interactions from the perspectives of clients and relatives. Methods: Questionnaire surveys were conducted with 62 clients and 52 relatives who received genetic counseling at the University of Tsukuba Hospital. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 33 participants. Data were analyzed using Steps for Coding and Theorization with reference to the Health Belief Model. Results: Genetic risk perceptions were reconstructed through lived experiences and risk communication, shaping readiness for family communication. Post-communication interactions included emotional sharing, relationship adjustment, relational distance, and differences in perceptions. Anxiety, relief, acceptance, and regret coexisted depending on context. Through these interactions, perceptions of genetic risk were integrated into the lifeworld through reinterpretation of values, emotional stabilization, and reorganization of daily life. Conclusions: Family communication of genetic risk was a dynamic process involving reconstruction of genetic risk perceptions, readiness formation, family interactions, and lifeworld integration. The findings suggest the importance of support that considers post-communication interactions and changes in meaning-making.

title: Genetic counseling for APOE ε4 variant as the secondary finding in multigene testing for familial hypercholesterolemia
en: Genetic counseling for APOE ε4 variant as the secondary finding in multigene testing for familial hypercholesterolemia
abs: Background; The APOE gene is included in a multigenic panel test targeting familial hypercholesterolemia(FH). Genome-wide association studies have linked APOE to various phenotypes, including Alzheimer Disease(AD), hyperlipidemia, myocardial infarction, aortic aneurysm and coronary artery disease. Apolipoprotein ε4 variant(rs429358) is a common DNA variant substituting arginine for cysteine at codon 112. Based on the allele frequency in Japanese, about 15% of Japanese people have at least one ε4 allele. Detection of common ε4 variant suggests a possible modifier of the hyperlipemia such as familial combined hyperlipidemia, while ε4 variant is one of the established risk factors for the onset of Alzheimer disease (AD) and appropriate disclosure of the APOE-related secondary findings in genetic counseling is ethically important issue. Case Report; In FH genetic testing, the ε4 variant is detected in over 40% of cases, underscoring the need for pre and post-test counseling on future AD risk. We conducted a qualitative analysis of result disclosure, patient preferences, psychological responses, and challenges in risk acceptance. Results and Discussion; In most ε4 heterozygotes, AD shows incomplete penetrance with onset in the late 70s, while dyslipidemia precedes by decades. As APOE4 indicates future dementia risk, disclosure preferences varied. For APOE4 carriers, preventive information reduced psychological burden and supported acceptance. These highlight the need for pre-test counseling and standardized communication tools for result disclosure.

title: Expanding NIPT Consultations Among Younger Pregnant Women: Subjective Anxiety and the Role of Genetic Counseling
en: Expanding NIPT Consultations Among Younger Pregnant Women: Subjective Anxiety and the Role of Genetic Counseling
abs: Background: After age restrictions for NIPT were removed under Japan's certification system, counseling requests from younger pregnant women increased. Although trisomy risk is related to maternal age, some clients seek NIPT to reduce anxiety rather than because of high medical risk. Objective: To examine age trends among NIPT genetic counseling clients and discuss the gap between statistical risk and subjective anxiety. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed pregnant women who received NIPT genetic counseling from October 2022 to March 2026. Consultation numbers, age groups, and testing rates were summarized. Because NIPT started at our clinic in October 2022, age trends were analyzed by half-year periods. Results: Consultations numbered 80 in the second half of FY2022, 204 in FY2023, 236 in FY2024, and 402 in FY2025, totaling 922. NIPT was performed in 830 cases, with an overall testing rate of 90.0%. Clients aged 25-29 years increased from 7 (8.8%) in the second half of FY2022 to 49 (23.1%) in the second half of FY2025. Those aged 30-34 years increased from 11 (13.8%) to 67 (31.6%). Clients aged 25-34 years increased from 18 (22.5%) to 116 (54.7%). Discussion: The increase in younger clients suggests that NIPT is expanding beyond women with high age-related risk. For clients, low statistical risk may still be experienced as a binary concern about whether their own child is affected. Conclusion: Genetic counseling should support scientific risk understanding while also addressing anxiety, values, and disability-related concerns.

title: A female with Fabry disease who underwent arrhythmia treatment and chaperone following cascade screening
en: A female with Fabry disease who underwent arrhythmia treatment and chaperone following cascade screening
abs: Fabry disease is an X-linked lysosomal storage disorder, and it is difficult to diagnose in heterozygous females. The patient was a woman in her 60s who was referred to our facility because her grandson was diagnosed with Fabry disease following newborn screening, followed by the diagnosed of her daughter. She had been noted to have arrhythmia for over 30 years and had been under observation at a local clinic. Her genetic testing identified the same GLA variant found in her grandson. This variant is responsive to pharmacological chemical chaperone. She was also referred to the cardiology department, where cardiac evaluation revealed cardiac hypertrophy and elevated cardiac enzymes level, so treatment was initiated. During follow-up genetic counseling, enzyme replacement therapy and chemical chaperone were explained, she opted treatment with chaperone therapy. When the patient was diagnosed, she felt guilty that the familial GLA variant had been passed on to her daughter and grandson. However, during genetic counseling, her daughter told the patient that the diagnosis through her son had been meaningful for the family, which helped the patient accept treatment with a positive outlook. In particular, in women with Fabry disease, diagnosis may be missed because there are no clear subjective symptoms. Genetic counseling, as well as consideration of genetic testing for relatives, is beneficial regardless of sex for families. With expanded newborn screening now in place, more women with Fabry disease are likely to be diagnosed in the future.

title: How Do We Support Children with Gorlin Syndrome? A Case of a Young Athlete
en: How Do We Support Children with Gorlin Syndrome? A Case of a Young Athlete
abs: Background: Gorlin syndrome is a tumor predisposition syndrome caused by PTCH1 variants and characterized by developmental anomalies and basal cell carcinoma (BCC) predisposition. Multiple odontogenic keratocysts are an important childhood clue. After diagnosis, counseling may be challenging when preventive recommendations affect daily life. Case: An 11-year-old boy with cleft lip and palate, ventriculomegaly, and ventricular septal defect was found to have multiple odontogenic keratocysts at age 10. Additional findings included fused vertebrae, Sprengel deformity, and facial features consistent with Gorlin syndrome. Molecular testing identified a pathogenic PTCH1 variant. After diagnosis, sun protection became a concern due to BCC risk. The patient was a soccer goalkeeper and wished to continue playing. Hats, sunscreen, and long sleeves were recommended, but evidence on safe ultraviolet exposure during outdoor sports is limited. Teammates and coaches supported him by wearing hats themselves and encouraging sunscreen use during practice, providing psychological support for the family. Discussion: This case highlights the challenge of counseling children with hereditary tumor predisposition syndromes when preventive recommendations conflict with valued activities. Repeated counseling was required because safe levels of ultraviolet exposure remain undefined, making it difficult to balance risk reduction with the patient's wish to continue soccer. Counseling should support informed decision-making while considering the child's values, quality of life, and social support.

title: Expanding phenotypic spectrum of SMARCA5-related neurodevelopmental disorders
en: Expanding phenotypic spectrum of SMARCA5-related neurodevelopmental disorders
abs: The SMARCA5 gene encodes a protein forming a NURF complex along with BPTF and SMARCA1 to function as a chromatin remodeling factor and nucleosome spacing ruler together with CTCF. In 2018, 12 patients with neurodevelopmental disorders harboring pathogenic variants in SMARCA5 were reported; however, their detailed clinical presentation remains unclear. Here, we report a patient with SMARCA5-related neurodevelopmental disorder. The patient is a 27-year-old male who presents with postnatal growth retardation, microcephaly (-3 SD), and motor developmental delay, as well as a thoracic vertebral compression fracture of unknown etiology during adolescence. He presents with moderate intellectual disability (IQ approximately 50), short stature (-3 SD), malocclusion, recurrent alopecia areata, and distinctive facial features (narrow palpebral fissures, micrognathia). We identified a previously-reported pathogenic variant in the SMARCA5 gene (NM_003601.3) c.1301_1306del, p.(Ile434_Leu435del) by whole-exome sequencing. In addition to common features such as a microcephaly, short stature, developmental delay, and dysmorphic facial features, this patient presents with autoimmune disease and dental abnormalities, suggesting these may expand the phenotypic spectrum of SMARCA5-related neurodevelopmental disorders. BPTF, SMARCA1, and CTCF, which function in concert with SMARCA5, are also associated with neurodevelopmental disorders and may share common phenotypes. SMARCA5-related neurodevelopmental disorders may be classified as chromatin remodeling disorders.

title: GWAS and Single-Nucleus Transcriptomics Identify Mesenchymal-Like Endothelial Cells in Moyamoya Disease
en: GWAS and Single-Nucleus Transcriptomics Identify Mesenchymal-Like Endothelial Cells in Moyamoya Disease
abs: Moyamoya disease (MMD) is a rare cerebrovascular disorder characterized by progressive stenosis of intracranial arteries and the development of abnormal collateral vessels. Although the rare RNF213 variant (p. R4810K, rs112735431) is strongly associated with MMD in East Asian populations, the broader genetic architecture and underlying cellular mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, we performed an integrative analysis combining genome-wide association studies (GWAS) and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) to identify susceptibility loci and disease-associated cellular states in MMD. GWAS identified multiple risk loci, including an HDAC9/ TWIST1 locus and a protective missense variant in RNF213 independent of the known rs112735431 risk allele. Using snRNA-seq of vascular tissue, we identified a distinct population of mesenchymal-like endothelial cells (MECs) that retained canonical endothelial markers while additionally expressing mesenchymal markers. Integration of genetic association signals with cell type specific expression profiles revealed significant enrichment of GWAS signals in MECs, supporting their potential role in MMD pathogenesis. Our findings demonstrate the value of integrating human genetics and single-cell transcriptomics to elucidate disease mechanisms and highlight MEC activation as a potential therapeutic target in MMD.

title: Updating Gene Lists for Intractable Diseases in Japan: Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia as a Model
en: Updating Gene Lists for Intractable Diseases in Japan: Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia as a Model
abs: Genetic testing under the Japanese designated intractable disease system and national health insurance is essential for rare disease care. Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) is a heterogeneous disorder causing chronic sinusitis, respiratory infections, bronchiectasis, situs inversus, and infertility. In Japan, PCD is included in designated intractable disease No. 340, "ciliary dyskinesia syndrome," and genetic testing has recently entered insured practice. Using PCD as a model, we examined how causative gene lists should be updated. We compared 51 PCD-related genes in the Japanese diagnostic criteria, 26 genes in an insured panel, and 58 genes in GeneReviews 2025. PCD genes have been continuously identified since DNAI1 in 1999, and recent international resources include genes not listed in the current Japanese criteria. The three resources did not fully overlap, reflecting differences in purpose, evidence evaluation, implementation, and update cycle. These differences should be viewed as a gap between stable administrative systems and continually updated disease genetics, rather than simply as deficiencies or delays. Updating gene lists requires structured evaluation of phenotype consistency, inheritance, evidence, functional plausibility, domestic cases, and clinical implementation. A web-based platform being developed with the National Institute of Genetics may support candidate gene sharing and expert review. This study proposes a framework for transforming designated intractable disease gene lists from static lists into continuously updated knowledge resources.

title: Population-Based Genomic Analysis Reveals an Expanded Spectrum of NOTCH3-Related Arteriopathy in Japan
en: Population-Based Genomic Analysis Reveals an Expanded Spectrum of NOTCH3-Related Arteriopathy in Japan
abs: Background: NOTCH3 causes cerebral autosomal dominant arteriopathy with subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy (CADASIL). East Asian founder and cysteine-sparing variants imply unrecognized carriers and challenge cysteine-based classification, but their distribution and clinical/imaging phenotypes remain unclear. Methods: In this cross-sectional analysis of data from the Japan Prospective Studies Collaboration for Aging and Dementia (JPSC-AD), NOTCH3 coding and splice-adjacent regions were sequenced in 10,277 participants; carrier groups were assessed for geography, white matter hyperintensity (WMH), stroke, and dementia. Results: We found 14 cysteine-altering variants in 36 carriers and 3 ClinVar pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants in 12 carriers: p.Arg75Pro (n=7), p.Arg544Cys (n=4), and p.Arg153His (n=1). p.Arg75Pro was cysteine-sparing; p.Arg544Cys overlapped the cysteine-altering group. P/LP carriers clustered at 2 western sites (Fisher exact test P=.027). Age-sex adjusted WMH burden was higher in cysteine-altering and P/LP carriers (both P<.001). In multivariable Firth models with imputation, cysteine-altering variants were not associated with stroke or dementia, whereas P/LP variants were associated with stroke (odds ratio [OR]=14.26; 95% confidence interval [CI], 4.59-44.31) and dementia (OR=6.06; 95% CI, 1.48-24.81). Conclusions: Community genomic screening identified clustered NOTCH3 P/LP variants, including cysteine-sparing p.Arg75Pro, refining disease understanding beyond cysteine-based classification and clinically recognized CADASIL.

title: Practical considerations for RNA-seq in diagnosing rare diseases
en: Practical considerations for RNA-seq in diagnosing rare diseases
abs: RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) is increasingly used to detect splicing and expression abnormalities in rare diseases; however, its practical limitations remain incompletely understood. We evaluated the utility and limitations of RNA-seq from 20 Coffin-Siris syndrome cases with previously identified pathogenic variants (3 splice variants and 17 SNVs/small indels) as positive controls. Using lymphoblastoid cell line (LCL)-derived RNA, we examined variant detection and splicing analysis conditions. It was difficult to detect pathogenic variants in 8/20 cases. Major factors affecting its analysis include low gene expression in LCLs, insufficient read coverage, nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD). In NMD-associated cases, abnormal transcript reads were markedly reduced, making variant detection difficult even with sufficient sequencing depth. In contrast, RT-PCR successfully confirmed splice abnormalities in several RNA-seq-negative cases. RNA-seq also contributed to variant interpretation in selected unresolved exome-negative cases through transcript-level evidence. These findings demonstrate that RNA-seq performance is strongly influenced by gene expression, transcript stability, and sequencing depth under the analytical conditions. While RNA-seq is a useful tool for rare disease diagnostics, negative findings alone are insufficient to exclude splicing abnormalities, highlighting the importance of integrated interpretation with genomic analysis and RT-PCR.

title: Iso-Seq reveals aberrant full-length transcripts caused by SMARCB1 and WDR45 genomic deletions
en: Iso-Seq reveals aberrant full-length transcripts caused by SMARCB1 and WDR45 genomic deletions
abs: HiFi long-read sequencing on the Revio platform generates long and accurate reads. Iso-Seq with the Kinnex full-length RNA kit enables high-throughput analysis of full-length cDNA molecules and direct evaluation of complex splicing patterns on individual isoform transcripts. We performed Iso-Seq using RNA from patient-derived lymphoblastoid cell lines in two cases with partial deletions involving SMARCB1 and WDR45. In the SMARCB11 case, a 9001-bp deletion including exon 9 of NM_003073.5 was identified. Iso-Seq detected five major aberrant transcripts lacking the normal last exon, including one with intron retention after exon 8 and others incorporating downstream sequences or cryptic exons. All were predicted to lack the normal C-terminal sequence and to introduce premature termination codons after short aberrant amino acid sequences. In the WDR45 case, a 2912-bp deletion from intron 1 to part of exon 7 of NM_001029896.2 was identified. Iso-Seq detected five major aberrant transcripts with distinct 5-prime structures, all sharing loss of a 516-bp segment containing the initiation codon. Short-read RNA sequencing can infer transcript changes, but direct linkage of multiple splicing events and deletion-associated sequences within the same molecule has been difficult to display. By resolving full-length transcripts at the molecule level, Iso-Seq clarified directly how genomic deletions altered cDNA structure and coding potential. These findings highlight the value of long-read transcriptome analysis for functional interpretation of disease-associated structural variants.

title: Etiologic analysis of megalocephaly by activated variant of AKT3 using mice model and potential of rapamycin treatment
en: Etiologic analysis of megalocephaly by activated variant of AKT3 using mice model and potential of rapamycin treatment
abs: The AKT3 protein, a component of the PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway, is highly expressed in the brain. Activating variants of the AKT3 gene causes megalencephaly-polymicrogyria-polydactyly-hydrocephalus syndrome 2 [OMIM: #615937]; however, its etiology is poorly understood and no treatment is established. We identified a novel AKT3 variant, c.233A>G, p.Q78R, in a patient exhibiting megalencephaly, cortical malformation, and epilepsy. We aimed to clarify the etiology by generating a knock-in mouse mimicking the patient's variant, termed as the Akt3QR mouse. They were born at Mendelian ratios and their phenotypes replicated those of the patient: megalencephaly occurred from embryonic stage and spontaneous seizures, thus we considered them suitable mice model for functional analysis, assessment of natural history, and development of treatment for AKT3 aberrations. The brain of Akt3QR showed somatic enlargement of neurons. Furthermore, these mice exhibited increased phosphorylation of Akt3 and downstream proteins, indicating hyperactivated PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway. While Akt3QR exhibited a shortened latency to pentylenetetrazol-induced seizures indicating increased seizure susceptibility, the administration of mTOR inhibitor rapamycin prolonged latency period for seizure onset and reduced neuronal hypertrophy. These results suggest that therapeutic strategies targeting the downstream of the PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway could effectively improve the pathological condition and suppress symptoms. We are continuing to investigate this possibility, including the use of another gene therapy method.

title: Urine-derived cells reveal autophagy defects caused by in-frame EPG5 variants
en: Urine-derived cells reveal autophagy defects caused by in-frame EPG5 variants
abs: Background: Vici syndrome is a severe multisystem disorder caused by biallelic variants in EPG5, an autophagy tether required for autophagosome-lysosome fusion. Methods: We investigated two siblings with Vici syndrome. Exome and genome sequencing were performed, followed by RNA sequencing and LC3 turnover assays using non-invasively collected patient urine-derived cells (UDCs). Patient-derived lymphoblastoid cell lines were also analyzed. Results: We identified novel compound heterozygous in-frame EPG5 variants: c.7690_7692del (p.Leu2564del) and an 8,298-bp intragenic deletion involving exons 17-22 (c.3098+2113_3983+337del). RNA sequencing of UDCs detected an aberrant splice junction from exon 16 to exon 23, consistent with in-frame skipping of exons 17-22, while total EPG5 mRNA expression was preserved. LC3 turnover assays showed elevated basal LC3-II levels and a blunted increase after bafilomycin A1 treatment in patient UDCs, indicating impaired autophagic flux. Similar abnormalities were observed in patient-derived lymphoblastoid cell lines. Conclusion: These findings provide functional evidence that biallelic in-frame EPG5 variants disrupt autophagy and cause Vici syndrome. UDCs are a practical, non-invasive cellular model for transcript and autophagy analyses in pediatric autophagy-related disorders.

title: A novel Zeb2-HA-flox mouse model for analyzing the pathomechanisms of Mowat-Wilson syndrome
ja: Mowat-Wilson症候群の病態機序解析のための新規Zeb2-HA-floxマウスモデル
en: A novel Zeb2-HA-flox mouse model for analyzing the pathomechanisms of Mowat-Wilson syndrome
abs: Mowat-Wilson syndrome (MOWS) is a multiple congenital anomaly syndrome caused by a haploinsufficiency of the ZEB2 gene and characterized by variable but consistent phenotypes, such as typical facial features, epilepsy, severe intellectual disability, Hirschsprung disease or chronic constipation, and congenital heart disease. Previous studies have demonstrated that most cases of MOWS are caused by loss-of-function variants, such as nonsense, deletion, or frameshift variants, leading to decreased functional ZEB2 protein. However, many aspects of the etiology remain unclear, including genotype-phenotype correlations, as well as knowledge of ZEB2 protein dynamics, since it is difficult to detect the ZEB2 protein using the available antibody. To resolve this issue, we attempted to establish a conditional knockout mouse for Zeb2 that introduced HA-tag to make detection easier. We created a mouse with HA-tag sequence at the C-terminus of the endogenous Zeb2 locus using the genome editing technique, improved gonadal nucleic acid transfer (i-GONAD) method. We confirmed that immunoblotting and immunohistochemical analyses can be readily performed on Zeb2-HA mice. Next, to generate a MOWS model that reproduces disease pathology, we created a mouse with exon 6 (215 bp) flanked by loxP sequences in combination with the HA tag (Zeb2-HA-flox). This approach differs from existing approaches that target exon 8 (approximately 2 kbp), the longest exon of Zeb2 in floxed mice. Here, we will present cell biological analyses of conditionally knocked-out neurons generated using Zeb2-HA-flox mice.

title: Reduced hepatic Igf1 expression in a Noonan syndrome mouse model with Rit1 mutation
ja: Rit1変異Noonan症候群モデルマウスにおける肝Igf1発現の低下
en: Reduced hepatic Igf1 expression in a Noonan syndrome mouse model with Rit1 mutation
abs: Noonan syndrome (NS) is a RASopathy characterized by facial dysmorphisms, cardiac defects, and short stature. Abnormalities in the growth hormone (GH)- insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) axis have been implicated in the pathogenesis of short stature in NS, particularly reduced IGF-1 production associated with GH resistance. However, the pathophysiology of decreased IGF-1 production is not fully understood. In the present study, we investigated the pathogenic mechanisms underlying reduced IGF-1 production in Rit1A57G/+ knock-in mice. Rit1A57G/+ mice exhibited significantly reduced body length and lower plasma IGF-1 levels compared with wild-type (WT) mice between 4 and 12 weeks of age. Hepatocytes cultured from mice showed no significant differences between Rit1A57G/+ and WT hepatocytes in their responses to GH stimulation, as assessed by IGF-1 levels in the culture supernatant and Igf1 expression in the hepatocytes. In the absence of serum and GH, IGF-1 levels and Igf1 mRNA expression were reduced in Rit1A57G/+ hepatocytes. These findings indicate that decreased hepatic Igf1 expression leads to reduced plasma IGF-1 levels, and that the reduced Igf1 mRNA expression in Rit1A57G/+ hepatocytes is more likely attributable to decreased basal expression under GH-unstimulated conditions rather than to reduced sensitivity to GH.

title: Juvenility-oriented analysis of pediatric physiology
ja: 小児生理学の若年性指向解析
en: Juvenility-oriented analysis of pediatric physiology
abs: A unique subset of genes is expressed during a juvenile phase, which realizes distinct physiologic features in pediatric cells in comparison to adult counterparts. The genes expressed during childhood realize the child-inherent properties of size increment and functional maturation, the characteristic positive changes in children. We categorize the genes which are exclusively highly expressed in the juvenile phase as juvenility-associated genes, or JAGs, and are committed to elucidating their function and the molecular network they constitute. JAGs execute molecular functions inherent to pediatric cells, such as organellar juvenility, age-dependent alternative splicing (ADAS), senescence resistance, juvenile metabolism, and juvenile compartment. These juvenile functions are characteristic of children and underlie juvenility, the pediatric physiology that includes growth, maturation, and behavioral characteristics.
