Loss of these juvenile properties could lead to pediatric pathophysiology. Likewise, by establishing therapeutics targeting juvenile physiological properties, we may establish a new approach to regenerative medicine or cancer treatment. In this study, we will show a comprehensive gene expression study performed in mice, providing transcriptome data across an organ landscape throughout the juvenile phase, with generalizability tested in human data. Further analysis led us to a higher-resolution transcriptome analysis in the hypothalamus, which showed the unprecedented finding of a specific subset of genes which characterizes the transitions of pediatric physiology.

title: The role of hypoxia in the regulation of transforming growth factor-beta in cancer-associated fibroblasts
ja: がん関連線維芽細胞におけるTGF-β制御での低酸素の役割
en: The role of hypoxia in the regulation of transforming growth factor-beta in cancer-associated fibroblasts
abs: Background: Tumor stroma consists of diverse cell populations that contribute to the establishment of a pro-tumorigenic microenvironment. Among these, cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are key stromal components involved in tumor progression. In this study, we investigated the role of transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) in the interaction between CAFs and TAMs under hypoxic tumor microenvironment conditions. Methods: To mimic hypoxic conditions in the tumor microenvironment, M2 macrophages were treated with deferoxamine mesylate, an inhibitor of hypoxia-inducible factor 1α degradation. Expression levels of transforming growth factor-alpha (TGF-α) mRNA were subsequently analyzed using real-time quantitative PCR. Furthermore, CAFs were cultured under the same hypoxia-mimicking conditions in the presence of TGF-α, and TGF-β mRNA expression levels in CAFs were evaluated. Results: Mimic hypoxic conditions increased TGF-α mRNA expression in M2 macrophages. Under the same conditions, TGF-β mRNA expression in CAFs was also elevated. Moreover, supplementation with TGF-α further enhanced TGF-β expression in CAFs in a dose-dependent manner. Discussion: These findings indicate that TGF-α produced by TAMs may promote TGF-β expression in CAFs within the hypoxic tumor microenvironment. Although additional studies are required to confirm this mechanism, cytokine-mediated interactions between TAMs and CAFs may contribute significantly to the formation of a tumor-promoting microenvironment.

title: Genomic imprinting of Klf14 is regulated by a paternal sub-TAD anchored at Mest and a shared enhancer in mice
ja: マウスKlf14のゲノムインプリンティングはMestに係留された父性サブTADと共有エンハンサーで制御される
en: Genomic imprinting of Klf14 is regulated by a paternal sub-TAD anchored at Mest and a shared enhancer in mice
abs: Variants at the human KLF14 locus are strongly associated with type 2 diabetes and metabolic syndrome, and KLF14 acts as a master regulator of adipose gene expression. Disease-associated alleles exert effects only when maternally inherited, consistent with KLF14/Klf14 being a maternally expressed imprinted gene. However, the imprinting mechanism remains unclear. KLF14/Klf14 lies approximately 200 kb from the paternally expressed imprinted gene MEST/Mest, controlled by a maternally methylated germline differentially methylated region (gDMR). We show that Mest and Klf14 reside within the same topologically associating domain (TAD), bounded by biallelic CTCF-binding sites. Allele-specific 4C-seq revealed that CTCF binding to the unmethylated paternal Mest gDMR establishes a paternal-specific sub-TAD encompassing Klf14. CRISPR-Cas9 deletion of the paternal Mest promoter region in embryonic stem cells and mutant mice abolished Mest expression and induced biallelic Klf14 expression, demonstrating that the Mest gDMR functions as an imprinting control region (ICR). In vitro analyses in AtT-20 cells identified a shared enhancer that regulates Mest on the paternal allele and Klf14 on the maternal allele. To test whether this enhancer also functions in vivo, we are conducting 4C-seq using E10.5 mouse embryos. These findings support a model in which allele-specific chromatin architecture directs enhancer usage and imprinting. Our study reveals a long-range function of the Mest gDMR and suggests that a similar TAD-based mechanism may operate at the human KLF14 locus.

title: Scriptaid Enhances ROSI Blastocyst Development Without Altering DNA Methylation
ja: ScriptaidはDNAメチル化を変えずにROSI胚盤胞の発生を促進する
en: Scriptaid Enhances ROSI Blastocyst Development Without Altering DNA Methylation
abs: Objective: Round spermatid injection (ROSI) is an option for azoospermic patients without mature sperm, but immature sperm precursors may impair epigenetic remodeling and embryo development. This study evaluated the epigenetic safety of the HDAC inhibitor Scriptaid in ROSI using round spermatids from healthy donors and azoospermic patients. Methods: Blastocysts derived from ROSI with or without Scriptaid pretreatment were analyzed by whole-genome bisulfite sequencing. Global CpG methylation, principal component clustering, differentially methylated regions (DMRs), imprinting control regions, promoter/enhancer regions, repetitive elements, and gene ontology of DMR-related genes were assessed. Results: Scriptaid markedly improved blastocyst formation in embryos from azoospermic patients, suggesting enhanced nuclear remodeling. WGBS showed highly similar global CpG methylation profiles among groups, and principal component analysis confirmed preservation of overall epigenomic structure. DMRs were limited, indicating minimal epigenetic impact. Parent-of-origin-specific methylation at imprinting control regions, including H19, PEG10, and SNRPN, was maintained. No aberrant methylation was detected in promoter or enhancer regions, and LINE1 and LTR retrotransposons remained stable. Conclusions: Scriptaid pretreatment improved developmental competence of ROSI-derived embryos from azoospermic patients while preserving normal DNA methylation patterns. These findings support the epigenetic safety of Scriptaid as an adjunct to ROSI.

title: Clinical trial of 5-aminolevulinic acid for ATR-X syndrome
ja: ATR-X症候群に対する5-アミノレブリン酸の臨床試験
en: Clinical trial of 5-aminolevulinic acid for ATR-X syndrome
abs: Background: ATR-X syndrome (MIM: #301040) is an X-linked intellectual disability syndrome, caused by loss-of-function variants of the ATRX gene, encoding an ATP-dependent chromatin remodelling protein, ATRX. ATRX binds to G-quadruplexes (G4s) to regulate nearby gene expression. We reported that 5-aminolevulinic acid (5- ALA) could restore cognitive function in mice with ATR-X syndrome as a prodrug of protoporphyrin IX that can bind to G4s instead of mutated ATRX. Here we report our exploratory, single-centre, non-blinded, single-group clinical trial to evaluate the safety and efficacy of 5-ALA for cognitive function in five participants with ATR-X syndrome. (jRCT2051220062) Method: The investigational product (IP) is a tablet containing 25 mg of 5-ALA, and the participants took the tablet(s)for 24 weeks. The dosage depended on their weight. We evaluated the safety and efficacy of 5-ALA on cognitive and social development using several developmental batteries and an eye-tracking device at 0, 12, and 24 weeks after IP administration. We also explored biomarkers to assess the effects of 5-ALA using DNA methylation, RNA-seq, and proteome analyses. Results: Two of the five participants (40%) showed improved cognitive function during 5- ALA treatment. No severe adverse events or adverse drug reactions were observed. The biomarker analysis indicated that some transcriptional or translational changes could occur after 5-ALA treatment. Conclusion: This study indicates that 5-ALA may be a disease-modifying agent for ATR-X syndrome. Further study is needed to verify our results.

title: iPS cell-based functional genomics reveals combinatory effects of functionally opposite SNPs in linkage disequilibrium
ja: iPS細胞ベース機能ゲノミクスが明らかにする連鎖不平衡にある機能的に逆向きのSNPの複合効果
en: iPS cell-based functional genomics reveals combinatory effects of functionally opposite SNPs in linkage disequilibrium
abs: Growing numbers of disease-associated single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) have been identified. Yet, limited availability and environmental variations of clinical samples have hindered studying their function and mechanistic insights. In particular, how the combinations of regulatory variants within linkage disequilibrium (LD) blocks shape cellular phenotypes remains insufficiently understood. Here, using human iPSC-derived macrophages as a highly sensitive and reproducible platform, we functionally deconvoluted COVID-19 severity-associated variants within the chemokine receptor cluster at chromosome 3p21.31. We show that functionally opposite SNPs co-exist within a single LD block harboring the risk haplotype, and that the phenotypes are determined by their additive effects rather than by any single SNP. Notably, diverse genotype combinations at these loci are observed worldwide, undermining the phenotype prediction based on individual SNPs. Thus, our study reveals the complexity of SNPs within the risk haplotype, underscoring the need for functional evaluation of individual variants.

title: A novel MITF mutation associated with hyperpigmentation
ja: 色素沈着亢進に関連する新規MITF変異
en: A novel MITF mutation associated with hyperpigmentation
abs: Melanocytes produce pigment called melanin, which determines the color of the skin, eyes, and hair. Microphthalmia-associated transcription factor (MITF) promotes melanocyte development and differentiation through activating pigment genes and fundamental genes for cell homeostasis, including cell cycle (e.g., CDK2), cell survival (e.g., BCL2), and metabolism (e.g., PPARGC1A). MITF loss-of-function mutations cause melanocyte loss in Waardenburg syndrome type IIA, whereas a gain-of-function mutation, MITF p.E318K, enhances its transcriptional activity and elevates melanoma risk. We identified a novel intronic MITF mutation in a patient exhibiting diffuse hyperpigmentation across the body. This mutation may interfere with the splicing of the final MITF exon, potentially generating a shorter MITF variant with gain of function properties. We established induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) from the patient and are inducing melanocytes from these patient derived iPSCs. The melanocytes carrying the MITF mutation will allow us to assess how this mutation affects MITF function.

title: Differential sensitivity of pituitary cell types to changes in Pou1f1 isoform proportions in mice
ja: マウスPou1f1アイソフォーム比率変化に対する下垂体細胞種ごとの感受性の違い
en: Differential sensitivity of pituitary cell types to changes in Pou1f1 isoform proportions in mice
abs: Introduction: Pou1f1 generates multiple isoforms, including the α and β isoforms, and deep intronic variants can alter the proportions of transcripts. While GH and PRL deficiency are typical features of human POU1F1 deficiency, TSH levels are variable, suggesting cell-lineage-specific sensitivity. Materials and Methods: We analyzed two mutant mouse lines (Pou1f1 c.143-83A>G, GE1; Pou1f1 [c.143-83A>G; c.143-93insA], GE2). In homozygous mice at 4 weeks of age, pituitary Pou1f1 isoform proportions were assessed, followed by analyses of body weight, serum pituitary hormone levels, and pituitary transcriptomes (bulk and single-cell), compared with wild-type controls. Results: In homozygous mice, the α isoform accounted for approximately 5% and 25% of total Pou1f1 transcripts in GE1 and GE2, respectively, whereas in wild-type mice it accounted for 95%. Total Pou1f1 transcript levels were 50% and 106% in GE1 and GE2, respectively, compared with wild-type controls. Homozygous GE2 mice exhibited milder growth failure than homozygous GE1 mice (55% vs 40%). Serum GH levels in homozygous mice were approximately 2.4% of the levels of wild-type in GE2, and fell below 1.0% in GE1. Serum TSH levels did not differ between homozygotes and wild-type mice in GE1. However, in GE2, TSH levels were 13-fold higher in homozygous than in wild-type mice. Pituitary transcriptomes were consistent with the serum results. Discussion: Somatotrophs were highly sensitive to Pou1f1 reduction in both variants. In contrast, thyrotrophs demonstrated resilience, indicating a lower functional threshold for Pou1f1.

title: Comprehensive Support for Cascade Genetic Testing in Minor Relatives in a Family With Marfan Syndrome
ja: Marfan症候群家系の未成年血縁者へのカスケード遺伝学的検査の包括的支援
en: Comprehensive Support for Cascade Genetic Testing in Minor Relatives in a Family With Marfan Syndrome
abs: Marfan syndrome is primarily caused by a pathogenic variant in the FBN1 gene and is inherited in an autosomal dominant manner. Because Marfan syndrome is associated with early-onset aortic disease, genetic testing is useful for relatives. However, cascade genetic testing for minors requires consideration of their decision-making capacity and psychological impact. This report describes a family case where comprehensive support was needed for cascade genetic testing of minor children. The proband was a 45-year-old man who underwent emergency graft replacement surgery for acute aortic dissection. Postoperatively, a pathogenic variant in FBN1 was found, and he was diagnosed with Marfan syndrome. The man had two minor sons, both of whom exhibited physical findings suggestive of Marfan syndrome. First, genetic counseling was performed with the couple to share the significance of cascade genetic testing. The proband wanted to proceed cautiously regarding genetic testing for the minors, but his wife desired genetic testing for the children as soon as possible. After providing age-appropriate counseling to the two sons, we individually explored the father's concerns regarding genetic testing for his children and subsequently performed genetic testing for both sons. Both were found to carry the same pathogenic FBN1 variant. In this case, there was a disagreement between the parents regarding the timing of cascade genetic testing for minor children, requiring consideration for each family member. We report a family requiring comprehensive support and discuss remaining challenges.

title: Current Status and needs of Genetic Counseling in Expanded Newborn Screening in Japan
ja: 本邦の拡大新生児スクリーニングにおける遺伝カウンセリングの現状とニーズ
en: Current Status and needs of Genetic Counseling in Expanded Newborn Screening in Japan
abs: Background: Expanded newborn screening (NBS) for new diseases has been introduced in Japan, and a pilot program started in 2024. Because the target diseases are hereditary, genetic counseling (GC) is important in NBS; however, the current status of GC remains unclear. Objective and Methods: This study was conducted as part of a national research project on expanded NBS. A questionnaire survey was conducted from March to May 2025 among 54 members of a research group on expanded NBS. The survey assessed systems, educational materials, and GC practices. Quantitative and thematic analyses were performed. Results: Thirty-seven responses were obtained (response rate: 53.7%) from 18 prefectures. About three-quarters of facilities provided face-to-face pre-test explanations, whereas one-quarter mainly used written materials because of staffing and time limitations. GC was provided in 84% of facilities at confirmatory testing and in almost all facilities at final diagnosis. The perceived need for GC increased according to the testing stage: pre-test (6%), confirmatory testing (76%), and final diagnosis (93%). At the pre-test stage, low prior probability and limited resources were major reasons for not requiring GC, whereas psychosocial and family support were emphasized at final diagnosis. Certified genetic counselors were recognized for multidisciplinary care and psychosocial support. Conclusion: The need for GC in expanded NBS changes as the process progresses. Based on these findings, we proposed a "stepwise genetic counseling model" for expanded NBS in Japan.

title: Evolving Reproductive Decision-Making in a Family with Mucopolysaccharidosis Type IIIB
ja: ムコ多糖症IIIB型家系における生殖に関する意思決定の変遷
en: Evolving Reproductive Decision-Making in a Family with Mucopolysaccharidosis Type IIIB
abs: Mucopolysaccharidosis(MPS) Type IIIB is an autosomal recessive neurodegenerative disorder caused by pathogenic NAGLU variants. Families with affected children may face difficult reproductive decisions regarding prenatal diagnosis and preimplantation genetic testing for monogenic disorders (PGT-M). We report genetic counseling for a couple whose reproductive decision-making evolved over time. The first child was diagnosed with MPS IIIB with compound heterozygous NAGLU variants, and both parents were confirmed as carriers. After natural conception, the couple sought prenatal diagnosis. After genetic counseling regarding disease prognosis and testing limitations, amniocentesis revealed that the fetus was a heterozygous carrier, and the couple continued the pregnancy. Subsequently, the mother developed anxiety disorder and became concerned that the second child might eventually bear caregiving responsibilities alone. After another natural conception, the couple again requested prenatal diagnosis. Amniocentesis revealed an affected fetus, and the couple elected termination of pregnancy. The couple later sought counseling regarding PGT-M. This case illustrates how reproductive decision-making in families with severe hereditary disorders may evolve according to caregiving experiences and psychological burden. The couple became interested in PGT-M to reduce the risk of pregnancy termination. Our experience highlights the importance of repeated and non-directive genetic counseling for complex reproductive choices.

title: Characteristics of Pregnant Women Requiring Deliberation After Genetic Counseling for NIPT
ja: NIPTの遺伝カウンセリング後に熟慮を要した妊婦の特徴
en: Characteristics of Pregnant Women Requiring Deliberation After Genetic Counseling for NIPT
abs: ObjectiveIn NIPT, autonomous decision-making by pregnant women and families is essential, yet the characteristics of those who defer their decision after genetic counseling remain unclear. This study aimed to clarify these characteristics. MethodsWe retrospectively reviewed 120 women who underwent NIPT genetic counseling at our institution between April 2024 and May 2026. All cases were handled and documented by a single provider, ensuring a consistent definition of deliberation. Women deciding at the initial session (immediate-decision group) were compared with those taking additional time (deliberation group). ResultsThe immediate-decision group comprised 101 women (84.2%) and the deliberation group 19 (15.8%). The latter tended to be younger, with fewer of advanced maternal age, and more often the woman or her partner was a healthcare professional. Deliberation rates by indication were 9.1% for advanced maternal age, 15.4% for anxiety, 66.7% (2/3) for fetal ultrasound abnormalities, and 50.0% for family history. Final uptake was 97.0% versus 42.1%. Some cited partner consultation or counseling differing from expectations; in family-history cases, recommendation from the woman's mother influenced the decision. ConclusionsAbout 16% of women deferred their decision, with deliberation most frequent and uptake lowest among ultrasound abnormality cases. This may reflect not mere delay but reconsideration of the test's meaning given fetal findings. For such cases, an intentional deliberation period, rather than concluding at the initial session, may be preferable.

title: Ethical considerations in prenatal diagnosis of X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy in an opposite-sex twin pregnancy
ja: 異性双胎妊娠におけるX連鎖副腎白質ジストロフィー出生前診断の倫理的考察
en: Ethical considerations in prenatal diagnosis of X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy in an opposite-sex twin pregnancy
abs: AbstractBackground: Adrenoleukodystrophy (ALD) is an X-linked disorder caused by pathogenic ABCD1 variants and characterized by demyelination and adrenal insufficiency. Prenatal diagnosis for at-risk male fetuses has been accepted, but age at onset and phenotype are difficult to predict. Early hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) may improve outcomes in childhood cerebral ALD. We report a case of prenatal diagnosis in a sex-discordant twin pregnancy. Case: After a negative result on noninvasive prenatal testing, the client learned that her maternal uncle, the proband, had died of ALD at age 55. She visited our hospital at 14 weeks and 5 days of gestation. At the first visit, her partner was absent, genetic information on the proband was unavailable, and carrier testing had not been performed for the client or her mother. Ultrasound showed one male and one female fetus. Within a limited time, the genetics team reviewed the medical and ethical issues, and counseling was provided with her partner. The familial variant was identified, and the client and her mother were confirmed to be heterozygous. Amniocentesis showed that the male fetus carried the variant. The couple chose to continue the pregnancy. Discussion: Prenatal diagnosis for ALD requires consideration of ethical aspects. In this case, decision-making was more complex because termination of the male fetus could also have resulted in the loss of the female co-twin, who was unaffected or expected to have a milder course. Rapid genetic evaluation and counseling that respects family values are important.

title: From Universal Tumor Screening for Lynch Syndrome to Genetic Care in Endometrial Cancer : Who Reaches Counseling?
ja: Lynch症候群のユニバーサル腫瘍スクリーニングから子宮体がんの遺伝医療へ：誰がカウンセリングに至るか
en: From Universal Tumor Screening for Lynch Syndrome to Genetic Care in Endometrial Cancer : Who Reaches Counseling?
abs: Background: At our institution, universal tumor screening (UTS) with mismatch repair (MMR) immunohistochemistry has been performed for endometrial cancer (EC) to identify Lynch syndrome (LS). Objective: To assess access to genetic services among EC patients with positive UTS results and factors associated with genetic counseling (GC) attendance. Methods Of 250 EC patients who underwent UTS from June 2020 to March 2026, 45 patients (18%) with loss of MMR protein expression were reviewed retrospectively. Age, family history of LS-associated cancers, MMR loss patterns, GC attendance, and genetic testing (GT) status were compared between GC attendees and non-attendees. Results: Thirty of 45 patients (67%) attended GC; 13 of 30 patients (43%) underwent GT; and four were diagnosed with LS. Median age was similar between attendees and non-attendees (55 [36-81] vs 56 [48-71] years). A family history of LS-associated cancers was common in the GC attendees (21/30, 70%). GC attendance was similar by MMR loss pattern: 17/26 (65%) for MLH1/PMS2 loss and 12/18 (67%) for MSH2/MSH6 loss. One patient with MLH1/MSH6 loss attended GC. Discussion: Among EC patients with positive UTS results, two-thirds attended GC, suggesting that family history may affect access to genetic services. However, post-GC pathways varied, and fewer than half proceeded to GT. Because LS information is relevant to health management for patients and relatives, UTS should be accompanied by support that enables patients to access information and make choices according to their clinical context and values.

title: Shared features of ZTTK syndrome, NKAP disorder, and ReNU syndrome - Temporal dysmorphology in RNA-related syndromes -
ja: ZTTK症候群・NKAP異常症・ReNU症候群の共通点：RNA関連症候群における経時的形態変化
en: Shared features of ZTTK syndrome, NKAP disorder, and ReNU syndrome - Temporal dysmorphology in RNA-related syndromes -
abs: ZTTK syndrome, NKAP-related disorder, and ReNU syndrome are RNA-related neurodevelopmental syndromes characterized by severe intellectual disability, hypotonia, facial dysmorphism, and skeletal abnormalities. We report three patients followed from infancy into adulthood for approximately two decades. In all three, external features were non-specific in infancy, whereas facial, habitus, and skeletal findings became more apparent with growth. In ZTTK syndrome, hypotonia, mild macrocephaly, and prominent ears were noted in infancy; after puberty, slender habitus, long limbs, and mandibular protrusion emerged. In NKAP-related disorder, external features were subtle in infancy, followed by thoracic deformity, elongated limbs, arachnodactyly, and joint dislocations. In ReNU syndrome, hypotonia and developmental delay predominated in infancy, whereas prominent joints, fractures, thoracic deformity, thick lips, and a deeply contoured face became evident later. Unlike many classical congenital anomaly syndromes, in which diagnostic features are recognized from birth or early infancy, these disorders showed gradual, age-dependent emergence of distinctive features. This may partly explain why ReNU syndrome remained unrecognized for many years. SON, NKAP, and RNU4-2 are involved in RNA splicing or RNA processing. The delayed emergence of features may reflect disruption of RNA processing across developmental stages. These observations support the value of temporal dysmorphology, or longitudinal assessment of dysmorphic features during growth, in RNA-related neurodevelopmental syndromes.

title: Novel HK1 intronic variant in congenital hyperinsulinism: impaired transactivation function for FOXA2
ja: 先天性高インスリン血症における新規HK1イントロンバリアント：FOXA2の転写活性化機能障害
en: Novel HK1 intronic variant in congenital hyperinsulinism: impaired transactivation function for FOXA2
abs: Hexokinase 1 (HK1) plays a critical role in glucose metabolism and is expressed in most tissues except pancreatic β-cells and hepatic cells. Recent studies have revealed noncoding variants within a ~50-bp regulatory region in intron 2 of HK1 encompassing the putative NFAT, NKX2, and FOX-binding sites in patients with congenital hyperinsulinism (CHI). These variants are thought to disrupt transcription factor binding, leading to loss of HK1 repression in β-cells; however, functional studies have not been performed for HK1 intronic variants. We performed whole-genome sequencing in a Japanese boy and his father with severe diazoxide-responsive CHI requiring high-dose diazoxide treatment. A novel heterozygous HK1 intronic variant (NC_000010.11:g.69348930T>C) located within the FOX-binding site was identified in both affected individuals. The variant was found to have occurred as a de novo event in the father and was assessed as "likely pathogenic" according to the ACMG/AMP guidelines. Furthermore, luciferase assays using HEK293T cells transfected with reporter vectors harboring the wildtype or variant FOX-binding site together with a FOXA2 expression vector showed a positive transactivation function for the wildtype binding site and an impaired transactivation function for the variant binding site. While it remains unknown how HK1 intronic variants lead to aberrant HK1 expression in β-cells and resultant development of CHI, the results indicate that the intronic variant is associated with functional alteration in response to FOXA2 stimulation.

title: Maternal uniparental disomy of chromosome 20: comprehensive clinical study in genetically confirmed 18 patients
ja: 20番染色体母性片親性ダイソミー：遺伝学的確定18例の包括的臨床検討
en: Maternal uniparental disomy of chromosome 20: comprehensive clinical study in genetically confirmed 18 patients
abs: Background: Maternal uniparental disomy of chromosome 20 [upd(20)mat] is a rare disorder characterized by growth failure and feeding difficulties. Gsα, encoded by GNAS, is predominantly expressed from the maternal allele in the proximal renal tubule, thyroid, pituitary, and ovary. Overexpression of Gsα may increase hormone receptor sensitivity. Objective: To clarify the long-term clinical features of upd(20)mat. Methods: We obtained detailed clinical findings in 18 Japanese patients with genetically confirmed upd(20)mat, using a questionnaire. We performed whole-exome sequencing and SNP array analysis to identify variants associated with the clinical features and to detect regions of isodisomy in all cases. Results: All had feeding difficulties during infancy, and two required tube feeding until school age. Height SDS improved in 11/12 patients treated with growth hormone therapy. The survey showed intellectual and developmental disabilities and neurodevelopmental disorders in 11% and 36% of patients, respectively, and Silver-Russell syndrome phenotypes in 53% of patients in infancy. Serum calcium levels in most patients remained within normal range. Five of the seven patients showed high-normal thyroid hormone levels from infancy, and three adolescents had subclinical hyperthyroidism. In a patient with severe growth failure, we identified a homozygous COL9A3 variant in a region of isodisomy. This variant has been reported as a heterozygous variant causing multiple epiphyseal dysplasia. Conclusion: Our study clarifies the long-term clinical characteristics of upd(20)mat.

title: A Case of ADAR-Related Disease Complicated by Ventricular Septal Defect
ja: 心室中隔欠損を合併したADAR関連疾患の1例
en: A Case of ADAR-Related Disease Complicated by Ventricular Septal Defect
abs: Introduction: Pathogenic variants in the ADAR gene, Abnormalities in the ADAR gene, which encodes adenosine deaminase acting on RNA 1, cause ADAR-related disease, presenting with a broad neurological spectrum from Aicardi-Goutieres syndrome type 6 to spastic paraplegia. Although pigmentary, growth, and immune abnormalities can occur, cardiac complications are rare. Case: A male infant born at 36 weeks (2,419 g) was postnatally diagnosed with ventricular septal defect (VSD) and underwent successful patch closure at 2 months. He exhibited global developmental delay; developmental testing at 4 years of age revealed a developmental quotient of 64. He was diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder at age 4. His gait was characterized by toe-walking, which caused frequent falls. While hypotonia was observed in the upper extremities and trunk, he exhibited hypertonia, hyperreflexia, positive Babinski signs, and ankle clonus in the lower extremities. No cutaneous or brain MRI abnormalities were noted. Whole-exome sequencing identified a heterozygous pathogenic ADAR variant [NM_001111.5: c.3019G>A (p.Gly1007Arg)], inherited from his asymptomatic father, suggesting incomplete penetrance. Conclusion: Although cardiac complications in ADAR-related disease are rare, they can reportedly be fatal. Cardiac involvement was noted in this case. While its relationship to ADAR dysfunction remains uncertain, further case accumulation is needed to clarify whether cardiac manifestations are part of the phenotypic spectrum of ADAR-related disease.

title: A pediatric case with minor glomerular abnormality and renal function decline caused by a novel MAFB variant
ja: 新規MAFBバリアントによる微小糸球体変化と腎機能低下を呈した小児例
en: A pediatric case with minor glomerular abnormality and renal function decline caused by a novel MAFB variant
abs: Introduction MAFB mutations cause Duane syndrome (DRS) characterized by a congenital eye misalignment, multicentric carpotarsal osteolysis (MCTO) characterized by bone lesions and psychomotor developmental delay, and isolated focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS). Patients with MAFB mutations develop FSGS in DRS but is not always present in MCTO. Mutation sites are specific for each disease. Case Presentation A 14-year-old boy was suspected of having short stature at the age of 6-year-old with proteinuria 1+, which was deemed normal. At the age of 14, his proteinuria progressed to 2+, which prompted further investigation. The patient was 150.2 cm (-2.0 SD) tall. None of psychomotor developmental delay, ocular and bone symptoms were observed. Laboratory findings were as follows: urine protein/ creatinine (Cr) 1.09 g/gCr; Cr, 0.73mg/dL; Cr-eGFR, 81.6ml/min. Renal histopathology showed no segmental or global sclerosis of the glomeruli but very mild interstitial fibrosis. NGS analysis revealed a novel in-frame variant in exon 1 of MAFB in a heterozygous manner, which was de novo and classified as likely pathogenic based on the ACMG criteria. Discussion Nephropathy in the present case may have been caused by a novel MAFB variant. Although the nephropathy was minor glomerular abnormality, a renal function decline had already been observed. MAFB variant site differed from those previously reported in DRS, MCTO, and isolated FSGS. This case highlights the importance of differentiating MAFB mutation in nephropathy and the diversity of clinical symptoms caused by MAFB mutation.

title: A Case of Loeys-Dietz Syndrome Type 3 Detected via Routine Health Screening and Treated with the Bentall Procedure
ja: 健診で発見されBentall手術を行ったLoeys-Dietz症候群3型の1例
en: A Case of Loeys-Dietz Syndrome Type 3 Detected via Routine Health Screening and Treated with the Bentall Procedure
abs: Case Report A man in his 60s underwent a routine health screening where a transthoracic echocardiogram (TTE) revealed an enlarged Valsalva sinus (53 mm) and moderate aortic regurgitation. Given his brother's history of Loeys-Dietz syndrome (LDS) type 3, the patient underwent genetic testing, which confirmed the same diagnosis. Following guidelines that recommend surgery when the aortic root diameter exceeds 40 mm, a Bentall procedure was successfully performed, and the patient's postoperative recovery was uneventful. Discussion LDS is a rare, hereditary connective tissue disorder linked to abnormalities in the TGF-β signaling pathway . It carries a higher risk of rapid aortic dissection and rupture compared to Marfan syndrome . LDS type 3, caused by SMAD3 gene mutations, accounts for 5-10% of cases and is characterized by severe vascular fragility and a predisposition to early-onset osteoarthritis . TTE is a non-invasive, real-time tool highly effective for the early detection of aortic root lesions . In this case, TTE was superior to plain chest CT in evaluating the aortic root, facilitating timely intervention before life-threatening complications occurred . Conclusion Early diagnosis and surgical intervention drastically improve the prognosis of LDS. This case underscores the importance of echocardiography screening during routine health checkups. Future efforts should focus on establishing multimodal imaging systems to detect and manage hereditary vascular diseases early.

title: X chromosome inactivation and clinical phenotypes: Analysis of female carriers of X-linked chronic granulomatous disease
ja: X染色体不活化と臨床表現型：X連鎖慢性肉芽腫症の女性保因者の解析
en: X chromosome inactivation and clinical phenotypes: Analysis of female carriers of X-linked chronic granulomatous disease
abs: [Background] X-linked chronic granulomatous disease (XL-CGD) is a primary immunodeficiency caused by pathogenic CYBB variants, which encodes gp91phox, a key component of NADPH oxidase complex. Generally, in females, one of X chromosomes is inactivated (XCI) at random. In contrast, skewed XCI is frequently observed in female carriers and develop or prevent symptoms. The correlation between XCI and clinical phenotypes such as neutrophil function is crucial for individualized management and genetic counseling. [Method] We analyzed two females carrying CYBB mutation (c.260C>A, p.Ser87X and c.742dupA, p.Ile248fs). The XCI ratios were determined using the human androgen receptor assay (HUMARA) and targeted long-read sequencing (t-LRS). Neutrophil function was evaluated through the dihydrorhodamine (DHR) flow cytometry and gp91phox protein expression. [Results] One of the carriers showed a severely skewed XCI pattern. XCI ratio revealed by t-LRS was 94.0:6.0, which was highly consistent with HUMARA results (87.0:13.0). This skewed pattern directly reflected the reduced DHR activity (93.9:6.0) and gp91phox expression (93.6:6.3). The other showed a random XCI pattern. XCI ratio by t-LRS was 58.0:42.0 (HUMARA: 64.2:35.8), correlating with the DHR activity (58.5:42.3) and gp91phox expression (58.3:41.7). [Discussion] This study successfully established a clear correlation between XCI and neutrophil functional parameters in XL-CGD. These findings indicate the clinical importance of assessing XCI patterns in female carriers, to provide personalized management and genetic counseling.

title: Solo-WCGW hypomethylation index reflects cumulative immune activation and correlates with T-cell receptor clonality
ja: Solo-WCGW低メチル化指数は累積的な免疫活性化を反映しT細胞受容体クローナリティと相関する
en: Solo-WCGW hypomethylation index reflects cumulative immune activation and correlates with T-cell receptor clonality
abs: Global DNA hypomethylation is frequently reported in immune-mediated diseases, but its biological interpretation remains unclear. Previously, we found that disease-associated hypomethylation is enriched at solo-WCGW CpGs, susceptible to replication-associated passive demethylation. Here we investigated whether this pattern reflects biologically meaningful immune processes. We analyzed methylation datasets from seven immune-mediated diseases and observed consistent solo-WCGW hypomethylation enriched in repressed chromatin and late-replicating regions. In contrast, cytokine-associated and genetically regulated CpGs were enriched in active chromatin, suggesting distinct mechanisms underlie replication-associated and regulatory methylation changes. Because solo-WCGW methylation in repressed chromatin showed strong concordance within individuals, we defined a hypomethylation index and searched for differentially methylated regions in active chromatin correlated with this index. In narcolepsy type 1 (NT1), the index was associated with a DMR at the T-cell receptor alpha locus, replicated independently, and correlated with T-cell receptor clonality from RNA-seq. In multiple sclerosis, a similar association was found at the immunoglobulin heavy-chain locus. These findings suggest that replication-associated hypomethylation retains epigenetic information on cumulative immune activation. Notably, in NT1, this signal was detectable despite limited evidence of ongoing inflammation at sampling, suggesting persistence of immune activation signatures beyond transient inflammatory states.

title: Clinical and molecular profiling of maternal uniparental disomy of chromosome 6: Silver-Russell syndrome-like condition
ja: 6番染色体母性片親性ダイソミーの臨床・分子プロファイル：Silver-Russell症候群様病態
en: Clinical and molecular profiling of maternal uniparental disomy of chromosome 6: Silver-Russell syndrome-like condition
abs: Background: Maternal uniparental disomy of chromosome 6 (UPD(6)mat) is a rare condition associated with fetal growth restriction (FGR), but its phenotypic spectrum and pathogenesis remain unclear. Methods: We screened 764 patients (309 born small-for-gestational-age and 455 with Silver-Russell syndrome (SRS)-like features) and identified four Japanese patients with UPD(6)mat (0.52%). Analyses included pyrosequencing, MethylationEPIC array, microsatellite and microarray analyses, exome sequencing, and Nanopore long-read methylation profiling of chromosome 6. Results: All four patients had severe FGR, met Netchine-Harbison criteria for SRS, and were born extremely preterm (27-29 weeks), often with oligohydramnios and placental underdevelopment. The three male patients had urogenital anomalies, and three had dysglycemia. Methylation analyses showed hypermethylation at maternally methylated chromosome 6 DMRs, without multilocus imprinting disturbance. These analyses confirmed mixed maternal hetero-/ isodisomy of chromosome 6 in three patients and segmental UPD in one. Nanopore and exome sequencing detected no other parent-of-origin methylation differences or pathogenic homozygous variants explaining the phenotype. Discussion: UPD(6)mat is a recognizable SRS-like condition with severe growth restriction, prematurity, urogenital anomalies, and dysglycemia. Epigenetic disturbance is confined to known DMRs, supporting a model where imprinting dysregulation (likely loss of paternal PLAGL1) is compounded by placental insufficiency, with recessive allele unmasking adding variability.

title: Intergenerational Association between Maternal Birth Weight and Congenital Malformations in Offspring
ja: 母体出生体重と児の先天奇形との世代間関連
en: Intergenerational Association between Maternal Birth Weight and Congenital Malformations in Offspring
abs: Background: Maternal birth weight (MBW) reflects fetal growth and may influence offspring health across generations. Epigenetic programming during early development has been implicated in intergenerational health effects. However, the association between MBW and congenital malformations in offspring remains unclear. Methods: Data from the Japan Environment and Children's Study (JECS) were analyzed. Among 103,060 pregnancies, 78,366 mother & infant pairs were eligible. MBW was categorized into five groups. Congenital malformations were identified from medical records and registry data. Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed after adjustment for maternal demographic, socioeconomic, and clinical factors. Results: Compared with an MBW of 3000 to 3499 g, low MBW (<2500 g) was associated with congenital heart disease (adjusted odds ratio: aOR 1.39, 95% confidence interval: CI 1.08 to 1.79), angioma (aOR 1.49, 95% CI 1.08 to 2.06), and inguinal hernia (aOR 1.75, 95% CI 1.19 to 2.57). High MBW (>4000 g) was associated with congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract (aOR 2.19, 95% CI 1.26 to 3.82) and arrhythmia (aOR 1.78, 95% CI 1.16 to 2.73). Several associations differed according to offspring sex. Conclusions: MBW was associated with multiple congenital malformations in offspring. These findings suggest that maternal fetal growth may influence developmental processes across generations, potentially through epigenetic mechanisms, and provide epidemiological evidence for intergenerational developmental programming.

title: Coalescent Distortion Index: Reference-Based Detection of Uniparental Disomy from a Single Genome
ja: Coalescent Distortion Index：単一ゲノムからの参照ベース片親性ダイソミー検出
en: Coalescent Distortion Index: Reference-Based Detection of Uniparental Disomy from a Single Genome
abs: In diploid organisms, chromosomes are typically inherited one copy from each parent, ensuring balanced genetic contributions. However, this rule is occasionally violated in uniparental disomy (UPD), in which both copies of a chromosome or chromosomal segment are derived from a single parent. UPD can disrupt genomic imprinting or expose recessive variation. UPD is estimated to occur in approximately one in 2,000 individuals, yet current approaches for detecting UPD typically rely on trio data, that is, genotypes from both parents and the offspring, limiting their applicability to datasets lacking parental information. Here we introduce the Coalescent Distortion Index (CDI), a statistic that enables detection of UPD from a single individual's genome using a reference sequence, without requiring parental data. CDI can be directly computed from variant call format (VCF) files as a simple function of genotype counts. Theoretically, CDI has an expected value of zero under a neutral coalescent model, and deviations from zero indicate distortions in genealogical structure. Applying CDI to HapMap Phase III ASW population data (chr17:6,689-8,202,065; GRCh36), we show that CDI successfully detects a known case of partial UPD (NA19918). Because CDI can be applied to single individuals, it enables large-scale genomic analysis and provides an efficient and interpretable framework for detecting deviations in genealogical structure.

title: Study of Recurrent Hydatidiform Mole: Clinical Utility of Genetic Testing in Determining Reproductive medicine
ja: 反復胞状奇胎の検討：生殖医療方針決定における遺伝学的検査の臨床的有用性
en: Study of Recurrent Hydatidiform Mole: Clinical Utility of Genetic Testing in Determining Reproductive medicine
abs: Hydatidiform mole (HM) is a form of abnormal pregnancy characterized by the excessive proliferation of placental trophoblasts and the absence or abnormal development of a fetus. Histologically, it presents with characteristic hydropic degeneration. The incidence of recurrent HM is reported to be approximately 1.8%. Although most cases occur sporadically, associations with genes involved in genomic imprinting, such as NLRP7 and KHDC3L, have been reported. The patient was a 40-year-old woman with a history of two partial HM, who presented to our department for her initial evaluation. Following genetic counseling regarding recurrent HM, the patient opted for intracytoplasmic sperm injection following controlled ovarian stimulation. After obtaining written informed consent, exome sequencing was performed for her and her husband. However, there was no disease-causing variant. The patient is currently under clinical observation for HM until medical clearance. Because HM carry a risk of recurrence or malignant transformation into an invasive mole or choriocarcinoma, a strict period of contraception and careful observation are required before attempting pregnancy. Given the patient's age and fertility concerns, this waiting period imposes a physical and psychological burden. In this case, performing parental genetic testing and initiating Assisted Reproductive Technology procedures during the mandatory observation period successfully prepared the patient for her next pregnancy and appeared to alleviate her psychological distress.

title: Multidisciplinary Evaluation of Germline Findings in Tumor-Normal Paired Whole-Genome Sequencing
ja: 腫瘍-正常ペア全ゲノム解析における生殖細胞系列所見の多職種評価
en: Multidisciplinary Evaluation of Germline Findings in Tumor-Normal Paired Whole-Genome Sequencing
abs: Background: Cancer genomic profiling has expanded opportunities to identify germline findings (GF). In Japan, the national "Action Plan for Whole Genome Analysis" project promotes whole-genome sequencing (WGS) for cancer patients. However, interpretation and disclosure of incidental GF remain challenging. Methods: We analyzed 1,693 tumor-normal paired WGS datasets from our WGS project through May 2026. Germline pathogenic variants (GPVs) associated with hereditary cancer syndromes (HCS) and other genetic disorders were evaluated. Cases requiring detailed discussion, including non-cancerous genetic disorders identified between February 2022 and September 2023, were reviewed by a multidisciplinary expert panel, the "Germline Findings Board (GFB)," to ensure appropriate disclosure. Results: Among 1,693 cases, 86 patients (5.1%) harbored GPVs associated with HCS. Approximately half were identified in tumor types not previously associated with the causative genes. Several patients harbored GPVs related to non-cancerous hereditary diseases. Since the establishment of the GFB, 868 consecutive cases have been reviewed, and only 7 (0.8%) were considered eligible for disclosure, including variants in LDLR, MYBPC3, and TTN in patients with relevant clinical phenotypes. Conclusion: Large-scale cancer WGS can reveal actionable GF beyond conventional HCS. Appropriate interpretation and disclosure require multidisciplinary evaluation integrating genomic and clinical data. As genomic medicine expands, expert panels with genetic counseling will be essential for patients and families.

title: Whole-genome discovery of pathogenic snRNA variants and efficient extended-exome screening
ja: 病的snRNAバリアントの全ゲノム探索と効率的な拡張エクソームスクリーニング
en: Whole-genome discovery of pathogenic snRNA variants and efficient extended-exome screening
abs: Pathogenic variants in small nuclear RNA (snRNA) genes have recently emerged as an important cause of Mendelian disorders, particularly neurodevelopmental disorders, yet they remain difficult to detect using conventional whole-exome sequencing (WES). Here, we reanalyzed whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data from 1,578 genetically unsolved probands in Japan. We identified pathogenic variants in multiple snRNA genes including RNU4-2, RNU2-2, RNU5B-1, and RNU4ATAC, accounting for 1.2% (19/1,578) of previously unsolved cases. Consistent with previous reports of a maternal-allele bias, all de novo variants in our cohort arose on the maternal allele, as determined by long-read sequencing where applicable. We then developed an snRNA-extended WES approach by incorporating custom capture probes targeting 50 snRNA genes into a standard exome design. Benchmarking demonstrated robust and uniform coverage across the targeted snRNA loci without increasing sequencing depth or compromising coverage of standard coding regions. Most targeted snRNA loci were covered predominantly by uniquely mapped reads despite high sequence similarity among paralogous genes. Application of this approach to patient samples successfully detected pathogenic snRNA variants previously identified by WGS. Our findings demonstrate that pathogenic snRNA variants contribute substantially to unresolved Mendelian disease cases and establish snRNA-extended WES as a cost-effective and scalable strategy for incorporating recent discoveries into routine clinical genomic diagnostics.

title: Indirect Somatic Genetic Rescue Caused by a Somatic ATP2A2 Mutation in Epidermolytic Ichthyosis: A Case Report
ja: 表皮融解性魚鱗癬における体細胞ATP2A2変異による間接的体細胞遺伝的レスキュー：症例報告
en: Indirect Somatic Genetic Rescue Caused by a Somatic ATP2A2 Mutation in Epidermolytic Ichthyosis: A Case Report
abs: Indirect somatic genetic rescue (ISGR), in which a somatic mutation in a gene distinct from the disease-causing gene compensates for the phenotype of a Mendelian disorder, is a rare phenomenon reported in only a limited number of diseases. Epidermolytic ichthyosis (EI) is a rare autosomal dominant disorder characterized by blistering due to keratin cytoskeleton fragility, granular degeneration of the epidermis, and subsequent hyperkeratosis of unknown pathogenesis. A 39-year-old woman with EI caused by a missense mutation in KRT10 developed a patch lacking hyperkeratosis on her back. Histopathological examination of the patch revealed granular degeneration without hyperkeratosis. Genetic analysis of the epidermis identified no somatic variants in KRT10. Instead, a novel homozygous missense variant in ATP2A2, the causative gene of another inherited skin disease, Darier disease, was detected (VAF 88.9%, CADD PHRED score 29.5), together with copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity involving the long arm of chromosome 12 containing ATP2A2. Because the homozygous ATP2A2 mutation, an exceedingly rare event, was detected in the majority of epidermal cells within the patch, we concluded that loss of ATP2A2 function suppressed KRT10 mutation-associated hyperkeratosis, thereby producing an ISGR patch. This case suggests that SERCA activity may represent a potential therapeutic target for hyperkeratosis in EI.

title: Automated phenotype-driven prioritization of genomic variants tool in rare diseases tested on inherited heart conditions
ja: 希少疾患向け表現型駆動型ゲノムバリアント自動優先順位付けツールの遺伝性心疾患での検証
en: Automated phenotype-driven prioritization of genomic variants tool in rare diseases tested on inherited heart conditions
abs: HIRU is a phenotype-driven variant prioritization platform designed to support clinical diagnosis and research using exome and whole-genome sequencing data. Developed for rare disease genomics, HIRU integrates structured phenotypic information (Human Phenotype Ontology; HPO) with genomic variants to enable automated and efficient variant interpretation. Variants are systematically annotated using VEP and enriched with molecular, clinical, and computational pathogenicity evidence. HIRU applies the Genomics England rare disease tiering framework and prioritizes variants using semantic similarity metrics (HPO, PanelApp UK+Australia), aggregated clinical evidence, pathogenicity predictors, and ACMG/ClinGen-based classification criteria. The platform generates a ranked list of candidate variants associated with the patient phenotype, facilitating clinical interpretation and diagnostic decision-making. Internal benchmarking showed 95.6% sensitivity (95% CI: 94.2–96.5) in 1,089 families with clinically and functionally validated variants. Testing on exomes from patients with different genetic cardiac conditions with known causal variants was performed in Grupo de Xenética Cardiovascular, within IDIS (Instituto De Investigación Sanitaria), in Santiago de Compostela (Spain). Genetic variants on the exomes were prioritised both with and without the inclusion of HPO terms in HIRU. The main advantage of incorporating HPO terms was a significant reduction in the number of prioritised variants while still retaining the pathogenic variants associated with the patient’s condition.

title: Improving diagnosis of neurodevelopmental disorders by screening spliceosome snRNA paralogues (RNU4‑2, RNU2‑2, RNU5B‑1) in an Indian cohort
ja: インド人コホートにおけるスプライソソームsnRNAパラログ（RNU4-2・RNU2-2・RNU5B-1）スクリーニングによる神経発達症診断の改善
en: Improving diagnosis of neurodevelopmental disorders by screening spliceosome snRNA paralogues (RNU4‑2, RNU2‑2, RNU5B‑1) in an Indian cohort
abs: Recently, monoallelic and/or biallelic variants in three major spliceosome related snRNA genes (RNU4-2, RNU2-2 and RNU5B-1) are increasingly being reported to cause distinct neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs). However, these genes are not yet included in routine exome sequencing used for identifying etiology of NDD. Among a large cohort of undiagnosed NDD families with inconclusive results on exome sequencing, 106 individuals from 106 families with phenotypic findings of global developmental delay and epilepsy were identified and targeted screening of three snRNA genes was performed by Sanger sequencing. A further 60 families whose genome sequencing data was available were also screened using a standardized bioinformatics pipeline. Overall, we identified seven individuals from six families with known disease-causing variants in one of these three genes. We identified two heterozygous de novo variants (n.64_65insT, n.69C>T) in the 18 bp critical region of RNU4-2 in three probands from three families, causing ReNU syndrome (MIM #620851). Further, we found one proband with a recurrent heterozygous variant, n.35A>G in RNU2-2 causing developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 119 (MIM #621304) while three individuals from two families were found to have two homozygous variants (n.45C>T, n.104T>C) in RNU2-2, causing RNU2-2 related recessive NDD. To our knowledge, this is the first cohort screening of disease-causing variants in major spliceosome related snRNA genes in the Indian population.

title: Historic Analysis of Genomic Research on Ainu people: Implications for Indigenous Data Sovereignty in Japan
ja: アイヌ民族を対象としたゲノム研究の歴史的分析：日本における先住民データ主権への示唆
en: Historic Analysis of Genomic Research on Ainu people: Implications for Indigenous Data Sovereignty in Japan
abs: Background and purpose: Indigenous Data Sovereignty (IDSov) is a movement to protect Indigenous interests in data, including genomic data, and upholds Indigenous rights to control and oversee studies using their data. In Japan, however, whether and how biospecimens and data from Ainu people have been collected, stored, and utilized in scientific studies remains unclear. Methods: This study systematically surveyed genomic studies on Ainu people using three major academic databases. After excluding studies unrelated to human genetics or not focused on the Ainu, we reviewed the "Materials and methods" sections to identify the origin, collection context, and reuse of biospecimens and data. Results: Among 82 eligible articles, most focused on the anthropological origins of the Ainu or other populations. Blood samples collected in the 1980s have been used repeatedly. A few studies reported consulting the Ainu Association of Hokkaido or explaining their studies to the regional community. Discussion: Ethical discussions of research on Ainu people have largely focused on human remains; comparatively little attention has been paid to the governance of biospecimens and data. In light of evolving international norms and domestic ethical expectations, continued reuse without community engagement may no longer be seen as appropriate. To respect Ainu rights to engage in research, discussions involving Ainu people, researchers, and genomic data stewards are needed to co-design an ethical research environment and infrastructure.

title: Public Views on Genetic and Genomic Discrimination in Japan (1): A Scenario-Based Questionnaire Survey
ja: 日本における遺伝・ゲノム差別に関する市民の見解（1）：シナリオベース質問紙調査
en: Public Views on Genetic and Genomic Discrimination in Japan (1): A Scenario-Based Questionnaire Survey
abs: Background: Japan's 2023 Genomic Medicine Promotion Act calls for preventing "unjust discrimination based on genomic information." However, public views on problematic situations involving real or presumed genetic and genomic characteristics remain unclear. Methods: An online cross-sectional survey was conducted in March 2026 among Japanese adults aged 20-69 years. The respondents evaluated five scenarios: predictive genetic testing before marriage, trait genetic testing at workplace, derogatory online comments about life with disabled family members, reduced insurance benefits for hereditary disease, and physician advice to discontinue infertility treatment for women at risk of hereditary disease. Results: There were 5,160 respondents (10.3% response rate). Conduct was rated inappropriate/unacceptable most often for online comments (83.5%), followed by insurance reductions (80.2%), physician advice (75.2%), workplace testing (68.0%), and premarital testing (55.9%). Perceived discrimination followed the same order (83.5%, 75.3%, 70.0%, 64.9%, 61.4%). Acceptance was higher among men and younger respondents, while perceived discrimination in the online-comments scenario was higher among women. Discussion: These findings suggest that perceptions of such discrimination depend on social context and the perceived controllability or avoidability of the condition or situation. Clarifying boundaries of acceptable responses to real or presumed genetic/genomic characteristics, including information use and stigmatizing speech, may foster public trust in genomic medicine.

title: T itle: Public Views on Genetic and Genomic Discrimination in Japan (2): A Scenario-Based Group Interview Study
ja: 日本における遺伝・ゲノム差別に関する市民の見解（2）：シナリオベース・グループインタビュー研究
en: T itle: Public Views on Genetic and Genomic Discrimination in Japan (2): A Scenario-Based Group Interview Study
abs: Background: Japan's 2023 Genomic Medicine Promotion Act calls for preventing "unjust discrimination based on genomic information." However, public views on problematic situations involving real or presumed genetic and genomic characteristics remain unclear. Methods: In March 2026, six face-to-face group interviews were conducted with 29 Japanese adults, stratified by gender and age (20s-30s, 40s-50s, and 60s-70s). Four scenarios addressed predictive genetic testing before marriage, trait genetic testing at workplace, derogatory online comments about life with disabled family members, and reduced insurance benefits for hereditary disease. Transcripts were analyzed using thematic analysis. Results: In the marriage scenario, many accepted genetic testing as preparation but objected to coercive third-party requests and evaluations based on inherited traits. In the workplace scenario, concerns focused on employer access to results, personnel use, and lack of transparency. In the social-media scenario, comments were criticized as offensive, discriminatory, or eugenicist, and some noted the risks of public online disclosure. In the insurance scenario, the participants questioned post hoc benefit reductions and emphasized prior explanations. Most men framed issues in terms of decision-making, procedures, and institutional rules, whereas most women highlighted relationships, dignity, and familial implications. Discussion: Although not generalizable, these findings suggest that scenario-based dialogue may clarify public views on genetic and genomic discrimination in Japan.

title: How Should Web-Based Information on Presymptomatic Testing and PGT-M for Rare Diseases Be Provided? Patient Insights
ja: 希少疾患の発症前検査・PGT-Mに関するWeb情報はどう提供すべきか：患者の視点
en: How Should Web-Based Information on Presymptomatic Testing and PGT-M for Rare Diseases Be Provided? Patient Insights
abs: Web-based information on presymptomatic genetic testing and PGT- M is important but limited for rare-disease patients and families in Japan, despite advances in national genomic medicine policy. Their perspectives on its design, framing, and links to specialist support are underexplored. Four online focus groups (January-March 2026) on web-based information for presymptomatic genetic testing and PGT-M, with nine rare-disease patients and family members, were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Four themes emerged. First, participants emphasized making genetic uncertainty visible: current explanations may obscure penetrance, de novo cases, and PGT-M's limits, and probabilities may be misread as family-level rather than per-pregnancy. Second, they highlighted reducing anticipated social pressure by avoiding framing that implies pressure to test or particular reproductive decisions, or that stigmatizes people living with such conditions. Third, they called for an information environment tailored to disease, audience, and context of access, rather than uniformly presented. Fourth, they viewed web-based information as a gateway to specialist support in genomic medicine, a role amplified by limited availability of such support. These findings suggest web-based information on these tests should be designed not merely as content, but as an ethically and clinically attentive environment, co-developed with patient communities, that makes uncertainty visible, minimizes social pressure, supports tailored access, and provides pathways to specialist support in genomic medicine.

title: Development of ICT materials for informed assent of middle school students in genome analysis research
ja: ゲノム解析研究における中学生のインフォームド・アセント用ICT教材の開発
en: Development of ICT materials for informed assent of middle school students in genome analysis research
abs: Background: Genome analyses are increasingly conducted on patients and healthy children to advance genomic medicine. While researchers must obtain appropriate assent from pediatric participants, explaining complex genetic concepts remains a major challenge. Objective: To promote children's genomic literacy and protect their rights, we developed an ICT-based educational tool to support explanations of genome analysis and facilitate informed decision-making. Methods: We developed an ICT tool tailored to middle school students. To evaluate its effectiveness for informed assent, we conducted a double-blind, randomized controlled trial with 112 healthy middle school students. Assessment was performed using the "Instrument to Assess Children's Assent (IACA)," which evaluates three core elements: "Understanding and Appreciation," "Expression of Choice," and "Reasoning and Consistency." Results: The developed tool, Monochrome-Genome: Future Edition, is an interactive web-based platform. The mean IACA score was 18.0±2.6 (range: 0-22). Statistical analysis revealed significant differences in the Expressing a Choice section (p<0.05) and one item within the Understanding and Appreciation section (p<0.01), specifically in open-ended responses requiring participants to describe genomics in their own words. Discussion: These findings suggest that Monochrome-Genome: Future Edition significantly enhances middle school students' comprehension of complex genetic concepts and effectively supports ethical assent processes in pediatric genome research.

title: Challenges of PGT-M for Cancer Predisposition Syndromes: Perspectives of Cancer and Genetics Professionals.
ja: がん素因症候群に対するPGT-Mの課題：がん・遺伝の専門家の視点
en: Challenges of PGT-M for Cancer Predisposition Syndromes: Perspectives of Cancer and Genetics Professionals.
abs: Background: Genetic diagnosis of Cancer Predisposition Syndromes (CPSs) may affect reproductive decision-making among individuals of reproductive age. PGT-M for CPSs is available in some countries as an option to avoid transmission of pathogenic variants to offspring. In Japan, discussions increased following the 2022 revision of the JSOG clinical opinion on PGT-M, and it has since been approved for several childhood-onset CPSs. Objective: To investigate healthcare providers' (HCPs) perspectives on PGT-M for CPSs and identify future challenges. Methods: An online survey was conducted in 2025 among Genetic Healthcare Professionals (GHPs), including clinical geneticists and certified genetic counselors. Responses from 365 GHPs at medical institutions were compared with data from our 2023 survey of 499 HCPs at a cancer center. Results: Awareness of PGT-M was significantly higher among GHPs than HCPs (96.2% vs. 21%, p<.01). Although response distributions differed between groups, over 90% of respondents in each group reported patient interest in PGT-M for CPSs. GHPs were more cautious regarding adult-onset conditions; however, 56.1% reported they would "provide support" and 36.9% would "decide on a case-by-case basis" upon patient request for PGT-M for CPSs. Discussion: A notable disparity in awareness of PGT-M existed between GHPs and HCPs. However, both groups recognized that individuals with CPSs may desire PGT-M. The cautious stance among GHPs may reflect the challenge of balancing respect for patient values with ethical concerns surrounding PGT-M for CPSs.

session: ランチョンセミナー1：早期診断がもたらすライソゾーム病治療の可能性
title: Therapeutic Opportunities in Lysosomal Diseases Enabled by Early Diagnosis
en: Therapeutic Opportunities in Lysosomal Diseases Enabled by Early Diagnosis
abs: The treatment of genetic disorders has made remarkable advances in recent years. In particular, in inborn errors of metabolism, direct therapeutic intervention at the protein level has become possible through replacement of deficient or dysfunctional enzymes. In lysosomal storage disorders, enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) was developed relatively early because of the therapeutic advantage provided by the cross-correction mechanism, whereby lysosomal enzymes secreted from normal cells are taken up by deficient cells through receptors on the cell surface and subsequently delivered to the lysosomes, thereby correcting the underlying metabolic defect. ERT, through the exogenous administration of recombinant enzymes, enables these enzymes to reach patient cells via receptor-mediated uptake and has been shown to reduce substrate accumulation in the liver, spleen, heart, skeleton, and skeletal muscle, leading to improvements or stabilization of clinical manifestations and substantial benefits to patients’ quality of life (QOL) . More recently, novel therapeutic strategies have been introduced, including the development of modified enzymes capable of crossing the blood–brain barrier, optimization of administration routes, and combination therapies with pharmacological chaperones. Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) has also demonstrated therapeutic efficacy in certain lysosomal storage disorders, including effects on the central nervous system when performed at an early stage of disease, and approaches to conditioning regimens continue to evolve. Furthermore, accumulating evidence indicates that early intervention with enzyme replacement, particularly during infancy or early childhood, can prevent or delay irreversible organ damage involving the central nervous system, skeletal muscle, and respiratory muscles, thereby providing substantial benefits in terms of long-term functional outcomes. In this context, mucopolysaccharidosis type I (MPS I; Hurler syndrome), mucopolysaccharidosis type II (MPS II; Hunter syndrome), and glycogen storage disease type II (Pompe disease) have been included in Tokyo’s publicly funded expanded newborn screening program since 2024, reflecting the growing recognition of the importance of early diagnosis and treatment. In this review, we discuss the clinical benefits of early treatment in these disorders, the current status and limitations of established therapies, and the prospects for emerging therapeutic approaches, including gene therapy and nucleic acid–based therapeutics.

session: ランチョンセミナー2：ロングリードDNAシーケンス：ヒトゲノムの未踏の地を明らかに
title: Long-Read DNA Sequencing: Opening the Previously Inaccessible Human Genome
en: Long-Read DNA Sequencing: Opening the Previously Inaccessible Human Genome
abs: Long-read sequencing is transforming human genetics by enabling analysis of genomic regions that remain difficult to resolve with short-read DNA sequencing. Using Oxford Nanopore (ONT) ultra-long reads with some PacBio HiFi reads, we constructed diploid telomere-to-telomere genomes of 12 Macaca fascicularis, generating 24 haplotype-resolved DNA sequences. These genomes revealed extensive repetitive and structural variation and enabled complete resolution of 24 MHC haplotypes, including haplotype-specific differences in gene content, copy number, segmental duplications, and genomic organization. Similar approaches should transform human immunogenomics by resolving highly polymorphic HLA, TCR, and BCR loci, that are likely to be associated with immune-related diseases. Long reads also permit accurate analysis of VNTRs reported in Science in 1987 and other tandem repeats, defining repeat number, internal sequence structure, and parental haplotype. Native-DNA ONT sequencing further enables simultaneous detection of sequence variation and DNA methylation. These capabilities are particularly important for rare diseases that remain unexplained after exome or short-read whole-genome sequencing, where causal alterations may include structural variants, repeat expansions, complex rearrangements, or epigenetic abnormalities. Integration of accurate ultra-long sequencing can therefore move human genetics from variant-centric analysis toward complete personal genomes encompassing haplotypes, repetitive sequences, immune-genomic diversity, structural variation, and epigenetic states.

session: ランチョンセミナー3：ロングリードシークエンサーを活用したヒトゲノム情報研究
title: From Linear References to T2T Genomes: New Opportunities in Genomic Medicine
en: From Linear References to T2T Genomes: New Opportunities in Genomic Medicine
abs: Human genome analysis relies on reference genomes such as GRCh38. Because GRCh38 was assembled from genomic clones derived from multiple volunteers, it does not represent the genome of any single individual. Advances in long-read sequencing have enabled Telomere-to-Telomere (T2T) genome assembly, allowing the reconstruction of continuous end-to-end chromosome assemblies. The Human Pangenome Reference Consortium has generated T2T genomes from 231 individuals representing populations worldwide. We have also released a pangenome graph from 10 Japanese and 9 Saudi Arabian individuals. These resources are emerging as alternatives to conventional linear reference genomes. Long-read sequencing and genome assembly are increasingly used in clinical genome analysis. By combining long-read sequencing with trio analysis or Hi-C, chromosome-scale assemblies can be generated with maternal and paternal haplotypes resolved separately. Although conventional reference-based analyses accurately detect structural variants, they remain limited in regions containing segmental duplications, multicopy genes, and complex structural polymorphisms. T2T genome analysis reconstructs patient-specific diploid genomes at chromosome scale, enabling direct characterization of copy number, gene organization, repetitive structures, and structural variants within individual haplotypes. This approach can reveal complex pathogenic variants and sequences absent from existing references, providing new opportunities to identify disease-causing variants in undiagnosed disorders and advance genomic medicine.

session: ランチョンセミナー4：シーケンスを再定義するTruPathソリューション
title: From Sequencing to Further Insights
en: From Sequencing to Further Insights
abs: Illumina offers a full range of sequencers—from compact to large-scale models—equipped with the latest technologies, such as XLEAP-SBSTM reagents and DRAGENTM. A wide range of multi-omics applications are being developed for these state-of-the-art sequencers. Already on the market and receiving positive feedback are Illumina Single Cell Prep, a single-cell solution with low upfront costs; the Illumina 5-base solution, which enables simultaneous genome and methylation analysis using a new enzyme that converts methylated cytosine to thymine; SomaSeqTM Discovery, which enables highly reproducible protein analysis using aptamers; and TruPathTM Genome, which enables long-range WGS analysis without the hassle of library preparation—a product that Dr. Miya will introduce. StrataMapTM Spatial, a new spatial expression analysis technology, was added to this product lineup in September. We will introduce Illumina’s latest multiomics platform, which goes beyond sequencing, including the integrated analysis software Illumina Connected Multiomics (ICM).

session: ランチョンセミナー4：シーケンスを再定義するTruPathソリューション
title: Does Illumina Dream of Long Reads?
en: Does Illumina Dream of Long Reads?
abs: Short-read sequencing (SRS) has transformed human genome analysis, yet tandem repeats, low-uniqueness regions, and complex structural variants (SVs) remain difficult to resolve. In these areas, long-read sequencing (LRS) has traditionally held the advantage. Illumina has long dominated SRS, but long-range genomic analysis has remained a major challenge. In 2026, Illumina (re)entered this arena with TruPath, a new approach that uses existing NovaSeq instruments while reconstructing short-read data into long-range haplotype information. In other words, Illumina is now taking the fight to LRS on its own territory. TruPath aims to combine long-range phasing and improved access to difficult genomic regions with Illumina’s strengths in throughput and cost efficiency. In this luncheon seminar, I will present our early hands-on experience with TruPath and direct comparisons with multiple sequencing platforms, focusing on difficult genomic regions, SV detection, genome-wide phasing, and clinically relevant disease-causing variants. So, does Illumina dream of long reads? If Illumina can match the genome-variant detection sensitivity of existing LRS technologies while delivering it at substantially lower cost, it may not simply enter the long-read race—it may rewrite the rules.

session: ランチョンセミナー5：ゲノムバリアント どうする？解析法
title: Next-Generation Mapping: Unlocking the Architecture of the Human Genome with Electronic Genome Mapping
en: Next-Generation Mapping: Unlocking the Architecture of the Human Genome with Electronic Genome Mapping
abs: Electronic Genome Mapping (EGM) is a single-molecule genome mapping technique that analyzes long, labeled DNA molecules using electronic detection. By providing long-range genomic analysis, EGM enables the detection and characterization of structural variants (SVs), copy number variations (CNVs), repeat expansions and contractions, and other complex genomic alterations that can be challenging to resolve using conventional genomic technologies. Structural variants (SVs) — including deletions, duplications, insertions, inversions, and translocations — underlie a substantial share of genomic variation associated with human disease and are frequently missed or incompletely resolved by conventional sequencing and cytogenetic methods. Accurate SV detection is therefore important for rare disease and hematologic malignancy research and for investigating genomic complexity across a wide range of clinical and translational research applications. EGM has the ability to combine genome-wide SV analysis with targeted analysis using either CRISPR/Cas9-mediated approaches or through targeted pipelines. One example of such a pipeline is the RepX pipeline, which supports sizing and analysis of repeat expansions at several disease-associated loci, including C9orf72, DMPK, FMR1 and FXN. This capability is of particular interest in rare disease research, where EGM can provide comprehensive characterization of the wide spectrum of “unstable alleles” at the single-molecule level. I will present recent results from Nabsys researchers and collaborators that demonstrate EGM’s performance and high resolution for detecting disease-associated SVs and CNVs in rare disease and hematologic malignancy research. This highlights EGM’s potential to provide complementary structural genomic information across applications currently investigated using tiered approaches involving multiple genomic technologies.

session: ランチョンセミナー5：ゲノムバリアント どうする？解析法
title: Structural Variants: Now What?
en: Structural Variants: Now What?
abs: Next-generation sequencing (NGS) is rapidly accelerating the identification of causal variants in rare disease research. National projects worldwide perform whole-exome sequencing (WES) analysis or whole-genome sequencing (WGS) analysis using short-read NGS. WES analysis identifies the cause in approximately 40–50% of undiagnosed cases, whilst WGS analysis finds new causes in around 10% of cases unresolved after WES analysis. Pathogenic variants are nonetheless highly diverse, SNVs, indels, copy number variants (CNVs), indels exceeding 500 bp, structural variants (SVs) such as large, band-level insertions, deletions and inversions, chromosomal translocations, and epigenetic modifications (e.g., methylation), and some escape detection by both WES and WGS. Although long-read NGS detects a wider range of variant types, it too has limits, and detecting large-scale SVs and segmental duplications remains particularly difficult. Plus, some variants may be missed computationally in whole-genome analyses. Detecting all potentially causative variant types is therefore the essential first step, and the analytical method must be selected accordingly. Genome Mapping (GM) analysis like Optical Genome Mapping (OGM) and Electronic Genome Mapping (EGM), which enables comprehensive detection of relatively large SVs including translocations, is increasingly used to complement the limitations of NGS analyses. In this talk, I will present practical examples and best practices for selecting variant types, analytical methods and analytical strategies.

session: ランチョンセミナー6：成人PKU患者の課題と薬物治療がもたらす生活の変化
title: Current Treatment Landscape and Unmet Needs in Adults with Phenylketonuria in Japan: Insights from the ATLAS Survey
en: Current Treatment Landscape and Unmet Needs in Adults with Phenylketonuria in Japan: Insights from the ATLAS Survey
abs: Phenylketonuria (PKU) is an autosomal recessive inborn error of metabolism caused by pathogenic variants in PAH, with an incidence of approximately 1 in 70,000 births in Japan and requires lifelong control of blood phenylalanine (Phe). Nationwide newborn screening has enabled early diagnosis since 1977, and medical nutrition therapy (MNT) has long been the cornerstone of treatment. However, adherence to dietary restriction and regular Phe monitoring becomes increasingly difficult from adolescence into adulthood. The Assessment of the Treatment and Management LAndScape of phenylketonuria (ATLAS) survey, the first study to characterize PKU management in Japan, evaluated 176 active patients from eight medical institutions before the introduction of pegvaliase. Overall, 76.7% were managed with MNT alone, while sapropterin use was more common in younger patients. Visit and Phe-monitoring frequencies decreased with age, and metabolic control deteriorated markedly after adolescence; except during pregnancy, the proportion of patients achieving target Phe levels declined in older age groups.
