Persistent hyperphenylalaninemia in adults is associated with impaired attention, working memory, executive function, processing speed, and neuropsychiatric symptoms, which may further complicate self-management. With the recent introduction of pegvaliase and sepiapterin, treatment options in Japan are expanding. Nevertheless, achieving sustained metabolic control while reducing treatment burden remains a major unmet need, particularly for adolescents and adults.

session: ランチョンセミナー6：成人PKU患者の課題と薬物治療がもたらす生活の変化
title: How Pegvaliase Has Changed PKU Care: Practical Management Tips
en: How Pegvaliase Has Changed PKU Care: Practical Management Tips
abs: Since pegvaliase (Palynziq) became available in Japan in 2023, treatment of classical phenylketonuria (PKU) has changed markedly. Pegvaliase lowers blood phenylalanine (Phe) independently of phenylalanine hydroxylase and its cofactor BH4. Although PEGylated to reduce immunogenicity, adverse reactions are very common, and both immune responses and the onset of benefit vary widely among patients. Many responders achieve a physiological Phe level of ≤120 µmol/L, and restrictions on natural protein intake may be lifted. Sustained Phe reduction in adults with PKU has highlighted the reversibility of the effects of hyperphenylalaninemia on the brain. Deep white matter lesions on brain MRI have shown improvements, and patients report less irritability and depression, fewer forgotten tasks, less procrastination, and better planning. Clinical benefit may take months or years to emerge, during which patients must cope with hypersensitivity reactions and injection pain. This seminar will discuss practical approaches to ease treatment burden and support patients through the early phases. Adjusting dietary Phe intake and reducing pegvaliase dosage after response will also be focused.

session: ランチョンセミナー7：古代DNAが解き明かす日本列島人の歴史―ターゲットキャプチャによる古代ゲノム解析の最前線―
title: The Formation History of Japanese Populations Revealed by Ancient Genomics
en: The Formation History of Japanese Populations Revealed by Ancient Genomics
abs: Homo sapiens reached the Japanese Archipelago 38,000 years ago. The formation of Japanese populations has been studied through archaeology, physical anthropology, and genetics. Ancient DNA (aDNA) provides direct evidence of past human movement and population relationships. Advances in next-generation sequencing have enabled genome-wide analysis of ancient remains, beyond earlier studies focused mainly on mitochondrial DNA. Ancient DNA is fragmented, scarce, and vulnerable to modern DNA contamination. Target capture selectively enriches specific DNA sequences, enabling recovery of genetic information from limited aDNA. Methods targeting many SNPs have improved analysis of poorly preserved remains. Ancient genomic studies show that Jomon people had a distinctive genetic composition, while migration from continental Asia after the Yayoi period strongly influenced Japanese population formation. Studies of ancient genomes have also shown regional differences in admixture between Jomon-related and migrant-related groups during the Yayoi period, followed by increasing homogenization across the archipelago during the Kofun period. Kinship analysis of Kofun individuals provides new insights into burial practices, family relationships, and social structure. This presentation will introduce ancient genomic analysis, focusing on target capture, and review findings on Japanese population formation. It will also discuss integrating genomics with archaeology, physical anthropology, and isotope analysis to reconstruct ancient mobility and social organization.

session: ランチョンセミナー8：Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome
title: Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome: Clinical Spectrum with a Focus on Milder Phenotypes
en: Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome: Clinical Spectrum with a Focus on Milder Phenotypes
abs: Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome (HGPS) is an ultra-rare premature aging disorder caused by LMNA variants that lead to the production of progerin or other abnormal prelamin A species. HGPS has traditionally been regarded as a childhood-onset disorder, meanwhile a broad clinical spectrum has been recognized. Disease severity appears to be determined by the molecular structure of progerin, the extent of aberrant splicing, the amount of the abnormal Lamin A. Notably, a Japanese patient with LMNA c.1868C>G (p.Thr623Ser), which produces prelamin AΔ35, exhibited milder phenotype, whereas other variants with remarkable increase of progerin caused neonatal progeria. Further support comes from somatic rescue, in which a secondary mutation reduces pathogenic splicing, demonstrating that even partial correction of abnormal Lamin A production can modify disease severity. The naturally occurring mild phenotypes therefore provide biological proof of concept for therapeutic strategies aimed at reducing the burden of pathogenic Lamin A. Lonafarnib reduces progerin toxicity by inhibition of farnesylation and is expected to delay vascular disease and prolong survival.

session: ランチョンセミナー9：ALS（筋萎縮性側索硬化症）に関する最新情報
title: Presymptomatic genetic testing for hereditary neuromuscular diseases
en: Presymptomatic genetic testing for hereditary neuromuscular diseases
abs: In hereditary neuromuscular diseases, disease-modifying therapies are being developed. With these therapeutic advances, presymptomatic genetic testing has become increasingly important for early intervention. In our previous nationwide survey in Japan, hereditary ATTR amyloidosis was the disorder for which presymptomatic genetic testing was most frequently performed following the introduction of disease-modifying therapies, with a testing rate of 75.2%. Clinical research targeting the presymptomatic stage is also underway. In amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, an ongoing study is evaluating the efficacy of presymptomatic administration of the antisense oligonucleotide in individuals carrying SOD1 variants. Along with these developments, in 2025, the Japanese society of neurology published the “Guidelines for presymptomatic genetic testing for adult-onset hereditary neuromuscular diseases in Japan.” The guidelines are intended for use not only in clinical practice but also in clinical research settings. They provide 45 recommended items organized into three phases: pre-testing, test performing, and describing the results and post-testing. However, the guidelines emphasize that the need for each recommended item may vary among clients and should therefore be determined based on an assessment of each client’s individual situation, with care taken to ensure that the guidance itself does not disadvantage clients. This presentation will provide an overview of presymptomatic genetic testing and genetic counseling for hereditary neuromuscular diseases.

session: ランチョンセミナー9：ALS（筋萎縮性側索硬化症）に関する最新情報
title: Tofersen Paves the Way for a New Treatment Strategy for SOD1-ALS
en: Tofersen Paves the Way for a New Treatment Strategy for SOD1-ALS
abs: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a progressive neurological disease characterized by generalized muscle weakness caused by motor neuron degeneration. Although several treatments are available, their efficacy remains limited, emphasizing the need for therapies targeting the underlying cause. Familial ALS accounts for 5–10% of all cases, and mutations of superoxide dismutase 1 (SOD1) gene are identified in approximately one-third of familial cases in Japan. Most SOD1-associated ALS (SOD1-ALS) shows autosomal dominant inheritance and is thought to result from a toxic gain of function of mutant SOD1 rather than loss of its normal activity. Reducing mutant SOD1 expression may therefore offer a disease-modifying treatment. Tofersen (Qalsody®) is an antisense oligonucleotide that binds to SOD1 mRNA, promotes its degradation, and decreases SOD1 protein production. Its efficacy and safety have been evaluated in the international Phase III VALOR trial since 2019, with participation from Japan. Tofersen was approved in Japan in December 2024 and is now available under health insurance. This seminar will review the clinical features of SOD1-ALS and present patients treated with tofersen at our institution. We will also discuss its clinical efficacy, safety, and practical considerations based on our experience and published evidence.

session: ランチョンセミナー10：From Technical Limitations to Clinical Implementation:Integrated Long-Read Sequencing Analysis in Rare Disease
title: From Technical Limitations to Clinical Implementation: Integrated Long-Read Sequencing Analysis in Rare Disease
en: From Technical Limitations to Clinical Implementation: Integrated Long-Read Sequencing Analysis in Rare Disease
abs: Long-read sequencing has long held promise for rare disease diagnosis, but clinical implementation has been constrained by cost, turnaround time, sequencing accuracy, and the complexity of interpretation. Recent advances, particularly major improvements in sequencing accuracy, are progressively changing this landscape and making practical clinical use increasingly feasible. As accuracy improves, long-read sequencing can reveal diagnostic information that remains difficult to resolve with conventional short-read approaches. This presentation reviews how historical technical limitations restricted the clinical value of long-read sequencing and how cumulative advances are enabling a transition from research use toward clinical implementation. Using an exceptionally rare case, we demonstrate the value of integrated long-read analysis, with particular focus on repeat contraction, structural variation, phasing, and DNA methylation abnormalities. We do not propose long-read whole-genome sequencing as a universal first-line test. Rather, we consider it an advanced complementary approach for unresolved cases in which conventional testing fails to yield a diagnosis. Through this experience, we aim to illustrate how technologies once difficult to implement clinically are becoming practical diagnostic tools, expanding the possibilities for rare disease diagnosis.

session: ランチョンセミナー11：SMA・DMDにおける最新の話題
title: Advances and Remaining Challenges in SMA Care: From Newborn Screening to Long-Term Multidisciplinary Care
en: Advances and Remaining Challenges in SMA Care: From Newborn Screening to Long-Term Multidisciplinary Care
abs: The introduction of disease-modifying therapies and newborn screening has dramatically changed the motor developmental trajectory of patients with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA). In particular, diagnosis and treatment before or shortly after symptom onset have enabled many affected children to achieve motor milestones that were rarely observed in the natural history of the disease. However, as survival and motor outcomes improve, new challenges are emerging, including long-term motor management, musculoskeletal complications, and the need to establish optimal rehabilitation strategies. Our experience in caring for patients with SMA, whether identified through newborn screening or diagnosed after symptom onset, has highlighted the importance of multidisciplinary follow-up, including early attention to scoliosis and other musculoskeletal problems. At Kobe University, pediatricians, rehabilitation physicians, and physical therapists hold regular multidisciplinary meetings to discuss the long-term management of children with neuromuscular disorders, including SMA, Duchenne muscular dystrophy, Fukuyama congenital muscular dystrophy, as well as other neuromuscular diseases and inherited metabolic disorders. We are also exploring how best to collaborate with rehabilitation professionals in the community. In this presentation, I will discuss the remaining challenges in long-term SMA care, the importance of multidisciplinary and regional collaboration, and the clinical questions for which further evidence is still needed.

session: ランチョンセミナー11：SMA・DMDにおける最新の話題
title: Gene Therapy for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy in Clinical Practice: Current Status and Challenges
en: Gene Therapy for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy in Clinical Practice: Current Status and Challenges
abs: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is a severe, progressive hereditary neuromuscular disease caused by variants in the DMD gene. Delandistrogen moxeparvovec (Elevidys®), a non-replicating recombinant adeno-associated virus (rAAV) vector-based gene therapy expressing a functional micro-dystrophin, was approved in Japan in 2025 and entered clinical practice in 2026. In Japan, eligibility is restricted to ambulatory patients aged 3 to under 8 years who test negative for anti-AAVrh74 antibodies, excluding specific genetic variants. While representing a promising therapeutic option, efficacy data from clinical trials remain limited. Furthermore, severe adverse events, including hepatotoxicity, immune-mediated myositis, and myocarditis, as well as fatal acute liver failure, have been reported. In real-world clinical practice, determining treatment eligibility requires a holistic evaluation that incorporates medical indications, predictable safety risks, and patient/family values, alongside multidisciplinary collaboration across cardiology, hepatology, and intensive care. In addition, informed decision-making with patients/families is paramount. To ensure appropriate candidate evaluation, rigorous safety management, long-term follow-up, and systematic collection of real-world effectiveness and safety data, administration of Elevidys® in Japan is restricted to 13 designated facilities accredited by the Japanese Society of Child Neurology. Here, we report the practical experiences and challenges of DMD gene therapy at our center alongside current evidence and clinical data.

session: ランチョンセミナー12：SMA治療における課題と遺伝子補充療法「ゾルゲンスマ®髄注」がもたらす可能性
title: Past, Present, and Future of Pediatric SMA Treatment
en: Past, Present, and Future of Pediatric SMA Treatment
abs: Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is an inherited neuromuscular disorder primarily caused by deletion or mutation of the SMN1 gene and is characterized by progressive muscle weakness and atrophy. In recent years, newborn screening (NBS) for SMA has been implemented in many regions of Japan, enabling presymptomatic diagnosis and earlier initiation of treatment. In parallel, the development and approval of multiple disease-modifying therapies over the past decade have dramatically transformed the management of pediatric SMA. While these advances have substantially improved patient outcomes, new challenges have emerged, highlighting the growing importance of comprehensive long-term care, including the maintenance of motor function and the management of scoliosis, respiratory complications, and nutritional issues. In this lecture, we will review the pathophysiology of SMA and trace the evolution of pediatric SMA treatment from the past to the present, focusing on how novel therapies and the expansion of NBS have reshaped the clinical landscape. We will then look toward the future of SMA treatment, drawing on accumulated evidence and clinical experience with systemic onasemnogene abeparvovec to explore the evolving potential of gene replacement therapy, including novel routes of administration, in pediatric SMA.

session: ランチョンセミナー12：SMA治療における課題と遺伝子補充療法「ゾルゲンスマ®髄注」がもたらす可能性
title: Future Perspectives in Adult SMA Care
en: Future Perspectives in Adult SMA Care
abs: In recent years, several disease-modifying therapies have been developed for spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), expanding treatment options across pediatric and adult populations. Advances in early diagnosis and early intervention improve patient outcomes, whereas treatment goals in patients with SMA are diverse, depending on patient backgrounds such as individual’s disease severity and life stage. Consequently, long-term treatment strategies and appropriate methods for treatment assessment have become increasingly important in SMA care. In this lecture, I will review the evolution of SMA treatment and share insights into the clinical challenges and unmet medical needs that emerge with the advent of therapy. I will also present the characteristics and evidence of efficacy of intrathecal onasemnogene abeparvovec, which was launched this year, and discuss treatment strategies and perspectives for adult with SMA.

session: ランチョンセミナー13：遺伝学的診断が切り拓くムコ多糖症Ⅱ型診療の未来
title: Early Diagnosis Is Transforming CNS Treatment in Severe MPS II
en: Early Diagnosis Is Transforming CNS Treatment in Severe MPS II
abs: Mucopolysaccharidosis type II (MPS II) is an X-linked lysosomal storage disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the IDS gene, resulting in iduronate-2-sulfatase deficiency and accumulation of heparan and dermatan sulfates. In severe MPS II, developmental stagnation and neurological regression emerge in early childhood, when CNS disease may already be progressing. In Japan, expanded newborn screening (eNBS) provides an opportunity to identify MPS II before symptoms appear. Biochemical and genetic testing can establish the diagnosis, while genotype, family history, and clinical findings help guide follow-up and treatment timing. This shift toward earlier diagnosis is particularly important in severe MPS II, where intervention before neurological regression may offer the greatest opportunity to preserve neurodevelopment. Intravenous enzyme replacement therapy improves systemic manifestations but has limited effects on CNS disease because the enzyme does not cross the blood-brain barrier. Intracerebroventricular enzyme replacement therapy enables direct delivery of enzyme to the CNS. At our center, we combine this approach with hematopoietic stem cell transplantation to address both CNS and systemic disease, including in patients with severe MPS II identified through eNBS. Our experience highlights the importance of linking early genetic diagnosis to CNS-directed treatment. MPS II care is shifting from treatment after symptom onset toward earlier diagnosis and intervention before neurological regression becomes established.

session: ランチョンセミナー13：遺伝学的診断が切り拓くムコ多糖症Ⅱ型診療の未来
title: Novel therapeutic strategy for central nervous system manifestations in mucopolysaccharidosis type II
en: Novel therapeutic strategy for central nervous system manifestations in mucopolysaccharidosis type II
abs: Mucopolysaccharidosis type II (MPS II) is an X-linked recessive disorder caused by deficiency of the lysosomal enzyme iduronate-2-sulfatase, resulting in accumulation of dermatan sulfate and heparan sulfate. In addition to systemic manifestations such as joint contractures, skeletal deformities, hepatosplenomegaly, and valvular heart disease, approximately 70% of patients develop central nervous system (CNS) manifestations, including developmental delay and neuronal regression. Intravenous enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) can improve systemic manifestations; however, it has limited effects on CNS manifestations. To address this limitation, we developed intra-cerebroventricular enzyme replacement therapy (ICV-ERT). Six patients with neuronopathic MPS II joined in the investor-initiated clinical trial. They received 30 mg (2 mL) of idursulfase beta every 4 weeks using a cerebrospinal fluid reservoir. The three patients who initiated ICV treatment at ≤3 years of age showed sustained increases in developmental age. Idursulfase beta for ICV administration was approved in January 2020 and is currently administered to more than 40 patients. Four patients who started the combination therapy of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) and ICV-idursulfase beta at ≤1 years of age, showed continuous increase of developmental age. All four patients showed age-appropriate development until 60,48,39,20 months old, respectively. This is the first demonstration in the world showing treatment of CNS manifestation is achievable by ICV-ERT using idursulfase beta in neuronopathic MPSII.

session: 大会賞候補セッション（口演）
title: Common variant architecture in the rare Mendelian disease of Retinitis Pigmentosa
en: Common variant architecture in the rare Mendelian disease of Retinitis Pigmentosa
abs: Retinitis pigmentosa (RP) is a rare Mendelian retinal disease for which gene therapy development is rapidly advancing, while its genetic architecture remains unclear. In particular, the contribution of common variants has been largely overlooked because most studies focus on rare coding variants. To investigate the role of common variants in RP, we performed a genome-wide association study (GWAS) meta-analysis in Japanese population. We analyzed 2,721 RP patients and 218,973 controls of Japanese ancestry and identified three significant loci: ADGRV1, EYS, and REEP6. The REEP6 lead variant (rs76079175 G>C, p.V90L), is enriched in the Japanese population (allele frequency = 0.034) and showed a strong recessive effect (odds ratio 38.4 under the recessive model). The EYS locus harbors nine independent signals, multiple of which were not linked with any known pathogenic rare variants, suggesting that they likely tag hidden pathogenic variants. To further address the genetic heterogeneity of RP, we analyzed patients lacking a Mendelian genetic diagnosis and identified a novel locus in HDLBP (rs183352284, OR 1.58, P = 1.1 × 10-8). We additionally conducted a cross-population GWAS meta-analysis including 5,971 cases and 1,189,036 controls of Japanese and European ancestry, which identified a shared association signal at ADGRV1. These findings demonstrate that common variants contribute to RP genetics through both hypomorphic disease-causing variants and susceptibility loci, revealing a previously underappreciated genetic complexity beyond classical Mendelian inheritance.

session: 大会賞候補セッション（口演）
title: Structural variation with CGG repeats expansion in oculopharyngodistal myopathy
en: Structural variation with CGG repeats expansion in oculopharyngodistal myopathy
abs: [Background] Oculopharyngodistal myopathy (OPDM) is caused by CGG repeat expansions in several genes. A subset of patients additionally carries structural variants near the repeat, yet whether these patients differ in repeat instability, methylation, or clinical course is unknown. [Methods] We applied CRISPR/Cas9-targeted nanopore sequencing to DNA from 91 individuals with LRP12, GIPC1, or NOTCH2NLC expansions, comparing repeat length, intra-patient size variability, methylation, age at onset, and predicted translation products between patients with and without structural variants near the repeat. [Results] We identified structural variation in four patients, namely 5′-flanking deletions in two LRP12 cases, a duplication spanning the transcriptional start and expanded repeat in one GIPC1 case, and a 3′-flanking deletion in one NOTCH2NLC case. Their repeat length and size variability lay within the range of other patients. Compared with patients carrying similar repeat sizes without structural variation, some of these cases showed earlier onset or promoter methylation beyond what repeat length alone would predict. Each variant was also predicted to lose near-cognate codons for repeat-associated non-AUG (RAN) translation in a gene-specific way, sometimes disfavoring polyglycine and instead predicting tandem or fusion products. [Conclusions] Patients with structural variants near CGG repeats showed a preliminary trend toward earlier onset with altered predicted translation products, cautioning the assumption of uniform polyglycine toxicity in OPDM.

session: 大会賞候補セッション（口演）
title: Identification of Cell-Free mRNA Profile Associated with Maturity of Multiple Fetal Organs in Amniotic Fluid
en: Identification of Cell-Free mRNA Profile Associated with Maturity of Multiple Fetal Organs in Amniotic Fluid
abs: Background: Current methods for assessing fetal maturity are largely limited to lung maturation, and no comprehensive approach for evaluating multiple fetal organs has been established. Objective: To develop a comprehensive evaluation of multiple fetal organ maturation using cell-free mRNA in amniotic fluid, we aimed to identify maturation-associated transcripts in amniotic fluid and characterize gestational changes in their expression levels. Method: Cell-free mRNAs from amniotic fluid samples at 16 and 38 weeks of gestation were analyzed by RNA sequencing. mRNAs that were undetectable at 16 weeks but reached >300 transcripts per million at 38 weeks were selected as candidates for fetal maturity-related mRNAs. As confirmation analysis, RT-qPCR was performed using 20 samples of cell-free mRNA each from amniotic fluid at 16 and 38 weeks. Results: Overall, 1,587 mRNAs were identified by RNA sequencing analysis. Among mRNAs that increased with increasing gestational age, five (SFTPC, CALML5, NAA10, SMIM29, IFITM3P6) showing the greatest change were prioritized. RT-qPCR confirmed that all five genes were significantly more highly expressed at 38 weeks than at 16 weeks (all p<0.0001; Mann-Whitney U test). Conclusion: This study identified the cell-free mRNA profile in amniotic fluid associated with fetal maturity, expressed in multiple fetal organs. Simultaneous quantification of the cell-free mRNA profile identified here could enable comprehensive monitoring of fetal maturity.

session: 大会賞候補セッション（口演）
title: Cross-Population Germline Analysis of Early-Onset Pancreatic Cancer
en: Cross-Population Germline Analysis of Early-Onset Pancreatic Cancer
abs: Background: Early-onset pancreatic cancer (EOPC; diagnosis <50 years) is increasing worldwide, but the germline basis of early onset and its population diversity remain unclear. Methods: We analyzed germline whole-exome sequencing data from Japanese and US EOPC cohorts and integrated publicly available whole-genome sequencing data from the International Cancer Genome Consortium. Pathogenic variants in established cancer-predisposition genes and rare loss-of-function (LoF) variants in DNA repair genes were evaluated using ancestry-matched controls. Pathway enrichment and CRISPR-Cas9 dependency screens prioritized candidate modifiers, followed by functional modeling in Kras-mutant pancreatic cancer cells. Results: In Western cohorts, 22% of EOPC cases carried pathogenic variants in cancer-predisposition genes, with BRCA2 being the most frequent (12.3% among individuals of European ancestry). In contrast, Japanese cases showed a low frequency of pathogenic variants in established predisposition genes (2.2%) and no BRCA1/2 mutations, but demonstrated aggregate enrichment of rare LoF variants in other DNA repair genes. Integrative analyses prioritized CUX1 as a candidate modifier. Partial CUX1 knockdown promoted proliferation and increased sensitivity to platinum-based chemotherapy. Conclusions: The germline genetic architecture of EOPC differs across populations and extends beyond established high-penetrance genes. Cross-population analysis reveals ancestry-related DNA repair gene burdens and candidate modifiers that may refine risk assessment and prevention strategies for EOPC.

session: スポンサードシンポジウム：AMEDが支援するゲノム・オミックスデータの利活用（共催：AMED）
title: Advancing Data-Driven Dementia Research through the Use of Clinical Imaging Data
en: Advancing Data-Driven Dementia Research through the Use of Clinical Imaging Data
abs: Under the Program for the Integrated Use of Health and Medical Research Data, AMED promotes the use of data generated through AMED-funded research in accordance with government policy. Since FY2024, the program has provided a pre-research service for genomic and omics data, enabling researchers to review data overviews and explore potential research opportunities. Beginning in FY2027, the program plans to expand data use to clinical research data, including imaging data related to dementia. Three projects have been selected through an open call, and MRI, PET, and SPECT imaging data from more than 2,500 cases will be made available, covering a broad spectrum from preclinical stages and mild cognitive impairment (MCI) to dementia and dementia with behavioral and psychological symptoms. The pre-research service will also provide access to more than 350 clinical and related data items, including imaging acquisition parameters, blood and other laboratory test results, and cognitive assessment scores for each case. In collaboration with the selected research projects, we are also deriving features such as brain volume and cortical thickness from brain imaging data and preparing them for use in pre-research. We expect these dementia imaging data to be used not only by dementia researchers but also by experts in data science fields such as artificial intelligence (AI), thereby advancing research and development in drug discovery and medical devices and contributing to the creation of new healthcare services.

session: スポンサードシンポジウム：AMEDが支援するゲノム・オミックスデータの利活用（共催：AMED）
title: Development of Three-Layer Datasets Integrating Health, Genomic, and Omics Data for Multifactorial Diseases
en: Development of Three-Layer Datasets Integrating Health, Genomic, and Omics Data for Multifactorial Diseases
abs: This program was conducted over a five-year period from FY2021 to FY2025 under a strategic policy that prioritized the analysis of biological samples to address the needs of both academia and industry. Eight projects were selected, and through the analysis of samples collected and stored in a variety of cohorts and biobanks, the program generated datasets that are readily available for research use. The program focused on common multifactorial diseases, including COPD, atrial fibrillation, chronic heart failure, and diabetes. Using biological samples obtained from the same individuals, researchers performed comprehensive multi-omics analyses, including WGS. These analytical results were subsequently integrated with health and clinical information to establish comprehensive “three-layer datasets.” The resulting datasets have been deposited in AGD, the public database operated by AMED. In addition, the associated metadata have been registered in CANNDs, AMED’s data utilization platform, enabling integrated searches across all projects supported by the program. Because the diseases targeted by this program are common conditions influenced by a complex interplay of genetic and environmental factors, the datasets are expected to provide valuable resources for advancing biomedical research. By making these “three-layer datasets” broadly accessible, the program aims to foster participation from researchers across diverse disciplines, promote new scientific insights, and expand the overall research community working toward the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of these conditions.

session: スポンサードシンポジウム：AMEDが支援するゲノム・オミックスデータの利活用（共催：AMED）
title: Integrating Genomics and Multi-Omics to Decipher Cardiovascular Disease Mechanisms
en: Integrating Genomics and Multi-Omics to Decipher Cardiovascular Disease Mechanisms
abs: Cardiovascular diseases arise from complex interactions between genetic susceptibility and environmental factors, yet how these influences converge to shape disease development and progression remains incompletely understood. Recent advances in genomics and multi-omics technologies provide an opportunity to move beyond the identification of disease-associated genes toward a comprehensive understanding of disease mechanisms at cellular and tissue levels. We have integrated large-scale human genomic data with transcriptomic, epigenomic, single-cell, and spatial omics analyses to investigate the molecular basis of cardiovascular diseases, including atrial fibrillation, cardiomyopathy, and heart failure. These approaches reveal that cellular mechanisms underlying genetic susceptibility may differ from those driving pathological tissue remodeling and disease progression. By resolving cell-type-specific regulatory programs and interactions among diverse cardiac cell populations, integrated multi-omics analyses provide new insights into how genetic and acquired factors contribute to disease heterogeneity. This framework enables a shift from disease classification based primarily on clinical phenotypes toward molecularly defined disease endotypes, providing a foundation for patient stratification and the development of mechanism-based precision cardiovascular medicine.

session: スポンサードシンポジウム：AMEDが支援するゲノム・オミックスデータの利活用（共催：AMED）
title: Facilitating genomic data sharing and utilization through the National Center Biobank Network
en: Facilitating genomic data sharing and utilization through the National Center Biobank Network
abs: The National Center Biobank Network (NCBN) is a collaborative framework connecting six National Centers in Japan, each operating a disease-oriented biobank. NCBN collects and manages high-quality biospecimens and associated clinical information across a wide range of diseases, providing valuable resources for biomedical research and genomic medicine. To establish a large-scale genomic reference dataset for the Japanese population, NCBN conducted whole-genome sequencing (WGS) of 9,850 individuals from five participating biobanks. The resulting dataset provides comprehensive information on genetic variation in the Japanese population and serves as an important control resource for studies of rare diseases and cancer. The data have been utilized in collaborative research projects, including investigations of population genetic diversity and disease-associated variants. To further promote the utilization of these genomic resources, the AMED Genome group sharing Database (AGD), operated by the DNA Data Bank of Japan (DDBJ), provides a platform for controlled access to individual-level genomic data. Sharing NCBN genomic data through AGD is expected to facilitate broader research access while ensuring appropriate data governance and protection of participant privacy. In this presentation, I will introduce the activities of NCBN, highlight the current utilization of its WGS dataset, and discuss ongoing efforts and challenges in establishing a sustainable framework for genomic data sharing.

session: スポンサードシンポジウム：AMEDが支援するゲノム・オミックスデータの利活用（共催：AMED）
title: BioBank Japan in CANNDS: Data Utilization, Sustainable Access, and Future Directions through TRE and JAMBO
en: BioBank Japan in CANNDS: Data Utilization, Sustainable Access, and Future Directions through TRE and JAMBO
abs: BioBank Japan (BBJ) supports research on common diseases through biospecimens and clinical and genomic data from approximately 270,000 patients. For CANNDS, BBJ selected 6000 participants to serve as controls for cancer/rare diseases, aiming for balanced representation across Japan's 47 prefectures. Their genomic data have been used by many researchers and are being analyzed as a reference resource for the Japanese population such as imputation panel. To ensure sustainable access, BBJ revised its data management framework in 2026. Whole-genome sequencing data are stored on the supercomputer, SHIROKANE, at the University of Tokyo, and access applications are reviewed by the BBJ Sample and Data Access Committee. This framework supports continued use of the CANNDS resource. BBJ is also preparing to introduce a Trusted Research Environment to enable secure data analysis and research collaboration while respecting consent restrictions and protecting personal information. BBJ also contributes to the Japan Mega Biobank and Cohort Consortium (JAMBO), launched in 2026. JAMBO brings together approximately 30 biobanks and cohorts, covering around 1.5 million participants. Its activities include harmonizing clinical and genomic data and developing pilot studies on the allergic march and age-dependent genetic effects on height, weight, and BMI. These efforts will connect disease biobanks with population and birth cohorts to advance life-course research. This presentation reviews CANNDS data use and outlines these ongoing activities.
